title: Harden EXIF orientation: limits after rotation, fallible allocation, strict IFD parsing
author: echelon
body:
Refs #285

Follow-up hardening of the EXIF-orientation code from #318, per AGENTS.md's never-crash rules.

## Changes
- **Limits after rotation** (`crates/codecs/src/lib.rs`): orientations 5–8 swap width and height, so `Limits` are checked again on the upright size before orienting. The error is the usual `LimitExceeded`.
- **Fallible allocation** (`orientation.rs`): the rotated buffer is allocated with `try_reserve_exact`, so running out of memory returns `LimitExceeded` instead of aborting the process.
- **Strict IFD parsing**: these read as orientation 1, and the tag is left alone:
  - an IFD0 offset below 8
  - an IFD table cut off before its next-IFD pointer
  - an Orientation entry whose count is not 1, or whose type is neither SHORT nor LONG (LONG is accepted because some cameras and tools write it)
- **Duplicates**: the first Orientation entry wins, like libexif. If that first entry is malformed, the tag is ignored even when a later duplicate is valid. `upright_exif` sets every well-formed duplicate to 1, so a reader that lets the last entry win can't rotate the pixels a second time.
- `upright_exif` changes only the tag's value bytes and writes 1 in the entry's existing type and width (2 bytes for SHORT, 4 for LONG).

## Tests
- `crates/codecs/tests/orientation.rs` has new tests:
  - `duplicate_orientation_entries_first_wins`
  - `strict_ifd_parsing_ignores_the_tag`

title: Use native brush cursors and endpoint-aligned desktop motion
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
Fast brush strokes now consume ordered OS positions instead of one position per frame. A cached native brush outline follows the OS cursor independently of canvas rendering. Usable relative motion adds a bounded, estimated interior curve between OS positions; the OS endpoints and acceleration remain authoritative.

The default input path covers macOS 14+ Game Controller motion, Windows Raw Input, and Linux XInput2/Wayland relative-pointer events when available. Windows/Linux reuse eframe/winit's existing event stream without new unsafe code or platform hooks. Missing samples, uncertain geometry, batched absolute positions, active touch/pen input and automation retain the OS-only path. Gesture, focus and view changes discard candidates; stroke interruption preserves ink in its owning document.

No input-engine selector or diagnostic UI remains. Smoothing receives the additional points in the existing paint engine. Large brush outlines, pixel-snapped Pencil footprints and web retain their required canvas cursor fallback.

GC lacks reliable per-delta timestamps; normalized Windows/Linux events also omit device IDs and individual timestamps. Arrival order and endpoint fitting estimate interior coordinates. Delayed callbacks, mixed devices and frame boundaries cannot be perfectly correlated. No waiting, prediction, retrospective edits or higher sampling-rate guarantee is introduced.

Validation for final production source `910e798`:

- **Windows:** [green final validation](https://github.com/TheSeanLavery/photocraft/actions/runs/37522806663): 22 alignment/tablet tests, 4 UI replay tests, linked native application, and strict all-target tablet/UI/app Clippy on Rust 1.99. Test-only profile overrides avoid a slow optimized cold build; production profiles are unchanged.
- **Linux:** 533 relevant library tests pass, 3 ignored; native application check passes. Final contact regressions and all-target lint checks pass on Rust 1.98.1.
- **macOS:** 596 relevant tests pass, 3 igno…

title: Stamp Visible (Cmd+Alt+Shift+E) and Stamp Down; Alt+Merge keeps the originals (#217)
author: echelon
body:
Part of #217 (Layers: Stamp Visible, and Alt+Merge keeps the originals)

## What changes
New engine commands in `crates/engine/src/stamp_cmds.rs`. Photoshop has no menu items for these; they are the ⌥ variants of the merge commands. Here they are commands with Photoshop's default shortcuts, so they can be rebound in Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts (listed at the end of the **Layer** section), recorded in actions, and driven by agents.

| Command | Default | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `layer.stampVisible` | ⌘⌥⇧E / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E | Merges every visible layer into a **new layer above the active one**, keeping the originals. |
| `layer.stampDown` | ⌘⌥E / Ctrl+Alt+E | Merges a **copy** of the active layer into the pixel layer below, keeping the active layer. With several layers selected, merges a copy of them into a new "… (merged)" layer above the top one. |

**Stamp Visible details**
- The stamp is named "Layer N".
- If the active layer is in a group, the stamp goes into that group.
- The stamp becomes the selected, active layer.
- Hidden layers and hidden groups are left out. Opacity, blend modes and styles are composited as displayed.
- It is one undo step.

**Alt+click in the Layer menu**
- ⌥ + Merge Visible runs `layer.stampVisible`.
- ⌥ + Merge Down or Merge Layers runs `layer.stampDown`.
- This is done in `menus::alt_click`. Errors from a menu click now show in the status bar.

**Memory**
- The composite is rendered in bands with `photocraft_compose::flatten_to_surface` (about 8 M px per band, written straight into the target surface, transparent tiles pruned). No full-size float copy of the document is held.
- On 24 MP that is one ~128 MB band at a time, instead of ~384 MB of f32 RGBA for the whole canvas plus a second full-size `Vec`, which is what `merge_visible` and `merge_layers` still do today.
- Speed: Stamp Visible on a 6000 × 4000 document with 4 layers takes **≈0.4 s** in release (`cargo test --release -p photocraft-engine --lib stamp_visible_24mp -- --ignored …

title: Liquify: avoid wasm Instant panic (#334)
author: 0xenzyme

## Summary

Fix `filter.liquify` crashing in the web build.

`std::time::Instant::now()` compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, but panics at runtime because wall-clock time is not implemented on that target. Liquify now uses the engine's existing wasm-safe `Stopwatch`, which reports `0 ms` on wasm and keeps native timing on desktop platforms.

title: Right-click on the canvas lists the layers under the pointer (#307)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #307

## What changes
This adds Photoshop's canvas layer context menu. New module: `crates/ui-egui/src/layer_pick_ui.rs`.

**Opening it**
- Right-click on the canvas with the **Move tool**, or **⌘/Ctrl+right-click with any tool**.

- `ui.pointer {button: "right"}` with the Move tool, or with `command: true`, opens the menu at that document point.

title: Polygonal Lasso: double-click closes the polygon; a new polygon replaces the selection in one step
author: rosematcha
body:
With the Polygonal Lasso, a double-click added a second point instead of closing the polygon, and the old selection stayed up while you drew a new one. Both now work as in Photoshop:

- A double-click closes the polygon at the point you clicked.
- In New Selection mode, the old selection is hidden while you draw and replaced in one history step when the polygon closes; Esc leaves it as it was. ⇧ or ⌥ at the first click keeps it, to add to or subtract from, and ↩ closes the polygon in that mode.

author: rosematcha
body:
Fixes #293

⌘-scroll (Ctrl-scroll on Windows) zoomed the canvas and ⌥-scroll (Alt-scroll) scrolled it. Photoshop does it the other way around:

- ⌘-scroll (Ctrl-scroll) scrolls sideways.
- ⌥-scroll (Alt-scroll) zooms the canvas about 5 % per wheel notch. Over a panel it still scrolls the panel.
- Trackpad pinch still zooms on macOS and in browsers. A Windows touchpad sends its pinch as Ctrl-scroll, so there it now scrolls sideways.

Scorecard row UI-217-18 moves to partial: the zoom-controls half is untouched.

title: Type: the Color panel, Swatches and Color Picker recolor selected text
author: rosematcha
body:
While editing type, picking a color in the Color panel, Swatches or the Color Picker only changed the foreground color. Only the text-color swatch in the options bar recolored the selection. Now all of them recolor the selected characters, as in Photoshop, inside the edit's single history step. With no characters selected they only set the foreground color, as before.

This also fixes the Color panel's HSB sliders, which rewrote the foreground color every frame for colors that don't survive the HSB round trip (#D8452E, for example). They now act only when you move a slider.

Tests: `type_tool_tests.rs` and `panels.rs` (a real swatch click, and idle sliders leaving the color alone).

title: Free Transform: Undo steps through the transform; handles are easier to grab
author: rosematcha
body:
During Free Transform, Undo undid the document's last step under the open box instead of the last scale or rotation. Undo and Redo now step through the transform itself, as in Photoshop: each drag, nudge or options-bar edit is one step, and ↩ still commits a single document step. That holds for every caller: the menus, shortcuts, and `edit.undo` / `edit.redo` sent over the control channel or MCP all go through the same check in `PhotocraftApp::run`. While the box is open, Toggle Last State and the History panel wait until you commit or cancel; over automation, Toggle Last State returns an error saying so.

The handles also grab within 12 pt instead of 8. With the Move tool's transform controls, a press just off a corner used to start a rotation; now it scales. On small boxes the nearest handle wins over the reference point.

Tests: `transform_undo_tests.rs` drives the real canvas with kittest, plus unit tests in `transform_tool.rs` and `panels.rs`.

Validation: each fixed behavior's test failed before the fix. `cargo fmt`, `clippy --workspace -D warnings`, the 553 UI tests, `xtask layers`, `wasm` and `scorecard --check` pass.

title: Canvas scrollbars, and Preferences > Tools > Overscroll works (#300)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #300

## What changes
**Canvas scrollbars.** New module `crates/ui-egui/src/scrollbars.rs`.

- A horizontal bar runs along the bottom of the document view and a vertical one along the right, like Photoshop's document window.
- Each bar shows only when the image doesn't fit along that axis. When everything fits, both are hidden.
- The thumb is the visible fraction of the scrollable extent: the image plus wherever the view has been scrolled past it. A minimum thumb length of 24 pt keeps it easy to grab on huge images.
- Dragging the thumb scrolls. The extent is frozen for the length of the drag, and the drag starts from the press point, not the drag threshold.
- Clicking the track pages one screenful toward the click, stopping at the image edge.
- The bars are drawn over the canvas edges and take the pointer there, so clicks on them never reach the current tool. The wheel still scrolls over them.
- They follow View › Flip Horizontal and use theme tokens (`chrome`, `separator`, `text_faint`, `text_dim` on hover). They work in every Window › Arrange cell.

**Preferences › Tools › Overscroll now does something.**
- With Overscroll off, the view is clamped **before anything is drawn**. The image can't be scrolled past its edges, and an image smaller than the window stays centred on that axis.
- When the clamp moves the view, a repaint is requested. Movements under 1e-3 px are ignored, so the clamp can't keep requesting frames.
- The setting was hidden from Edit › Preferences because nothing read it (`prefs::HIDDEN_UNTIL_IMPLEMENTED`). It is now shown, and `docs/scorecard.md` is regenerated: settings that do nothing went from 61 to 60 of 133.
- With Overscroll on (the default), the view is free as before, and the bars grow to include the overscrolled area.

## Per-frame cost
Measured with the bars shown on a 1280 × 800 canvas over a 6000 × 4000 image, in the optimized test profile, over 2000 frames:
- `scrollbars::show`: **≈0.9 µs per frame**
- `clamp_view`: **≈8 ns …

author: echelon
body:
Fixes #297

## What changes
**Alt+right-drag** with a painting tool now changes the brush instead of painting. This is Photoshop's Windows/Linux gesture; on macOS, Ctrl+Option+drag (#271) already does it.

- Left/right sets the diameter, and the circle's edge follows the pointer. Up/down sets the hardness; down makes it harder.
- It reuses `crates/ui-egui/src/brush_resize.rs`, so it shows the same tinted circle and the same Diameter/Hardness readout as #271.

title: Alt+scroll zooms the canvas in 5% steps around the pointer (#293)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #293

## What changes
Holding **Alt** (Option on a Mac) while scrolling over the canvas zooms around the pointer, about **5% per wheel notch**. This matches Photoshop with Preferences › General › Zoom with Scroll Wheel off.

- New `crates/ui-egui/src/wheel_nav.rs` decides what a frame of wheel input does to the view:
  - plain scroll pans (Shift scrolls sideways, as before)
  - pinch or ⌘/Ctrl+scroll is egui's zoom gesture, unchanged
  - ⌥/Alt+scroll zooms in notch steps: `1.05^(delta / line_scroll_speed)`
  - with Zoom with Scroll Wheel on, a plain scroll still zooms as before
- egui spreads one notch over several frames. If the Alt state were read from the live modifiers, releasing Alt mid-notch would turn the rest of it into a pan. So the Alt state comes from the wheel events themselves and lasts until the next wheel event, the way egui keeps its own wheel modifiers.
- It works alongside the held-key tools (#249/#275): Space, ⌘Space and ⌘⌥Space don't change the current tool, and Alt+scroll still steps by notches while they're held. ⌘⌥+scroll is ⌘-scroll, which wins.
- Non-finite deltas, a zero or NaN notch size, or factors that overflow produce no zoom, never a NaN view.

## Tests
- `wheel_nav` unit tests:
  - one notch is ×1.05, and three notches back out are ×1.05⁻³
  - a notch smoothed over four frames multiplies back to ×1.05
  - a plain scroll pans
  - pinch and ⌘-scroll still zoom
  - the Zoom with Scroll Wheel preference still applies
  - hostile values (NaN, ±inf, 1e30, zero or negative notch size) never produce a bad zoom
- `input_tests` with real egui wheel events through the canvas:
  - an ⌥ notch zooms 5% and the document point under the pointer stays put, with Alt released right after the event while egui is still smoothing the notch
  - a plain notch pans and doesn't zoom
  - ⌘-scroll still zooms in bigger steps
  - Alt+scroll zooms while Space is held, and the Brush is still the tool afterwards

title: Open HEIC/HEIF photos (#355)
author: ljkx
body:
Fixes #355.

HEIC is what every iPhone (and a Mac screenshot or export) saves by default, and PhotoCraft had no HEIF code at all: `.heic` files didn't appear in File › Open's "All Formats" filter, and opening one anyway failed with "unrecognized image format". Photoshop opens them.

## What changed

- **`photocraft-codecs`: new `Format::Heif`** (`.heic` / `.heif` / `.hif`, `image/heif`), decoded by [`heic-rs`](https://crates.io/crates/heic-rs). It is pure Rust, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, MIT OR Apache-2.0, needs no C toolchain, and builds for wasm. That means it works on the web build too, not only behind a C feature as `docs/architecture.md` had planned for libheif.
  - It handles single pictures and **grid-tiled photos** (how every iPhone photo is stored). Tiles decode in parallel on native and on one thread on wasm.
  - **8-bit → U8; 10/12-bit → U16**, so depth is kept. Auxiliary alpha → RGBA.
  - Keeps the **ICC profile** (`colr`/`prof`, e.g. Display P3), **EXIF** and **XMP**. Pixels stay in the file's own colour space; PhotoCraft colour-manages them through the ICC, rather than clipping them to sRGB.
  - **Orientation:** the container's `irot`/`imir`/`clap` are applied and EXIF Orientation is rewritten to 1. HEIF's EXIF tag only repeats the container's, so applying both would rotate the photo twice. `keep_orientation` returns the coded pixels and the original EXIF.
  - `Limits` are checked against the container's declared size before any pixel is decoded, and passed down as `max_pixels`.
  - **Read-only**, listed in `ASYMMETRIC_EXCEPTIONS`: writing needs an HEVC encoder, and the mature ones (x265, libheif) are C. Saving still works through every other format.
  - Detection uses the `ftyp` brands (`heic`, `heix`, `heim`, `heis`, `mif1`, `miaf`, …). AVIF still wins when a file carries both `mif1` and `avif`. Sequence-only files (`msf1`/`hevc`) are recognised, so opening one says "image sequence, not supported" instead of "unrecognized format".

title: Packaging: Arch Linux AUR packages (photocraft, photocraft-bin) and publish workflow
author: ulises214
body:
## What

Arch Linux packages on the AUR, published automatically on every release, so Arch users can `yay -S photocraft-bin` (or `photocraft` to build from source).

- `packaging/arch/photocraft-bin/PKGBUILD`: repackages the release's `photocraft-<v>-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.tar.gz`. Installs in seconds.
- `packaging/arch/photocraft/PKGBUILD`: builds the tag's source with the system `cargo`. Mirrors the staging in `packaging/linux/package.sh` (desktop entry, MIME, metainfo, icons) and sets `PHOTOCRAFT_BUILD_SHA`/`PHOTOCRAFT_BUILD_DATE`, because the source tarball has no `.git`.
- `packaging/arch/update.sh <version>`: points both PKGBUILDs at a published release (pkgver, checksums from `SHA256SUMS.txt`, the tag's commit) and regenerates `.SRCINFO`. It maps pre-releases like `0.3.0-rc.1` to the pkgver `0.3.0rc.1`.
- `.github/workflows/aur.yml`: runs on `release: published` (pre-releases are skipped) or by hand, with a `dry_run` input. In an `archlinux:base-devel` container it runs `update.sh`, builds and installs `photocraft-bin`, runs `photocraft-cli --version` and `namcap`, and verifies the source package's checksums. It then pushes `PKGBUILD` + `.SRCINFO` to `ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/<pkg>.git`. The AUR host key is checked against its published fingerprint. Without the secret it only checks and warns, like the signing secrets in `release.yml`.
- Docs: `packaging/arch/README.md` and a new *Arch Linux (AUR)* section in `docs/releasing.md`.

Arch's pacman hooks refresh the desktop, MIME and icon caches, so there's no install script. Windowing and GPU libraries are dlopen()ed, so `depends` lists them by hand, mirroring `nfpm.yaml`. pacman has no "A or B" dependencies, so it lists both `vulkan-icd-loader` and `libglvnd`.

title: Paste: a copied image file pastes its pixels (part of #338)
author: Ar-maan05
body:
## Problem

Copying an image file in a file manager (GNOME Files, Dolphin, Finder, Explorer) and pressing Ctrl+V in PhotoCraft does nothing: the status bar says the clipboard holds no image. File managers put the file's path on the clipboard (`text/uri-list` on Linux), not its pixels, and the native clipboard service only asked arboard for image data. This is the paste half of #338.

Reproduced on Fedora 44, GNOME 50 Wayland, with the v0.2.0 RPM, driving the app through the control channel:

| Clipboard contents | v0.2.0 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Image data (`image/png`, e.g. a screenshot) | pasted | pasted (unchanged) |
| Copied file (`text/uri-list`, CRLF, `%20` in the name) | "the clipboard is empty" | pasted, centred like any foreign image |
| Copied non-image file | nothing to paste | nothing new to paste (unchanged) |

## Fix

`apps/photocraft/src/services.rs`: when `get_image()` finds no image, `clipboard_get_image` falls back to `get().file_list()` (arboard 3.6, already a dependency, on Linux, Windows and macOS) and returns the first file that decodes, through `photocraft_codecs::decode`, so EXIF orientation and the decode limits apply as on open. The UI side is unchanged: it still receives RGBA8 and the clipboard is still read only on an explicit paste.

- Non-images are skipped after reading a 256-byte header (`codecs::detect`), so copying a large video and pressing Ctrl+V does not read the whole file.
- TGA has no magic number and `detect` guesses it from header plausibility, so a TGA guess also needs a `.tga` extension.
- arboard splits `text/uri-list` on `\n` only, but the format is CRLF-terminated (RFC 2483) and GTK writes it that way, so a path copied in GNOME Files arrives as `/home/me/pic.png\r` and fails to open. The trailing `\r` is trimmed.

## Tests

New unit tests in `services.rs`: a copied PNG pastes its pixels; a CRLF path with a space resolves; missing files, directories and text files are skipped for the first real image; a truncated PNG …

title: Content-Aware Scale: 13x faster seam removal, bit-identical output (part of #211)
author: Ar-maan05
body:
## Problem

Content-Aware Scale on 24 MP is scorecard row P28: 954 s measured against a 3 s budget (#211). In `crates/algo/src/seam.rs`, every removed seam recomputed the full energy map, ran the seam search with fresh allocations, and copied the whole image into a new buffer, all on one thread.

Per seam on a 6000x4000 RGBA f32 image (16 threads, release):

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Seam search (`find_seam`) | 85-89 ms | 10-13 ms |
| Energy | 133 ms full map, every seam | 2-5 pixels per row next to the seam |
| Seam removal | new 384 MB buffer | in-place row shift, in parallel |
| **Total per seam** | **319 ms** | **23.6 ms** |
| 600 seams (10% narrower) | ~191 s (extrapolated) | 14.1 s |

## Fix

- The image, protection and energy buffers keep their original row stride. Removing a seam shifts only the rest of each row (`copy_within`), with rows in parallel (rayon on native, sequential on wasm like the rest of `algo`).
- A pixel's energy changes only when a neighbour changes. After a removal, that is within one pixel of the seam in its own row and the rows above and below, so only `min(seam[y-1..=y+1]) - 1 ..= max(...)` is recomputed per row. Full and incremental energy share one `energy_at` function, so their values are bit-identical.
- The seam search reuses its buffers across seams, and its interior loop has no edge tests, so it vectorizes. It makes the same comparisons in the same order: ties still go to the pixel straight up, then up-left, then up-right, and to the leftmost end at the bottom.
- Enlarging uses the same carver, with the original column tracked per pixel, instead of `Vec::remove` on a per-row index list.

## Output is unchanged

- A new test, `output_bits_are_pinned`, pins an FNV hash of the output bits of 8 carves taken from the previous implementation. They cover shrink, enlarge past half the width, both axes, protection, 1/3/4 channels, and tie-heavy quantised noise.
- Outside the repo, I compared the old and new `carve` bit …

title: Content-Aware Scale: enlarging a 1 px wide or tall layer no longer panics
author: Ar-maan05
body:
## Problem

Edit > Content-Aware Scale on a layer (or selection) that is 1 px wide, enlarged horizontally, fails with "`edit.contentAwareScale` failed with an internal error (logged); the document is unchanged". The same happens for a 1 px tall layer enlarged vertically. Underneath it is a panic that the session's last-resort guard catches:

| Input -> target | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1x48 -> 5x48 | panic in `write_region`: "region data length mismatch" (192 vs 960) | the column is repeated |
| 1x5 -> 6x10 | panic in `seam::transpose` (index out of range) | 6x10 |
| 64x1 -> 64x4, 16x1 -> 21x2, 7x1 -> 3x8 | panic (same, through the height pass) | correct size |

## Cause

To enlarge, `carve_width_with` finds `k` seams on a shrinking copy and duplicates them, but the loop stopped as soon as the copy was 1 px wide (`if tw <= 1 { break; }`). A 1 px wide image therefore found no seam, `added == 0` ended the loop, and the image came back at its old width instead of `new_w`. `carve_with` then transposed it as if it were `new_w` wide (panic), or the engine wrote it into the `new_w` region (assertion).

## Fix

One line: the loop now stops only at width 0, so a 1 px wide copy gives up its one column as the seam, and that column is duplicated. Duplication averages it with its right neighbour, which for the last column is itself, so the column is repeated exactly. For any image at least 2 px wide the guard never fired anyway: a round takes `k <= cw / 2` seams, so the copy always keeps at least 2 columns. So nothing else changes.

## Tests

- `seam::tests::one_pixel_lines_enlarge_by_repeating`: exact pixels for 1x5 -> 4x5, 5x1 -> 5x3 and 1x1 -> 3x2, plus output sizes for the shapes that panicked, with protection on.
- `edit_menu_cmds::tests::content_aware_scale_enlarges_a_one_pixel_line`: the command on 1 px wide and 1 px tall layers, with and without a change on the other axis. It panicked before the fix.
- Outside the repo, I compared old and new `carve` on 5,045 ran…

title: fix(engine): use wasm-safe timing for Liquify
author: naumanAhmed3
body:

Fixes the WebAssembly runtime panic in `filter.liquify`.

- WebAssembly builds use the safe fallback and no longer panic.
- The returned `ms` value remains finite and non-negative.
- Liquify's existing behavior and response metadata are preserved.

## Implementation

- Replaced the Liquify timing call with `crate::photo_cmds::Stopwatch`.
- Added regression coverage for the elapsed-time response.
- The regression explicitly asserts the WebAssembly fallback returns `0 ms`.

The implementation was validated with:

- Focused Liquify regression: passed
- Full `photocraft-engine` suite: 597 tests plus integration tests passed

title: Profile mismatch: compare profiles by colour, not bytes (sRGB vs sRGB prompt)
author: ljkx
body:
Follow-up to the "Embedded Profile Mismatch prompt for sRGB vs sRGB" I mentioned in #332.

## The bug

Open nearly any Photoshop file and PhotoCraft asks:

> Embedded Profile Mismatch: **sRGB IEC61966-2.1** vs **sRGB IEC61966-2.1**

`ColorMgmt::open_policy` decided there was a mismatch by comparing `content_hash()`, a hash of the ICC **bytes**. Photoshop embeds the classic v2 sRGB profile (3,144 bytes, 1024-entry TRC tables), while PhotoCraft's working sRGB is its own v4 encoding (parametric curves). They describe the same colours but never share a byte, so the prompt appeared every time. The same byte comparison also stopped 32-bit documents in Photoshop's linear sRGB ("sRGB IEC61966-2.1 (Linear RGB Profile)") from getting the existing stay-linear exemption, so they prompted too.

**Measured on the test corpora:** of the 75 profile-tagged PSDs in `corpus/` (Photoshop oracles, psd-tools, ag-psd), **all 75 prompted on open**. With this change **6 do**: two Adobe RGB, two Gray Gamma 2.2 (against the sGray working space) and two SWOP CMYK (against the synthetic coated CMYK). Each is a real mismatch.

## The fix

- **`photocraft-cms`: new `Profile::same_colors(&other)`.** Two profiles are the same if they share a colour space and every sample of a device-value grid has the same colour through both: relative colorimetric to Lab D50, max ΔE76 ≤ `SAME_COLORS_MAX_DELTA_E` = 0.5. The grid is 17³ for RGB and 9⁴ for CMYK. The threshold is calibrated on real profiles:

  | pair | max ΔE76 |
  |---|---|
  | Photoshop's / Windows' sRGB IEC61966-2.1 vs built-in sRGB | 0.025 |
  | Photoshop's linear sRGB vs built-in linear sRGB | 0.005 |
  | SWOP vs SWOP re-encoded | 0.000 |
  | sRGB vs sRGB with the red primary scaled 2% | 1.0 |
  | Gray Gamma 2.2 vs sGray | 2.9 |
  | sRGB vs Display P3 / Adobe RGB | 35 / 50 |

  Colours are compared rather than round-tripped. My first version checked that profile A → profile B was the identity, but CMYK → PCS → CMYK isn't an identity even through…

title: PSD: read smart-filter masks (FEid) with one section per smart object
author: EthanSuquet
body:
Photoshop writes the smart-filter mask block (`FEid`) as **one length-prefixed section per smart object**. `crates/psd/src/filter_effects.rs` read only the first section, so a file with smart filters on more than one smart object warned "unexpected bytes after the data" and the later smart objects' filter masks weren't loaded.

It wasn't caught because all 28 files with an `FEid` block in the public corpora have a single section. I found it running a batch of real-world, Photoshop-saved PSDs through `photocraft-cli` (files not shareable; the test below is synthetic).

- **Reader:** walks every section, and still accepts the older several-items-in-one-section layout.
- **Writer:** emits one padded section per item, as Photoshop does.

**Tests:**
- `reads_one_section_per_item` (new) fails before the fix (parse error) and passes after.
- `reads_several_items_in_one_section` keeps the old layout covered.
- On the real files the warning is gone, and renders are unchanged.

Ran `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test` for psd, compose, io and gpu, plus `cargo xtask test-corpus` for psd and io, all green. Not run locally: `xtask wasm`.

title: Shapes: a hairline vector stroke no longer darkens the shape's edge pixels
author: EthanSuquet
body:
On shape layers with layer effects, a hairline stroke (e.g. 0.25 px) came out as a solid dark line: an edge pixel of 122 where Photoshop has 220. `fit_stroke` (`crates/compose/src/shape_split.rs`) painted our own stroke colour at the alpha fitted from Photoshop's pixels. Photoshop snaps the shape to the pixel grid ("Align Edges"), so most of that fitted alpha is really fill, not stroke.

**Fix:** the fitted stroke now takes the colour that, drawn over our fill, reproduces Photoshop's pixel.

**Tests:**

- On a batch of real-world PSDs (not shareable), the affected file went from 0.21% of pixels off by more than 32 to 0.01%. The other 29 files were unchanged.

title: 32-bit documents: Exposure works on the stored linear values
author: floflo777
body:
In a 32-bit document the samples are already linear light, but Exposure still went through the 2.2 tone curve (`Transfer::for_exposure`) before scaling, so the gamma was applied twice. Photoshop applies `(v · 2^exposure + offset)^(1/gamma)` to the stored values directly.

I checked it by fitting the Photoshop oracles: on `adjustments/rgb32/exposure.psd` and `gray32/exposure.psd` that formula is within 0.5/255 of the merged image everywhere. Before this change they were 69/255 and 44/255 off.

The change itself is small: `Transfer::for_mode(mode)` becomes `Transfer::for_document(mode, depth)` and returns `Gamma(1.0)` for F32. It's used in the three places that built the transfer: the CPU compositor context, the GPU plan context (so the canvas stays in sync, and the existing F32 Exposure case in `gpu/tests/parity.rs` still passes), and the destructive Image › Adjustments path. 8 and 16-bit documents are unchanged.

Numbers:
- photoshop oracles 128 → 130 / 258 (rgb32 and gray32 exposure), so I raised the floor in `io/tests/corpus.rs` and regenerated the scorecard
- io corpus and psd-tools corpus: same counts as main, nothing regressed

Tests: new `exposure_scales_32_bit_samples_as_stored` in compose (fails without the change: 0.274 instead of 0.4). compose, engine and gpu tests pass, plus `cargo xtask test-corpus` (photoshop/psd/psd-tools), clippy, layers and wasm.

One unrelated thing I hit: on an NVIDIA RTX 5080 (Linux, Vulkan) `gpu/tests/parity.rs::adjustment_layers` already fails on main with a 1/255 Hue/Saturation difference at (18,23). It has nothing to do with this PR, same result with and without it.

author: ljkx

title: 32-bit documents: Levels don't clip the input and output ranges
author: floflo777
body:
Builds on #400: the first two commits are that PR, the last two are this one.

Same story as Exposure: in 32-bit documents Photoshop's Levels doesn't clip. Fitting `adjustments/rgb32/levels.psd` (input 15..230, gamma 1.3, output 10..245), the merged image follows

```
t = (v - in_black) / (in_white - in_black)
out = out_black + sign(t) * |t|^(1/gamma) * (out_white - out_black)
```

with no clamp on `t` and no shadow toe: a pixel at 0.0497 comes out at 3/255 (the clipped curve gives 10/255), and 0.947 lands on 255 instead of 245. That's within 0.5/255 of Photoshop on the whole file. Before this change it was 10/255 off.

- `levels_float` is the curve above. `tone_luts_depth(adj, depth)` uses it for RGB-space Levels in F32 documents and falls back to `tone_luts_q` otherwise. Rows are still sampled on 0..1 and kept in 0..1, like every other adjustment result in the compositor.
- `apply_depth` and the GPU `adjustment_program` now take the depth instead of the quantum. The quantum for 8/16-bit still comes from `adjustment_quantum`, so integer documents don't change, and the CPU and the canvas share the same LUT rows. `apply_with` keeps passing `None` (unrounded, clipped).
- Curves at 32-bit already matched (rgb32/curves.psd passes), so I left them alone.

Numbers: photoshop oracles 130 → 132 / 258 (rgb32 and gray32 levels), floor raised and scorecard regenerated. io and psd-tools corpora unchanged.

Tests: `levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit` checks the Photoshop pairs above plus the 8-bit clipping. compose and engine tests, `cargo xtask test-corpus`, clippy, layers and wasm all pass. On the GPU side the F32 Levels case in `parity.rs::adjustment_layers` passes. That test still stops later on the NVIDIA Hue/Saturation 1/255 issue mentioned in #400, which exists on main too.

title: Photoshop-style UX: moving and floating selections, Distort mode, transform undo, Layers panel and Mac menus
author: jason4short
body:
A set of Photoshop-parity fixes found by using PhotoCraft day to day on macOS: selections, Free Transform / Distort, smart objects, the Layers panel and Mac menu behaviour.

The smart object perspective fix (a distorted smart object losing its fourth corner on re-render) is split out into #426, as an engine/format/PSD change that can be reviewed on its own. This PR doesn't depend on it.

## Selections
- **Drag to move:** with the Marquee or Lasso, dragging inside the marching ants moves the selection outline. A click inside without moving deselects. The pointer shows a move cursor over the ants.
- **⌘-drag cuts and floats the pixels:** the selected pixels are cut and follow the pointer live. Plain drags then move the floating piece again without re-cutting. It drops into the layer (one `edit.transform`, one history step) on deselect, any other edit, or a click elsewhere. ⌘Z while it's floating puts it back.
- **Fast on big images:** the layer is split once per drag, cropped to the selection, and each move only places the piece. On a 6000×4000 layer with a 500×400 piece that's 9 ms to start and 4 ms per move, down from about 2.4 s per move.
- **Marching ants while drawing:** marquee and lasso drag previews use the same ants as the finished selection, instead of a thin white outline.

title: PSD: read/write the artboard lock at Photoshop's lspf bit 3 (#395)
author: agorevski
body:
## Summary
- Photoshop writes layer locks (`lspf`) with the artboard bit at **0x08**; a Background layer carries **0x0D** (transparency + position + bit 3). PhotoCraft read the artboard bit at **0x10**, so `0x0D` decoded to `0x05` and the lock bytes drifted on every re-save.
- Maps the artboard lock to bit 3 on both read and write, so Photoshop's values round-trip byte-for-byte.
- Still accepts `0x10` on read so files written by older PhotoCraft builds keep their lock; those are rewritten at `0x08`.

Closes #395

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-io` — all suites pass, no regressions
- [x] Updated `blocks::tests::locks_and_labels` to cover Photoshop's `0x0D`/`0x08` values and the `0x10` backward-compat path
- [x] New end-to-end test `artboard_lock_round_trips_byte_for_byte` in `crates/io/tests/psd_structure.rs`: injects `lspf = 0x0D` on a layer, runs import → export, asserts the exported block is still `0x0D`

title: Layer Style: the shadow/bevel Angle slider now moves the light (#350)
author: agorevski
body:
## Problem (#350, item 2)
"drop shadow in layer styles not actually changing the angle"

The Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow and Bevel & Emboss pages of the Layer Style dialog exposed an **Angle** slider but no **Use Global Light** checkbox. The engine defaults `use_global_light` to `true` (`engine/src/layer_style.rs:67`), and when it's true the compositor uses the document's fixed global light angle and ignores the per-effect angle (`compose/src/effects.rs:532`). The dialog also never sent `useGlobalLight`, so it was re-defaulted to `true` on every apply. Net effect: dragging **Angle** did nothing.

## Fix
- Add Photoshop's **Use Global Light** checkbox to Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow and Bevel & Emboss.
- Round-trip `useGlobalLight` through the dialog fields (`values_of` / `defaults`) so it survives reopen.
- When global light is on, show the effective (global light) angle in the slider.
- When global light is on, drive the document's shared light angle from the slider (`layer.layerStyle.globalLight`) so the shadow follows the Angle — exactly as in Photoshop. Unchecked, the per-effect angle is used directly.

## Tests
- New regression test `drop_shadow_angle_reaches_the_effect` (ui-egui `layer_style`): asserts the per-effect angle is stored when global light is off, that the slider moves the shared light when it's on, and that the checkbox + effective angle round-trip. Fails before the fix (global light stayed at 120; `useGlobalLight` was absent).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` → 498 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean.
- `cargo xtask layers` → no violations.

title: Smart objects keep their four-corner (Distort / Perspective) placement
author: jason4short
body:
Smart objects could only store an affine placement, so a smart object with a Distort / Perspective placement lost its fourth corner.

**Repro:** open a mockup PSD whose screen is a perspective-distorted smart object. It looks right on open, because PhotoCraft is showing Photoshop's cached pixels. Then double-click the layer, edit the contents and save. The re-render places the source with the affine from three corners (`parse_transform` dropped the bottom-right), so the screen becomes a parallelogram.

## Changes
- **`SmartObject.perspective: Option<[f64; 9]>`** holds the full projective map (source px → document px, row-major 3×3) when the corners aren't a parallelogram. `transform` keeps its affine approximation at the source origin, for code that only needs scale and position.
- **Rendering:** re-renders go through it (`place_source_projective`, which applies the warp first, then the homography). So do whole-pixel moves (`shift_smart`), canvas rotations and flips (`canvas_geom`), and `edit.transform`. Distort / Perspective on a smart object now composes into the placement instead of being refused ("aren't supported yet").
- **PSD:** import reads the quad (`nonAffineTransform`, else `Trnf`) through `parse_smart_perspective`. Export writes the projective corners to `Trnf` / `nonAffineTransform` / `PlLd`, and an unmoved template keeps its exact quad (compared within 1e-6).
- **.pcraft:** `ContentM::Smart` gains `perspective`, skipped when absent, so affine documents serialize exactly as before and older files load unchanged.

## Testing
- `cargo test` for engine, io, format, algo and doc passes, and clippy is clean.
- New test `distort_survives_edit_contents`: Distort a smart object, then Edit Contents → Save. The placement and the rendered pixels are unchanged, and the old bottom-right corner is empty.
- `transforms_re_render_from_source_losslessly` used to assert that perspective on a smart object errors. It now asserts the projective placement.

## What changed

**#412: `dark` was advertised but ignored.** The MCP `ui_set` tool, its `fields` doc and the method list in `control.rs` all named a `dark` field that the `ui.set` handler never reads. The handler skipped any key it didn't know and replied `ok`, so `{"dark": true}` (or a typo such as `{"thme": "classic"}`) reported success while nothing changed.

- `ui.set` now checks every key against `UI_SET_FIELDS` (the 16 fields it reads) **before applying any of them**. An unknown key is an error that lists the accepted fields, so a rejected call never half-applies.

**#413: the unknown-theme error listed 3 of 5 themes.** The list was a fixed string (`studio, studioLight, classic`). Every in-repo `ui.set` caller (tests, the snapshot example's docs) uses only known fields, so nothing that worked before is rejected.

title: MCP command_batch and serve batch honour each step's `wait` (#415)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What changed

The MCP `command_batch` tool reuses `command_run`'s `RunParams` for its steps, so `tools/list` advertised a per-step `wait`. The tool then mapped each step to `{command, params}` and dropped the field, so a step with `"wait": false` blocked until the filter finished and started no job.

The schema was right, so this PR makes the behaviour match it rather than removing the field:

- **MCP headless:** each step is sent as `{command, params, wait}` (default `true`), and the headless `batch` starts it through `command_start`, the same path `command_run` uses.
- **MCP bridge:** the same `wait` goes to the app's `engine.execute`, which already honours it.
- **`photocraft-cli serve`:** `batch` command steps accept `wait` too, so the JSON-lines server and MCP agree.
- **Behaviour:** a step with `wait: false` returns `{job, pending: true}` at once, and the job appears in `jobs_list`. Later steps that edit the same document fail with the engine's existing "job running" message until it ends. Steps without `wait` still return their results inline.
- **Docs:** the `steps` schema doc and `docs/control-protocol.md` (the MCP batching paragraph and the `serve` method table) describe the per-step `wait`. The narrower `{id, params}` shape the issue pointed out is gone.

## Tests

- `command_batch_step_without_waiting_starts_a_background_job` (MCP, headless):
  - A batch fills a layer, then blurs it with `wait: false`.
  - The blur returns a job id, the job is listed, and it reaches `done`.
  - A step without `wait` still returns the filter result inline.
- `bridge_command_batch_forwards_each_steps_wait` (MCP, bridge against the fake app): the first step reaches `engine.execute` with `wait: false`, the second with `true`.
- `batch_steps_can_start_background_jobs` (`serve`): same as the headless case, over the JSON-lines `batch` method.

title: Headless saves without `path` never flatten over the opened file (#416)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What changed

In headless automation (MCP without `--bridge`, and `photocraft-cli serve`), a save without `path` fell back to the document's own file for **any** format:

- `doc_save {}` on a document opened from a PNG or JPEG replaced it with a flattened export (re-encoded for JPEG, even with no edit).
- `doc_save {"format":"png"}` on a layered PSD wrote PNG bytes under the `.psd` name.

The desktop's File › Save already avoids this by writing back only to layered files.

**One rule, shared by all three save paths.** `photocraft_engine::file_cmds::saves_in_place` (with `extension`) replaces the private `menus::saves_in_place`. It's used by:

- the desktop's File › Save (unchanged behaviour),
- the control channel's `app.save`, which had the same fallback for any format,
- the headless save behind MCP `doc_save` and `serve` `doc.save`.

**The rule.** Without `path`, a save writes back only to a PSD, PSB or `.pcraft` file, in its own format. Anything else (a flat file, or a `format` override that differs from the file's) is an error that tells the client to pass `path`, and nothing is written.

**Unchanged:**
- An explicit `path`, including the opened file's own path, writes and returns its warnings (flattened, lossy compression).
- A document saved as `.pcraft` saves in place from then on.
- Bridge-mode `doc_save` still requires `path`.

**Docs:** the MCP `doc_save` description and its `path` doc, plus the `doc.save` and `app.save` entries in `docs/control-protocol.md`, state the rule.

**Small fix along the way:** the old helper took the extension of the whole path, so a file with no extension inside a dotted folder (`my.psd/notes`) counted as a PSD. The shared helper reads the file name only.

## Tests

- `save_without_path_never_flattens_over_the_opened_file` (MCP, headless, real files in a workspace root) covers the issue's acceptance criteria:
  - A PNG with a Curves layer, and an unedited JPEG: `doc_save {}` is refused and the bytes are unchanged.
  - `doc_…

- `file.automate.lensCorrection`
- `file.automate.runDroplet` and `photocraft-cli droplet`, which run batch
- `photocraft-cli batch`

So `a.png` and `a.jpg` saved as JPEG, or the same file name in two input folders, lost one result. The run still listed both in `files` (or printed `ok` twice) and exited 0.

**The fix: report, never overwrite.** A new shared helper, `photocraft_engine::file_cmds::OutputClaims`, records each output a run has written. Both the engine's `process_files` (behind the three commands and droplets) and the CLI's own `batch` loop use it.

- An input whose output path was already written in the run is skipped before any work and goes to `errors`, e.g. `not written: out/a.jpg already holds the result of in/a.jpg from this run (same output name)`. The CLI prints `FAIL` and exits non-zero.
- The first input's result is kept untouched.
- Names are compared **ignoring case** (`A.png` vs `a.png`), as the default macOS and Windows file systems do. Otherwise the same loss happens there.
- An input that failed for another reason doesn't claim its name.
- Runs whose names don't collide are unchanged, including the issue's control: the same stem kept in its own formats (no `format`) writes both `a.png` and `a.jpg`.

The params docs of the batch, Image Processor and droplet commands, which agents read through `command_list` and MCP, mention the rule.

I chose reporting over renaming (`a-1.jpg`) because renaming quietly invents names a script then can't predict. Naming templates belong to #219.

title: Alt-click with the Brush, Pencil, Gradient or Paint Bucket samples a colour (#417)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What changed

Holding **Alt (Option on macOS)** with a painting tool now turns it into the Eyedropper for that press, as in Photoshop:

- **Click:** sets the foreground colour.
- **Drag:** keeps sampling as the pointer moves.
- Nothing is painted, no history step is recorded, and the background colour is untouched.
- **Tools:** Brush, Pencil, Gradient and Paint Bucket. The Eraser, Clone Stamp and Healing Brush keep their own Alt behaviour.
- **Decided at press time:** Alt pressed or let go mid-stroke never switches a stroke between painting and sampling. Every new press re-decides, so a missed release can't leave the tool sampling.
- **Brush resize:** Control+Alt stays the brush-resize drag (#231). Alt+right-drag (#297) is handled before this.
- **Cursor:** while Alt is held over the canvas, the tool shows the Eyedropper's crosshair instead of the brush outline.
- **Agents:** `ui.pointer` (MCP `ui_pointer`) with `"alt": true` drives the same path.

It is implemented as a small hook in `canvas::tool_event` (`alt_eyedropper`, plus `app.alt_sampling` for the press). It reuses the Eyedropper's `sample_eyedropper`, passing no Alt so the sample sets the foreground rather than the background.

## Tests

- `alt_with_a_painting_tool_samples_the_foreground_instead_of_painting`:
  - For each of the four tools, an Alt-click sets the foreground and a drag re-samples.
  - The background is unchanged and the document revision doesn't move.
  - The same through `ui.pointer` with `alt`.
  - Without Alt, the Brush paints, even with Alt pressed mid-stroke.
  - Control+Alt and the Eraser don't sample.
- Gates:
  - `cargo +1.99.0 fmt --check` passes.
  - `clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` passes.
  - `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` passes (557 tests).

The only visual change is the cursor, which is an OS cursor and doesn't appear in offscreen snapshots.

Fixes #417

title: fix(cli): reject unknown flags and answer <subcommand> --help/-h
author: Mawfyy
body:
Fixes #423

`photocraft-cli` silently ignored any `--flag` it did not know (`--fromat jpg` reported `2 succeeded, 0 failed` with exit 0 while writing the wrong format), and `<subcommand> --help` / `-h` either produced a misleading error, was read as a file name (`info -h` → `I/O: -h: No such file`), or started a long-running server (`mcp`, `serve`).

## Change (`apps/photocraft-cli/src/lib.rs`)

- New `allowed_flags(cmd)` per-subcommand allow-list covering exactly the flags each subcommand accepts today (including `--quality` on `run`/`batch`, which works but is missing from the usage text).
- After parsing, any `--flag` — both the `--flag value` and `--flag=value` forms — not in the selected subcommand's list fails with `error: unknown flag <flag> for <subcommand>`, usage on stderr, exit 2, **before** any input is read, file written or server started.
- `photocraft-cli <subcommand> --help` and `photocraft-cli <subcommand> -h` print `USAGE` to stdout and exit 0, handled before dispatch (so `mcp`/`serve` never start).
- No subcommand names, flag names or output formats changed; every invocation in `USAGE`, `README.md` and `docs/development.md` keeps working.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-cli` — new in-process tests: `subcommand_help_exits_zero` (8 subcommands × `--help`/`-h` → exit 0, no side effects), `rejects_unknown_flags` (`--fromat` in both forms and `--param` → exit 2 naming the flag), `valid_flags_keep_working` (every documented flag form → exit 1/0, never 2, covering `mcp`/`serve` without starting a server). Existing suite unchanged and green.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: CLI: unknown flags are usage errors, `<subcommand> --help` prints usage, usage lists --quality (#421, #423)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What changed

**#423.** `photocraft-cli` recorded any `--flag` it didn't know and each subcommand read only the flags it wanted, so:

- `batch … --fromat jpg` (or `--fromat=jpg`) silently wrote the source formats and exited 0;
- `run … --param '{"radius":3}'` turned the JSON into a stray positional ("run needs exactly one of <file>…");
- `<subcommand> --help` / `-h` ran the subcommand: an error, `-h` read as a file name, or for `mcp` / `serve` a server that never returned.

Now one table, `SUBCOMMANDS`, lists each subcommand's **value flags**, **bare flags** and **handler**. It replaces the shared `VALUE_FLAGS` list and the dispatch `match`, so the flags a subcommand accepts and the code it runs are defined in one place.

- **Unknown flags:** a flag the subcommand doesn't take, in either form, is a usage error before any work: `error: unknown flag --fromat for batch`, then the usage text, exit 2. A value on a bare flag (`--json=yes`) is also an error.
- **Help:** `--help` or `-h` after a subcommand prints the usage to stdout and exits 0, without reading inputs, writing files or starting a server.
- **Unchanged:** every flag each subcommand takes today keeps working, in both `--flag value` and `--flag=value` forms, and bare `--compact` / `--json`. I checked every invocation in `README.md`, `docs/` and `book/` against the table.

**#421.** The usage text lists `[--quality <1-100>]` for `run` and `batch`, which already honoured it. The usage also says that `<subcommand> --help` works and that unknown flags are errors. The book's CLI page (`book/src/automation/cli.md`) describes the stricter parsing.

title: Liquify remembers its brush settings between uses and launches (#418)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What changed

#418: "it resets Density to 50 each time you activate Liquify". The issue asked for settings that survive within a run, a way to keep them as the default, or both. This does both, the way Photoshop's Liquify keeps its brush tool options:

- **Saved on every close:** OK, Cancel, Esc or the control channel's `cancel` / `commit`. The settings go to `prefs.dialogs["filter.liquify"]`, the same store Edit › Fill uses for its remembered choices: tool, size, density, pressure, rate, show mesh, mesh size, show backdrop, backdrop opacity.
- **Restored on open:** the next time Liquify opens, including after a restart, it comes back as it was left. The first use still starts from the defaults, with a brush about a tenth of the image.
- **One parser for agents and saved preferences:** `LiquifyOpts::apply` / `to_json`. The control channel's option setter (`filter.liquify {"ui": {...}}`) now goes through `apply` as well, which also gains `backdropOpacity`.
- **Damaged preferences:** out-of-range numbers are clamped and wrong types or unknown tools are skipped, so Liquify always opens.
- **One cancel path:** the three ways of cancelling (button, Esc, control channel) share one `liquify_ui::cancel`.

The report also mentions jagged edges at the default Density. That's the brush falloff itself, and remembering a higher density covers it for now. Our default matches Photoshop's (50).

## Tests

- `brush_settings_are_remembered_between_uses`:
  - First open has the defaults.
  - After setting nine options and cancelling, the next open has exactly those.

  - A damaged saved object (`"tool": "nope"`, `"density": "lots"`, `"size": 1e12`) opens with the default tool and density, the size clamped and the valid `rate` kept.

title: The main window opens centred on the screen (#419)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What changed

#419: the window's start position looked random, "the same distance from the top and left, about 124/160/512 px". The window was created without a position, so Windows placed it with its default cascade: each new window steps down and right from the top-left corner, giving a different offset each launch.

The reporter suggested either "start in the middle each time" or "remember the window location". This does the first:

- The main window now starts **centred on the main monitor** (eframe's `NativeOptions::centered`), at the same 1440 × 900.
- eframe first shrinks that size to fit the monitor (`clamp_size_to_monitor_size`, on by default), so the centred position is always on-screen. `work_area::fit_window` (#343) still maximizes a window that doesn't fit, e.g. on 1366 × 768.
- Wayland compositors place windows themselves, unchanged. macOS already centred new windows.
- The window options moved from the middle of `main()` into `native_options()`, so they can be tested.

Centring is always on-screen; remembering a position risks opening on a monitor that has since been unplugged or rearranged. If we want remembered placement later, eframe's `persist_window` would need the `persistence` feature. That seemed better as a separate change.

## Verification

- **On Windows 11 (2560 × 1440):** I launched the dev build twice with a fresh config directory and read the window rectangle through the Win32 API. Both runs: `L=560 T=270 R=2016 B=1209` (1456 × 939 outer). That's centred and identical between launches. The few px off exact centre are the title bar and the invisible resize borders.
- **Test:** `the_window_opens_centred_at_its_default_size` in `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs` checks `centered` is on, the default size is unchanged, and the monitor clamp isn't turned off.
- **Gates:**

Fixes #419

title: prefs.reset resets a single colorSettings key (#445)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #445.

## What changed

`prefs.get` and `prefs.set` route `colorSettings.*` paths to the colour state. `prefs.reset` only special-cased the whole `colorSettings` section, so a nested path such as `colorSettings.bpc` fell through to `Preferences::reset`. That struct has no `colorSettings`, so the reset failed with "unknown preference `colorSettings.bpc`" and the value stayed as it was.

`prefs_reset` now has a `colorSettings.*` arm. It reads that key's default from `ColorSettings::default()` and sets it through `set_pref`, the same path `prefs.set` uses, so the value is validated and marked for saving in the same way. Unknown keys under `colorSettings` still return "unknown preference".

## Tests

- New test `prefs::tests::reset_one_colour_setting`:
  - It sets `colorSettings.bpc` and `colorSettings.workingRgb`, resets `bpc`, and checks that `bpc` is back to `true` and `workingRgb` is untouched.
  - Resetting `workingRgb` then brings all colour settings back to their defaults.
  - `colorSettings.notAField` is still rejected.
  - On `main` it fails with the error from the issue.
- Gates:
  - `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib prefs::tests` passes (15 tests).
  - `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
  - `cargo fmt --check` passes.

## Not changed

`prefs.reset` and `prefs.set` don't call `psblend::set_text_gamma`, while `edit.colorSettings` and `load_prefs_json` do. So resetting `colorSettings.blendTextGamma` this way, or resetting the whole section, updates the stored value but not the gamma that is already in use until the next load. That was true before this change as well. I left it alone so this PR stays scoped to #445.

title: Image Size shows the one-pixel minimum it applies (#441)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #441.

## What changed

The Image Size dialog's Width and Height fields share `dim_field` with Canvas Size. That field allows negative values because Canvas Size's relative mode needs them. So when you typed `0` as the width, the dialog kept 0 and the preview read **0 px × 1 px** (the linked height was already clamped with `.max(1.0)`). Pressing OK then resized the image to 1×1, which the preview never showed.

`image_size()` now raises an edited width or height below one pixel to 1 before the linked dimension is computed. The fields and the Dimensions row then show the size `image.imageSize` will apply. Canvas Size and `dim_field` are unchanged.

## Before / after

Steps: a 4×4 document, Image → Image Size, proportions linked, type `0` in Width, then press Tab. I rendered both with `cargo run -p photocraft-ui-egui --example snapshot` and cropped them to the dialog.

title: Keyboard layer navigation: Alt+[ / Alt+] / Alt+, / Alt+. and Shift to add (part of #352)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What changed

#352 asks for shortcut parity, "especially the hidden shortcuts". The menu shortcuts are already covered, per the shortcut audit: every displayed shortcut dispatches. The layer-navigation keys that have no menu item in Photoshop were missing entirely. This adds them as engine commands in a new module, `crates/engine/src/layer_nav_cmds.rs`:

| Shortcut (Win / Mac) | Command | Does |
|---|---|---|
| Alt+] / ⌥] | `layer.selectAbove` | select the layer above |
| Alt+[ / ⌥[ | `layer.selectBelow` | select the layer below |
| Alt+. / ⌥. | `layer.selectTop` | select the top layer |
| Alt+, / ⌥, | `layer.selectBottom` | select the bottom layer |
| Alt+Shift+] / ⇧⌥] | `layer.addAboveToSelection` | add the layer above to the selection |
| Alt+Shift+[ / ⇧⌥[ | `layer.addBelowToSelection` | add the layer below to the selection |

- **Row order:** they follow the Layers panel's rows top to bottom (`layer_nav_cmds::panel_rows`). A group's row comes before its children, and a collapsed group is one row (`Group::expanded`, the same flag the panel's disclosure triangle sets). A layer selected inside a collapsed group (e.g. picked on the canvas) steps from that group's row.
- **Ends:** at the first or last row the selection stays put.
- **No history:** selecting isn't an edit, so it never dirties the document (`set_selection` / `select_layer`, as clicking a row does).
- **Rebindable:** no menu path, as in Photoshop. They're listed at the end of the Layer section of Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts, like Stamp Visible.
- **Agents:** they're ordinary commands, so MCP `command_run` and the CLI can call them.
- **i18n:** labels in every catalog (ja, zh-hant, zh-hans, es, ru, cs), written from the meaning with each catalog's own words for select / layer / above / below.

## Tests

- `steps_follow_the_panel_rows_and_stop_at_the_ends`:
  - Background, A, Group{B, C}, D gives rows D, Group, C, B, A, Background.

title: Number keys set opacity, Shift+[ / Shift+] step hardness, Shift+Cmd+A opens Camera Raw (part of #352)
author: bflatastic
body:
## What changed

More of the "hidden" shortcuts from #352, following #470 (keyboard layer navigation).

**Number keys set opacity** (new `crates/ui-egui/src/opacity_keys.rs`):

- 1–9 set 10–90%, and 0 sets 100%.
- Two digits typed within 0.8 s give an exact value: 4 then 5 is 45%, 0 then 0 is 0%.
- What the keys change depends on the tool:

| Tool | Digit | Shift+digit |
|---|---|---|
| Brush, Eraser | brush Opacity | brush Flow (1% minimum, like the options bar) |
| Pencil | brush Opacity | nothing (no flow) |
| Gradient, Paint Bucket | their Opacity option | nothing |
| Move, the selection tools, Type, Crop, Hand… (tools without an opacity) | active layer Opacity | active layer Fill |
| Dodge/Burn, Blur/Sharpen/Smudge, the healing and clone tools… | nothing: their number is a strength, exposure or tolerance, and guessing would set the wrong value | nothing |

- **Edge cases:** the locked Background keeps its opacity, and with no document nothing happens.
- **Undo:** brush changes go through `tools.setBrush` and layer changes through `layer.setProps` (one undo step each), so they're journaled and replayable.
- **Layouts:** digits are matched by physical key, so Shift+digit works whatever symbol the layout puts on it.
- **Other shortcuts:** digits held with ⌘/Ctrl/Alt are left alone (⌘1 = 100% zoom, ⌘3 = channel, and so on).

**Shift+[ / Shift+] step hardness** by 25% (0 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 100%) for painting tools. They're checked before `[` / `]`, because egui's `consume_key` ignores Shift and the size keys would otherwise take them.

**Filter › Camera Raw Filter…** gets its default shortcut, Shift+Cmd+A (Shift+Ctrl+A on Windows and Linux). It's set in both the engine spec and the menu catalogue.

Still to do for #352: transform a copy (Ctrl+Alt+T / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T). That needs duplicate-and-transform as one history step and will come as its own PR.

author: bflatastic

The other hidden "quick transform" shortcut from #352: **⌥⌘T** (Ctrl+Alt+T on Windows and Linux), Free Transform on a copy. It pairs with ⌥⇧⌘T, step and repeat, from #474.

title: Color Picker and Color panel fields accept typed values
author: carterwsmith
body:
## What changed

Typing into the Color Picker's hex field did nothing: the field was rebuilt from the colour every frame, so anything short of six valid digits was thrown away and it stayed at `000000`. It now keeps what you type while it has focus.

The Lab and CMYK fields applied every keystroke through clamped sRGB, so typing `60` into L went through L = 6 first and changed a and b (you'd end up at L = 80). The dialog now keeps the typed Lab/CMYK values, as it already did for HSB.

The Color panel's Hue and Saturation fields (Studio and Classic themes) reset to 0 on black and greys; they now keep the typed values. `parse_hex` also no longer panics on multi-byte text.

## Tests

- 4 new tests type into the real widgets one key at a time (hex, Lab, CMYK, Color panel HSB) and fail on main.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`, clippy and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

title: Dialogs keep their top-left when their content resizes
author: sommerper
body:
Dialogs were anchored at the screen centre, so when a dialog's body changed height (e.g. Layer Style switching from Stroke to Inner Shadow) it re-centred and the title bar jumped.

Now a dialog opens centred, then pins its top-left after the first laid-out frame (skipping egui's invisible sizing pass), so it grows down and right like Photoshop's. Dragging the title bar moves the pinned corner, still clamped so the whole dialog stays on screen. If a dialog grows past the bottom of the window, egui's area constraint pushes it up, and it returns to its spot when it shrinks.

The change is in `dialogs.rs`, so it applies to every dialog.

**Test:** `color_range_ui::dialog_shrinks_back_when_a_mode_needs_fewer_controls` now also asserts the dialog's top-left is unchanged across grow and shrink (it fails without the fix). `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` and clippy pass.

title: Type layers keep their name in step with their text (#483)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #483.

## What changed

A type layer is named after its first line when it's created. After that, only the Type tool's first editing session renamed it again (`type_tool::commit`, for layers with `created: true`). Any later edit kept the old name:

- clicking back into the layer and retyping,
- `type.edit`,
- Paste Lorem Ipsum into the layer.

So a layer committed with the "Lorem Ipsum" placeholder and retyped later kept saying "Lorem Ipsum".

Now, like Photoshop, a type layer whose name is still the one its text gives it is renamed on every text edit, in the same history step:

- **Where:** `with_text_layer` (`type_cmds.rs`) and `with_text` (`type_extra_cmds.rs`). These are the two helpers every type edit goes through. The new `is_auto_named` checks `layer.name == layer_name(text)` before the edit.
- **Custom names are kept:** a layer given a name at creation or renamed later keeps it. A `name` passed to `type.edit` still wins.
- **Empty text:** the name becomes "Type Layer" and keeps following the text.
- **Undo:** restores the old text and the old name together.
- **Paste Lorem Ipsum:** a new layer made with it no longer gets the fixed name `"Lorem ipsum"`, so it follows its text too.

## Before / after

Steps: Type tool, click on the canvas, commit the placeholder (⌘↩), click back into the text, ⌘A, type `Heading`, commit. Rendered with `cargo run --release -p photocraft-ui-egui --example snapshot` driving those steps through `ui.pointer` / `ui.key` / `ui.type`, cropped to the Layers panel.

title: Move drag reveals a larger-than-canvas layer's off-canvas pixels
author: sommerper
body:
## Problem

Dragging a layer larger than the canvas with the Move tool smeared the pixels at the canvas edge along the drag path. The part of the layer beyond the canvas should come into view instead.

## Cause

The live Move preview (`move_ui`) redraws only where the moving layers were and are. It took the layers' bounds at drag start **clipped to the canvas** and translated that rect each frame. For a layer that overflows the canvas, the clipped rect never covers the strip that slides in from beyond the edge, so that strip is never recomposited and keeps showing stale pixels. The commit on release (`layer.translate`) was already correct.

## Fix

`MovePreview` keeps the bounds unclipped (`change_bounds` against an unbounded rect) and clips each translated rect to the canvas.

## Tests

- New: `move_ui::tests::dragging_a_layer_larger_than_the_canvas_redraws_what_comes_in_from_beyond_the_edge`. Without the fix it fails with damage `x 9..64` instead of `0..64`, missing exactly the strip that slid in.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.

title: Ctrl+Insert copies and Shift+Insert pastes on Linux; Shift+Insert pastes images on Windows
author: sommerper
body:
Ctrl+Insert (copy) and Shift+Insert (paste) now work on Linux, and Shift+Insert pastes images on Windows.

**Linux**
- On the canvas, Ctrl+Insert runs Copy and Shift+Insert runs Paste, the same as Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V. Image paste works.
- In text fields and inline type editing, Ctrl+Insert copies the selected text. Shift+Insert sends `ViewportCommand::RequestPaste`, so egui-winit reads the clipboard and the text arrives as a Paste event on the next frame.

**Windows**
egui-winit already turns Ctrl+Insert / Shift+Insert into Copy / Paste. When the clipboard holds only an image, it drops Shift+Insert, the same way it drops Ctrl+V. `clipboard_keys` already recovers Ctrl+V from its key release; the Shift+Insert release now does the same.

macOS is unchanged.

All changes are in `shortcuts::clipboard_keys` (`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`).

**Testing**
- New test `shortcuts::tests::ctrl_and_shift_insert_copy_and_paste_on_linux` (Linux-only).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib shortcuts` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- Not run: `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm32 target on this machine). The change only uses `cfg!` and egui APIs that exist on every target.

title: Unsaved-changes prompt: (D)on't Save / (C)ancel / (S)ave keys, Tab order

The unsaved-changes prompt (shown when you close a document, Close All, or quit) can now be answered from the keyboard:

title: Gradients honour explicit transparency stops; smart filter commands accept an explicit layer target (#465, #466)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #465 and #466.

**#465 `paint.gradient` ignored `transparency`.** Explicit transparency stops now apply with `colors`, a `gradient` preset, explicit `stops` or the current gradient, in `paint.gradient` and `gradient.fill.create` (which had the same bug).

**#466 smart filter commands checked the active layer, not `params.layer`.** `layer.smartFilter.*` with an explicit `layer` now checks its precondition on that layer (temporarily active, then restored), so the active layer never changes. Menu greying is unchanged.

title: CLI batch: recorded-action steps, --format .ext, strict --quality, refuse --out = --in (#489, #490, #491, #492)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #489, #490, #491 and #492 (one commit each).

- **#492, data safety:** `batch` refuses an `--out` folder that is the `--in` folder, comparing canonical paths, so `in`, `./in/`, an absolute path and a symlink all count. It refuses before creating anything. The message names the opt-in `--in-place`, which is documented in USAGE, `batch --help`, `docs/development.md` and the book. This matches the reference Batch dialog, where saving over the originals is a separate destination choice.
- **#489:** `--actions` takes what recorded actions and droplets store: `[id, params]` pairs, `{"command"/"id", "params"}` objects or bare ids, as a list or wrapped in `{"actions"}`, `{"steps"}` or a droplet. The CLI's own object-only parser is gone. It reuses the engine's step parser through a new `automate_cmds::parse_action`, split out of `parse_script`.
- **#490:** `--format .jpg` writes `<stem>.jpg`, the same as `--format jpg`.
- **#491:** `--quality` accepts only whole numbers 1–100; every other value (0, 101–255, 256+, -1, `50.5`, text) gets the same error. `convert` and `run` now validate options before doing any work.

title: Automation: non-object params rejected; headless sees finished jobs; serve stdio survives a bad line; MCP batch keeps results (#503, #504, #505, #506, #529)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #503, #504, #505, #506 and #529 (one commit each).

- **#505, data safety:** over `serve` stdio, an over-long (>1 MiB) or non-UTF-8 request line gets one error reply. The rest of that line is skipped without buffering, and the session (with its open documents) keeps serving instead of exiting. `read_bounded_line` now reads bytes, so a cut multi-byte character counts as too long rather than an I/O error. - **#503, data correctness:** headless requests apply finished background jobs first, through one `Headless::sync_jobs()` at the top of `Headless::handle` and in the MCP `headless_op` closure. Save, export, inspect, render and `session.list` no longer see the pre-job state.

- **#504:** MCP `command_batch` charges the escaped size of each step result (it is embedded as a JSON string), so a batch stopped by the reply budget still returns `completed`/`failed`/`results` instead of one opaque error. `serve` keeps its plain budget.
- **#529:** docs: the 1 MiB request-line limit applies to TCP and headless JSON-lines stdio, not to MCP stdio input (book security pages and `docs/control-protocol.md`).

title: Recovered documents keep their recovery data until saved or closed (#444)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #444: a second crash could lose recovered unsaved documents.

**Cause.** At launch the app deleted each recovery entry as soon as it loaded it, and a recovered document was only written again after a full autosave interval. A crash in that gap lost it. Entries were also keyed `doc-{DocId}`, and ids restart every launch, so simply keeping old entries would have let new documents overwrite them.

**Fix.**
- **New `RecoveryStore`** (`photocraft-format`, native only):
  - `recover()` deletes nothing.
  - A recovered document **adopts** its entry: its autosaves overwrite that entry in place.
  - New documents get a per-launch key (`doc-<time>_<pid>_<n>-<id>`), so they can never clobber a surviving entry; old `doc-N` entries still load.
  - `discard` (on save or close) removes the document's own and adopted entries.
  - Writes stay atomic.
- **`list_recovery` is stricter:** a sidecar's key must be sanitized and match its file name, since entries are now deleted by key.
- **App wiring:**
  - `Services` has a new `adopt_autosave` hook, and `RecoverFn` returns `Recovered { key, path, doc }`.
  - On launch, each recovered document adopts its entry and marks its revision as autosaved.
  - The desktop closures moved into `recovery_services(dir)`, using `try_borrow_mut`, not a panicking borrow.
- **Web:** never had recovery; unchanged, and now documented in `docs/development.md` with the new lifecycle.

**Tests.**
- `services::tests::recovered_documents_survive_a_second_crash_until_saved_or_closed`: four simulated launches. It fails with the old delete-on-load put back.
- `format/tests/autosave.rs`:
  - `recovered_entries_survive_a_second_crash_until_saved_or_closed`
  - `new_documents_never_overwrite_surviving_entries`
  - `sidecars_cannot_point_at_other_bundles`
- `prefs_ui::tests::recovered_documents_adopt_their_entries_until_saved_or_closed`

author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #440, #530 and #534 (one commit each).

- **#440:** shortcuts pressed in the same frame now all run, in the order they were pressed. Before, only the first match in binding-table order ran and the rest were dropped (⌘Z then ⌘S saved the un-undone state). `dispatch_pressed` consumes presses one at a time and stops when a shortcut hands the keyboard to a menu, dialog, the unsaved-changes prompt, a warp or inline type, so later keys go there. A press matching several bindings still goes to table order (⇧⌘Z before ⌘Z).
- **#530 (Windows):** egui-winit turns Shift+Delete into a Cut event, so the canvas cut the selection instead of opening Edit › Fill. Outside text fields, a Cut with Shift and without Ctrl is now Shift+Delete again (a pure, tested helper, `clipboard_press`). Ctrl+X still cuts, and text fields keep the Windows convention.
- **#534:** the shape Fill/Stroke swatch, and both text-colour swatches, open egui's colour picker in a popup that egui re-placed every frame. Its width follows the R/G/B readouts, so near the right-hand dock it flipped between the right and left of the swatch while dragging, moving under the pointer and changing the colour. A new `widgets::swatch_popup` pins the popup's left edge while it is open, with room for the readouts to widen.

author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #517, #519, #521 and #522 (one commit each).

- **#517, data loss:** `.pcraft` files with about 40+ nested group levels saved but could not be reopened (serde_json's 128 recursion limit).
  - **Loading:** a linear, non-recursive bracket-depth scan runs first; then the manifest parses with `unbounded_depth`.
  - **Stack use:** layers decode one at a time, with the large conversion moved out of line.
  - **Limit:** `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 100`, measured to fit in 384 KB of stack in debug and release (256 levels needed up to 1 MB, which would overflow the 1 MB Windows/wasm main thread).
  - **Saving:** a deeper document is refused at save with `LimitExceeded`, instead of writing a file that can't be opened. The reference app allows 10 levels, and before this fix only ~41 ever loaded, so nothing that opened before stops opening.

- **#521:** exporting transparency to formats without alpha (JPEG, HDR, …) composites over white (no ink in CMYK), the same way flattening does, instead of dropping alpha. Warning: "transparency composited over white".
- **#522:** RGB in another profile (linear, Display P3, …) exported to formats that can't embed ICC (GIF, BMP, TGA, QOI, ICO, Netpbm) is converted to sRGB through `photocraft-cms` (perceptual + BPC, like Quick Export). sRGB documents are unchanged. title: Preferences merge with other tabs/windows and retry failed saves; web startup shows a Reload hint (#475, #476, #477)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #475, #476 and #477.

- **#476, preference loss:** the saved revision moves only after a successful write. A failed save stays pending and retries on its own (2 s, then 4, 8, 16, then every 30 s; a newer edit retries sooner, at most every 2 s). The first failure shows in the status bar ("… Retrying…"). The third in a row posts a notice, which clears when a save succeeds ("Preferences saved"). Applies to desktop and web: the logic is shared in `prefs_ui::persist`. A change that leaves the values unchanged no longer writes at all.
- **#475, preference loss:** saving re-reads storage and three-way merges. The base is what this instance last loaded or saved, so only the values this instance changed are written over what another tab or window stored. Objects merge key by key; other values (lists included) are replaced whole; the latest save wins for a value both changed. If storage is unreadable, this instance's preferences are written as-is.
- **#477:** if the web build's files never load, no Rust runs, so the existing loading text in `index.html` now reveals, after 20 s (CSS only, no script), a hint that the files may have failed to download, with a Reload link and a pointer to the console. The app removes the element as soon as it runs.

Tests:
- `failed_preference_saves_are_retried` (backoff sequence, one notice, newer edit retries sooner, notice clears)
- `merge_keeps_changes_made_elsewhere`
- `saving_keeps_preferences_another_instance_changed` (two apps on one store)
- `loading_page_offers_a_reload_when_startup_stalls`

title: Import warns when it keeps only the first frame or page, or a JPEG ends early (#518, #523)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #518 and #523.

Import warnings already reach `photocraft-cli info` (`warnings`), `convert`/`batch` stderr, MCP and `serve` `doc.open`, and the app's open notice. The missing piece was codecs → io. This PR adds that link and nothing parallel: a `DecodeWarning` enum and a `warnings` field on `photocraft_codecs::Image` (codecs stays standalone), which `image_to_document` puts first in `ImportResult.warnings`.

- **#523:** "only the first of N frames/pages was imported" (or without N when the file doesn't say). The kept frame's pixels are unchanged.
  - APNG: frames from `acTL`, counting a separate default image.
  - GIF: blocks walked without decompressing.
  - Animated WebP.
  - Multi-page TIFF: the directory chain is walked without decoding, capped at 10,000; thumbnails and transparency masks don't count.
- **#518:** a bounded JPEG marker/scan walk detects data ending before the end-of-image marker. It handles byte stuffing, restart and fill bytes, an EOI inside an EXIF thumbnail, and trailing junk.
  - Data cut short: the lenient decode is kept, with the warning "JPEG data ends early (the file is truncated or damaged); part of the image is missing".
  - File ends before any scan data: now an error, where it used to open as an all-grey image.

Tests (no committed binaries; every file is generated in-test):
- `crates/codecs/tests/decode_warnings.rs` (14 tests):
  - truncated JPEG: gray, RGB and CMYK, baseline and progressive;
  - JPEG edge cases: EXIF EOI, trailing data, restart and fill bytes;
  - GIF with 1, 2 and 3 frames, and with no trailer;
  - APNG at 8 and 16 bit;
  - hand-built animated WebP;
  - multi-page TIFF at U8, U16 and F32;
  - single images get no warnings.
