# PR #718 — fix(engine): migratePresets marks the preferences dirty

**Branch:** `fix/718-migrate-presets-rev`
**Title:** fix(engine): migratePresets marks the preferences dirty (#718)

## Body

Fixes #718.

The preset library persists with the preferences document, and every other preset-mutating path signals that through `Session::presets_changed` (bumps the preset revision *and* the preferences revision). The shell's persist loop is gated solely on `prefs.rev()`. `migrate` only incremented the preset revision, so a migration that appended groups was never written to the preferences file until some unrelated preference change happened — quitting before that loses the migration.

**Fix:** call `presets_changed()` when the migration actually adds something, exactly like the sibling preset commands. A migration that adds nothing still leaves both revisions untouched.

- importing a new gradient group must bump `prefs.rev()` (on main it stays at 0 while `presets.gradients` grows)

title: Windows DX12: never load a foreign dxcompiler.dll from PATH (#712)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #712.

wgpu's default DX12 shader compiler setting (`Auto`) loads `dxcompiler.dll` **by name**. Windows' DLL search falls through the app directory and System32 (where Windows ships no DXC) to the current directory and `PATH`, so any other program's DXC build there (a Chrome/Playwright folder, an SDK `bin`) was loaded into PhotoCraft and could crash on the first shader compile (the report's `0xc000041d` in Chrome's `dxcompiler.dll`) or fail device creation.

The app now sets the compiler explicitly when it configures wgpu (`gpu_startup::configure`):

- FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows, resolved from System32), which is what every user without a stray DXC on `PATH` already ran.
- Or a `dxcompiler.dll` shipped beside `photocraft.exe`, loaded by its full path (so a packager can still opt into DXC).
- `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` still picks one explicitly (documented in `docs/development.md`).

Reproduced on Windows 11 with the Windows SDK's `dxcompiler.dll` (10.0.22621) prepended to `PATH` and `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12`:
- before: the app exits at startup with `RequestDeviceError(Device(Lost))`;
- after: it starts and opens a Photoshop-authored PSD with layer effects (`corpus/photoshop/effects/bevel-outer-on-gradient-bg.psd`); the loaded compiler module is `C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\d3dcompiler_47.dll` and no `dxcompiler.dll` is loaded.

**Tests**
- `gpu_startup::tests::dx12_compiler_is_fxc_or_dxc_beside_the_exe`: FXC by default, DXC only by full path from beside the exe, the env override (and an unknown value ignored), and that `configure` replaces wgpu's by-name `Auto` default (fails before the fix).

**Gates:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test -p photocraft`, `cargo +1.99.0 clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`.

title: New Document: changing Resolution keeps the physical size when a physical unit is shown (#758)
author: Luna161
body:
Fixes #758

With Width/Height shown in a physical unit (in, cm, mm, pt, pica), changing Resolution in the New Document dialog only updated `resolution` and left the pixel width/height alone. The physical size you were looking at silently changed instead, e.g. A4 at 300 ppi switched to 150 ppi stayed 2480 × 3508 px and turned into 16.53 × 23.39 in.

Photoshop keeps the physical size and changes the pixel count in that case, and keeps the pixels when the unit is Pixels. This does the same.

## Approach

- New `set_resolution(f, new_ppi)` helper in `new_doc_ui.rs`, called from the Resolution field. If `__unit` isn't `px` it scales width/height by `new_ppi / old_ppi` (through `px_value`, so they stay whole and clamped to 1–300000) and clears `__preset`, like the Width/Height edits do. In `px` it only sets the resolution.
- Pulling it out into a helper means it can be tested without an egui window.
- I didn't touch the Pixels/Inch ↔ Pixels/Centimeter dropdown. It only changes how the number is shown. The stored `resolution` is always ppi, so switching it doesn't change ppi and width/height are already right.

## Tests

New unit test `resolution_keeps_physical_size_in_physical_units_and_pixels_in_px`:
- A4, unit `in`, resolution → 150: 1240 × 1754 px at 150 ppi, preset cleared
- A4, unit `px`, resolution → 150: 2480 × 3508 px at 150 ppi

With the scaling disabled the test fails:

```

assertion `left == right` failed
  left: (Number(2480), Number(3508), Number(150.0))
 right: (Number(1240), Number(1754), Number(150.0))
```

With the fix it passes, and so do the other `new_doc_ui` tests (11/11).

title: ui.set validates every field before applying the first one
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

`ui.set` applied fields as it validated them, and several wrong inputs were silent no-ops:

- **Partial application on error**: `{"tool": "zoom", "theme": "nope"}` changed the tool, then failed on the theme and replied `ok:false`. A caller told "failed" assumes nothing changed — the app state moved anyway. (The existing test claims "a rejected call applies none of its fields", but that guarantee only held for the up-front *unknown-field* check, not for values.)
- **Nested objects no-op'd with success**: a non-object `"panels"`/`"dockTabs"` skipped the merge silently and replied `ok:true`; an unknown nested key (typo like `"layers2"`) was inserted into the JSON and then dropped by the serde round-trip, also `ok:true`. The #412 guarantee stopped at the first nesting level.
- **Wrong-typed scalars silently ignored**: `selectionMode: "add"`, `brushSize: "big"`, `center: [1]` (wrong arity) all replied `ok:true` while doing nothing.
- **`brushSize` had no range**: `{"brushSize": 1e300}` set the brush size to `inf` (`1e300 as f32`).

## Change

The whole handler now runs in two passes: every field is **validated and materialized into a local first** (type checks, nested-key checks, theme/tool/blend-mode names, `center` arity); the apply pass afterwards cannot fail, so a rejected call applies none of its fields. The known-key set for `panels`/``dockTabs`` is taken from the serialized current state, so it tracks the structs automatically as fields are added. `brushSize` is validated up front against the engine's `tools.setBrush` limit (finite, at most 5000 px; larger values are rejected, not clamped), so the journaled brush command cannot fail after other fields were applied; a non-numeric `brushSize` keeps the API's historical no-op.

`ui_set_applies_all_fields_or_none` (late invalid field leaves the tool untouched; seven wrong-typed/nested payloads all error, panels bit-identical) (includes `brushSize: 1e300` → rejected, tool untouched). The existing `ui…

title: pcraft directory saves: re-verify a rolling share of cached objects; stronger file signature
author: tanish2k09
body:
Follow-up to #752, as agreed when it merged.

## What and why

After a directory save verifies an object, later saves skip the full check while the file's signature (length and modification time) is unchanged. That made repeat autosaves fast (731 ms → 12 ms on a 24 MP 16-bit document). But a file damaged **in place** with the same length and modification time (bit rot, or a tool that restores timestamps) was trusted until the writer was recreated, and nothing tested that case.

- **Stronger signature on Unix:** inode, device and change time are part of it. An in-place rewrite changes the change time even when the modification time is restored.
- **Rolling re-verification:** each directory save also re-reads and re-checks cached objects, oldest-checked first, up to `DEFAULT_REVERIFY_BUDGET` (16 MiB of compressed data, at least one object), so over enough saves every object is read again and a damaged one is rewritten. Small documents get a full check every save; large ones pay a bounded cost per save. `PcraftWriter::set_reverify_budget` tunes it (`0` trusts signatures, `u64::MAX` checks everything).
- **Docs:** `PcraftWriter`'s doc comment states exactly what the cache trusts.

## How it was verified

- `same_size_same_mtime_tamper_is_repaired_on_the_next_save`: damages a tile in place keeping its length and mtime; the next save rewrites it. With the budget set to 0 it **fails on Windows** (no change time there), so it pins the rolling check.
- `rolling_reverify_reaches_every_object_with_a_tiny_budget`: with a 1-byte budget (one object per save), the damaged object is reached within one pass over the objects; a fresh writer still verifies everything on its first save.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-format --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft-format` (all suites), `cargo xtask wasm` (rustc 1.99, as CI).

## Scorecard and parity

title: Headless saves write a flat TIFF unless they ask for layers
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

Maintainer decision on #672 ([comment](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/672#issuecomment-6046504558)): the app's **Save As keeps TIFF layers** as Photoshop does, while **scripted and agent saves stay flat by default**, with layers opt-in. #672 merged with `ExportOptions::default().tiff_layers = true`, and nothing headless turns it off, so every CLI, batch and MCP TIFF save became layered.

## Changes

title: fix(codecs): large PNG exports no longer lose bytes at a band's sync flush
author: ajsongpilot
body:
## Problem

Some large PNG exports can't be read. The IDAT zlib stream fails to decode with `invalid literal/length code`: ffmpeg, Python's `zlib` and browsers all reject the file.

Repro (main at 2cbb13a, 16 cores): `photocraft-cli convert detailed-3000x3000.png out.png`, where the input is a detailed illustration (36 MB of RGBA). The output is a single 15.9 MB IDAT, and decoding stops about 7.2 MB in. Smooth images, flat colours and small images come out fine, which is why this is easy to miss.

## Cause

`parallel_idat` deflates bands of rows separately and joins them with sync flushes. Each band started with an output buffer of `len / 2 + 64` and resumed the flush whenever the buffer filled.

miniz_oxide (flate2's Rust backend) can return from a sync flush that filled the output buffer before it has compressed the last lookahead bytes, which can be up to 258. The next call only drains the pending output (`compress_inner` returns right after `flush_output_buffer`) and comes back with output space left over. By zlib's rules that means the flush is complete, so the loop stopped. On the failing image, band 16's first call took all 423,047 input bytes and filled the buffer exactly. The second call drained the rest, and 216 bytes never reached the stream, so every band after it decoded as garbage.

Calling again doesn't help: each extra sync flush emits another empty stored block, so you can't tell when it's done.

## Fix

The band deflate step moves into `deflate_band`, which gives the output buffer room past deflate's worst case (`len + len/8 + 1024`). One call then consumes the band and completes the flush (or finish). If that single call doesn't finish, it returns `None`, and the parallel path falls back to the serial encoder instead of writing a broken stream.

## Tests

- New `bands_that_end_just_past_a_block_keep_all_their_data`: synthetic xorshift data that deflates to about 0.6 of its size, cut just past one of miniz_oxide's block boundaries. Every case round…

title: Layer › Smart Objects › Convert to Layers (#535)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #535.

Layer › Smart Objects had no way back from a smart object to its layers. This adds **Convert to Layers** (`layer.smartObjects.convertToLayers`, the catalog id), which decodes the smart object's contents and puts its layers back into the document where the smart object placed them, as one undoable step.

- **Several layers** land in a group named after the smart object. The group carries the smart layer's opacity, blend mode, layer mask, vector mask, style, clipping and locks, and is isolated (never pass-through) so the result looks like the smart object did.
- **A single layer** replaces the smart object directly, taking its name, opacity, blend mode, clipping and locks, when nothing on the smart layer (mask, style, fill opacity, Blend If) would change the look by folding in. Otherwise it is wrapped in a group as above. So Convert to Smart Object followed by Convert to Layers gives back the original layer, pixel for pixel.
- **Placement**: whole-pixel moves are an exact shift. Scale and rotate go through the Free Transform path, so type, shapes and nested smart objects stay live. Distort/Perspective applies to pixels; it asks you to rasterize type and shapes first, as Free Transform does. A warped smart object returns a clear error that suggests Rasterize, and the document is left unchanged.
- The contents are converted to the document's colour mode, profile (through the CMS) and bit depth. A Background inside the contents becomes "Layer 0". Nested PSD placed layers get their embedded files, so they keep rendering.
- Smart filters are discarded, as in Photoshop; the result reports `discardedSmartFilters`.
- Also available in the Layers panel right-click menu (after Edit Contents) and in the Properties panel's quick actions for smart objects, as in Photoshop. Translations added for every language with complete menus.

title: JPEG: decode Adobe YCCK with libjpeg's convention; write transform-2 files
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Photoshop saves CMYK documents as JPEG with **APP14 transform 2 (YCCK)**: the YCbCr carries the *inverted* inks and K passes through. Our YCCK decode branch instead took the YCbCr result directly as ink and inverted only K — that is `jpeg-encoder`'s private `cmyk_to_ycck` convention, which no real-world writer produces. **Every real Photoshop CMYK JPEG decoded with the three chromatic channels value-inverted** (white paper came out saturated cyan/magenta).

Two more problems in the same corner:

- Our **encoder** wrote APP14 **transform 0** with all-inverted planes (`ColorType::Cmyk`) — readable by our own decoder, but not the flavour Photoshop writes.
- The `jpeg_ycck_decodes_to_cmyk` test round-tripped against the encoder's own convention, so CI could never see the divergence.

## Change

- **Decode** follows libjpeg's documented `ycck_cmyk_convert` (and zune-jpeg): YCbCr→RGB, then C = 255−R, M = 255−G, Y = 255−B, K unchanged. The plain-CMK (transform 0) branch is untouched, so files PhotoCraft wrote before still decode.
- **Encode** switches to `CmykAsYcck` over an inverted buffer, so the file holds YCbCr(R,G,B) with a straight K under **transform 2** — exactly the Adobe layout, so our CMYK JPEGs are standard instead of self-consistent-only.
- The YCCK test now builds a documented Adobe-layout file (inverted buffer → `CmykAsYcck`), and the round-trip test asserts the `Adobe…\x02` transform marker.

A Photoshop-authored CMYK JPEG for `photocraft-corpus` is the natural follow-up oracle (the conventions here are verified against libjpeg's documented conversion and the vendored encoder/decoder sources).

## Tests

`jpeg_adobe_ycck_decodes_to_cmyk` (rewritten: Adobe-layout input, psnr > 32), `jpeg_cmyk_roundtrip_with_adobe_marker` (now asserts transform 2), `jpeg_cmyk_flat_colour_exact_ish` unchanged and green.

title: Filter previews stay inside the selection on large documents (#740)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #740.

The live on-canvas preview of a filter dialog runs the real filter command on a downsampled proxy of the document (so what you preview is what you get), but the proxy was built without the selection. On any document large enough to need a proxy (over ~5 MP, i.e. most photos) the preview therefore filtered the whole layer, while OK correctly changed only the selection. The proxy now downsamples the selection along with the pixels, so the preview is limited to the (feathered) selection exactly like the result.

- Every schema-driven filter/adjustment dialog that previews on canvas (Gaussian Blur, Add Noise, Unsharp Mask, …) now previews only inside the active selection, like Photoshop.
- Small documents (previewed at full size) already kept the selection; they are unchanged.
- Thumbnails, Color Range and the adjustment-layer previews keep their behaviour (Color Range still clears the selection on its own proxy; composites ignore it).

Tests

- `proxy::tests::proxy_scales_the_selection`.
- Visually checked with the offscreen snapshot (3200×2400 document, rectangle selection, Add Noise dialog open: noise only inside the marquee).

title: fix(engine): Camera Raw clamps the noise amounts to their range (#707)
author: bfenty
body:
Fixes #707.

`filter.cameraRaw` deserialized its params verbatim, so an out-of-range `noiseLuminance` reached the denoise stage and became a guided-filter radius of `round((1 + 3 * n/100) * pixelScale)`. A value of `1e9` turned six box-mean passes into unbounded work — the command never finishes. `noiseColor` had the same defect through its blur sigma.

`raw_params` now clamps the four noise fields to the documented `0..100`, matching how the sibling lens commands (`lens_params`) clamp their ranges at the same boundary. The in-range path is untouched.

## Test plan

`crates/engine/tests/camera_raw_noise_clamp.rs` — 3 tests:
- huge values clamp to 100 (red on main: passes through unclamped)
- negative values and the two detail fields clamp to the range
- in-range values pass through untouched (control)

Full engine suite: 0 failures. fmt + clippy clean.

title: fix(algo): Path Blur clamps per-path speeds (#708)
author: bfenty
body:
Fixes #708.

`filter.blurGallery.pathBlur` clamps the scalar `speed` to `0..500`, but each entry of the documented `paths` array was deserialized without any clamp. The halo takes the maximum speed and computes `Radius(v.max(0.0).ceil() as i32 + 1)`: a large finite speed saturates the float-to-int cast to `i32::MAX` and the `+ 1` overflows, so the command dies in a caught panic — and wraps to a negative halo with overflow checks off.

The fix clamps each entry speed to the same `0..500` the scalar path uses, right where the params are built.

## Test plan

`crates/engine/tests/path_blur_speed_clamp.rs` — 3 tests:
- `1e20` entry speed succeeds instead of the internal-error panic (red on main)
- `-1e20` likewise
- in-range `120.0` still blurs (control)

Full engine suite: 0 failures. fmt + clippy clean.

title: fix(io): artboard guide indices follow resource 1032 order (#722)
author: bfenty
body:
Fixes #722.

`guides_in` built the artboard's `guideIndeces` by numbering the document's guide list horizontal-first, but `psd_export::guides_resource` writes resource 1032 vertical-first (and the doc comment on `write_artboard` says the indices are "into the document's guide list (resource 1032)"). With guides of both orientations, an artboard got associated with the wrong guides.

The fix flips `guides_in` to vertical-first so both sides agree on 1032's order.

**Tests** (`crates/io/tests/artboard_guide_order.rs`):
- `guides_in_numbers_vertical_first_like_resource_1032` — unit-level: a rect containing only the vertical guide must select index 0; with both inside, vertical precedes horizontal.
- `exported_artboard_indices_match_guides_resource` — end-to-end: exports a PSD, walks resource 1032's bytes to confirm the on-disk order is vertical-first, then reads the `artb` descriptor's `guideIndeces` and asserts it names the vertical guide (index 0).

**Evidence:** red on main (`left: [1], right: [0]` and `left: 1, right: 0`), green after the fix, full `cargo test -p photocraft-io` sweep: 0 failures.

title: PSD: decode the merged composite only when something consumes it
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Every PSD/PSB open decoded the merged composite **unconditionally** — but a normal layered Photoshop save carries a composite nobody reads: with layers present and nothing behind the colour channels, the decoded planes went straight to the drop. That composite is typically **~half the file's bytes**, and for ZIP-compressed files the parse-time validation had already inflated the same stream once, so layered ZIP opens paid the composite **twice** for nothing. Context: P18 (*open a 20 MP layered PSD*) measures 1753 ms p50 against a 1000 ms budget on the committed baseline.

## Change

`psd_to_document_with` decodes the merged image only when a consumer exists:

- a **flattened** file (the composite becomes the Background layer),
- a **multichannel** file (the composite is the ink channels),
- or **extra alpha/spot channels** behind the colour ones (`channels > colour + merged-alpha`).

A layered file without extra channels skips the decode entirely — everything a layered import shows comes from the layer records either way. The parse-time ZIP validation is deliberately untouched: deferring it would break the corrupt-stream rejection the psd fuzz tests pin down, and with the decode skipped, layered ZIP opens now inflate the composite once (validation) instead of twice.

## Tests

`layered_import_skips_the_unused_merged_composite` makes the skip observable: a layered file whose composite data is garbage imports cleanly (no merged warning) when nothing is behind the colour channels, and warns when an extra channel forces the decode. Flattened/extra-channel paths are covered by the existing fallback, multichannel and channels round-trip tests, all green.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-psd -p photocraft-io` green · clippy `--no-deps` clean · `cargo fmt` · `xtask wasm` · `xtask test-corpus`.

title: Layer masks: Invert and Image › Adjustments edit the selected mask (#780)
author: rosematcha
body:
Fixes #780

With a layer mask's thumbnail selected, Cmd+I inverted the layer's pixels instead of the mask. The selected mask was UI state that only brush-style tools received. Menu commands and shortcuts never saw it, and the engine's adjustments ignored `"target":"mask"` anyway. Now Image › Adjustments (Invert, Levels, Curves, Posterize, Threshold and the rest of that family) edit the mask, matching Photoshop's documented behavior.

With a selection it works per selection tile.
- **Edit › Fade:** it notices a changed default and fades the default along with the canvas.
- **Dialogs:** with the mask targeted they use the proxy preview, which runs the real command on the mask.

Tests: `adjust_cmds` covers 8/16/32-bit, all four color modes, selections, undo, Fade, the session flag, the journal, a targeted color channel winning, an explicit layer, and the no-mask error. `mask_thumbs_ui` clicks the mask thumbnail, then goes through the menu path and the Levels preview. title: Warp: reject extreme rect params with BadParams instead of running a giant warp (#808 follow-up)
author: Luna161
body:
Follow-up to #808. After it merged, @tanish2k09 pointed out that the geom fix alone isn't enough. Now that `Rect::width()`/`height()` return the real extent instead of overflowing, an extreme `rect` gets all the way into the warp itself. They asked for two things: reject an oversized rect in `warp_cmds.rs` with BadParams, and add an engine test that sends the repro and expects BadParams rather than "internal error". This PR does both.

### Repro

```json
{"cmd": "edit.transform.warp", "params": {"style": "arc", "bend": 50, "rect": [-1e30, -1e30, 1e30, 1e30]}}
```

The same happens with `layer.smartObjects.warp` on a smart object. On main, both return `failed with an internal error`.

### Fix

`target()` in `crates/engine/src/warp_cmds.rs` is the single entry point for both commands (via `apply()`). It only checked `rect.is_empty()`. It now also rejects any side larger than `MAX_WARP_SIDE` (100 000 px) with:

```
BadParams: rect too large for warp: 4294967295 x 4294967295 (max 100000 per side)
```

100k px per side is far larger than any real layer, so normal warps aren't affected.

### Tests

New test `warp_cmds::tests::extreme_rect_is_bad_params_not_a_giant_warp`. It sends the repro rect to both `edit.transform.warp` and `layer.smartObjects.warp`, asserts `EngineError::BadParams` with the "rect too large" message, then checks that a normal rect still warps.

title: Photo Filter and gradient glows render like Photoshop (#442, #443)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #442.
Fixes #443.

Both were PSD rendering-fidelity bugs, fitted against the Photoshop-authored oracles (`corpus/photoshop`: `adjustments/*/photo-filter.psd`, `effects/outer-glow-gradient.psd`) plus psd-tools `layer_params.psd`.

**Photo Filter (#442).** We multiplied the encoded RGB by the filter colour and rescaled to Rec.601 luma. Photoshop does something else. It multiplies the pixel's D50 XYZ (relative to white) by the filter colour's XYZ, mixed by Density. Preserve Luminosity then restores the encoded luminosity the way the Luminosity blend mode does (SetLum + ClipColor, 0.3/0.59/0.11). This is why pure blue picks up red under a warming filter and white stays white. The XYZ multiply is a fixed linear map, so it is folded into one 3×3 linear-light matrix (`compose::adjust::photo_filter_matrix`). 32-bit documents keep luminance Y instead (the matrix is normalised).

**Gradient glows (#443).** Outer/Inner Glow gradients were laid out across the canvas like a gradient overlay (a vertical linear gradient), so the colour bands ran top to bottom. Photoshop colours the glow at strength `v` (its ranged, contoured value) with the gradient at `1 − v`, so the first stop hugs the shape on every side. The glow is opaque from `v = range²` on.

- CPU (`compose`) and GPU (`gpu`, new `GlowGradient` paint and photo-filter kernel) changed together. GPU parity tests now cover softer outer/inner gradient glows and Photo Filter at 16 and 32 bit.
- Photo Filter, measured as max (mean) error against Photoshop's merged image:
  - rgb16: 0.5/255 (0.2), was 125/255 (20.8). It now passes.
  - rgb8: 5/255 (0.3), was 124/255 (20.8). The rest is Photoshop's own 8-bit precision: its rgb8 and rgb16 renders differ by up to 5/255 at the same pixels.
  - rgb32: 9/255 (0.9), was 63/255 (6.9).
- outer-glow-gradient.psd: max 9.9/255 (mean 1.4), was 252/255.
- Photoshop oracle pass count 132 → 133, and the floor is raised to match. The io and psd-tools floors are unchanged (146, 229).

author: bflatastic
body:

title: ui-egui tests: GPU adapter catch_unwind stops swallowing setup-command failures (#760)
author: Luna161
body:
Fixes #760

Both GPU canvas tests (`canvas_16f.rs`, `color_managed_canvas.rs`) ran their setup commands with `.expect()` inside the `build_eframe` closure. kittest calls that closure synchronously, so it ran inside the `catch_unwind` that's only meant to catch a missing adapter. Any setup command that returned `Err` was reported as "skipping: no GPU adapter" and the test passed.

The fix keeps `catch_unwind` around the harness build only. Setup commands now run afterwards through `harness.state_mut()`, after the adapter capability checks. A failing command now fails the test and names the command. In `color_managed_canvas` that includes the `reopen` revision tweak, and its bare `unwrap()` became an `expect`. Only test files change.

**Verification**

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --test canvas_16f --test color_managed_canvas`: 7 + 2 passed

My box only has a software adapter with no float render targets, so the GPU tests skip ("adapter can't render Rgba32Float") before setup runs. I couldn't reproduce the GPU-present failure locally. To check it on real hardware, give `edit.assignProfile` a bogus profile in `color_managed_canvas.rs` and run `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --test color_managed_canvas`. On `main` it skips green. With this branch it should fail on `assign`.

I didn't add a dedicated regression test. The fix is structural: setup no longer runs under the `catch_unwind`, and a synthetic test couldn't exercise the GPU path on CI hosts without an adapter anyway.

title: TIFF: BigTIFF, every IFD and SubIFD, banded parallel decode (FILE-215-8, part of #215)
author: ljkx
body:
Closes the "Large and BigTIFF import with banded decode across all IFDs" item of #215 (scorecard FILE-215-8). Builds on the layered TIFF work merged in #672.

Large and multi-page TIFFs now open the way Photoshop opens them: every directory is found, the first full-resolution page becomes the document (reduced-resolution thumbnails are skipped), and the pixels are decoded in bands, in parallel, straight into the output image instead of through a second full-size buffer.

## What's in it

**`photocraft-codecs`: `tiff_ifd` (new).** A bounds-checked directory walker for classic TIFF and BigTIFF in both byte orders. It follows the IFD chain and SubIFDs (tag 330), with a seen-set, a depth limit of 4 and a 10,000-directory cap against cyclic or hostile files. `tiff_info` lists every page (size, kind: page / thumbnail / mask, parent); `decode_tiff_page` opens any page. Plain `decode` still opens the default page and reports the rest with the existing `MorePages` warning.

**Banded decode.** The `tiff` crate still does the decompression; it sees the chosen directory through a patched view of the file, so SubIFDs and pages after IFD0 decode too. The output is allocated once and each strip or row of tiles decodes into it, in parallel natively (rayon) and sequentially on wasm. Each worker holds at most one strip- or tile-sized scratch buffer.

**Newly supported:** planar configuration 2 (it errored before), palette images (opened as RGB), 1/2/4-bit gray, 64-bit samples, premultiplied alpha (converted to straight), non-alpha extra samples (dropped). title: Resampling reads a bounded window, however small the target (#713)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #713.

## What changed

`resample::resize` sized each band's source read from the filter support, which grows as `1/scale`, and read it with one `read_region`. Shrinking a 6000×4000 image to 1×1 allocated about 3 GB. A large sparse document (two tiles in opposite corners of 300000²) needed terabytes. This affects every caller: Image Size, transform's reduction pass, place, variables and the Wide Angle proxy.

- **Reads never extend past the content.** Taps outside the source's content all read the default pixel, so `taps` folds their weight into an `outside` term (summed exactly, not by subtraction) instead of reading them.
- **Bounded memory for any scale or aspect.** Source rows are read in chunks under a 64 MB budget and go straight into the band's output rows. There is no full-height intermediate, so an uneven stretch such as 300000×300000 → 300000×1 stays bounded too. Rows are added in ascending order, as before, so the sums are unchanged.
- **Empty tile rows aren't read.** A tile row with no stored tiles counts as rows of the default pixel, and each output row takes it once with the rows' summed weight. A sparse source costs what it holds, not its area.

Pixels are unchanged. Surfaces with a non-zero default pixel (masks) can differ by ≤ 1e-6, because their empty rows are now summed rather than read.

**Measured** (release, 6000×4000 RGBA8, best of 3):

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| → 1×1 bicubic: peak memory / time | 3.19 GB / 3.29 s | 129 MB / 0.10 s |
| ×0.5 bicubic | 77 ms | 54 ms |
| ×0.37 Lanczos | 99 ms | 59 ms |
| ×2 bicubic | 452 ms | 430 ms |

Output pixels were identical in every case. `cargo xtask perf --quick` has no resize scenario.

Not changed: `taps` still evaluates the filter over its full `1/scale` support per output sample before keeping the inside part. That costs time and memory linear in the source width, not its area, and normalization needs the full sum.

title: Automation: an allowed command can't run a denied one on its behalf
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What

Untrusted sessions (MCP, the control channel) authorized only the top-level command, plus the steps of `actions.play`. Every other command that runs commands internally ran them unchecked. Concretely, the allowed `file.automate.conditionalModeChange` ran `image.mode.*`, which the desktop gate (`authorize_desktop_engine_command`) denies because it resolves the user's configured colour profiles.

`Session::dispatch` now applies `Session::authorize` to every command, nested ones included, before any side effect (even before a floating selection drops). This closes the whole class instead of patching one command. Sessions without a gate (local UI, `photocraft-cli run`) behave exactly as before.

An audit of the ~40 nested `execute` calls outside tests found this to be the only allowed → denied path today. The gate keeps future composed commands, and the script-event runner, under the same policy.

## Tests

- `engine`: `conditional_mode_change_cannot_run_a_mode_change_the_gate_denies`. A gate that denies `image.mode.*` refuses the nested step and leaves the document RGB. A command that composes only allowed steps (`fitImage`) still runs.
- `automation`: `filesystem_commands_fail_closed` now drives a real session through `authorize_desktop_engine_step`.
- Both tests failed before the fix: the gated session switched the document to grayscale.
- `panic_hunt` passes, as do clippy and fmt. The ui-egui control-gate tests pass.

Pre-existing Windows-only failures, identical on main without this change:
- `agent_tasks` cleanup (`remove_dir_all`, OS error 32)
- two preset-store tests (`actions.json` path, OS error 3)
- a Rust 1.97 `manual_range_contains` lint in a `fill_cmds.rs` test

## Docs

`book/src/security/automation-security.md` now states that the policy covers commands run on a command's behalf. The `Session::authorize` doc comment is updated to match.

title: Preset store: a missing store folder no longer warns about actions.json (Windows test failures on main)
author: bflatastic
body:
Two engine tests failed on Windows on `main` (since #622 added `actions.json`):
`actions_cmds::tests::actions_persist_with_the_preset_store` and
`preset_store::tests::group_with_sampled_8_and_16_bit_tips_round_trips`, both with
`actions: actions.json skipped: actions.json: The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)`.

**Cause.** This was a real product bug, not a test-isolation problem. The store does create its folder before writing (`DirBackend::write` calls `create_dir_all`). The problem was on load: `open` read `actions.json` every time and decided "the file is missing" by matching the error text (`not found`, `no such file`, `os error 2`). On Windows, a file inside a folder that doesn't exist yet fails with `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` (os error 3, "cannot find the path specified"), which none of those strings match. So on a fresh Windows install, where the store folder only appears on the first save, every launch showed a spurious "actions.json skipped" warning until something was saved. On Linux and macOS the same case is ENOENT (os error 2), which is why only Windows was affected.

**Fix.** `actions.json` is now read only when the store's listing contains it, the same way `index.json` already was. The error-text heuristic (`missing_file`) is gone, so nothing depends on how a platform or backend words a missing file. A file that is listed but unreadable or corrupt still produces a warning.

- Fresh install (store folder doesn't exist yet): no warnings, empty Actions list; the folder is created on the first save (unchanged).
- Corrupt or unreadable `actions.json`: still reported as a warning (unchanged).

Windows CI on `main` hasn't confirmed this yet: every `main` CI run since #622 was cancelled by the next push. The last green run (#372) was before #622 landed. The failure reproduces locally on Windows 11.

author: louwers
body:
Adds Photoshop's **Magnetic Lasso Tool** (in the Lasso flyout, `L`, after the Polygonal Lasso): a selection border that snaps to edges as the pointer moves.

[Screencast From 2026-10-08 00-59-25.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c7da85b-dbb9-411a-86e6-ff3c63f70c57)

## Using it

title: Gaussian Blur: large radii are fast, live preview included (#464)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #464.

**Cause.** Gaussian Blur (radius > 4) and Box Blur (radius > 4) ran per output tile with a halo of 3σ around each tile. The halo was materialised (edge-repeated) and then copied, premultiplied, padded per row and transposed twice, so at radius 500 every 2048² tile worked on a ~5050² window: ~25 MP of floats for 4 MP of output. That is the memcpy-heavy profile in the issue, and it grew with the radius.

**Fix.** These blurs now filter the whole area at once (`algo::apply_box_blur` → `blur::box_blur`):
- the horizontal running-sum passes run over the source rows only, the vertical passes over 64-px column strips, both in parallel;
- the canvas edge is repeated virtually (each line is padded only to the passes' reach), never as a 2-D margin, so a huge radius costs about what a small one does;
- results go straight to the layer's tile columns, written in parallel;
- memory stays bounded: very large areas run in column bands of ~256 MB of floats (the old path could allocate several GB per batch of tiles at large radii);
- cancellation (jobs) is checked per row and per strip; progress per band.

Same algorithm (Kovesi's three boxes), so the look is unchanged: 8-bit output is identical except 114 of 2.1 M samples one level apart (float summation order at rounding ties); 16-bit within 2/65535. The small-radius exact kernel is unchanged.

**Timings** (release, best of runs; this machine was under heavy load from parallel builds, so absolute numbers are noisy):

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `bench_gaussian` 2048² r 50 / 80 / 150 / 250 / 500, 1 thread | 825 ms / 908 ms / 2.11 s / 2.02 s / 2.03 s | 152 / 172 / 231 / 382 / 261 ms |
| `bench_gaussian` 2048² r 80 / 150 / 500, all threads | 253 / 258 / 515 ms | 48 / 54 / 76 ms |
| `bench_gaussian` 6000² r 50 / 250 | 5.09 s / 1.49 s | 338 / 306 ms |
| Gaussian Blur dialog preview, 2048², r 250 (proxy run + flatten) | 268–420 ms | 86–108 ms |

title: Windows test job: tolerate teardown file locks in agent_tasks, treat a missing preset directory as empty
author: ljkx
body:
Two Windows-only failures make the `test (windows-latest)` job red on main-based branches (seen on #835, #868 itself, #880 and locally on Windows 11). Both are fixed here; the Linux and macOS jobs are untouched.

**1. `crates/automation/tests/agent_tasks.rs`** (3 of 4 tests):

```
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Os { code: 32, ... "The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process." }
```

Each test removes its temp directory right after `c.cancel().await`; the server task spawned by `connect` is still closing its files at that moment and Windows refuses to delete an open file. The cleanup now retries briefly (up to 2 s) and otherwise leaves the directory for the next run's `tmp()`, which already clears leftovers at the start. Test-only.

**2. `crates/engine/src/preset_store.rs`** (`actions_persist_with_the_preset_store`, `group_with_sampled_8_and_16_bit_tips_round_trips`):

```
["actions: actions.json skipped: actions.json: The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)"]
```

`DirBackend::read` passed the OS message through, and Windows words a missing *directory* differently from a missing file, so `missing_file()` did not recognise it and attaching a store on a path that does not exist yet reported `actions.json` as skipped. The backend now reports every `NotFound` as `<name>: not found`, the wording the predicate and the memory backend already use. Regression test: opening a store on a nested missing directory warns about nothing and writes nothing.

Before: 3 + 2 tests fail on Windows. After: `cargo test -p photocraft-automation --test agent_tasks` passes 4/4 in three consecutive runs and `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` passes; `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The `corpus tests` failure on this PR is main's own (`tiff_corpus` since #825 changed the headless default); #835 fixes that one.

title: Automation: Apply Data Set works for text and visibility data sets (#806)
author: rosematcha
body:
Fixes #806

`image.applyDataSet` was refused outright for automation clients (MCP, `serve` and `--control`), even for data sets that only set text or visibility and never touch a file. The authorize check only sees the command id and its params, not the document, so it had no way to tell those sets apart from Pixel Replacement ones.

The fix drops the unconditional deny. `apply_data_set` now asks `Session::authorize`, the gate every untrusted session installs and that `actions.play` already uses for nested steps, about each Pixel Replacement path before it edits anything. Text and visibility sets now apply over automation. A set with a pixel path still fails closed, as the issue asks, and nothing in that set is applied. Trusted sessions (the local dialog, `photocraft-cli run`) have no gate installed, so Pixel Replacement works there as before.

One limit: a pixel path inside `--automation-read-root` is still refused, because the engine can't yet read files through the workspace capability. That could be a follow-up.

Tests: an untrusted headless session applies a visibility set, and refuses a mixed visibility and pixel set while leaving the document unchanged. The old `filesystem_commands_fail_closed` entry for this command is removed.

Validation: `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings` on engine and automation, the engine variables and automation suites, `panic_hunt`, `xtask layers` and `xtask wasm` all pass.

title: Automation tests: wait for the MCP server to exit before deleting their temp dirs (Windows)
author: rosematcha
body:
`agent_tasks` fails on Windows on `main` (and on every PR, e.g. #838, #847, #850): `agent_edits_text_by_position`, `agent_records_and_replays_an_action` and `agent_play_refuses_a_recorded_file_open` panic at `remove_dir_all` with "The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process" (os error 32).

Each test spawns the MCP server as a detached tokio task and deletes its temp directory right after `c.cancel()`. Since #763 the server's `AuthorizedWorkspace` holds directory handles (`cap_std::fs::Dir`), and the task can still be alive when the test deletes the directory. Windows refuses to delete a directory that's still open; Linux and macOS don't mind.

`connect` and `connect_headless` now return the server's `JoinHandle`, and a `shut_down` helper cancels the client, waits for the server task to finish, then removes the directory. This only touches test code.

Validation: `cargo test -p photocraft-automation --test agent_tasks`, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt. The Windows result is in this PR's CI.

Related: #863 fixes the other Windows failure on `main` (the engine preset store).

title: Curves: add black, gray, and white point eyedroppers
author: mralonsocorona
body:
## Summary

Adds Photoshop-style Black Point, Neutral Gray Point, and White Point eyedroppers to the Curves adjustment dialog.

## Changes

- Add three eyedropper controls with localized labels and active picker states.
- Sample pixels using the existing document sampling infrastructure.
- Support repeated sampling with live previews.
- Preserve existing Curves edits where representable.
- Commit changes as one undoable operation; Cancel restores the original state.
- Handle near-endpoint samples safely through parameter serialization roundtrips.
- Restrict automated pointer sampling to Down events.
- Add translations for all supported languages.
- Update the Curves UI parity scorecard.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`

- `cargo xtask wasm`
- `cargo xtask scorecard`

All checks passed after rebasing onto upstream/main.

## Known limitations

- Neutral Gray uses Rec. 709 luma to neutralize color casts while approximately preserving sampled brightness, accounting for the existing master curve.
- RGB supports all three eyedroppers; grayscale supports Black and White.
- CMYK and Lab eyedroppers are not supported yet.
- Sampling uses the merged visible composite rather than exclusively the active layer.

title: Variables dialog: malformed entries can't crash an edit
author: tanish2k09
body:
Follow-up from the 2026-10-07 hardening triage. No open PR covered it.

## What

`ui.dialog.set` (control channel and MCP) stores any JSON value in a dialog field as-is. The Image › Variables dialog keeps its state in `__variables`, and its pages write into list entries: `d["name"] = …` on Define, and `set["name"] = …` / `values[i]["value"] = …` on Data Sets. A `defs` or `dataSets` entry that is a number or a string makes the next edit panic with "cannot access key "name" in JSON number".

`variables_ui::body` now normalizes the state on entry and keeps only object entries in `defs`, `dataSets` and each set's `values`. Malformed entries are dropped. The engine commands that OK sends them to would reject them anyway.

## Audit of the other dialog editors

The triage also flagged `adjust_editors.rs:847` (`v[key]["range"] = …`). That write is safe: `hue_saturation` resets `v[key]` to `{}` when it isn't an object (line 762), earlier in the same call and for the same range. The adjustments dialog's top-level `values` is always an object, because `params_of` builds it from the field map. No other non-test nested JSON writes in ui-egui take externally settable values.

## Tests

- `tests/variables_data_sets.rs`: `malformed_variable_entries_are_dropped_before_an_edit`. It opens the dialog with malformed state on both pages and types into the first name field. It failed before the fix with the panic above.
- `variables_ui::tests::normalize_keeps_only_object_entries`.
- clippy and fmt pass. The ui-egui suite passes, except for GPU canvas tests (`canvas_16f`, `color_managed_canvas`, `drag_preview_canvas`, `live_stroke_canvas`) that panic in egui-wgpu on this machine's adapter, identically on main.

title: agent_tasks: wait for the MCP server task before removing the test folder (Windows os error 32)
author: tanish2k09
body:
`test (windows-latest)` fails on main and every PR: `agent_edits_text_by_position`, `agent_records_and_replays_an_action` and `agent_play_refuses_a_recorded_file_open` (`crates/automation/tests/agent_tasks.rs`) panic at `std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap()` with OS error 32 ("being used by another process").

**Cause:** the headless session's `AuthorizedWorkspace` opens its read/write roots as `cap_std::fs::Dir` handles (`workspace.rs:95`), and the test's MCP server task owns that session. `c.cancel()` closes the client, but the spawned server task drops the session asynchronously, so the directory handles are often still open when the test deletes the folder. Linux allows deleting a directory with open handles; Windows doesn't. Main's own CI runs were always cancelled before #800, so this never showed there.

**Fix (test-only):** `connect` / `connect_headless` return the server's `JoinHandle`, and a `shutdown` helper cancels the client and **awaits the server task** before the folder is removed. No product code changes; the workspace keeping its handles open while a session is live is intended.

Verified on Windows: `cargo test -p photocraft-automation --test agent_tasks` passes 4/4, three runs in a row (previously 3 of 4 failed); clippy `-D warnings` clean.

title: Preset store: a store directory that doesn't exist yet reads as empty on Windows too
author: tanish2k09
body:
Two engine tests fail on Windows on clean main: `actions_persist_with_the_preset_store` and `group_with_sampled_8_and_16_bit_tips_round_trips`, with `actions: actions.json skipped: … The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)`.

**Cause:** `load_actions` treats a missing `actions.json` as an empty list through `missing_file()`, which matches the error *text* ("not found", "no such file", "os error 2"). When the store directory itself doesn't exist yet, as on a first launch, Windows reports **os error 3** ("path not found"), which none of those match. So a fresh store warned "actions.json skipped". That's user-visible on a first Windows launch, not only in tests.

**Fix:** `DirBackend::read` maps `io::ErrorKind::NotFound` (which covers os errors 2 and 3) to the same `"{name}: not found"` wording the in-memory backend already uses, so missing-file detection no longer depends on the platform's message.

**Verified on Windows:** a new test, `a_store_directory_that_does_not_exist_yet_opens_without_warnings`, fails on main and passes with the fix; the two previously failing tests and all other `preset_store` tests pass; clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean (rustc 1.99).

title: Lossy WebP: a pure-Rust VP8 encoder with quality and lossless controls (#648)
author: ljkx
body:
Closes #648 (the lossy half; the lossless encoder is still `image-webp`'s).

## What

A pure-Rust lossy WebP encoder. `crates/codecs/src/codecs/vp8/` is a clean-room VP8 key-frame encoder written from RFC 6386, and `webp.rs` wraps its output in the RIFF container. No C library, nothing new in `Cargo.toml`.

- **`vp8/bool_encoder.rs`**: the boolean entropy coder (§7), literals and tree-coded values, with the RFC's decoder in the tests for round trips.
- **`vp8/predict.rs`**: 16×16/8×8 DC, V, H, TM prediction and all ten 4×4 `B_PRED` sub-block modes with the frame-edge rules (127 above, 129 left, above-right replication on the last column).
- **`vp8/transform.rs`**: forward DCT and Walsh–Hadamard transforms derived from the RFC's inverse constants, next to the bit-exact inverse transforms the decoder uses; the encoder reconstructs with the inverse so prediction never drifts from the decoder.
- **`vp8/tables.rs`**: the RFC's trees, default/update coefficient probabilities, bands, zig-zag, `dc_qlookup`/`ac_qlookup`, key-frame mode probabilities.
- **`vp8/mod.rs`**: BT.601 4:2:0 conversion; per-macroblock mode decision (16×16 modes against a 4×4 `B_PRED` search with real reconstruction, SSE + λ·mode cost); Y2/WHT path for whole-block modes; quantisation with the spec's Y2 and UV clamps; two-pass token coding (statistics, then per-frame probability updates where they pay for themselves); `mb_no_skip_coeff` with skipped macroblocks and the context reset the decoder expects; the key-frame header. Quality 0–100 maps to a quantiser index on a gentle curve (q80 ≈ qi 22).
- **`webp.rs`**: `encode()` now routes `webp_lossless: false` to the VP8 path instead of returning `Unsupported`. A bare `VP8 ` chunk when there is nothing else; `VP8X` with an uncompressed `ALPH` plane (only when some pixel is translucent), `ICCP`, `EXIF` and `XMP ` otherwise. title: Automation: apply text and visibility data sets; refuse only pixel replacement (#806)
author: tanish2k09
body:
Closes #806.

## Why

`image.applyDataSet` was a hardcoded arm of the ambient-path deny list (`automation/src/workspace.rs`). Image › Variables could be defined and filled over MCP, `serve` and the control channel, but no data set could ever be applied, even though text and visibility values touch only the document. The refusal message pointed to "capability-scoped document methods", and there isn't one for variables.

## How

The automation gate is a `fn(id, params)` with no view of the document, so it can't tell what a named data set contains. The command now judges itself instead, as the issue suggests:

- `apply_data_set` (`engine/src/variables_cmds.rs`) computes the image files its Pixel Replacement values would read. If the session has a gate (`Session::authorize`, which untrusted sessions install), it asks the gate with `{"pixelFiles": [...]}` before changing anything. The list comes from the data set, never from the caller.
- The automation policy refuses `image.applyDataSet` whenever `pixelFiles` is present (`applies_pixel_files`). Any other id the policy doesn't list stays allowed by default, which is why the check reuses the command's own id rather than a new one.
- Text and visibility data sets now apply over automation. Pixel replacement stays refused, as the issue asks. Resolving it through the read root would be a separate feature.
- The local UI and `photocraft-cli run` have no gate, so they behave as before.

- `engine`: `apply_data_set_asks_the_gate_only_about_the_pixel_files_it_reads`. A text and visibility set applies under a gate. title: A PSD layer with bounds but no channel data no longer aborts on a 360 GB allocation (#755)
author: ianswope
body:
Fixes #755.

### Cause

`record_surface` (`crates/io/src/psd_import.rs`) sized the interleave buffer as `w * h` from the layer record's rectangle, whose only bound is the parser's 300000-per-side limit. A layer with that rectangle and no channels in the file reached `interleave` with every plane `None`, and `vec![0u8; n * ch * bps]` asked for 360 GB before any pixel was read. Rust aborts on allocation failure, so a few-hundred-byte PSD took the process down.

### Change

A buffer is built only when at least one colour or transparency channel decodes. The channel decoders already bound their output by the bytes in the file (Raw needs every byte, RLE expands at most 64x, plus the `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` backstop), so a decoded plane is data the file actually carries. When nothing decodes, the layer imports as an empty surface with a warning, the same outcome as the existing "channel present but undecodable" path just above it. Layers with real channel data, including ones missing only their transparency channel, are unchanged.

### Tests

`psd_structure::layer_bounds_without_channel_data_allocate_nothing` pushes a 300000x300000 record with no channels and asserts an empty raster plus a warning naming the layer. On `main` it aborts with `memory allocation of 360000000000 bytes failed`.

`cargo test -p photocraft-io`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. The corpus run (`--features corpus` for psd, codecs, io, engine) passes, including `photoshop_oracle_corpus`, except `tiff_corpus::corpus_round_trips_through_layered_tiff`, which fails identically on `main` without this change (698 tested, 670 "layer structure changed").

title: Lasso: Alt clicks add straight segments, releasing Alt closes the outline
author: jason4short
body:
Refines the Lasso's Alt state machine (`lasso_ui`) to match the reference behaviour more closely. This came from using it day to day.

**Before:** Alt at the first press always latched subtract, even with nothing selected. Pressing Alt during a drag pinned a straight line instead of continuing freehand. Releasing Alt between clicks left the outline open until a double-click.

**Now:**
- **Alt at the first press with no selection starts straight segments,** as a new selection, since there's nothing to subtract from. With an existing selection, Alt at the first press still subtracts, as before.
- **While the button is down, the outline follows the pointer,** with or without Alt. An Alt-click adds a straight segment and an Alt-drag adds a freehand stretch to the same outline. Between Alt-clicks, only the rubber band moves, so hover never draws.
- **Releasing Alt while the button is up closes the outline and makes the selection** in one history step. Double-click and clicking the first point still close it too.
- **No "−" badge** for Alt when nothing is selected.
- **The Polygonal Lasso no longer draws handles** on its vertices. They can't be grabbed, so only the outline and rubber band are drawn.

**Tests:**
- Two `lasso_ui` tests encoded the old behaviour (an outline staying open after Alt is released, and Alt mid-drag pinning a straight line). I rewrote them as `alt_clicks_add_straight_segments_and_releasing_alt_closes_the_outline` and `a_drag_with_alt_held_draws_freehand`.
- New: `alt_at_the_first_press_without_a_selection_starts_straight_segments`, which makes a triangle from three Alt-clicks.
- The badge test now sets up a selection for its subtract checks and asserts no badge without one. `initial_alt_still_subtracts_and_initial_shift_still_adds` and the real-canvas lasso test pass unchanged.
- Clippy, `cargo fmt --check` and the UI crate's tests all pass.

title: Move tool: layers with effects that overhang the canvas drag ~2x faster (#761, #128)
author: bflatastic
body:
Improves #761 and #128 (doesn't close them; see "Still open").

**Cause (#761).** The GPU compositor clips a layer's effect region to the canvas grown by the effect reach. A layer about the canvas's size overhangs that window as soon as it is dragged, so its region changed size on every Move tool frame, and the "moved by whole pixels, reuse the maps" path never applied: every frame rebuilt the layer's shape, its distance fields (on the CPU) and every effect over the whole canvas. Small layers inside the canvas were unaffected (their region keeps its size), which is why only some layers felt "cursed".

**Fix.**
- `gpu::bounds::effect_region`: a layer whose whole effect region is at most 1.25x the canvas window keeps it unclipped, so its size stays fixed while it moves and the maps move with it. Far larger layers are still clipped (memory). Maps are exact either way.
- `Surface::translated` (raster): moves a surface by copying the encoded tile bytes tile to tile, with no float round trip and no full-size intermediate buffer. Moves by whole tiles share the tiles. It produces the same surface (tiles included) as the old `to_interleaved` + `write_interleaved` and is 2.3x faster: 20 MP RGBA8 58 → 24 ms, 150 MP 16-bit 0.7 → 0.3 s. Used by `layer.translate`, Move tool drag previews (`layer_multi_cmds::moved`) and `algo::resample::translate_surface`.

**Timings** (perf_scenarios, 20 MP layered document, RTX 4090, p50; the machine was heavily loaded by parallel builds, so the before/after pairs ran back to back):

title: Relight: halo covers the blur reach, no silent no-op above 8 MP, box-Gaussian blur (follow-up to #735)
author: mvanhorn
body:
## What

Follow-up to #735, covering the review points from @tanish2k09.

## The change

1. **Tile seams.** The halo is no longer a fixed 97 px. It's now derived from the actual blur reach: `3σ + 1` plus the finite-difference step (σ, capped at 32), computed from the document's σ through `FilterParams::halo_for(bounds)`. When the size is unknown it falls back to the σ = 96 cap. At default softness on a 1600 px short side, that's a 129 px read, which goes past the old radius.
2. **No silent no-op above 8 MP.** The kernel no longer returns the input unchanged when the luma field is larger than 8 MP. Large rects are split into overlapping horizontal bands, so the working set stays bounded and the whole image is still relit.
3. **Blur performance.** The per-tap O(nσ) blur is replaced by the existing three-box Gaussian (`fxutil::gauss_blur_n`), with a weight channel so non-finite samples still don't spread into their neighbours.

## Timings (AGENTS rule 8)

These are release-mode numbers from `bench_filters2 relight` on 6000×4000 RGBA8 with default Relight parameters. The machine was Linux 6.12, 4× Intel Xeon (1 thread per core), 16 GB RAM, rustc 1.99.0.

| | 24 MP |
|---|---|
| Before | 83.55 s |
| After | 1.94 s |

## Tests

- New `tiles_match_a_full_apply_past_the_old_halo`: a 128 px tiled apply matches a full-frame apply on a 1600×1600 document.
- New `layers_above_8mp_are_relit`: a single-tile apply on 4096×2048 (8.39 MP) changes pixels.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib`: 263 passed, 3 ignored, including all 12 Relight tests.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine relight`: 6 passed.
- Clippy `-D warnings` is clean, and `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask parity` (626/626), and `panic_hunt --ignored` all pass.

| ⌘-drag | cuts the selected pixels and floats them (`select.float`) | moves the whole layer |
| ⌘⌥-drag | **copies** the selected pixels and floats the copy, leaving the original (`select.float {"copy": true}`) | duplicates the layer and moves the copy |

- **Badge:** while ⌘ is held, the cursor shows no add/subtract badge.
- **Engine:** `select.float` gains `"copy": bool=false`, used when the piece is created, so agents can copy as well as cut.

**Testing:** `copy_floats_a_duplicate_and_leaves_the_original` (engine), `cmd_alt_drag_floats_a_copy` (marquee), and `cmd_drag_inside_the_selection_floats_it_with_the_polygonal_lasso`.

title: file.new at 300000x300000 no longer fills ~360 GB of tiles before returning (#705)
author: ianswope
body:
Fixes #705.

### Cause

`Document::with_background` fills the background with `Surface::fill_rect`, which called `tile_mut` for every tile in the rect and wrote each one. At the 300000x300000 size `file.new` accepts, that is ~1.37 million 256x256 tiles, about 360 GB of 8-bit RGBA, before the command returns.

### Change

`fill_rect` now inserts one shared `Arc<Tile>` for every tile the rect fully covers, and writes only the partially covered edge tiles as before. Surfaces are already copy-on-write (`Arc::make_mut` in `tile_mut`), so editing a pixel splits that one tile off and leaves the rest shared. A solid fill of any size now costs one tile plus the tile index, so the fix doesn't need a lower size cap. Photoshop's own maximum is 300000 px, so the limit stays.

I checked the caches keyed by tile pointer. `compose::bounds` caches bounds within the tile, and `format::store` caches a content hash. Both depend only on the tile's contents, so sharing one tile across coordinates is safe there, and the save path stores it once. The other caches hash the pointer together with the coordinate.

### Tests

- `raster::tests::fill_rect_shares_covered_tiles_and_edits_stay_local` fills 300000x300000. It checks that covered tiles are pointer-equal, that the partial edge tile is separate, that pixels inside and outside are right, and that a `write_pixel` changes only its own tile. On `main` it tries the full allocation.
- `engine::tests::file_new_at_the_size_limit_does_not_fill_every_tile` runs `file.new` at 300000x300000 with `white`, `black`, `backgroundColor` and a hex colour, then reads the corner pixels. It takes about 1 s per document, most of it building the 1.37M-entry tile index.

`cargo test` for raster, doc, compose, format and engine passes, `panic_hunt -- --ignored` passes, and clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt are clean. `cargo xtask perf --quick` ran, but it skips the regression check on this machine, because the baseline comes from the M4 machine class.

title: Median, Dust & Scratches: run time grows linearly with the radius, identical output at 8, 16 and 32-bit (#498)
author: Ar-maan05
body:
Fixes #498.

Filter > Noise > Median and Dust & Scratches gathered every sample of a disc of the given radius (about pi r^2 values) for each pixel and channel and selected the median, so each doubling of the radius multiplied the work by about four. On a 1920 x 1280 image radius 32 took 48 s, and radius 252 on a 192 x 128 image took 113 s.

## Fix

`median_ranked` (in `crates/algo/src/noise.rs`) replaces the per-pixel selection for radius 2 and up:

- Per tile and channel, every sample in the window is replaced by its rank among the window's distinct values, ordered by `total_cmp` (the order the selection used). 8-bit samples (every sample exactly `k / 255`) use their level directly, without sorting.
- A histogram of the disc's ranks moves in a serpentine over the tile (left to right, down one, right to left, ...), so each step removes one end and adds the other end of each disc row, or of each disc column on the step down: O(radius) per pixel, and the histogram is filled once per tile instead of once per row.
- The median rank is tracked as samples move in and out (Huang). Ranks are also counted in blocks of about sqrt(ranks) bins, so on 16-bit and float layers, where a window can hold millions of distinct values, the median crosses empty stretches a block at a time.
- The value returned is the window sample with the median rank, which is the same sample `select_nth_unstable_by(total_cmp)` returns, and the threshold rule is unchanged, so the output is bit-identical.

Radius 1 keeps the direct selection, now `median_direct`, which is also the oracle in the new test. Selection, undo and cancellation are untouched (they live in `apply_in_with`, per tile).

## Timing

`apply_in`, release build, 4 rayon threads, one run each. Output hashes (f32 bits of the whole result) are identical to `main` in every row.

1920 x 1280 RGBA, Median:

| Depth | Radius | main | This PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8-bit | 2 | 0.70 s | 0.15 s | 4.7x |
| 8-bit | 8 | 3.73 s | 0.27 s …

title: Motion Blur: 6x to 70x faster (one merged kernel applied over whole rows)
author: Ar-maan05
body:
Filter > Blur > Motion Blur took `distance + 1` bilinear samples for every pixel, each through `Image::sample`, which checks the edge policy for each of its four taps. At distance 100 that is about 400 edge-checked reads per pixel and channel, so a 3 MP layer took over 3 s, and the dialog's maximum distance of 2000 took over two minutes.

## Fix

The sample offsets along the line are the same for every pixel, and so are their bilinear weights. `motion` now merges the taps of all samples once per tile into a fixed kernel (an integer offset and a weight per tap, with taps that land on the same pixel added together), premultiplies the tile's window once, and adds each tap to a whole output row at a time (`row[x] += w * window[x + dx, y + dy]`), a plain multiply-add the compiler vectorizes. Colour is then unpremultiplied by the summed alpha, as before. Samples outside the source still read as transparent, and the halo is unchanged.

This is the same premultiplied mean of the same bilinear samples; only the order of the f32 additions changes.

## Timing

`apply_in`, Motion Blur, 2000 x 1500 RGBA8, release build, 4 rayon threads, one run each:

| Angle | Distance | main | This PR | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 10 | 0.233 s | 0.039 s | 6x |
| 30 | 10 | 0.393 s | 0.037 s | 11x |
| 30 | 100 | 3.17 s | 0.085 s | 37x |
| 45 | 500 | 19.4 s | 0.337 s | 58x |
| 0 | 2000 | 130 s | 1.83 s | 71x |

Peak RSS is about the same at distance 100 (131 MB against 153 MB on `main`) and higher at distance 2000 (547 MB against 328 MB), from the premultiplied copy of each tile's window.

## Output

Not bit-identical, because the sums are added in a different order. After rounding to 8 bits, on the benchmark image:

| Angle | Distance | Samples that differ | Largest difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| 30 | 10 | 0.033% | 1 level |
| 30 | 100 | 0.0037% | 1 level |
| 45 | 500 | 0.0072% | 1 level |
| 0 | 2000 | 0.094% | 1 level |

title: Layer style: an Outside stroke at Fill below 100 % leaves the interior clear
author: llduyll10
body:
## What

**Fill 0 % + an Outside stroke** is Photoshop's "outline only" look: the stroke sits outside the layer's pixels and the interior shows the backdrop. On **pixel layers** PhotoCraft painted the outside stroke beneath the *whole* interior at full coverage and relied on the layer composited on top to hide it. With the fill lowered, the interior showed the stroke colour (a solid disc instead of a ring).

Minimal repro (`photocraft-cli` 0.3.0): place a white disc, `layer.setProps {"fill":0}`, `layer.layerStyle.stroke {"position":"outside","size":10,"color":"#ff0000"}` → centre pixel `(255,0,0,255)`; expected transparent / backdrop. Shape layers were already right (`vector ? 0`).

## Fix

The share beneath an interior pixel is now `(1 − a) / (1 − c)`, where `a` is the shape's coverage and `c` the layer's alpha after fill:

- `c = 1` (100 % fill, opaque pixel) → `1`, exactly as before, so PSD renders at full fill don't move;
- `0 %` fill → `1 − a` (only the part of an edge pixel the shape leaves, nothing inside);
- in between, the layer over the stroke gives the same result as treating stroke and shape as disjoint areas (cf. `outline_share`).

CPU (`compose/src/effects.rs`) and GPU (`gpu/src/compose.wgsl` `fs_fxstroke`, plus `plan.rs` seeding the coverage texture with the layer's alpha for pixel layers too, as the outline path already did) agree.

## Tests

- `compose`: `outside_stroke_at_zero_fill_leaves_the_interior_clear` at U8 / U16 / F32, fill 0, 0.5, 1.0 (fails before the fix).
- `gpu` parity: an Outside stroke at fill 0 and 0.5 (fails with only the CPU change, passes with the shader change).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose` (130), `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity` (26), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask test-corpus`: green on macOS (Apple silicon, Metal).

title: Tablet input on Windows: honest pressure + real right brush popup WIP
author: siraxe
body:
# Pen tablet input on Windows: real right click, honest pressure, no jitter

Closes #XXX (winit drops `WM_POINTER` pen data on Windows)

## What was wrong
Had issues with pressure only working with Windows ink.
winit 0.30 reports a Windows pen only as `WindowEvent::Touch` and lets egui emulate the mouse
from it. That drops everything that makes a pen a pen:

- A **barrel (right) click** painted as a left tap.
- **Press-and-hold** (Windows Ink's right-click gesture) cancelled the contact, but winit never
  saw `POINTER_FLAG_CANCELED`, so egui believed the emulated left button was still down forever —
  every later stroke was dead until restart.
- A **fast tap** could start and end between two UI frames, so its dab painted at full pressure
  (a blob) or not at all.
- **Light strokes flickered**: a digitizer touching lightly reports raw pressure 0 on many frames
  (below its activation threshold), and the stroke collapsed to nothing instead of holding the
  pen's last real pressure.
- The Wacom driver's **Tip Feel curve** was ignored (the driver only applies it on its Wintab
  path), so moving it in Wacom's properties did nothing.

## The fix (`crates/tablet`, the workspace's one isolated unsafe crate)

- **`windows.rs`** — a `WM_POINTER` window subclass takes the pen over from winit: it swallows the
  pen's frames and synthesizes the standard mouse messages instead (hover, tip drag, a real right
  button for the barrel and for Windows Ink's right-click gestures), which winit and egui handle
  natively. Finger touches pass through unchanged. It also parks the cursor on the pen
  (`SetCursorPos`) — swallowing the frames otherwise means the pen never moves the real cursor —
  and swallows the parking's own `WM_MOUSEMOVE` echo, which reported stale positions and made
  straight lines jitter. A small click slop keeps a jittery tap a click.

Adds the **Pattern Stamp** tool to the S-group flyout, next to Clone Stamp. It paints the current pattern through the active brush, so you can lay down texture by hand instead of filling a whole selection.

title: Slice Options and Divide Slice are one undo step; a rejected one changes nothing (#910, #911, #912)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #910, fixes #911, fixes #912.

All three came from the same thing: `target()` promoted an auto slice in its own "Promote to User Slice" history step *before* the command checked anything else.

- **#910** `slice.set {"number":1,"kind":"bogus"}` promoted the auto slice, then failed. An off-canvas `rect` was committed, then the command returned "slice is off the canvas".
- **#911** `slice.divide` on an auto slice recorded Promote and Divide separately (two undos); a rejected divide still promoted.
- **#912** `slice.set` coalesced into the previous step whenever its label was "Promote to User Slice", including a separate, explicit Promote.

Now the addressed slice is resolved to a `Target` (stored id or auto rect) and an auto slice is stored *inside* the command's own `Session::edit`, which is all-or-nothing. Slice Options also checks that the slice is still on the canvas inside that edit. The coalescing hack is gone.

Tests: `rejected_slice_options_change_nothing`, `dividing_an_auto_slice_is_one_step`, `slice_options_after_an_explicit_promote_is_its_own_step` (each failed before), plus the existing slice tests.

title: Save for Web: slices never overwrite each other; overlapping slices keep their HTML cells (#908, #909)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #908, fixes #909.

**#908** Two slices with the same name (or names that sanitize alike, `a/b` and `a?b`) wrote the same `images/<name>.<ext>`, the second overwriting the first. Names are now made unique (`tile.gif`, `tile_2.gif`), compared case-insensitively because macOS and Windows file systems are, and `spacer.gif` is reserved when HTML is written.

**#909** The resolver says later slices cover earlier ones, but the HTML table dropped any slice whose grid cells touched an earlier-*listed* one (display order, not stacking order), losing its link, text and image. With HTML on, each slice is now cut to the part no later slice covers (`slices::auto_slices` over the slices above it), and each visible piece is its own cell and image (`under_01.png`, `under_02.png`…, like Photoshop's subslices), keeping the slice's link and alt. Without HTML every slice still exports whole.

Tests: `slices_with_the_same_name_get_distinct_files`, `overlapping_slices_keep_the_later_slice_in_html` (both failed before) plus the existing Save for Web tests.

title: Filter Gallery: Angled Strokes paints strokes, not a smear; Rough Pastels' texture shows in dark areas (#879)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes the two filters named in #879 (Rough Pastels, Angled Strokes). The reporter hasn't tested the rest yet, so this doesn't claim to fix every gallery filter.

**Angled Strokes** was two diagonal box blurs mixed by luminance, so it looked like motion blur (at Stroke Length 50 the image was just smeared), and Sharpness barely changed anything. Now:
- the image is repainted in discrete strokes `strokeLength` px long and 2 px wide; each stroke takes the colour at its middle, and neighbouring lanes start at staggered points (`paint_stroke`), so strokes stay separate instead of smearing
- light and dark areas are painted in opposite directions, with Direction Balance moving the split (0: all ↘, 100: all ↗)
- Sharpness maps to an unsharp amount of 0.2–2.5, so the slider visibly matters

**Rough Pastels** was buried under an even, strong canvas relief (the "garbage noise"), with smeared strokes. Now its chalk strokes are discrete too (Stroke Detail keeps more of the image inside them), and the texture relief is scaled by darkness (`texturize_by`): thick chalk in bright areas, scraped off to show the texture in dark ones, which is how Photoshop describes this filter.

Checked visually on a public-domain painting (Van Gogh, *Sunflowers*) at default and extreme settings. Crosshatch, which shared the old Angled Strokes branch, is unchanged.

Tests: `rough_pastels_and_angled_strokes_respond_to_every_slider` sets each slider of both filters to its min and max, asserts the output changes, and asserts the result is the same at 16 px and 256 px tiles. It caught a reach bug while I wrote it (`fract()` is negative for negative coordinates; it's `rem_euclid` now). The existing every-effect tile-independence test still passes, and `cargo xtask wasm` is clean.

- **Press-and-hold** (Windows Ink's right-click gesture) cancelled the contact, but winit never
  saw `POINTER_FLAG_CANCELED`, so egui believed the emulated left button was still down forever —
  every later stroke was dead until restart.
- A **fast tap** could start and end between two UI frames, so its dab painted at full pressure
  (a blob) or not at all.
- **Light strokes flickered**: a digitizer touching lightly reports raw pressure 0 on many frames
  (below its activation threshold), and the stroke collapsed to nothing instead of holding the
  pen's last real pressure.
- The Wacom driver's **Tip Feel curve** was ignored (the driver only applies it on its Wintab
  path), so moving it in Wacom's properties did nothing.

- **`windows.rs`** — a `WM_POINTER` window subclass takes the pen over from winit: it swallows the
  pen's frames and synthesizes the standard mouse messages instead (hover, tip drag, a real right
  button for the barrel and for Windows Ink's right-click gestures), which winit and egui handle
  natively. Finger touches pass through unchanged. It also parks the cursor on the pen
  (`SetCursorPos`) — swallowing the frames otherwise means the pen never moves the real cursor —
  and swallows the parking's own `WM_MOUSEMOVE` echo, which reported stale positions and made
  straight lines jitter. A small click slop keeps a jittery tap a click.

title: Windows: selection and other crosshair tools stay visible over grey (#737)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #737.

Every tool whose canvas cursor is the system crosshair (marquees, lassos, Magic Wand, Crop outside its frame, shapes, Pen…) uses `CursorIcon::Crosshair`. On Windows that's `IDC_CROSS`, which **inverts** the pixels under it, so over mid-grey (the pasteboard, and plenty of photos) it inverts to about the same grey and vanishes. That matches the screenshot in the issue: the tool works, but there's no pointer.

On Windows the canvas now draws its own crosshair (a 1 px white cross with a dark outline, a small gap at the hotspot, like Photoshop's) and hides the system cursor. That's the same approach the Precise painting cursor already uses. macOS and Linux keep the system crosshair, which is drawn black on white and stays visible.

- `canvas::visible_crosshair` does the swap; unit test `windows_draws_its_own_crosshair`.
- Checked visually by forcing the Windows path on in an offscreen snapshot (marquee tool hovering a photo): the cross is visible on both light and dark areas.

title: gradient.fill.stop rejects an out-of-range index with BadParams instead of overflowing (#958)
author: mnmlyw
body:
Fixes #958.

## What changed

In `crates/engine/src/gradient_fill_cmds.rs`, the `midpoint` action of `apply_stop` evaluated `i + 1 >= v.len()` on the raw `index` param. An index of `usize::MAX` therefore overflowed: it panicked with overflow checks on and wrapped to a silent no-op success with them off.

- **One bounded index parser:** the shared `index` helper now takes the number of entries it can address and returns `BadParams` "no {what} {i} (there are {len})" before any arithmetic on the index. Out-of-range input is rejected in both build modes, before anything changes, so the gradient and history stay as they were. This is the outcome the issue asks for.
- **Every action uses it:** move, delete, color and opacity, for both colour and opacity stops, plus midpoint. Midpoint bounds the index by the segment count (`len - 1`, saturating), which replaces the overflowing `i + 1`. Each action's separate bound check is gone.
- **Midpoint writes through `get_mut(..)?`:** an `if let` could silently skip the write.

## Tests

- `gradient_fill_cmds::tests::stop_rejects_huge_indices_without_panicking`:
  - Uses indices `u64::MAX`, `usize::MAX`, `u64::MAX - 1`, `1 << 32` and `2` on a two-stop gradient for every indexed action:
    - midpoint, plus move, delete and color on colour stops
    - move, delete and opacity on opacity stops
  - Each returns `BadParams`, the fill is unchanged and no history step is added. Midpoint index 1 still returns "no segment 1 (there are 1)".
  - Control: `{"action":"midpoint","index":0,"location":0.25}` still sets `midpoints` to `[0.25]` as one undo step.
  - On `main` it fails with `attempt to add with overflow` at `crates/engine/src/gradient_fill_cmds.rs:454:16`.
- Gates (all pass or clean):
  - `fmt --check`
  - `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` (photocraft-engine)
  - `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` (787 passed)
  - `xtask layers`
  - `xtask wasm`
  - `panic_hunt -- --ignored`

No UI change, so no screenshots.
