title: Paint Bucket: All Layers finds the region in the merged image (#1118)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1118.

The Paint Bucket's **All Layers** checkbox did nothing. It edits `tool_options.sample_all_layers`, but the canvas click never sent it and `paint.bucket` had no such parameter. So the bucket always found its region in the target layer's own pixels: on an empty layer above other content it filled the whole layer, with the option on or off.

## Change

- **Engine:** `paint.bucket` takes `sampleAllLayers` (default `false`), like `select.magicWand`. When it's on, the region comes from the merged image, using the `selection_cmds::sample_rgba8` the Magic Wand already uses, and the active layer is still the one filled. The params doc string is updated.
- **Target:** a mask or channel target (`"target": "mask" | "quickMask" | {"channel": i}`) keeps sampling itself, following the retouch tools' `sampleAllLayers && targets_pixels(p)`. Happy to change this if the Photoshop behaviour for masks differs.
- **Algorithm:** new `photocraft_algo::paint::bucket_fill_sampled` finds the region in a given 8-bit RGBA sample instead of the surface it fills. It returns `false`, without indexing, for a sample that doesn't cover the area. `bucket_fill_src` keeps its own sampling, including dropping the sample before compositing.
- **UI:** the canvas sends `"sampleAllLayers": o.sample_all_layers` with the click.

## Screenshots

These show the real app rendered offscreen (wgpu) with real pointer events, on the issue's layout. The Background's left half is black, an empty Layer 1 is active, All Layers is checked, and the bucket is clicked on the white half:

title: Select › Modify refuses a radius below the dialog's minimum instead of clamping it to 0 (#993)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #993.

Thanks to #1274 for working on this too. The difference is that #1274 still accepts radius 0 and other values below each command's minimum (for example Border 0.5 or Feather 0). The issue's restoration check asks for every value below the documented minimum to be refused, and names `select.modify.feather {"radius":0}` explicitly.

## What changed

`modify()` in `crates/engine/src/selection_cmds.rs` now checks each command's documented range from its params string:

| Command | Range |
|---|---|
| `select.modify.border` | 1..200 |
| `select.modify.smooth`, `expand`, `contract` | 1..500 |
| `select.modify.feather` | 0.1..1000 |

Before, it rejected only values that were not finite or were above the maximum, and then clamped the radius to 0 with `r.max(0.0)`. Now any radius outside the range (including NaN or infinity) returns a `BadParams` error that gives the real range (e.g. "radius must be a number in 0.1..1000"), and the selection is not changed. The clamp is removed. Results:

- A Border radius of 0 or below no longer clears the selection while reporting success.
- Expand and Contract below 1 no longer report success without doing anything.
- Feather 0 is refused as out of range instead of being accepted.

The canvas-bounds padding that recently landed on main is unchanged.

## Tests

The new test `selection_cmds::tests::modify_refuses_radii_below_the_minimum` checks:

- Every Modify command refuses -5 with `BadParams`.
- Sub-minimum values are refused: Border 0.5, Smooth 0, Expand 0, Contract 0.9, Feather 0 and 0.05.
- After each refusal, the whole selection mask is identical to the one before.
- The minimums are still accepted: Feather 0.1 and Expand 1, and Expand 1 still grows the selection.

The test fails on main, where Border -5 returns `Ok` and clears the selection. The existing over-maximum checks in `modify_commands` and the canvas-bounds tests are unchanged.

title: Fix #1288: keep edits to a video frame when the playhead moves
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1288.

## Problem
Paint, fills and filters edit a video layer's displayed raster. The layer's frame stack (`VideoData::frames`) kept the old pixels, so `video_cmds::sync` put the stale frame back over the edit on every playhead move (`timeline.*`) and on every frame in Render Video. The result: a Fill on a blank video layer disappeared after `timeline.setFrame` and was missing from GIF and image-sequence renders.

## Fix
- New `video_cmds::store(doc)` writes each video layer's displayed raster back into its frame at the playhead. It recurses into groups and uses `get_mut`, so there is no indexing.
- `store` is called before anything re-syncs: `timeline_cmds::with_timeline`, `edit_video` (so Duplicate Frame copies the edited frame), New Blank Video Layer, New Video Layer from File, and Render Video.
- `sync_layers` now uses `get()` instead of indexing.

## Tests
- New `video_cmds::tests::edits_to_a_frame_survive_scrubbing_and_render`: fill frame 0, scrub to frame 1 and back, Duplicate Frame, then fill and render. The rendered PNG keeps the edit.
- All `video` and `timeline` engine tests pass locally.
- `panic_hunt` (`--ignored`) passes locally.

title: Perspective Warp: replacing the planes mid corner drag ends the drag (#952)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #952.

A Perspective Warp corner drag holds `(plane, corner)` indices into the plane list. Replacing the planes through the control channel (`edit.perspectiveWarp` with `{"ui": {"planes": [...]}}`) kept the drag, so the next pointer move or release indexed the new list. With fewer planes it panicked in `set_corner`:

```text
index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0
```

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/perspective_ui.rs`)

- Replacing the planes clears the drag.
- `set_corner` uses `get_mut` and skips indices that no longer exist, so a stale group can't index out of bounds.

## Test

`perspective_ui::tests::replacing_the_planes_mid_corner_drag_ends_the_drag` follows the issue's steps on its 100 x 80 fixture: it draws a plane, presses its corner, replaces the planes with `[]`, then moves the pointer, and in a second pass releases it. Before the fix both passes panic at `set_corner`. After it the drag is gone and the plane list is empty.

## Gates (macOS arm64, Rust 1.95)

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --no-fail-fast`: all pass except `canvas_16f::damage_rect_uploads_into_the_float_texture`, which fails the same way on unmodified `main` on this Mac's GPU.

title: PSD type layers without pixels are rendered on import; PostScript font names resolve to the installed family
author: diegochagas
body:
Fixes #1405.

A PSD whose type layers carry no image data (ag-psd, GIMP's exporter, GIMPhoto's psd-text) opened with every type layer empty, and *Replace All Missing Fonts* replaced an installed font because the run named the family guessed from the PostScript name ("CC Wild Words") instead of the installed one ("CCWildWords").

## Changes

- **`crates/io/src/psd_import.rs`**: a `TySh` layer's record pixels become the cache only when there are some (Photoshop's rendering stays authoritative when the file has it).
- **`crates/io/src/text_import.rs`** (new, called at the end of the PSD import so every open path gets it: app, CLI, control channel, MCP): for each run with a PostScript name whose family is not installed, resolves it with `FontDb::resolve_postscript` exactly as `Layouter::layout` already does, and writes the installed family, weight and italic back into the run; then renders every type layer that has no cache from its model with the shared engine.
- **Tests** (`crates/io/tests/psd_type_bounds.rs`): a type layer exported without pixels imports rendered, within a pixel of the engine's own render; a run named `JetBrainsMono-Regular` (the heuristic says "Jet Brains Mono") imports as the bundled family "JetBrains Mono"; the existing cases still keep Photoshop's pixels as the cache.

## Verified

- `cargo test -p photocraft-io -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-text`: all green; `cargo clippy` clean on io; `cargo xtask layers` OK.
- `photocraft-cli info` on the reporter's page (7 type layers from ag-psd, CC Wild Words at 300 ppi): bounds go from `[0,0,0,0]` to the real boxes and the font reads `CCWildWords`; `type.replaceAllMissingFonts` now reports `missing: []`; `convert` to PNG shows the lettering in the right font.

title: Puppet Warp: an expansion that empties the mesh is refused, not a panic (#951)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #951.

With at least one pin, a density or expansion that remeshes to no vertices panicked in `PuppetSolver::new`. `locate` falls back to vertex 0 when nothing is closer, and the union-find over the empty mesh indexed it:

```text
index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0   (crates/algo/src/puppet.rs:479)
```

The issue reports this through the control channel and the options bar's Expansion field. Its -50 minimum empties the issue's 20 px tall bar. The engine command has the same bug: `edit.puppetWarp` with pins and `"expansion": -200` reaches it through `puppet_warp` → `deform`, where the dispatch guard caught the panic.

## Change

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| `algo/src/puppet.rs`, `PuppetSolver::new` | With no vertices, bind no pins (every pin loop zips `bound`), instead of binding to a vertex that doesn't exist |
| `algo/src/puppet.rs`, `puppet_warp` | With no triangles, return the source unchanged. With only the change above, the engine command **erased the layer**, since rendering keeps only pixels inside the mesh. I checked: the layer came back all zeros. |
| `ui-egui/src/puppet_ui.rs` | A remesh that leaves no triangles is refused, as `begin` already refuses a layer without opaque pixels. The previous density, expansion and mesh come back. The control channel returns `Could not use Puppet Warp: no opaque pixels at this density and expansion`, and the options bar's fields snap back. |

## Tests

| Crate | Test | Before the fix |
|---|---|---|
| `algo` | `puppet::tests::an_expansion_that_empties_the_mesh_warps_nothing`: `PuppetSolver::new` on an empty mesh with a pin; `puppet_warp` at expansion -200 keeps the pixels | panic at `puppet.rs:479` |
| `engine` | `distort_cmds::tests::puppet_with_an_expansion_that_empties_the_mesh_keeps_the_layer` | panic at `puppet.rs:479` (caught by dispatch, so the command errored) |

title: Fix #1371: read large macOS display ids, keep ICC bytes out of the error
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1371 (thanks @misterlumiere for the precise root cause).

## Problem
- The macOS display reader coerced `NSScreenNumber` with `as integer`. A `CGDirectDisplayID` above AppleScript's integer range (2²⁹) came back as a real, printed `2.077748985E+9`.
- `parse_reply` rejected it and dropped the only display, so colour management fell back to sRGB.
- The resulting error quoted the entire raw line, including the base64 ICC profile. It filled the "Display profile not used" notice and Edit › Color Settings.

## Fix (`apps/photocraft/src/monitor_profile.rs`)
- The helper now asks NSNumber for `stringValue`, which is plain integer text with no locale.
- `display_id` also accepts an exact scientific-notation id as a fallback. It refuses one that is negative, fractional, non-finite or above `u32::MAX`.
- The error now shows only the start of the first field, capped at 80 characters and marked with `…`. A profile never reaches the notice.

## Tests
- New `large_display_ids_and_short_errors`:
  - plain and scientific ids;
  - rejected values;
  - a reply line with a scientific id parses;
  - an unreadable line with a 4000-character profile gives a short error without the profile.
- `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft monitor_profile`: 5 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

I couldn't run the AppleScript change itself here, since this is not a Mac. `stringValue` is a standard NSNumber method, and the Rust fallback covers the old output.

title: Vibrance: Photoshop's Saturation and Vibrance, measured (linear light, 0.288 R + 0.712 G grey)
author: Unemars
body:
**Cause.** Vibrance › Saturation −100 greyed each colour to its HSL lightness, (max + min) / 2. Photoshop keeps the brightness: yellow (255, 255, 0) becomes white there, and grey 128 here. On a real poster, a yellow logo in Lighter Color with Brightness/Contrast +150 and Vibrance (Saturation −100) clipped to it shows white in Photoshop. PhotoCraft left it yellow: the logo turned grey 128, darker than the yellow beneath, and Lighter Color kept the yellow. The Vibrance slider was a guess as well: HSL saturation boosted by `1 − saturation`, never checked against Photoshop.

**How Photoshop behaves.** Measured black-box on Photoshop 25.4. The 8-bit colour charts were run through Image › Adjustments › Vibrance by ExtendScript in 16-bit mode, and the results were read back as RAW:
- a 7,400-colour chart: a 17³ RGB lattice, greys and 2,000 random colours;
- HSV sweeps: 72 hues × 33 saturations × 11 brightness levels;
- sRGB, Adobe RGB and ProPhoto documents.

Observation only: no code, binaries or profiles were looked at.

- Both sliders work in **linear light through the document's tone curve**: sRGB, a 2.2 power for Adobe RGB, 1.8 for ProPhoto. The Vibrance slider applies first, then Saturation (checked on 9 combinations, ≤ 0.23/255).
- **Saturation** `s` moves each colour away from (or towards) the grey `g = 0.288 R + 0.712 G` by `1 + s`, then clips each channel. Blue has no weight, and the weights are the same in every profile. Within 0.07/255 for every `s` from −100 to +100.
- **Vibrance** is an HSV change in linear light that keeps the hue. Here `t = 1 − min/max` and `V = max`:
  - negative (`a = −v`):
    - `t' = t (1 − a/4)(1 − a + a t (1 + t) / 2)`;
    - `V' = V − a t (1 − t)(2 − t + t²) V (1 − V)`.

    0.04–0.19/255 on average. In the deepest shadows (`V < 0.05` linear) Photoshop desaturates less, up to 13/255 on the chart.
  - positive:
    - `V' = V + (v/4) t (1 − t)(2 − t + t²) V (1 − V)`: exact;
    - the saturation boost grows as `t` and `V` fall. It is da…

title: Fix #1381: selecting type on Wayland no longer deletes it
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1381 (thanks @hash-mc, and @Kougami901 and @LeviLeal for narrowing it to Wayland).

## Cause
On Wayland, the input method sends an empty preedit, and at times an empty commit, every time the caret rectangle moves. Ctrl+A, Shift-arrows and drag-selecting all move it. With nothing being composed, `type_tool::ime_update` treated that as "replace the selection with nothing", so selected text disappeared as it was selected. XWayland (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY=`) sends no such events, which is why the workaround helped.

## Fix
`ime_update` returns early for an empty preedit or commit when no composition is in progress. A real composition still replaces the selection. Clearing an active composition still removes only the composed text.

## Tests
- New `empty_ime_events_never_delete_the_selection`:
  - empty preedit and commit events keep the text and the selection;
  - composing replaces the selection;
  - cancelling the composition leaves the rest.
- The test fails on main and passes with the fix.
- All `type_tool` tests pass (16).

title: Large document: a notice explains a slow CPU fallback redraw (#1015)
author: ianswope
body:
Part of #1015 (the small, separate piece agreed in the thread). It doesn't fix the freeze itself.

### Problem

When the GPU canvas declines a full refresh (most often "layers exceed the GPU memory budget"), `upload_composite` composites the whole document on the CPU inside the frame. On a large document that blocks the canvas for seconds to minutes, and the only trace is a `log::info` line plus Help › System Info. To the user the app looks hung, as in the report from @realjonnysax in #1015.

### Change

`ensure_gpu` passes every CPU `full` refresh to the new `notices::slow_cpu_refresh`. The first one per document that takes over a second posts a notice (informational, not an error) saying:

- how long the redraw took;
- that edits changing the whole document (a layer's blend mode, opacity or visibility) redraw all of it;
- for the budget fallback (now the constant `gpu_canvas::OVER_BUDGET`), that raising Memory usage in Preferences › Performance raises the budget, up to a quarter of RAM, which is what `memory_budget` does;
- for any other fallback reason, that reason as the GPU reported it.

The documents already told are kept in `UiState::slow_refresh_noticed`, so automation can read it like the other notice state.

**Limitation:** the refresh is synchronous in the render path, so the notice explains a freeze after it ends, not while it runs. A live indicator needs the refresh off the frame, which belongs with the overview and visible-pages work proposed in #1015.

### Translations

The five new strings are in the 12 complete catalogs, as `every_tl_literal_is_translated` requires. I wrote them from the meaning of the English and reused each catalog's existing words for Preferences, Performance and Memory usage, but I'm not a native speaker of most of these languages, so corrections are welcome.

### Tests

`notices::tests::a_slow_cpu_refresh_is_explained_once_per_document` covers the cases:
- a quick refresh (and NaN) posts nothing;
- a slow budget fallback posts …

title: Fix Linux Open filters for uppercase and mixed-case extensions
author: AlanRockefeller
body:
File → Open on Linux hid supported images with uppercase or mixed-case extensions because the native picker used case-sensitive patterns such as `*.jpg`. An affected Lightroom folder contained uppercase `.JPG` files that did not appear in the dialog.

The shared filters for File → Open and single-file imports now use case-insensitive Unix glob patterns, covering all supported extensions and the dedicated PhotoCraft filter. Windows and macOS retain their literal extensions.

Validation:

- `cargo test -p photocraft`: 81 unit tests and 2 integration tests passed after rebasing onto upstream PhotoCraft 0.5.0. The filter regression test checks every supported extension: its pattern must match the lowercase, UPPERCASE and both alternating mixed-case spellings (`JpG`, `jPg`), and must not match a longer or shorter extension or `txt`. The test fails when the patterns lose their uppercase letters.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo xtask layers`: passed.
- Files picked with uppercase extensions open normally: every extension check after the dialog (`codecs::from_extension`, `file_cmds::extension`, the `.abr`/`.grd`/`.aco`/`.ase` preset routing) lowercases first.
- `cargo build --release -p photocraft`: passed on the original pre-rebase branch used for manual testing.
- GTK's native file-filter API: all 428 extension casing variants across the current 41 supported extensions matched; unsupported filenames remained excluded. The original filter rejected `.JPG` and `.JpG`, and the updated filter accepted them.
- Manual testing confirmed uppercase JPG files now appear in the affected directory.

title: Fix Transform Again action playback applying the transform twice
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Fixes #1351.

Recording Edit › Transform › Again stored its inner Free Transform and the outer Again wrapper. Playback therefore translated the layer twice: a square recorded at x=8 replayed at x=12.

Exclude the already-expanded Again wrapper from the Actions replay filter, retaining the concrete transform and its resolved parameters. Both entries remain in the session journal. The live Actions count uses the same filter, so it agrees with the recorded action.

Regression coverage checks one stored/played transform, matching pixels, one undo step, undo/redo, and 8/16/32-bit sources. A separate explicit-transform control still records and replays once. The new Again regression fails before the fix; the control passes. The issue's exact CLI reproduction also fails before and passes after.

Validation on macOS / Rust 1.95: 894 engine tests passed, 15 existing tests ignored; the full adversarial-parameter panic hunt passed separately. Formatting, layering, and Wasm checks passed. title: Canvas: a huge view centre draws the selection outline without overflow (#980)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #980.

`ui.set` accepts any finite `center`, and the canvas quantised the visible region for the selection outline with unchecked `i32` arithmetic. The float-to-`i32` casts saturate, then the padding overflowed:
- `attempt to multiply with overflow` for a huge positive centre;
- `attempt to subtract with overflow` for a huge negative one.

This panicked the canvas frame outside any dispatch guard. In release builds the region wrapped to an inverted, empty rectangle.

## Change (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`)

The visible corners are clamped to ±2³⁰ before the cast. No document reaches that far, and the padding (at most 2 · 256 · 64 px when zoomed far out) can't overflow `i32` from there. The quantisation and cache key are unchanged for every real view.

I kept the fix in the canvas rather than range-checking `center` in `ui.set`, because #820 rewrites that handler. The canvas fix also covers any other way a view could get a huge centre.

## Test

`canvas::tests::a_huge_view_centre_draws_the_selection_outline_without_overflow`:
- **Setup:** a 1024 x 1024 document with a 512 x 512 selection. Each case sends `ui.set` with a centre and zoom, then draws a frame through `canvas_view`.
- **Centres:** `[1e30, 1e30]`, `[-1e30, -1e30]` and `[3e9, -3e9]` (just past the `i32` range).
- **Zooms:** 100 % and 1/64. At 1/64 the trace step, and so the padding, is largest.
- **Control:** centring on the selection's corner still traces a non-empty outline at both zooms. That catches a fix that just turns the outline off.

Before the fix it panics at `canvas.rs:1721` (the multiply).

## Gates (macOS arm64, Rust 1.95)

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --no-fail-fast`: all pass except two tests that fail the same way on unmodified `main` (24d10c3):
  - `prefs_ui::tests::preference_labels_are_translated`: the Polish catalog lacks "System title bar".
  - `canvas_16f::damage_rect_uploads_into_the_float_texture`: fails on this Mac's GPU.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask wasm`…

title: Plug-ins: a missing parameter's default is clamped to the declared min..max (#1012)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1012.

## What the user saw

`docs/plugins.md` promises that every number the host passes to a plug-in is inside the parameter's `min..max`. A manifest could still declare a `number` or `int` default outside its own range, for example `"min":0,"max":100,"default":1000`. When the value was missing, the plug-in received that default unclamped. This happened on two paths: a direct `Plugin::apply` call with omitted or `null` parameters, and a smart-filter re-render after `layer.smartFilter.setParams` emptied the stored plug-in parameters. In both cases the module got `1000`. A plain `plugin.run` was not affected, because it resolves twice and the second pass clamps.

## What changed

`Manifest::resolve_params` now clamps a missing or null `number`/`int` value's default to `min..max`, the same way it already clamped supplied values. Both affected paths go through this function, so the one change covers both. The doc comment now says defaults are clamped too.

**Why this scope:** the alternative was to reject such manifests in `validate()`. That would also refuse valid manifests. An `int` parameter's `default` is optional and falls back to `0`, so `{"type":"int","min":1,"max":16}` is a reasonable declaration whose implicit default sits outside its range. `docs/plugins.md` does not state an install-time rule for defaults; what it does promise is that values are clamped. So this change enforces the documented promise where values are resolved and leaves install-time validation alone. Supplied values, in-range defaults, `bool`/`choice` parameters and `plugin.run` behave exactly as before.

## Tests

`manifest::tests::out_of_range_defaults_are_clamped` checks the following:
- Out-of-range defaults resolve into range for `{}`, `null` and explicit-`null` input: number above max, number below min, int above max, and int with no default and `min > 0`.
- Supplied out-of-range values are still clamped, and in-range supplied values pass through unchanged.
- The existing examp…

title: Opening a file with different horizontal and vertical resolutions says the vertical one is not kept (#1018)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1018.

**What the user saw:** some files have different horizontal and vertical resolutions, for example a PNG with 300 x 150 ppi or a PSD whose resolution record has two different values. Such a file opened at the horizontal resolution, and nothing said so. Saving it then wrote the horizontal value on both axes, so the vertical resolution changed without any notice.

**What changed:** a document has one resolution, so it still takes the horizontal value. The import now adds a note to `ImportResult.warnings`, the list the io crate already uses for other things it approximates or drops. The note reads, for example: "the vertical resolution (150.00 ppi) differs from the horizontal (300.00 ppi); the document keeps 300.00 ppi for both".

- `crates/io/src/lib.rs`: new helper `unequal_resolution_warning(x, y)`. It returns the note when the two values differ by 0.01 ppi or more. Smaller differences would look the same in the message, so they get no note.
- `crates/io/src/flat.rs`: flat imports (PNG, TIFF, JPEG and the other flat formats) now read the vertical value as well and add the note.
- `crates/io/src/psd_import.rs`: converts each axis to ppi with its own unit, so pixels/cm becomes ppi per axis, then adds the note. The document still takes the horizontal value.
- `crates/io/src/tiff_layers.rs`: a TIFF with Photoshop layers opens through the PSD importer. Before this change, its resolution record was built from the horizontal value only, so the vertical value was also lost silently on this path. It now passes both values, and the PSD importer adds the note.

**Why this scope:** these three are the only places where io reads a file's resolution, and each one dropped the vertical value. Saving is unchanged. Files with equal axes, the common case, open exactly as before with no new note.

- a PNG at 300 x 150 ppi

title: Control channel: ui.click rejects a count above 256 instead of queueing unbounded input (#982)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #982.

**What the user saw**
`ui.click {x, y, count}` used `count` straight as a loop bound. For each click it pushed a press event and a release event into the synthetic input queue on the UI thread, and it did this before the handler returned. A request of a few bytes, such as `{"method": "ui.click", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 100, "count": 1000000000}}`, would try to queue 2 billion events (more than 134 GiB). The app would freeze or be killed instead of returning an error. The call can come from an authenticated control connection or from MCP `control_call` in bridge mode. Neither limits the number itself, only the size of the request.

**What changed**
- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` adds `pub const MAX_CLICKS: u64 = 256`. `ui.click` works out the click count first and checks it before it queues anything, including the pointer move. A larger count returns `{"ok": false, "error": "`count` must be at most 256 (got N)"}` and nothing is queued. Each click is fed in its own frame before the reply, so 256 clicks are far more than any real use: one is a click, two are a double-click. 256 is also the limit the transport already puts on the steps of one batch request (`MAX_BATCH_STEPS`).
- `ui.move` still queues only the pointer move, because its click count is 0. Clicks with a count of 1 to 256 queue exactly the same events as before.
- The rustdoc method list and `docs/control-protocol.md` now state the limit. The protocol doc did not list `ui.click` and `ui.move` before, so this adds them.

**Why this scope**
The issue is about one handler that sized a queue from user input without a limit. The fix is in that handler and nowhere else. Other synthetic input methods are not changed, the queue type is not changed, and no other control methods are changed.

**Tests**
`huge_click_count_is_rejected` sends `ui.click` with a count of 257, 1e9 and `u64::MAX`. For each one it checks that the reply is an error and that nothing is queued. It then checks that a single clic…

title: [P1] Enforce PNG text metadata decode limits
author: Streetblock
body:
PNG text metadata could bypass the configured decode budget. Decoded text and XMP now share `Limits.max_alloc`, including keywords, Latin-1 expansion and chunks after IDAT. The documented budget covers decoded UTF-8 text separately from pixels; it is not a total process-memory cap.

title: Compose: restore the Lab-mix flag instead of clearing it after a tile (#1112)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1112.

`render_tiled_with` set the thread-local `psblend::LAB_MIX` to the document's value around each tile, then set it to `false` afterwards. A nested rayon job, such as a gradient fill, can let a thread render another tile in the middle of an outer one. Clearing the flag there made the rest of the outer Lab tile mix Normal blending in sRGB.

## Change

- **`psblend::with_lab_mix(lab, f)`:** sets the flag, runs `f`, and restores the previous value with a drop guard, so it is also restored on unwind. This mirrors `photocraft_color::convert::with_cmyk_space`.
- **Callers:** the three set/clear pairs in `render_tiled_with` (single tile, effect-map preparation, per-tile closure) use it.

## Evidence

**Unit test:** `tests::rendering_restores_the_lab_mix_flag_it_found` sets the flag to `true` and to `false`, renders a Lab and an RGB document on the single-tile and multi-tile paths, and checks the flag is unchanged afterwards. Before the fix it fails with `Lab with tile 256 inside a tile that had LAB_MIX = true`.

**The issue's own pixel reproduction:** a 4096 px Lab document with a gradient fill and two 50 % fills, 60 full renders compared against a per-tile reference. I ran it as a temporary release-mode test with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4`, twice each way, on macOS arm64:

| | run 1 | run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| before | 6 of 60 renders differ, worst 65536 px (one whole tile) | 2 of 60, worst 65536 px |
| after | 0 of 60, worst 0 px | 0 of 60, worst 0 px |

The RGB control was clean in every run. I didn't commit that test: it takes about 100 s in release and only fails intermittently, so the deterministic unit test above guards the fix instead.

## Gates (macOS arm64, Rust 1.95)

- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose` and `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu` (CPU/GPU parity included): all pass.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask wasm`: clean.
- **Clippy:** the changed files have no clippy warnings.

title: Crop: an explicit rectangle past 300000 px per side is refused (#960)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #960.

`image.crop` took any explicit `width`/`height`. A crop to 100000000 x 100000000 succeeded (tiles are lazy) and left a canvas that a following full-canvas flatten, such as `image.trim` or `image.duplicate {"mergedOnly": true}`, could only abort on allocating. A `catch_unwind` guard can't stop an allocation abort.

## Change (`crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs`)

An explicit crop refuses a side over **300000 px** with a bad-params error, before the document changes. `file.new`, Image Size and Canvas Size already clamp to that limit. Extending the canvas up to the limit still works (`crop_to_explicit_rect_can_extend_canvas` is unchanged).

I refuse instead of clamping, because clamping would crop a different rectangle from the one asked for.

## Test

`image_cmds::tests::crop_refuses_a_canvas_side_past_the_new_document_limit`:
- 1e8 x 1e8, 300001 x 10 and 10 x 300001 are refused, and the document size and history are unchanged.
- 300000 x 2 still extends the canvas.

Before the fix, `unwrap_err()` found `Ok` for the 1e8 crop.

## Not covered

As the issue says, 300000 px per side is not a pixel budget. A 300000 x 300000 canvas, which `file.new` also allows, still makes `image.trim` and merged duplicate attempt a ~1.4 TB flatten. The engine has 11 `photocraft_compose::flatten` call sites, so a whole-canvas budget (like `MAX_MODIFY_PIXELS` for Select › Modify) looks like a separate design decision. This PR only closes the unbounded crop.

Internal callers of `image.crop` (Reveal All, the centred crop in `analysis_cmds`) pass sizes derived from the document, so the limit doesn't affect them in practice.

## Gates (macOS arm64, Rust 1.95)

title: fix(psd): write Photoshop-compatible Photo Filter adjustment blocks
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1455.

PSD documents containing a Photo Filter adjustment layer could fail
to open in Adobe Photoshop.

The exported `phfl` additional-layer-information block used an
18-byte representation. Photoshop expects the version-2 block to
be padded to a four-byte boundary.

This PR corrects newly written blocks and repairs malformed blocks
preserved from older PhotoCraft files.

## Root Cause

The Photo Filter payload consists of:

- Version
- RGB color structure
- Density
- Preserve Luminosity flag
- Required padding

title: Camera RAW: a measured Nikon D4 profile (image area, white level, colour matrix, tone curve)
author: Unemars
body:
**Cause.** A Nikon D4 NEF (uncompressed) decodes fine, but it develops badly. NEF carries no colour description, unlike DNG:
- **pale colours:** the camera channels are taken as sRGB primaries ("no colour calibration for this camera" warning);
- **dark, flat image:** there is no tone curve;
- **purple stripe:** the stripe on the right is the sensor's optical-black columns, because the whole 4992×3292 data is shown;
- **pink highlights:** green saturates before red and blue, and the white level came from `clip_level` (16383, or max × 0.995).

**Clean-room.** Every number here comes from measuring the camera's own output: the raw data against the full-size JPEG the camera embeds in each NEF. No other converter's tables or profiles (dcraw / LibRaw / Adobe) were used. The frames are 148 uncompressed NEFs from one D4 body (ISO 100–10000), my own photos, not committed.

**What was measured (Nikon D4):**

| | How | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Image area | Aligning the embedded JPEG (4928×3280) with the sensor data by gradient correlation (0.96 / 0.95 on sharp frames) | `(8, 6, 4928, 3280)`. 2 columns of optical black on the left, 50 + 8 zero columns on the right |
| Black | Darkest image pixels across frames | 0 (black-subtracted in camera); the false "black level assumed 0" warning goes |
| White | Raw histograms of clipped frames, per CFA colour | Green saturates at 15546–15672, red/blue at 15687–16383. **15520** makes clipped highlights white without moving the white balance (one scale for all channels) |
| Colour + tone | Fit `JPEG = enc(ProPhoto→sRGB · T(sRGB→ProPhoto · M · wb · raw))`, robust least squares on smooth areas (4×4 means), 52 frames with Picture Control Standard and Active D-Lighting off | `M` (rows sum to 1, so neutral stays neutral) gives the **ForwardMatrix** (white-balanced camera → XYZ D50). **T** is a per-channel tone curve in linear ProPhoto (like DNG ProfileToneCurve): a linear toe through 0, and a shoulder reaching (1, 1) so clipped white stays whit…

title: .pcraft: a tile index outside the i32 pixel range is a corrupt file (#938)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #938.

The `.pcraft` loader accepted a manifest tile at any `i32` index. `TileCoord::rect` multiplies the index by the tile size, so an index past ±2²³ loaded fine and then panicked wherever the layer's bounds were asked for: the status bar, Properties, `edit.transform`, the compositor. Release builds wrapped to a rectangle unrelated to the tile.

The issue derived the panic from the source without running it. I ran it on `main`: the bundle with a tile at `tx = i32::MAX` loaded with `Ok`, and asking that layer for `content_bounds()` panicked:

```text
panicked at crates/geom/src/lib.rs:120:25:
attempt to multiply with overflow
```

## Change (`crates/format/src/convert.rs`)

`Loader::surface` refuses a tile whose rectangle doesn't fit in `i32` on both edges, which means indices -8388608 ..= 8388606. It returns `FormatError::Corrupt` ("tile (x, y) is outside the coordinate range"), the same way it already refuses a duplicate tile. In-app editing can't produce such an index (tile indices come from `div_euclid(256)` of `i32` pixels); only a damaged or crafted manifest can.

## Test (`crates/format/tests/corruption.rs`)

`tile_coordinates_outside_the_i32_pixel_range_are_rejected` rewrites a raster layer's first tile in the sample bundle's manifest:
- **Refused:** just past each end of the range for `tx` and for `ty`, plus `i32::MAX` and `i32::MIN`.
- **Still loads:** the extreme valid indices `(hi, hi)`, `(lo, lo)` and `(hi, lo)`. The test checks the tile is where it was put and the layer's bounds compute.

Before the fix, `unwrap_err()` found `Ok` for the first out-of-range bundle.

## Gates (macOS arm64, Rust 1.95)

- `cargo test -p photocraft-format -p photocraft-io --no-fail-fast`: all pass.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask wasm`: clean.
- **Clippy:** the changed files have no clippy warnings.
- **Overlap:** open PRs touching `crates/format` (#1289, #1122, #1088, #903) don't change these lines.

title: Zoom: wheel steps of exactly x1.1 with no easing, and zoom up to 12800%
author: Jeremy8776
body:
**Cause.** Two separate things made zooming feel off.

1. **Wheel zoom was eased and small.** Alt + wheel (and the wheel with Zoom with Scroll Wheel on) zoomed 5% per notch, fed from egui's *smoothed* scroll delta, so every notch was spread over about eight frames. The target behaviour applies a notch at once.
2. **Zoom stopped at 3200%, and not for one reason.**
   - The status bar and Navigator percentage boxes were limited to 1 to 3200%. egui's `DragValue` forces its value into its range on every frame, so any zoom above 3200% was clamped and written straight back to the view as 3200%, whatever scrolled it there.
   - The Navigator slider ended at 2^5 (3200%).
   - The Ctrl/Cmd +/- step table and Fit/Fill ended at 32 (3200%).
   - Alt + wheel, the Zoom tool and the view commands each had their own clamp at 64 (6400%). The target limit is 12800%.

**Reference behaviour.** Observed on screen recordings (60 fps), black box: no code or assets looked at.
- Each wheel notch changes the zoom by exactly x1.1. Scale between consecutive distinct frames, from feature matching, is 1.100. The step lands on one frame, with no in-between frames.
- Zoom runs from 1% to 12800%.

**Fix.**
- `wheel_nav`: zooming reads this frame's wheel events (`Input::raw`) instead of the smoothed delta, one x1.1 step per notch (`NOTCH`, was `ALT_NOTCH` = 1.05). The smoothed tail of a notch is ignored for zooming, so it neither eases the zoom nor turns into a pan when Alt is released. Panning still uses the smoothed delta. Whole notches, points and pages are all converted to notches.
- `zoom_tool::MAX_ZOOM` is 128 (12800%) and is the single limit. The canvas wheel zoom, Fit/Fill, `view.*` commands, the `ui.set` control command and the step table (which gains 64 and 128) all use `MIN_ZOOM`/`MAX_ZOOM` instead of their own literals.
- `zoom_tool::percent_field` is the one zoom percentage box, used by both status bars and the Navigator, with the full range. The Navigator slider uses the same limits.

…

title: Canvas: checker moves with the image; pixel grid from 500%, over pixels only
author: Jeremy8776
body:
**Cause.** The transparency checker and the pixel grid are drawn by the same canvas shader, but they were anchored to different things.
- The pixel grid sits on document pixel edges, so it moves with the image.
- The checker was anchored to the top-left corner of the canvas *viewport* (`view.d.xy`, the canvas rect's minimum). When you pan or zoom, the image and its grid move and the checker stays put, so the two drift apart and the checker appears to slide under the picture.
- The grid also appeared late (from 800% on the GPU canvas, 1200% on the CPU fallback), was faint, and was drawn across transparent pixels, over the checker, which made the mismatch more visible.

**Reference behaviour.** Observed on screen recordings and screenshots at several zooms, black box: no code or assets looked at.
- The checker cell is a fixed 8 screen pixels at every zoom (the Medium preference), and its pattern is anchored to the document's top-left corner, so it travels with the image.
- The pixel grid is absent at 500% and present from just above it.
- A grid line over a dark pixel moves it a quarter of the way to white (a pixel of 30 reads 87 on the line).
- The grid is not drawn over empty (fully transparent) pixels, only over pixels with content.

**Fix.** All in the GPU canvas shader (`gpu_canvas.rs`), with the CPU fallback's grid brought in line.
- `checker()` measures from the document origin (`view.b.xy`) instead of the viewport corner. Cell size is unchanged: still `checker_square` device pixels. The old anchor uniform (`d.xy`) is no longer read.
- The grid is drawn above 500% zoom (`p.zoom > 5.0`, was `>= 8.0`) and its alpha is scaled by the pixel's own alpha, so it never draws over the checker.
- Strength over a dark pixel is 0.25 (was 0.16). Over a light pixel it stays at 0.16, as before.
- CPU fallback (`canvas.rs`): the grid threshold is above 500% (was 1200%) and its stroke is white at alpha 64 (was 40, about 0.25). The CPU checker already tiles from the document corn…

title: Puppet Warp: pins that stretch the content too far are refused (#1019)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1019.

`edit.puppetWarp` accepted pin destinations that are finite but arbitrarily far away. The renderer (`warp::warp_triangles`) sizes its tile, bin and lookup collections from the deformed mesh's bounds. The issue measured 17,623,204 tiles (at least 846 MB of bookkeeping) for a pin dragged to `(1048576, 1048576)`, all allocated before a pixel is drawn.

## Change

| Where | Change |
|---|---|
| `algo/src/puppet.rs` | New `MAX_WARP_PIXELS` (2³⁰, about 16000 tiles; the same budget as `MAX_MODIFY_PIXELS` in Select › Modify). `puppet_warp` returns `Option<Surface>`: `None` when the deformed mesh's bounding box exceeds the budget or isn't finite. This is checked after the solve and before `render`, so no destination-sized collection is allocated. |
| `engine/src/distort_cmds.rs` | `edit.puppetWarp` returns a bad-params error ("the pins stretch the content too far"). The edit is discarded, so the layer is unchanged and no history step is added. To let the command refuse, the warp callback of the private `run_on_layer` / `deform_selected` helpers now returns `Result<Surface>`. Liquify and Perspective Warp just wrap theirs in `Ok`, with no behaviour change. |
| smart filters | A stored Puppet Warp smart filter too far to render leaves the smart object's pixels as they were. The replay hook still recognises the filter rather than falling through to the other handlers. |

The issue's growth probes, with pins 4000–16000 px out (up to about 3.2e8 px), stay inside the budget and still complete.

## Tests

- `algo`: `puppet::tests::a_pin_dragged_absurdly_far_is_refused_before_rendering`. Pins at `(2^20, 2^20)` and `(-1e7, 62)` are refused, and a near pin still renders.
- `engine`: `distort_cmds::tests::puppet_refuses_pins_that_stretch_the_content_too_far`.
  - **Refused:** the issue's command at 8, 16 and 32-bit, with and without a selection (both `deform_selected` paths). The error says "too far", the layer is unchanged, and there is no history step.

title: Preserve document depth when splitting stroked vector shapes
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Fixes #1115.

A stroked vector shape with a layer effect or clipped layers was rasterized into RGBA8 fill/stroke surfaces even in a 16- or 32-bit document. A 4000-pixel gradient consequently had only 256 levels. The split now uses the compositor's document depth, and the cache key includes that depth so the same shape cannot reuse a lower-precision split. Float stroke fitting also preserves HDR RGB values above 1.

The working surfaces remain RGBA; the existing GPU upload format is unchanged. Both GPU split callers receive the document depth.

### Validation

- The new precision/cache tests and extended HDR edge test fail on the old implementation (3 failures); all 10 focused CPU tests pass with the fix.
- Both existing GPU stroke/effect/clipping tests now cover U8, U16 and F32 (18 small fixture variants, including existing paged-compositor checks); they passed on the actual GPU.
- Full compose/GPU tests: 186 passed. Strict Clippy with `-D warnings`, formatting, diff check, layering and WebAssembly checks passed using Rust 1.95.0.
- Full `cargo xtask test-corpus`: 2,077 passed, 20 existing ignored. `cargo xtask perf --quick` passed (quick mode does not enforce full-size budgets; its stored M4 Pro baseline is a different machine class, so automatic regression comparison was skipped).

### 24 MP measurement

title: Apply the transform when another layer is selected (#1400)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1400.

While Free Transform was open (Ctrl+T, or after dragging a handle of the Move tool's "Show Transform Controls"), selecting another layer in the Layers panel left the transform box and its lifted preview on the previous layer. `transform_tool::end_if_left` only ended the session when its layer or document went away, or when the tool changed.

## Change
- `end_if_left` now also **applies** the transform when the active layer is no longer the one being transformed. Photoshop applies the transform on a layer switch too.
  - The edit lands on the original layer as one history step.
  - The next Free Transform, or the Move tool's box, follows the newly selected layer.
- Transform Selection is not tied to a layer, so it stays open.
- When there is no active layer at all, the session is left alone, as before.

title: Optimize Radial Blur sampling without changing output
author: optimalbytee
body:
Radial Blur repeatedly computes sample transforms and checks source coordinates for each channel. This change prepares transforms once per operation and reads each bilinear tap across channels together, retaining the existing tiled application pipeline.

Draft/Good/Best keep their 64/256/4096 interval ceilings, discrete positions and alpha rounding. Preparation covers only interval counts reachable in the output area, so small Best jobs avoid the full ~64 MiB table. title: Mesh warp of a gray surface writes the old and warped regions separately (#995)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #995.

`warp_mesh_gray`, reached by `select.transformSelection` with a warp mesh, cleared the source and warped regions as one dense buffer over their union. A mesh that moves a selection far away therefore allocated a buffer that grows with the square of the distance. The issue computes about 37 GiB of floats for a 48 px selection moved 100000 px.

## Change (`crates/algo/src/warp.rs`)

This is the same fix b70fbd4 made in the homography path (`transform_cmds::warp_gray`): clear the old region, then write the warped region on its own. `Surface` is tile-sparse, so a distant region costs only its own tiles. The output is unchanged: same pixels, and the old region is still cleared.

## Measurement

I moved a 48 px selection 8192 px with `warp_mesh_gray`, using a temporary test binary run under `/usr/bin/time -l` on macOS arm64:

| | peak RSS | time |
|---|---|---|
| before | 346 MB | 0.41 s |
| after | 3 MB | < 0.01 s |

I didn't run the issue's 100000 px case on the old code; it would request about 37 GiB.

## Test

`warp::tests::a_mesh_warp_far_off_canvas_writes_only_the_two_regions` warps 8-bit and 32-bit gray selections by +100000, -100000 and 300 px. It checks that the result is the translated block, that it is set at the new place, and that the old place is cleared.

## Gates (macOS arm64, Rust 1.95)

- `cargo test --no-fail-fast -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine`: all pass.

title: Divide Slice: one division makes at most 10000 parts (#1020)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1020.

`slice.divide` clamped `horizontal` and `vertical` to 1..1000 each but checked no total. One request could make up to a million slices. Resolving the slice list (`slices::resolve`, used by `slice.list` and export) is quadratic in the slice count, about 5×10¹¹ rectangle visits at a million.

## Change (`crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs`)

- A division over **10000 parts** (for example 100 × 100) is refused with a bad-params error before any part is created. The params doc now says "at most 10000 parts".
- 10000 is a budget I chose: resolving 10000 slices is about 5×10⁷ visits, and the test lists them in well under a second. I don't know Photoshop's own limit for Divide Slice; happy to change the number.

## Not covered

Resolution itself stays quadratic. The `auto_slices` coverage scan and the linear `Slices::get` lookups in `resolve` and `resolved_json` (both named in the issue) could be made sub-quadratic, but that's a larger change in `photocraft-doc`. Slices added one at a time with `slice.new` aren't budgeted here either.

## Test

`slice_cmds::tests::divide_refuses_more_parts_than_one_division_makes`:
- 101 × 100, 100 × 101 and 1000 × 1000 are refused with "10000" in the error, and the slices and history are unchanged.
- 100 × 100 makes 10000 parts and `slice.list` resolves them.

Before the fix, 101 × 100 was accepted (10100 parts).

title: Font menu keeps its height and focuses its search field (#1369)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1369.

## Causes and changes (`crates/ui-egui/src/type_tool.rs`)
- **Height:** egui 0.36 measures a popup only on the frame it opens and never lets it grow back. Once the filtered font list shrank the menu, clearing the query left it short until it was reopened.
  - While searching, the list now keeps the height it had unfiltered (capped at 460).
  - Trade-off: a search with few results leaves blank space below them instead of shrinking the menu.
- **Focus:** the search field was only focused while the query was empty, so a reopened menu with a leftover query had no focus.
  - It is now focused on every open. The request repeats until the field has focus, because egui's first popup frame is an invisible sizing pass.
- **Clicks:** the ComboBox used egui's default `CloseOnClick`, so clicking the search field closed the menu.
  - It now uses `CloseOnClickOutside`, and picking a font closes the menu explicitly.

- New file `crates/ui-egui/src/type_font_picker_tests.rs` (egui_kittest, linked as `type_tool::font_picker_tests`):
  - `clearing_the_query_restores_the_menu_height`
  - `reopening_focuses_the_search_field_and_clicking_it_keeps_the_menu_open` (also checks that picking a font still closes the menu)
- Both fail on the old code: after clearing, the height was 78 vs 400; there was no focus on reopen; clicking the search field closed the menu.

author: Unemars

**Problem.** A crop with Delete Cropped Pixels off keeps the pixels it cuts away, and a moved or pasted layer can reach past the canvas too. In Photoshop, those pixels show as soon as you start editing the crop frame, so you can see how much is hidden and pull an edge back out over it. PhotoCraft's Crop tool drew only the canvas: the hidden pixels stayed invisible until you committed a bigger crop or ran Image › Reveal All.

title: Release CPU canvas and Navigator textures when documents close
author: GamerWil26
body:
Closing a document releases the GPU canvas, but leaves its CPU canvas textures in `PhotocraftApp::canvases`. Navigator textures are stored in egui context data and also survive document close. Repeated CPU-rendered open/close cycles therefore accumulate texture handles and can reuse stale textures when a native document is reopened with its preserved ID.

Move Navigator texture ownership into the app's document cache and prune both caches in `sync_views`, alongside the existing document/view cleanup. Other open documents and their per-monitor textures remain intact. This does not purge open-document history or disable GPU rendering.

Verification:

- A regression fails on the previous implementation immediately after `file.close`; fixed coverage verifies both display textures are released, another open document is preserved, Navigator handle ownership is released, and reopening the same document ID builds a fresh texture.
- Manual allocation measurement: six 3000×2000 CPU canvases, with upload deltas drained each cycle. With the previous cleanup behavior, egui reports 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144 MB of allocated textures after closing. With cleanup, every closed cycle reports zero. These are texture allocation sizes, not an RSS reduction claim; the measurement harness does not submit GPU uploads.
- Full algorithm/UI unit and integration suites: 1,308 passed, 10 ignored; the focused close-cleanup checks and manual allocation run pass separately. Clippy, layering and Wasm checks pass.

This fixes a demonstrated document-lifetime leak. It does not claim to eliminate graphics-driver/allocator retention: on an older Windows test build, six 14 MP open/resize/close cycles still left about 883 MiB working set in DX12 mode versus 196 MiB with software rendering. That larger GPU-path footprint needs separate profiling.

The ignored `closed_canvas_memory_measurement` test reproduces the allocation accounting. There is no visual UI change and no personal-image evidence in this PR. …

title: Retouch tools: stroke points outside ±1e6 are refused, as for painting (#976)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #976.

The retouch tools parse `points` with `parse_brush`, which skipped the coordinate bound the painting tools apply in `parse_points` ("an absurd coordinate would mean billions of dabs"). `parse_brush` is shared by Dodge, Burn, Sponge, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Clone Stamp, Healing Brush, Spot Healing and History Brush. A segment to `(1e300, 0)` has an infinite length, so the dab walker never reaches its end. Finite far points mean work and allocation in proportion to the distance.

## Change

The bound check moves out of `brush_cmds::parse_points` into `brush_cmds::check_coords`, called by both parsers. It keeps the same ±1e6 limit and message, so the painting tools behave exactly as before.

## Test

`retouch_cmds::tests::retouch_strokes_refuse_absurd_point_coordinates` sends four far-point cases to **all ten** retouch commands at 8, 16 and 32-bit:
- a single point just past the bound;
- a 2e6 px segment;
- a segment to `1e300`;
- a single `1e300` point (the issue's dab-rectangle overflow).

Each must return the coordinate error, with the layer pixels and history unchanged. As a control, a Dodge stroke on the canvas still changes the pixels.

The reporter only confirmed `paint.dodge`; this covers the other nine too. Before the fix, the first case was accepted (`paint.dodge` returned damage at x = 999990). I put that case first so a regression fails fast instead of looping on the `1e300` segment.

title: TIFF: alpha after an unspecified extra sample opens transparent (#1349)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1349.

**Why**
TIFF 6.0 lets ExtraSamples mark any extra component as alpha. A file with ExtraSamples `[0, 2]` (unspecified, then unassociated alpha) opened fully opaque with no warning, so its transparency was lost on export. There were two causes: the decoder only looked at the first extra sample, and for RGB/CMYK the `tiff` crate drops every sample after its own colour type.

**Change** (`crates/codecs/src/codecs/tiff.rs`)
- The alpha is the first extra sample marked associated (1) or unassociated (2), wherever it sits.
- When an RGB or CMYK file has its alpha after another extra sample, the decoder asks the crate for every sample. It does this by patching the photometric to gray, as it already does for WhiteIsZero and palette files. The decoder then picks the colour and alpha samples itself.
- Planar files read the alpha from its own plane.
- Associated alpha is made straight whatever its position.
- Gray files with ExtraSamples `[0, 2]` now open as GrayA instead of Gray.
- An alpha position past a pixel's samples returns an error, not a panic.

**Tests**
- New test `alpha_after_an_unspecified_extra_sample_is_kept` in `crates/codecs/tests/tiff_pages.rs`:
  - covers RGB, CMYK and gray with `[0, 2]` at 8, 16 and 32f bits, chunky and planar, both byte orders, classic and BigTIFF;
  - also checks the issue's exact 2×2 file and associated alpha `[0, 1]`;
  - fails on main (the RGB case decodes as `Rgb`) and passes with this change.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs`: green. The existing `[2, 0]` test still passes.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Not included / not verified**
- No end-to-end `photocraft-cli serve` run with the issue's jsonl.
- JPEG-compressed RGB with a non-first alpha (now decoded as multiband) is untested. If the crate refuses it, open returns an error.
- wasm, perf and corpus runs are left to CI.

title: PSD: warn that Color Lookup tetrahedral interpolation is saved as trilinear (#1347)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1347.

**Why**
A Color Lookup adjustment layer set to tetrahedral interpolation reopened from PSD as trilinear. The composite changed and neither the save nor the open reported anything. Photoshop's `clrL` descriptor has no interpolation setting, so PSD cannot carry this choice: public readers such as ag-psd handle only `lookupType`, `NM  `, `Dthr`, `profile`, `LUTFormat`, `dataOrder`, `tableOrder`, `LUT3DFileData` and `LUT3DFileName`, and Photoshop's panel offers only Dither. As the issue suggests for this case, the save now reports the loss. `.pcraft` keeps the setting.

**Change**
- PSD export adds one warning per Color Lookup layer with tetrahedral interpolation: `layer "<name>": Color Lookup tetrahedral interpolation is saved as trilinear (PSD has no interpolation setting)`.
- Trilinear Color Lookup layers save exactly as before, with no warning.

**Tests**
- New test `color_lookup_tetrahedral_warns_on_psd_save` in `crates/io/tests/adjust_blend_roundtrip.rs`. It round-trips through PSD bytes and asserts that tetrahedral gives the warning, trilinear gives none, and the LUT survives. It fails on main (no warnings) and passes with this change.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

**Not included / not verified**
- No private PSD key to keep the tetrahedral setting: `crates/io` has no established pattern for PhotoCraft-only data in PSD, and Photoshop would ignore such a key anyway.
- No Photoshop-authored PSD with a Color Lookup layer was inspected.
- The CLI reproduction from the issue was not run end to end.

title: Add opt-in native AVIF import and export
author: optimalbytee
body:
AVIF still-image import/export is now **opt-in for native builds** (`cargo build -j12 -p photocraft --features avif`, or `-p photocraft-cli`). Default builds recognise AVIF files and report unsupported decoding/encoding; Export As and native save filters omit AVIF. Browser AVIF support is deferred.

The decoder is now the official [memorysafety/rav1d](https://github.com/memorysafety/rav1d), pinned to [upstream commit d3d1cd67059f47803919be8276650e5870c9fd02](https://github.com/memorysafety/rav1d/commit/d3d1cd67059f47803919be8276650e5870c9fd02), replacing `sqzer-rav1d`. The published rav1d 1.1.0 crate predates the safe Rust API used here, so an exact Git revision is necessary. Assembly is disabled. Upstream still declares `cc`/`nasm-rs` build dependencies, but its assembly-disabled build script invokes neither a C compiler nor an assembler. No local unsafe code is added; upstream decoder internals contain unsafe Rust.

**Maintainer decision still required:** the optional, unmodified `avif-parse` 2.1.0 parser remains MPL-2.0. Making it opt-in does not resolve acceptance of that licence in this project.

Import supports 8/10/12-bit still pictures, alpha, ICC, supported CICP spaces, monochrome expansion and common YUV matrices. Export produces lossy 8/10-bit RGB 4:4:4 with alpha and ICC, using profile-aware document conversion. Export controls expose quality, speed, bit depth and alpha quality. title: Undo: a paint stroke's undo keeps the painted layer active (#1356)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1356.

**Why**
Selecting a layer isn't a history step, so each history state kept the layers that were selected when that state was created. Undo restored that old selection. In the issue's steps (rasterize a shape while Background is active, select the rasterized layer, paint, Ctrl+Z), Background became active again. Photoshop keeps the painted layer active.

**Change**
- `Session::edit` and compound steps (`analysis_cmds.rs`) read the selection just before the step. They write it into the state they leave behind with the existing `History::set_current_layers`. Undo therefore returns to what was selected when the step was taken.
- Undo of a stroke or fill keeps the painted layer active.
- Undo of New Layer goes back to the layer that was active before it.
- Undo of Merge reselects the merged layers.
- Undo of Delete brings the layer back selected.
- Coalesced edits and the post-edit reselect path are unchanged.
- Doc comments on `LayerTarget` and `DocState::selected_layers` now describe this.

**Tests**
- New `crates/engine/tests/undo_keeps_active_layer.rs`. Both tests fail on main (undo selects Background).
  - The issue's repro: shape, rasterize with Background active, select, stroke, then undo / redo / undo.
  - Fill and New Layer undo / redo.
- Two existing tests asserted the old target and are updated:
  - `merge_selected_into_top_most`: undo now reselects the merged `[a, c]`.
  - The layer-reveal undo scenario: undoing New Layer reactivates the inner layer it was made from and scrolls it into view.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ops` and the `photocraft-ui-egui` lib tests pass.
  - Two GPU test binaries (`drag_preview_canvas`, `full_res_preview`) crash with an access violation on this Windows machine. They crash the same way on main.

title: Control: reject queued requests after their reply deadline (#1109)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
A desktop control request can time out while the UI is not draining its queue, then execute when the UI resumes. Retrying an Add Layer request can therefore create two layers after the first request already reported a timeout.

Give native requests one absolute 60-second deadline, use its remaining time for the reply wait, and reject expired requests immediately before UI dispatch. In-process requests without a deadline retain their behavior, and already-started jobs continue to completion. Document that timeout boundary.

Fixes #1109.

## Validation

- The expired Add Layer regression fails before enforcement and passes after it. The baseline includes only the new optional deadline field and tests; it is not an untouched-main run.
- Queue coverage verifies one layer/undo step for the live retry, continued processing after an expired request, and deadline-free callers whose receiver was dropped. A real Gaussian Blur started before expiry still applies afterward; the native TCP test checks deadline attachment.
- Full UI suite: 1,068 passed, five existing ignored. Full desktop suite: 79 passed; the native AppKit menu smoke test also passed. Formatting, diff, layering and Wasm checks passed.
- Required strict Clippy stops on unchanged `text/cjk.rs:71` (`nonminimal_bool`). A supplemental selected-package run with `--no-deps` finds existing warnings in `analysis_ui.rs:270,629`, `canvas.rs:3239` and `transform_tool.rs:778`; none of those files changed, and no warnings were suppressed.

The reported minimized-macOS-window/60-second scenario was not manually reproduced; the regression drives the actual UI queue deterministically.

title: MCP bridge: do not replay edits after a lost reply (#1007)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
When the desktop app applies an edit and its reply is lost, the MCP bridge reconnects and resends the same request. One Add Layer call can therefore add two layers while reporting success.

Remove automatic replay after an operation exchange fails. Report that the operation may have completed, discard the failed connection, and reconnect/authenticate on the next separate call. Update the protocol documentation to describe the uncertainty and recovery behavior.

Fixes #1007.

## Validation

- A loopback regression uses a real Headless editing session: apply Add Layer, close before replying, then inspect through a fresh authenticated connection. Before the fix it creates two layers and reports success; after the fix it reports uncertainty, preserves exactly one added layer/undo step, and the next call succeeds.
- All 74 automation tests passed, including normal bridge forwarding, stale reply IDs, authentication, oversized replies and the new regression.
- Formatting, diff, layering and `cargo xtask wasm` passed. Strict selected-package Clippy (`--no-deps`) passed. The required dependency-inclusive run stops on unchanged `plugins/manifest.rs:125` (`collapsible_match`); no warnings suppressed.
- Validated on base `0b580350`, which includes the maintainer's async Swatches fix #1528. This resolves the unrelated Swatches compilation failures seen in the initial native/Wasm CI run; this PR still changes only the bridge, its regression test and protocol documentation.

title: MCP previews: reject unsupported document indices (#1005)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
The MCP preview tools accept a document `index` even when returning a screenshot of the entire app window. A client can mistake that successful image for a preview of the requested document.

Give `ui_screenshot` a schema containing only `max_side` and reject unsupported arguments. Reject `index` in bridged `doc_render_preview` with an explanation that bridge previews capture the window. Indexed headless document rendering and ordinary screenshot downscaling are preserved.

Fixes #1005.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the new MCP regression failed because both bridge tools accepted `index: 0` and returned images. After the fix, errors name `index`, no rejected request reaches the app, and ordinary calls still return correctly scaled PNGs.
- A headless control decodes previews from white landscape and black portrait documents, checks dimensions and pixels, and confirms the active document stays unchanged. The tool schema still exposes headless `index`.
- All 75 automation tests passed. Formatting, diff and strict selected-package Clippy (`--no-deps`) passed. Dependency-inclusive Clippy stops on unchanged `text/cjk.rs:71` (`nonminimal_bool`); no warnings suppressed.
- Layering and `cargo xtask wasm` passed.

title: Free Transform: the reference point moves with the box when scaling (#1329)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1329.

**Why:** In Photoshop's Free Transform the reference point is attached to the bounding box. Scaling from a corner or edge, skewing, distorting or applying perspective carries it along, so it keeps its relative place in the box: the centre stays the centre, and a reference point on a corner stays on that corner. PhotoCraft left it at its old canvas position for all of these drags.

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs`)
- New helper `carry_pivot`: it finds the reference point's position in the old box's unit frame and puts it at the same place in the new box. If the box has collapsed or the result isn't finite, the point stays where it was, so nothing panics or becomes NaN.
- `apply_drag` now calls it after scale, skew, distort and perspective drags. Before, the scale branch mapped the point back through the *old* box, and the other branches never updated it.
- ⌥-scaling, which scales about the reference point, and rotation leave it fixed, as before.
- Moving, nudging and the options-bar X/Y/W/H/angle fields already behaved correctly and are unchanged.

**Tests**
- New `transform_tool::tests::the_reference_point_moves_with_the_box`. It covers corner scale, edge scale with a corner reference point, skew, distort, perspective, ⌥-scale, rotation and a collapsed box. It fails on main: the point stays at `[50.0, 25.0]`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui transform`: 63 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Not included / not verified**
- No visual check in the running app.
- A related problem, left out of this PR: with ⌥ held and the reference point off-centre, the box is re-centred on the point, whereas Photoshop scales about it. This behaviour is older than this change.
- The other open PRs that change `transform_tool.rs` merge cleanly with this one (#1496), or already conflict with main without it (#1236, #573).

body:
Fixes #1455

### Description
Photoshop fails to open PSD files exported by PhotoCraft containing a Photo Filter adjustment layer. Photo Filter (\phfl\) adjustment layer data was previously written with 18 bytes (padded to 2 bytes), but Photoshop expects \phfl\ tagged blocks to be padded to a 4-byte boundary (20 bytes).

title: fix(ui): the font dropdown restores its height, fits its names and keeps the search focused
author: roaldosulejmani
body:
## What

Fixes the font dropdown's sizing and search-focus bugs reported in #1369.

## Why

`font_picker` was an `egui::ComboBox`, which caused three problems:

1. **Height** — filtering the list shrank the popup, and clearing the query left it short. An egui popup keeps the size it last laid out and never grows back until it is reopened.
2. **Focus** — reopening with a query still in the box did not focus the search field, so the first click landed on a row (or outside) and closed the popup.
3. **Click inside** — the list overlapped the search field, so clicking the field hit a row and closed the popup.

## How

Replaced the `ComboBox` with a custom `egui::Popup` toggle button (`close_behavior(CloseOnClickOutside)`), and:

- **Height**: pin the popup with `ui.set_min_height(list_h)` so it grows back the moment the query is cleared. Deliberately *no* `set_max_height` — it does `max_rect |= min_rect`, which moves the layout cursor back to the top of the popup and makes the list overlap the search field (row 0 then swallows the field click).
- **Focus**: a `first` flag (the button was clicked and is closed, or the popup is open and was not open last frame) calls `search.request_focus()`, even when a query is already there.
- **Click inside**: selecting a row uses `ui.close()`; the popup only closes on a click outside.
- **Width**: size the popup to the widest matching family (at least the button width, at most the screen) instead of `ui.available_width()`, which in an unconstrained popup is the whole window.
- **Style**: the search field is a plain `TextEdit`; the menu style made it transparent and cramped.
- `type_panels_ui::family_picker` now delegates to `type_tool::font_picker`, so the properties panel and the options bar share one implementation.

## Screenshots

Clearing a query after filtering to `arial`:

| Before | After |
|---|---|

## Root Cause

title: Fill and adjustment layers take the active path as their vector mask (#1419)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1419.

**Why:** In Photoshop, a path selected in the Paths panel becomes the vector mask of a new fill or adjustment layer. That path can be a work path drawn with the Pen, one made from a selection, or a saved path. So Layer › New Fill Layer › Solid Color on a path makes an editable shape. The path wins over an active selection, and with no path selected the selection becomes a layer mask (#1250). PhotoCraft ignored the path, so Solid Color filled the whole canvas.

**Change**

*Engine*
- `layer.newFillLayer.solidColor`, `.gradient` and `.pattern`, and every `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.*`, take an optional `"path"`: `"work"`, a saved path's name, or a path object. It becomes the new layer's vector mask.
- Without `"path"`, or with `null`, the selection becomes the layer mask as before.
- A missing or malformed path is an error and adds no layer; it never panics. The shared helper is `commands::mask_new_layer`.

*UI*
- The path selected in the Paths panel is passed as `"path"` (`vector_ui::with_active_path`).
- Drawing a work path with the Pen, or Make Work Path, selects it.
- Clicking the panel's empty area deselects it.
- After the layer is made, its vector mask becomes the active path, as in Photoshop, so the next fill layer isn't masked by the work path again.

**Tests**
- Engine, `new_fill_and_adjustment_layers_take_the_active_path_as_their_vector_mask`:
  - Solid, gradient, pattern and invert, at 8, 16 and 32-bit, with the work path and with a saved path, while a selection is active.
  - The vector mask equals the path and there is no layer mask.
  - Pixels outside the path are unchanged, and undo removes the layer.
- Engine, `new_fill_layer_with_a_missing_path_fails_without_a_layer`: a missing work path, an unknown name, a number and a malformed object each return `Err` and add no layer.
- UI, `vector_ui::tests::new_fill_layer_takes_the_selected_path_as_its_vector_mask`:

title: Fix #1543: oversized Satin and Bevel & Emboss sizes render instead of panicking
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1543.

**Problem:** a Satin `size`, or a Bevel & Emboss `size` or `soften`, of `1e308` reached the box blur unclamped. The kernel radius saturated to about 2⁶² taps, and every render panicked with `capacity overflow`. At `1e6` the render ran for minutes instead. Drop Shadow was unaffected because `margin()` already clamps its reach.

**Fix:** a single helper, `effects::box_width`, caps a blur width at `MAX_REACH`, the reach `margin()` already allows, and maps NaN to 1. `box_weights`, which is behind `tent_kernel` and the GPU convolutions, and `box_geom`, behind the CPU tent, both go through it. Values from commands and from imported files are therefore bounded the same way. Photoshop's own ranges (size ≤ 250, soften ≤ 16) sit well inside the cap, so normal renders are unchanged.

**Tests:**
- `layer_style::tests::oversized_satin_and_bevel_sizes_render` covers the issue's five cases (`1e308` and `1e6` sizes and softness) and renders each. It panicked with `capacity overflow` before this change.
- `tent_kernel_is_two_boxes` now also checks that huge, infinite and NaN widths are capped.
- `photocraft-compose` and `photocraft-gpu` tests pass.

title: Speed up exact Shape Blur convolution
author: optimalbytee
body:
Shape Blur now prepares its binary span kernel once per operation, fuses the existing f32 premultiplication into f64 row prefixes, and accumulates contiguous output rows in the original addition order. This removes the extra premultiplied image buffer while preserving the existing command, sampling, normalization, alpha handling and color models. No approximation, dependency, unsafe code or CPU-specific intrinsic is added.

Checked sizes and fallible reservations guard prefix/output allocations. Direct radii are bounded to 0–1000, nonfinite radii use zero, and Shape Blur tile overrides clamp to 1–2048. Shared tile-coordinate advancement saturates near i32::MAX. A failed tile stops the cancellable operation; the legacy surface API returns the original surface because it has no allocation-error channel. These guards do not impose a document-size limit or a workspace-wide memory budget.

Performance evidence comes from the supplied handoff: Windows 11, Ryzen 7 9700X, Rust 1.97.1 MSVC, ordinary release profile, eight Rayon workers, one warmup and three timed repetitions. Timings include `apply_in` tile reads, edge extension, filtering and writes; source setup, result destruction, engine history and UI/GPU refresh are excluded.

| Case | Before → after | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| All 81 standard 24 MP cases: nine shapes × radii 5/25/100 × U8/U16/F32 | Every case improved | 1.33–2.84×; mean case ratio 1.96× |
| 24 MP RGBA8 Circle, radius 1000 | 154.272 → 50.448 s | 3.06× |
| 36 MP RGBA32F Ring, radius 100 | 5.616 → 2.018 s | 2.78× |

All 27 small cases also improved, by 1.43–2.02×. Circle/r1000 process peak fell from 6.16 to 4.73 GiB, but this case still takes tens of seconds and multiple GiB. Full samples, memory methodology and limitations are recorded in `docs/shape-blur-performance.md` and `perf/shape-blur-2026-10-09.json`. No Linux/macOS/ARM/wasm runtime speedup or global budget compliance is claimed.

title: Fix #1544: Image Size refuses a resample past the raster budget; resampling writes bands as it goes
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1544.

**Problem:** `image.imageSize` accepted a resize from 64×48 to 300000×300000. Each side is within the 300000 px limit, but together that's 90 billion pixels, and the command started allocating destination-sized `f32` bands with no budget.

**Changes:**
- **A budget for the result.** Image Size now refuses a resampled canvas whose raster alone would exceed the decoders' default allocation budget: 8 GiB on 64-bit, 2 GiB on 32-bit and wasm. That works out to 2147 megapixels at 8-bit RGBA. The error is actionable: "300000 x 300000 px is 90000 megapixels; resampling at this bit depth is limited to 2147 megapixels. Choose a smaller size, or turn Resample off to change only the resolution". The check runs before the edit, so the document, its history and its revision stay unchanged.
- **Resolution-only changes still work.** With Resample off, Image Size changes the resolution without resampling, so the budget doesn't apply.
- **Bounded band memory.** `algo::resample` now writes its output bands a group at a time, two per thread, instead of collecting every band first. The `f32` rows held at once now scale with the thread count rather than the destination size.

**Tests:** `image_cmds::tests::image_size_refuses_a_raster_past_the_budget` covers the issue's case:
- the oversized resize is refused with "megapixels" in the error;
- the size and history are unchanged afterwards;
- a resolution-only change at that size still works;
- the 128×96 control resizes.

The `image_cmds` and `algo` resample tests pass, and so do clippy and a wasm32 check of `photocraft-algo`.

title: fix(engine): finish background job bookkeeping on its document
author: shmuelbiller1
body:
Fix a background-job bookkeeping bug that can associate a completed editing operation with the wrong document when the user switches tabs during processing.

## Problem

When a background filter finishes, PhotoCraft correctly applies the result to the original document. However, it restores the previously selected document before running post-command bookkeeping.

Because that bookkeeping uses the active document, features such as **Edit → Fade** and layer-based slice updates can be associated with the wrong document.

## Fix

- Run successful post-command bookkeeping while the edited document is still active.
- Restore the user's previously selected document afterward.
- Preserve document selection when the job reports an error.
- Keep the existing behavior for jobs that create new documents.

## Regression test

Added a deterministic test that:

1. Starts a background filter job on Document A.
2. Switches to Document B while the job runs.
3. Completes the background job.
4. Verifies that Document B remains selected and unchanged.
5. Verifies that Edit → Fade is associated with Document A, not Document B.

## Files changed

- `crates/engine/src/jobs.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/jobs_tests.rs`
