- a cube when the colour isn't a web colour.

Each sits over a chip of the nearest colour t…

title: feat(ui): hide and show layer effects from the Layers panel (#1622)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Fixes #1622

The eye toggles on the Effects group and on individual effect rows in the Layers panel did nothing. The document model and compositor already honored an effect's `enabled` flag, but there was no way to change it.

This adds `Effects::set_enabled` in `photocraft-doc`, a `layer.layerStyle.setVisible` engine command (undoable), and wires the master Effects eye and each effect's eye in the Layers panel to it. Engine tests cover that a hidden effect leaves the composite unchanged and that undo restores it, and a Layers panel test covers the toggles.

title: fix(ui): Delete and Backspace delete layers and can be assigned as shortcuts (#1621)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Fixes #1621

Two problems kept Delete and Backspace from deleting layers:

- In the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog an unmodified Backspace or Delete was treated as clear-this-shortcut instead of being recorded, so neither key could be assigned to Delete Layer.
- With a canvas selection active, the Delete key always acted on the selection, even when the Layers panel had focus, so the layer could not be deleted from the panel.

Both keys are now recorded as bindings, and Delete/Backspace remove the active layer when the Layers panel has focus. Regression tests cover key capture and the delete-layer dispatch.

title: Layers panel: drag layer effects onto another layer to move them, Alt-drag copies (#1719)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1719.

**What you saw:** dragging an effect (Drop Shadow, Stroke…) or the fx badge from one layer to another did nothing. The effect was never picked up, with or without Alt. Dragging the fx badge dragged the whole layer.

**Cause:** the effect sub-rows in the Layers panel only took clicks, and the fx badge was part of the layer row, so a drag started on it was a layer drag. Nothing could move effects between layers, and no command existed for it.

**What changed** (Photoshop's behaviour):
- Dragging the fx badge or the "Effects" row onto another layer moves all the effects there. They replace that layer's style, as Paste Layer Style does.
- Dragging one effect row moves only that effect. It replaces an effect of the same kind on the target, or is added.
- Holding Alt on release copies instead of moving. While Alt is held, the cursor changes to the copy cursor. The effect name follows the pointer, and the target row is outlined.
- The badge takes the drag the way the eye column already does, so clicking it still selects the layer.
- Each drop is one undo step, made by a new engine command, `layer.layerStyle.transferEffects` (`{"from","to","effect"?,"copy"}`). It has no menu entry, like Show All Effects, so agents and the control channel can use it too.

**Tests**
- Engine: copy all, move one, move all, one history step with undo, and bad params (same layer, missing or unknown layer, bad effect index, a source with no effects) return an error and leave history unchanged.
- UI (egui_kittest): Alt-drag the Color Overlay row onto another layer copies just that effect. Dragging the fx badge moves every effect and leaves the layer order alone.

title: fix(blend): keep 32-bit Hue/Saturation/Color/Luminosity above 1
author: hideoneric
body:
## Summary
- Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity used the ISO 32000 ClipColor formula. It only stays in range while the luminosity is in 0..1, so 32-bit colours with luminosity above 1 came out inverted (Luminosity of a grey of 2 over (0.5, 0.25, 0.125) gave (1.0, 2.32, 2.99)), and near-greys divided by rounding noise.
- `clip_color` now returns the grey when the luminosity has no in-gamut colour, so results are stable.
- 32-bit documents clip at `f32::MAX` instead of 1 (only negatives are pulled in), so bright colours keep values above 1. 8/16-bit output is unchanged.
- The per-document setting reuses main's `psblend::HDR` flag (set via `with_hdr`, which restores the previous value so nested rayon tile work can't reset it): `blend_rgb_hdr` now keeps the non-separable modes above 1 too.
- GPU: `compose.wgsl` mirrors the CPU clip, and reads the existing `F_HDR` pass flag that `plan.rs` sets for 32-bit documents. Before this, Hue over a grey of 2 gave CPU 1.0 and GPU 2.82.
- The adjustment path that calls `set_lum` passes `1.0` explicitly, so it keeps clipping at 1.

## Testing
All run locally (Linux, Radeon RX 7800 XT) on this commit; all pass.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-color -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu`: passes, including the new tests `non_separable_modes_unchanged_on_integer_inputs`, `non_separable_modes_stable_when_luminosity_is_out_of_range`, `document_settings_nest_and_restore`, `non_separable_modes_keep_values_above_one_in_32_bit` and `non_separable_modes_on_hdr_values` (ran on a real GPU adapter, not skipped).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-color -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask layers`: no violations.
- `cargo xtask wasm`: all crates build.

title: Liquify: a stroke segment walks only the dabs that can reach the field (#937)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #937.

`LiquifyField::stroke_segment` walked one dab per spacing step along the whole segment. A stroke to `(1e15, 0)` meant about 3.3×10¹⁴ steps, so `filter.liquify` wouldn't return.

## Change (`crates/algo/src/liquify.rs`)

A dab whose footprint maps to no field node already returns from `dab` before touching anything. The dab centres are linear in the step index (`a + (b - a)·(k - o)/steps`, with `o` = 1 for the dragging tools and 0 for the stationary ones), so the steps that can do something form one contiguous run.

The new `reachable_steps` computes that run from the node grid, padded by a node and a step, and the loop walks only it. Nothing is rejected, and every result is **bit-identical** to the full walk. The dabs left out each returned an empty rect.

## Evidence

- **Equivalence test** (`a_segment_walks_only_the_dabs_that_can_reach_the_field`): a copy of the old full walk runs side by side with the new one. It covers all ten brush tools at sizes 6 and 40 over nine segments: inside, in from far away, out to far away, diagonal through, parallel just outside (where the brush still reaches), parallel far outside, along an edge, wholly outside, and shorter than a step. The field, freeze mask and dirty rect are compared exactly.
- **Far segments return** (`a_segment_to_a_far_off_point_returns`): the issue's `1e15` segment, a segment whose length overflows `f64`, and a `±1e15` Bloat stroke.
- **Engine** (`distort_cmds::tests::liquify_with_a_far_off_stroke_point_returns`): the issue's exact `filter.liquify` request returns at 8, 16 and 32-bit. A stroke entirely off the canvas leaves the layer unchanged.
- **Timing:** a 3×10⁷ px segment took 68 ms in a release build before the change and 22 µs after. The old cost was linear in the length; that's about 26 days for the issue's segment by extrapolation, which I didn't run.

title: fix(indexed-color): integer counts, palette stops and asynchronous previews
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Indexed Color accepted fractional color counts and calculated its live preview on the UI thread, blocking the window on larger images. This validates whole counts in 2–256, adds a **linear** count slider with markers/snapping at 8/16/32/64/128/256 (direct entry and arrow keys still allow other integers), and calculates native previews on one background worker.

Palette construction, quantization and result composition run off the UI thread. While dragging, the previous preview of the same source remains visible; intermediate requests are coalesced. Completed results must match the current document revision, active layer, dialog, parameters and proxy factor before upload. Closing/reopening a dialog cannot publish an old result. Web and explicitly inline sessions remain synchronous; GPU upload/display conversion remain on the UI thread.

The pixel path uses exact nearest-color lookup: linear scans for small palettes and a balanced kd-tree above 64 entries, retaining the original distance arithmetic and tie order. Fixed palettes skip an unused histogram, and the output-layer conversion reuses its pixel buffer instead of allocating per pixel. No sampling, approximate RGB LUT or dithering changes.

title: fix(ui): one Cmd+V pastes one layer (#1638)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1638.

## Cause (macOS)

1. The menu bar's Edit › Paste has Cmd+V as its key equivalent, so AppKit takes the key-down and winit never sees the press.
2. `NativeMenu::raw_input` gave egui that press **plus a made-up release**.
3. winit still delivers the real key-up: winit 0.30's `send_event` override forwards key-ups while ⌘ is held.
4. `shortcuts::clipboard_keys` treats a ⌘V release without a paste event as an image paste. egui-winit drops ⌘V when the clipboard holds no text, so this rule is how image pastes reach us. Each of the two releases therefore added another paste.

Result: three pastes per ⌘V. A test reproduced it: 2 layers became 4 instead of 3. Copy and Cut were never affected, because the release rule exists only for V.

## Fix

- **`native_menu.rs`:** a key equivalent adds only its press, placed before its key-up when that key-up is already queued in the same frame. The real release comes from winit.
- **`shortcuts.rs` (`clipboard_keys`):** a ⌘V key press that reaches egui counts as the paste, so its release adds nothing. This covers the Mac menu's key equivalent and Shift+Insert on Linux. Any V/Insert release clears that mark.
  - This also fixes a related Linux/Windows case. If Ctrl was released before V after a text paste, the stale mark silently swallowed the next image paste.
- **`apps/photocraft/tests/mac_menu_appkit.rs`:** now expects only the key press.

## Tests

Each new or updated test fails without the fix and passes with it:
- `native_menu::tests::a_paste_key_equivalent_pastes_once`: ⌘V through the menu, then the real key-up, both in a later frame and in the same frame. Without the fix: 4 layers instead of 3.
- `shortcuts::tests::each_paste_key_is_one_press`: a ⌘V press and its release give one press; releasing Ctrl before V doesn't block the next image paste.
- `native_menu::tests::key_equivalents_run_through_the_normal_shortcut_path`: updated to expect one event.

title: fix(codecs): read the resolution from EXIF, XMP and Photoshop APP13; write it consistently (#1691)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1691.

## Reading

**JPEG:** the resolution now comes from, in order:
1. APP13 Photoshop ResolutionInfo (`0x03ED`)
2. XMP `tiff:X/YResolution`
3. EXIF IFD0 `X/YResolution` + `ResolutionUnit`
4. JFIF density

A JFIF segment with unit 0 (aspect ratio only) is never used. Adobe doesn't document this order; it follows Phil Harvey's observation of Photoshop on the exiftool forum (own resource → XMP/TIFF → EXIF, JFIF not used). It also matches the files: cameras write correct EXIF, while many tools write a default JFIF of 72.

**Other formats:** the format's own field still wins (PNG `pHYs`, TIFF tags). When it is missing, the decoder falls back to XMP, then EXIF. This covers WebP, HEIF, PNG without `pHYs`, and the other formats decoded through `image`.

**Parsing:**
- `ResolutionUnit` 2 = inch (also assumed when the tag is missing), 3 = cm (×2.54); 1 or anything malformed counts as no resolution.
- X/Y must each be one RATIONAL with a non-zero denominator. Both byte orders are handled, every offset is checked, and when a tag appears twice the first wins.

The D3200 file from the issue now reports 300 ppi (it was 72).

## Writing

JPEG, PNG (eXIf/XMP), WebP, TIFF (XMP), PSD and the Save for Web JPEG now write the image's resolution into the EXIF and XMP they carry:
- RATIONAL values are rewritten in place and `ResolutionUnit` is set to 2. Everything else stays byte for byte.
- An entry that can't be rewritten safely is removed from IFD0, without moving other data.

JFIF, EXIF and XMP now agree. Example: open the issue's file, set Image Size › Resolution to 240 with resampling off, save. exiftool then shows `[JFIF] 240` and `[IFD0] 240`, inches, with Make kept.

## Code

- New `crates/codecs/src/resolution.rs`: the readers and rewriters. It reuses the IFD0 reader of `orientation.rs` and has no workspace dependencies.
- `jpeg.rs`, `png.rs`, `webp.rs`, `tiff.rs`, `web.rs`, `lib.rs`, `crates/io/src/psd_export.rs`, codecs README.

title: Equalize, Average and Clouds edit the targeted channel, not the layer (#935)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #935.

`image.adjustments.equalize`, `filter.blur.average`, `filter.render.clouds` and `filter.render.differenceClouds` ran through `extra_cmds::map_pixels`. That function always rewrote the active layer and ignored the `"target"` that `Session::execute` injects from the Channels panel. With an alpha channel or the Quick Mask targeted, they changed the layer and left the channel alone.

## Change (`crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs`)

- `map_pixels` takes the params. When they target an alpha channel, the Quick Mask or the layer mask, it rewrites that grayscale surface through `channel_cmds::channel_surface_for_filter`, the way the core filters do (`filters.rs`).
- Its pixel loop already converts through `to_rgba`/`from_rgba_into` for the surface's own format, so the four commands' maths is unchanged.
- The layer path keeps its lock checks and locked transparency.
- Equalize and Average now pass their params through. Their registrations used to discard them.

## Test

`extra_cmds::tests::equalize_average_and_clouds_edit_the_targeted_channel` runs **all four commands on all three targets at 8, 16 and 32-bit** (36 cases):
- **Targets:** the Quick Mask and an alpha channel get their target injected by `Session::execute`, as in the app. The layer mask uses `"target": "mask"`.
- **Checks:** the layer is untouched, the target changed, there is exactly one history step, and undo restores the target.

Before the fix, the first case failed: Equalize left the Quick Mask unchanged.

## Gates (macOS arm64, Rust 1.95)

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --no-fail-fast`: all pass.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`: passes.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask wasm`: clean.

title: inspect: report each smart object's source
author: jmverges
body:
`info` / `document.inspect` list smart objects but not where their contents come from, so a script can't tell duplicates of one placed file from independent contents. PSD template checks need that, e.g. "every location in a mockup template has its own `art` smart object".

This adds `smartSource` to every smart object node, following the model:

- `{"kind": "embedded", "fileName": …}`
- `{"kind": "linked", "path": …}`: a file path after Place Linked or Relink, and for a PSD placed layer (embedded or linked in Photoshop) the `Idnt` uuid of its `lnk2` file. Duplicates share it; New Smart Object via Copy embeds its own copy and reports `embedded`.

Two embedded smart objects report only their file name, so they can't be told apart by it. That's out of scope here.

`docs/development.md` lists the new field next to the other `doc_inspect` fields.

**Validation**

title: Selective Color and Color Lookup: a wrong-typed key is an error (#936)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #936.

## Problem

`selective_from_params` and `lookup_from_params` (`crates/engine/src/adjust_cmds.rs`) read their keys with lenient `as_str` / `as_array` / `as_f64` / `as_bool`, so a wrong-typed key was dropped and the command returned `Ok`. `adjust_params` promises "a key of the wrong type is an error", and every other adjustment kind keeps that promise through `Reader`. Before this change, all of these succeeded:

- `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.selectiveColor {"method": 5, "reds": "not-an-array"}` made a relative layer with every range at zero.
- `{"colors": "reds", "cyan": "50"}` dropped the cyan value.
- `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.colorLookup {"lut": 42, "interpolation": 5, "dither": "yes"}` made an empty, trilinear, undithered layer.
- `layer.setAdjustment` with the same keys silently kept the layer's old values.

## Fix

Both parsers now read every key through small checked helpers (`given`, `opt_str`, `opt_bool`, `percent`). Any of the following is `BadParams`, and the message names the key:
- a key of the wrong type;
- a per-range array that isn't exactly 4 numbers (as `Reader::numbers` requires for Color Balance and Channel Mixer);
- an unknown `method`, `colors` or `interpolation` value (as Photo Filter does for an unknown `filter`).

Unchanged:
- `null` still counts as "not given", matching `Reader::get`.
- Numbers still clamp to -100..100.
- An empty `file` is still ignored, which the Image › Adjustments dialog relies on.
- The Properties panel and the dialog only ever send well-typed values, and their tests pass.

## Tests

`adjust_cmds::tests::selective_color_and_color_lookup_reject_wrong_typed_params` runs 18 bad keys (10 Selective Color, 8 Color Lookup):
- through `image.adjustments.*` and `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.*` at 8/16/32 bits in RGB, CMYK and Lab, checking for `BadParams` naming the key, no new layer, no history step and unchanged pixels;
- through `layer.setAdjustment` on an existing layer of each kind, checking that its values are untou…

title: View › Show › Target Path hides the path outlines (part of #1119)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Part of #1119: this fixes **View › Show › Target Path**. The issue's other flags are left for follow-ups (see the end).

## Problem

`show.target_path` had no reader outside `view_cmds.rs`, so View › Show › Target Path (and View › Extras) only flipped the checkmark. The canvas kept drawing:

- the active shape layer's path;
- a targeted vector mask's path;

title: Image › Adjustments: apply per tile in parallel (#1772)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1772 (the freeze). Running adjustments as background jobs, the issue's third suggestion, is left out; see the end.

## Problem

`adjust_surface` (`crates/engine/src/pixels.rs`) is the path every destructive `image.adjustments.*` command takes on a layer. It read the whole content bounds into one buffer and ran a serial per-pixel loop. On a 50 MP layer it held four full-size `f32` copies at once: the raw samples, the straight RGBA buffer, the original for the selection blend, and the encoded output.

## Fix

`adjust_surface` takes the tiles covering the content bounds (`Surface::take_tiles`, as `fill_cmds::blend_into` does) and runs the existing per-pixel code (`adjusted`) on each tile in parallel with rayon. It then puts the tiles back. Memory is now one tile's buffers per thread instead of four layer-sized copies.

The output is unchanged:
- Every tile is processed with its absolute coordinates, so selection sampling and position-keyed dither see the same pixels as before.
- Tiles inside the bounds that were never allocated are filled and processed, as the old `write_region` did.
- `take_tiles` returns every tile in the area, so no tile can be lost.

`adjust_mask` (masks and channel targets) is unchanged.

## Numbers

`large_image_bench --size 6336x7920 --op invert` (new op), release build, Apple M3 Pro:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Invert, 50 MP layer | 1095 ms | 106 ms |
| Invert, half-transparent layer (Layer via Copy of half the canvas) | 499 ms | 52 ms |
| Process peak RSS (open alone: 748 MB) | 2550 MB | 1470 MB |

## Tests

New `pixels::tests::tiled_adjustment_matches_one_pass_over_the_content` compares the tiled pass with the old single pass and requires bit-identical surfaces. It covers:
- 16 adjustment kinds, including dithered Gradient Map and Color Lookup, whose output depends on pixel position;
- RGB, CMYK, Lab and Gray at 8, 16 and 32 bits with alpha, plus RGB 8-bit and Gray 16-bit without;
- runs with no selection and with a soft sele…

title: fix(layers): Layers panel thumbnails of tall documents fill the thumbnail height (#1762)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1762.

The layer thumbnail texture is a letterboxed 64x64 square (`thumb_image`): the document is centred and the bars around it are transparent. `draw_layer_thumb` painted the checkerboard and the texture over the whole square cell, so on a tall document (e.g. 6336x7920) the transparent bars showed the light checker as white space left and right of the image.

Pixel-layer thumbnails now go through `channels_panel::fit_thumb`, the same helper the Channels panel uses: the image is drawn into the document-shaped part of the cell with the matching UVs, and the checker is painted only there, so the sides show the row background. The cell, its border and the badges stay as they were.

Scope: only pixel-layer thumbnails in the Layers panel. Square documents look the same; wide documents get the same treatment on top and bottom. Group, adjustment, text and fill thumbnails are unchanged.

Test: `layer_thumb_of_a_tall_document_fills_the_height` checks that a 100x400 document's thumbnail rect spans the full cell height, is a quarter of its width, and uses the matching quarter-width UVs.

title: Crop tool: Enter crops to the selection's frame (#1789)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1789.

**Why:** In Photoshop, if a selection is active when you pick the Crop tool, the crop frame starts at the selection's bounds, and Enter/Return crops the canvas to that frame. With no selection, the untouched frame covers the whole canvas and Enter does nothing. PhotoCraft treated every untouched default frame as a no-op, so selection → C → Enter did nothing.

**Change**
- `canvas::commit_crop`: an untouched default frame is a no-op only when it covers the whole canvas. A default frame taken from the selection now crops through the existing `image.crop` path, which deselects afterwards, as Photoshop does.
- This covers every commit path, since Enter and the options bar's commit button both go through `commit_crop`.

**Tests**
- New `crop_ui::tests::enter_on_the_selection_frame_crops_to_it_at_8_and_16_bit` (fails before the fix with `left: 200x100, right: 30x40`, passes after):
  - At 8 and 16 bit, selection → Crop frame → commit gives the selection's size, and the selection is cleared.
  - Committing the whole-canvas frame afterwards changes neither the size nor the history.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui crop`: all pass, including the existing `picking_the_tool_frames_the_canvas_or_the_selection`.

title: Rasterize Vector Mask keeps a feathered edge (#992)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #992.

## Problem

`layer.rasterize.vectorMask` multiplied the vector mask's raw path coverage (`vector_mask_values`, which ignores `feather`) into the pixel mask. The compositor draws each mask blurred by its own feather, and the pixel mask through its density (`masks::combined_mask`). So rasterizing a feathered vector mask hardened the edge: with an 8 px feather and no pixel mask, the flattened composite changed by up to **0.73** along the soft edge.

## Fix

When the vector mask is enabled and a feather on either mask, or the pixel mask's density, shapes the edge, the new pixel mask is now built from `combined_mask` over the canvas. That is the same effective mask the CPU compositor applies and the GPU path uploads. Those settings are baked in, so the new mask has feather 0 and density 1.

- Past the canvas, the mask keeps the old pixel mask's density-applied default, as the existing code keeps the old default there.
- Hard masks (no feather, full density) and disabled vector masks keep the existing path, which was already exact.

A side effect worth flagging: when the existing pixel mask had its own feather or density below 100%, those values are baked into its pixels rather than kept as editable settings. That's the only way the single mask left after rasterizing can show what both masks showed before. Tell me if you'd rather keep the pixel mask's own feather editable and accept a small appearance change in that case.

## Tests

`vector_cmds::tests::rasterizing_a_vector_mask_keeps_what_the_masks_show` flattens the document before and after rasterizing at 8, 16 and 32 bits. Cases:
- an 8 px feathered vector mask without a pixel mask;
- the same with a pixel mask;
- a 4 px feathered pixel mask;
- a 50% density pixel mask;
- both masks feathered, with 70% density.

Controls:
- hard vector mask, without and with a pixel mask;
- a disabled feathered vector mask over a feathered pixel mask.

The two composites must match within the rounding of the mask's storag…

title: Control: shell dialogs are listed and driven as "shell" (#1004)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1004.

## Problem

The shell's own dialogs live in `UiState::shell.dialog` (`workspace_ui.rs`):
- Window › Workspace › New Workspace and Delete Workspace;
- View › Pixel Aspect Ratio › Custom Pixel Aspect Ratio…;
- View › Show › Show Extras Options…;
- View › 32-bit Preview Options….

`ui.inspect` built `dialogs` from `app.ui.dialogs` only, and `ui.dialog.set` / `confirm` / `cancel` address that list by numeric id. So a shell dialog opened through `ui.menu.invoke` was invisible over control, and an agent couldn't fill it in, confirm it or cancel it.

## Fix

- `ui.inspect` lists the open shell dialog in `dialogs` as `{"id": "shell", "kind", "title", "fields"}`. At most one is open, since `shell.dialog` is an `Option`.
- `ui.dialog.set`, `ui.dialog.confirm` and `ui.dialog.cancel` accept `{"dialog": "shell"}`.
  - Confirm runs the automation authorizer on the dialog's command, as the numeric-id confirm does, then calls the new `workspace_ui::confirm`.
  - `ui.dialog.apply` on it returns an error pointing to `confirm`, since apply is Preferences-only.
- `workspace_ui::confirm` is the dialog's OK, now shared by the egui button and the control channel. It runs `dialog_command` through `menus::invoke`, closes the dialog on success, and keeps it open with the error otherwise, exactly as the button did. `workspace_ui::title` is extracted the same way.
- Numeric ids are unchanged, and `"shell"` can't collide with them.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` documents the id.

A string id was the smallest change that keeps existing numeric-id clients working. If you'd rather move the shell dialogs into `ui.dialogs` itself, I'm happy to rework it that way.

The org has 5 macOS slots in total on GitHub Team, shared across every repo's CI and release builds; PR CI kept them full, so release builds queued behind it (~750 macOS minutes/day of PR CI across PhotoCraft, PdfCraft and DeckCraft).

macOS is now built and tested only by `release.yml`. If a release fails on macOS, it is fixed and rebuilt. Linux and Windows CI are unchanged.

title: Dialogs: tall filter dialogs scroll; a moved dialog reopens in place
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1829. Two dialog problems found while testing the app (the first was also reported as #1829):

1. **Filter › Render › Flame doesn't fit a small window.** Its body is taller than the window, so OK and Cancel are cut off unless the app is maximized. In a 1000×560 window, OK sat at y≈974.
2. **Dialogs always open centred.** A dialog's position was kept per dialog *instance* in temporary egui memory, so every new opening started centred again. Photoshop reopens a dialog where you last left it.

## Fix

- **Fit:** the schema-built filter body (`filter_dialog::body`) now sits in a vertical `ScrollArea` capped at the window height minus the dialog's title, button row and frame (`DIALOG_CHROME`). Short dialogs look exactly as before. Custom dialogs (Layer Style, Preferences, Export, …), which manage their own scrolling, are untouched.
- **Position:** when a user drags a dialog, its offset is stored in egui's persisted memory under a per-command key (`("dialog-place", command)`, or the dialog kind for non-command dialogs). The next opening starts there. The existing first-frame clamp keeps it fully on screen if the window has shrunk since. A dialog never moved keeps opening centred, so a dialog that changes size doesn't reopen off-centre.

title: Filter dialogs: OK keeps the preview until the filter lands
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Found while testing the app (no existing issue): with **Preview** on, clicking **OK** in Gaussian Blur, Motion Blur or any other previewed filter dialog briefly flashed the *unfiltered* image before the result appeared.

## Cause

`dialogs::confirm` dropped the dialog's preview (`app.filter_preview = None`) and then ran the filter. In the desktop app, filters run as background jobs. Until the job finished, the canvas had no preview to show and drew the unchanged document.

## Fix

- `confirm` runs the command first. If that started a background job on the previewed document, it marks the preview `committing` instead of dropping it. Otherwise (inline runs, errors, other documents) it drops the preview as before.
- `canvas::committed_filter_preview` keeps showing a committing preview while that document's revision is unchanged and its job is still running.
- A job stays in the running list until `poll_jobs` applies it, and applying bumps the revision in the same call. So the hand-over from preview to result has no gap frame.
- A job that fails or is cancelled ends with the revision unchanged, so the preview is dropped and the untouched document shows.

When Low Resolution Previews is on, the held preview is the reduced proxy, the same image that was on screen before OK.

## Tests

`dialogs::tests::a_filters_preview_stays_on_screen_until_its_job_lands` (Gaussian Blur on a 256×256 document) checks three cases:
- **Background job:** after OK the preview is still shown, at full size; once the job lands, the revision has changed and the preview is gone.
- **Cancelled job:** the preview is gone and the document is unchanged.
- **Inline (no background jobs):** nothing is held.

On `main` it fails at "the preview is shown"; it passes with the fix. Checked by hand in the desktop app: Gaussian Blur and Motion Blur with Preview on no longer flash on OK.

## Checks

title: Removed 22 unit radius that doesn't exist in other Craft app icons
author: stevanmarjanovic
body:
PhotoCraft's Windows and Linux icons had squarer corners than VectorCraft, PdfCraft and the other Crafting Apps, both on the desktop and in the app bar.

All the apps share the same master tile: a 512-unit square with rx=112. But PhotoCraft's packaging/icons.sh cropped 22 units off each side before rendering the hicolor PNGs and the .ico, which cut into the rounded corners. VectorCraft renders the full tile, so its corners keep the full radius.

This PR removes the crop and regenerates the icons, so PhotoCraft's corners now match the other apps.

author: maxm11
body:
Fixes #1818

`u8::from_str_radix` accepts a leading `+`, so a hex pair like `"+5"` decoded as `0x05` instead of failing as corrupt hex. Now checks that both characters are ASCII hex digits before calling `from_str_radix`.

title: fix(app): exit with status 2 when --control setup fails (#1816)
author: maxm11
body:
Fixes #1816

When control authentication or the automation workspace cannot be configured, the app printed an error and returned `Ok(())`, exiting with status 0. A script that launched PhotoCraft with `--control` saw success even though no control server was running.

Now exits with status 2, matching the `--control` port parse failure path, so scripts can detect the failure.

title: fix(ui): horizontal ruler keeps ticks when View > Flip Horizontal (#1814)
author: maxm11
body:
Fixes #1814

With View > Flip Horizontal on, `ViewXform::to_doc` negates x, so the horizontal ruler's `(d0, d1)` came out reversed (d0 > d1) and the tick loop `while v <= u1` never ran — the ruler lost all its ticks and labels.

Now normalises to `(min, max)` before the loop, the same pattern `visible_doc_rect` uses for rotated views.

Adds a regression test that checks the normalised range is non-empty for both flipped and unflipped views.

title: Image Size reports the size it applied (#1815)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1815.

## Problem

With `resample: "none"`, `image.imageSize` changes only the resolution and ignores `width`/`height`. `resolution_only_change` and the #1544 test pin that contract. But the command returned the *requested* size anyway (`{"width": nw, "height": nh}`), so a caller sending `{"width": 999, "resample": "none", "resolution": 300}` was told the canvas was now 999 px wide when it hadn't changed.

## Fix

The result is now the document's size after the command. Behaviour is unchanged: Resample off still applies the resolution and ignores the pixel size, as the existing tests expect. The params doc now says what's returned and that `"none"` changes the resolution only.

I chose this over rejecting the call (the issue's other option) because the existing tests show the ignore-and-apply-resolution behaviour is intended.

## Tests

- `image_size_reports_the_size_it_applied` checks the result against the document after each of: a Resample-off call with a new size, width only, height only (aspect kept), explicit width and height with Resample off, and no params. It runs at 8, 16 and 32 bits.
- `resolution_only_change` now also checks its result is `{"width": 40, "height": 20}`.

Both fail on `main` and pass with the fix.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`: all pass.
- `panic_hunt --ignored`: passes.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- sizing`: 4 passed.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: nothing in the changed code. The `manual_range_contains` hit in `image_cmds.rs` is in the existing #1114 test.

title: feat(web): fetch Arabic craft-fonts beside the wasm
author: hamada147
body:
Related to https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts/pull/11

The web build no longer goes without craft-fonts. It still embeds none of them, because they would push the wasm over the 24 MiB size gate. Instead it fetches the faces listed in crates/text/web-fonts.txt from fonts/<sha16>/ next to the wasm. The browser checks each file against its SHA-256 (Subresource Integrity). Noto Sans Arabic loads before the app starts because the first frame needs it as a fallback. The other Arabic families (Cairo, Tajawal, Almarai, IBM Plex Sans Arabic, Amiri, etc.) load in the background, four at a time. If a face fails to load, the app logs it and runs without it.

- text: build.rs generates WEB_FONTS (URL and SRI) from web-fonts.txt and the craft-fonts manifest. A face missing from an older craft-fonts checkout is left out with a warning. A broken list is an error only with CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1, and it never costs the desktop build its craft fonts.
- text: the desktop build now also registers the Arabic craft fonts. Noto Sans Arabic is the fallback; the others are picked by name.
- text: FontDb::generation plus a lock-free global fonts::generation() change whenever fonts are added.
- ui-egui: the Type tool's family list and layout cache key on the font generation, so fonts that arrive later show up. The cached list doesn't wait on the text engine lock.
- packaging: copy-fonts.sh copies the listed faces into dist/web/fonts. It runs as a Trunk post_build hook. nginx, _headers and .htaccess serve the font files with long cache lifetimes. The Dockerfile takes craft-fonts as a named build context and gzips the fonts.
- docs: describe the Arabic web fonts in development.md and the web packaging README.
- contributors: add the people.toml entry for hamada147.

title: RAW: check the orientation range before narrowing (#1817)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1817.

## Problem

The five RAW readers (`dng.rs`, `cr2.rs`, `orf.rs`, `rw2.rs`, `tiffep.rs`) read EXIF orientation as `tag_uint(..).map(|o| o as u16).filter(|o| (1..=8).contains(o))`. `tag_uint` returns a `u32`, and the cast ran before the range check, so a LONG of 65538 truncated to 2, passed, and rotated the image.

## Fix

A shared `tiff::orientation(Option<u32>) -> u16` keeps the value only when the `u32` is in 1..=8 (then narrows it with `try_from`), and otherwise falls back to 1. All five readers call it.

## Tests

- `tiff::tests::orientation_is_range_checked_before_narrowing`: absent, 0, 9, 65537, 65538 and `u32::MAX` give 1, and 1..=8 pass through.
- `tests/dng.rs` `an_orientation_past_u16_is_not_truncated_into_range`: a synthetic DNG whose Orientation entry is rewritten from a SHORT to a LONG. A LONG 65538 now reads as 1; without the fix it read as 2 (`left: 2, right: 1`). Control: a LONG 6 still reads as 6.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-raw`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-raw --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo xtask wasm`: ok.
- `cargo xtask layers`: ok.

title: MCP: tool schemas without $ref, $defs or boolean schemas (#1782)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1782.

## Problem

Strict tool-schema validators reject the whole request if one tool uses a construct they don't support. The issue hit it with Moonshot Kimi-K3 via Volcano Ark, and notes OpenAI strict mode and some Gemini/Qwen endpoints are similar. Our `tools/list` had three such spots:
- `ui_pointer.properties.events.items`: `true` (schemars' schema for `Vec<Value>`);
- `command_batch.properties.steps.items`: a `$ref` into `$defs`;
- `command_batch`: the `$defs` themselves.

## Fix

- **`ui_pointer` events** get a concrete object schema through `#[schemars(with = "Vec<PointerEvent>")]`: `kind` (`down|move|up`), `x`, `y`, `pressure`, and the `tiltX`/`tiltY`/`rotation` a simulated pen sends to `ui.pointer`. It only affects the schema; events are still forwarded as JSON, so nothing changes at runtime.
- **`strict_schema`** runs once over every tool's input schema when the server is built (`with_backend`), so future tools are covered too:
  - `$ref`s are inlined (the use site's `description` wins over the definition's) and `$defs` is dropped;
  - any `true` in a schema position (`properties`, `items`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`, `not`, `prefixItems`) becomes `{}`;
  - inlining stops at a fixed depth, so a recursive definition can't loop.

## Tests

- `tests/mcp.rs` `tool_schemas_pass_strict_validators` lists the tools over a real MCP client connection and walks every tool's schema for `$ref`, `$defs` and boolean schemas. On `main` it reports exactly the three spots above; with the fix it reports none. It also checks the inlined shapes: an event has `kind`, `x`, `y` and `pressure`, and a batch step keeps its `id` description with the example ids.
- `command_ids_in_tool_schemas_exist` (#378) still passes: it now finds `command_batch`'s example ids in the inlined step schema.
- `server::tests::strict_schema_inlines_refs_and_stops_on_recursive_definitions` covers nested refs, use-site descriptions, `true` schemas, and a self-referencing defin…

title: Layers: a new empty layer no longer recomposites every layer (#1771)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1771.

## Why
Layer › New › Layer left the session's damage as "everything", so the canvas recomposited every layer over the full canvas after each new layer. Undo and redo of it did the same, because `step_damage` bailed on any change in layer count. The cost grew with layers × canvas. On a 6336×7920 document with full-canvas layers, the refresh after a new layer took 48 ms at 10 layers, 9.3 s at 100 and 24 s at 300. Photoshop adds a layer instantly at any layer count.

## Change
- `inert_at`: true for a layer that draws nothing wherever it sits. That means an empty pixel layer or empty group, in Normal or Pass Through, with no masks, effects or Advanced Blending, and not becoming the base of clipped layers above it.
- `layer.new.layer` and `layer.new.group` report empty damage when the new layer is inert. The check looks only at the new layer and its neighbour.
- `step_damage` pairs layers by id and steps over inert layers that only one side has, so undo and redo of a new empty layer refresh nothing. Every other structural change still gives a full refresh.
- `perf_scenarios`: new row "new layer in the many-layer document + refresh" as scenario P51 (16 ms p95, `enforce = false` until it has a baseline); scorecard regenerated.

After the change, the canvas refresh is about 0.03 ms at 10, 100 and 300 layers (was 48 ms, 9.3 s and 24 s). On the existing 150-layer perf document the new row went from 13.3 ms to 2.1 ms p50.

## Tests
- `new_empty_layers_and_groups_damage_nothing`: at 8, 16 and 32-bit, a new layer, its undo and redo, a new group and a new layer inside a group all report empty damage, and the composite is unchanged.
- `new_layers_that_change_pixels_still_recomposite_everything`: inserting a clipping base, a painted layer or a non-Normal layer still gives a full refresh.
- `damage_is_reported_for_strokes_only` now expects empty damage after a new layer.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`: lib 939 passed, all integration tests green.
- `cargo test -p…

title: GPU canvas: convert changed layer tiles once each, in parallel (#1774)
author: davidmann4
body:
> **Updated description:** this now covers both commits (87fc5f1f added the GPU-side tile copies); the numbers below are new.

Fixes #1774.

## Why
Select All + Fill on a 50 MP document is fast in the engine; the freeze comes from the GPU canvas refresh afterwards. For 16-bit layers, and any other non-RGBA8 format (CMYK, Lab, Gray, 32-bit), every changed tile was converted to Rgba16Float one after another on the UI thread. Every tile was then uploaded from the CPU on its own, even though a full-canvas fill shares one tile: 775 conversions and 387 MB of uploads per refresh, about 1.4 s per fill. In Photoshop the fill is effectively instant.

## Change
All in `crates/gpu`:
- **Convert each distinct tile once:** the layer-page sync groups changed tiles by identity and converts them in parallel batches of 64 (sequential on wasm, through the existing `fx::par_map`).
- **Upload a shared tile once:** a tile shared by several coordinates goes once into a scratch tile, then `copy_texture_to_texture` copies it to the other coordinates on the GPU. This covers solid fills, cleared areas (Delete) and non-zero defaults such as masks.
- **New layer pages** take the same path instead of assembling the whole page in a zeroed staging buffer. Filling a new layer grows its page, so this is the common case.
- **Faster 16-bit conversion:** 16-bit RGB and grayscale tiles convert to RGBA16F through a lookup table. The bytes are identical to the general path.

## Measurements
Release app over the control channel, 6336×7920, new layer, Select All + Fill, RTX 5070 Ti:

| | main | first commit | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16-bit fill | about 1.4–1.5 s | 88–133 ms | 15–19 ms |
| 8-bit fill | about 60 ms | 21–44 ms | 10 ms |

The main column is the first commit's earlier measurement of the time to the next frame. The other two columns are `perf.timings.compositeMs` (CPU time of the GPU refresh), measured the same way on both builds.

title: GPU parity tests: give the one-step tolerance f32 slack (#1848)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #1848.

## Cause
`crates/gpu/tests/parity.rs` compares the GPU render with the CPU compositor and allows a difference of one 8-bit step: `TOL = 1.0 / 255.0`. The limit has no room for f32 rounding. On NVIDIA (RTX 4080 SUPER, driver 615.71.09) `adjustment_layers` fails on every run: at the Hue/Saturation pixel (18,23) the premultiplied green values differ by `0.0039216876`, which is 1.00003 steps and 1.19e-7 (one f32 ulp) above `TOL`. RADV and lavapipe do not hit it.

## Fix
`TOL` is now `1.0 / 255.0 + 4.0 * f32::EPSILON`, about 0.0001 of a step. A real two-step error still fails. All three uses of `TOL` (the check in `diff_rect` and two `<= TOL` assertions) share the constant, and nothing else uses it. Test code only.

## Tests
`parity` on this branch, all 28 tests, on one Vulkan driver at a time (`VK_DRIVER_FILES`):

| Adapter | Before | After |
|---|---|---|

title: Canvas: edits that change no pixels (a lasso selection) don't recomposite (#1773)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #1773.

## Why
`Session::edit` reported "recomposite everything" for every edit, including edits that change no pixels. Committing a lasso selection on a 6336×7920 document therefore re-rendered all 50 MP. When the layers don't fit in the GPU memory budget that is a full CPU composite, and the frame after releasing the lasso took 2.4 s with 20 canvas-sized layers and 11 s with 105. A frozen frame right after one lasso is also when the next stroke gets sparse, coalesced pointer input. Photoshop never recomposites the image for a selection change.

## Change
- New `layer_multi_cmds::same_pixels(a, b)`. It uses the exhaustive pixel/non-pixel field classification that undo and redo already use through `step_damage`. Tiles are compared by pointer, no bounds are computed, and recursion stops at a depth bound, beyond which the edit counts as changed.
- `Session::edit` reports empty damage when `same_pixels(before, after)`, and full damage (`None`) otherwise. Commands that set their own damage afterwards are unaffected.
- This covers every pixel-neutral edit: selections, guides, paths and layer names.
- Adds `crates/ui-egui/examples/lasso_bench.rs`, the offscreen harness behind the numbers below. It drives the real `PhotocraftApp` with a spiral lasso drag. Options: `--size --moves --layers --full --selection --zoom --render`.

Frame after a lasso commit (6336×7920, release, offscreen):

| Layers | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 20 canvas-sized (CPU path) | 2,400 ms | 5.7 ms |
| 105 canvas-sized | 11 s | 6 ms |
| 4 (GPU path) | 17–34 ms | 4–6 ms |

## Not included: why this is only "part of"
- The drag frames themselves measured flat: 0.3–0.9 ms of app logic at any document size and layer count, and `lasso_ui` is O(1) per event. On the reporter's PSB, something this synthetic document doesn't have may still make frames slow, for example text, smart objects or effects. Profiling that file with `lasso_bench` is the next step.
- Even with fast frames, Windows coalesce…

title: camera_raw_scope: serialise the GPU tests with GPU_LOCK (#1855)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #1855.

## Cause
On a machine with the NVIDIA and lavapipe Vulkan drivers both installed, `camera_raw_scope` crashed with SIGSEGV in about a third of the runs, inside `libvulkan` (`vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties`, called from `wgpu::Instance::new` through `egui_kittest`). Its three GPU tests build harnesses on separate test threads at the same time. The other GPU test binaries either take a process-wide `GPU_LOCK` (`canvas_16f.rs`, `gpu_device_loss.rs`, `device_loss.rs`, `parity.rs`) or have one GPU test. This file had no lock. The measurements and the driver matrix are in #1855.

## Fix
`camera_raw_scope.rs` gets the same `GPU_LOCK` and `gpu_lock()` as `canvas_16f.rs`. `both_clipping_warnings_leave_unclipped_preview_pixels_visible_on_gpu`, `curve_gpu_paints_the_moved_handle_in_every_theme` and `pixel_hover_gpu_badge_single_band_and_crosshair_appear_and_clear_in_all_themes` hold it for their whole run, harness included (the guard is declared first, so it drops last). The other 18 tests in the file do not touch the GPU and still run in parallel. Test code only.

## Tests
`camera_raw_scope`, default loader configuration (NVIDIA, RADV and lavapipe all visible), same machine and commit, running the compiled test binary in a loop:

| | Runs | SIGSEGV |
|---|---|---|
| Before (no lock) | 60 | 20 |
| After (this PR) | 60 + 40 | 0 |

`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --test camera_raw_scope` passes (21 tests) on this branch, as does `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`, with Rust stable 1.98.0.

I audited the other GPU test binaries too: 18 binaries in `crates/gpu/tests` and `crates/ui-egui/tests`, 15 runs each in the default configuration. Only this one crashed, so the others are unchanged here. `parity` fails on NVIDIA for a different reason (#1848, fixed in #1852).

title: Fix browser Save for Web downloads and stale export dimensions
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Fixes #1700.

Save for Web (Legacy) now sends browser exports through the platform download service, including slice images, the spacer GIF and HTML. The engine shares its existing encoder through a writer callback; native exports retain their command/filesystem path. Browser HTML references the downloaded images as sibling files. Authorization is checked before a deferred picker, moved selections are committed before encoding, and write errors reach the status bar.

Reopening the dialog keeps encoding choices while starting at the current document's full dimensions. Estimate-only calls and failed exports no longer replace the last successful export settings.

In the browser, verified a downloaded **60 × 40 PNG** from a 120 × 80 image at 50%, then a second 240 × 160 document reopening at 100%. Verified both slice PNGs, spacer GIF and HTML actually downloaded and all HTML image references loaded. The browser used PhotoCraft's automatic CPU fallback after an unrelated GPU pipeline error.

title: fix(engine): preserve edited layouts before applying layer comps
author: 0x6Ason
body:
After a Layer Comp is created or applied, ordinary layout edits leave `last_applied_comp` set. Applying a comp again then skips the Last Document State backup, so the edited layout cannot be restored.

Compare the live layout with the last applied comp before applying another comp. Changes to recorded visibility, position or appearance now refresh the backup; cycling or reapplying unedited comps keeps it. Capture flags and absent properties in imported comps are respected. The comparison runs only when applying a comp, with no new scans during normal painting and no persistence changes.

Fixes #919.

Regression coverage:

- The original undo/redo test now follows the real user path; it no longer clears `last_applied_comp` manually.
- Movement, visibility, opacity and blend edits independently at 8/16/32-bit depth, then apply and restore.
- Repeated comp cycling and replacing a stale backup with a later edited layout.
- A visibility-only comp does not overwrite the backup because of position/appearance differences it intentionally leaves unchanged.

- Passed: direct rustfmt on both changed Rust files and `git diff --check`.

title: New Document starts from the last document's settings (#1810)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1810.

## Problem

File › New always opened at 1920 × 1080 and 72 ppi. Photoshop starts the dialog from the settings of the last document made with it. The issue's other request, the clipboard image's size, already works on `main` through the Clipboard preset (#891).

## Fix

- OK remembers the dialog's `width`, `height`, `resolution`, `mode`, `depth`, `background` and display units (`__unit`, `__resUnit`) in the preferences, under `dialogs["file.new"]`. This is the same place Fill keeps its last choices.
- `PhotocraftApp::new_document_fields` lays them over the defaults. Each value is validated, so a corrupt preference falls back field by field.
- The name, the preset and the clipboard size aren't remembered.
- An image on the clipboard still sets the size through the Clipboard preset, applied after the remembered values.
- A failed Create remembers nothing.

The code is in `lib.rs` and `dialogs.rs`, with the tests in a new file, so it doesn't touch `new_doc_ui.rs`, which open PR #527 is changing.

## Tests

`new_doc_remember_tests`:
- The first dialog is exactly the defaults.
- After creating a 640 × 480, 300 ppi, CMYK 16-bit, transparent document shown in inches, the next dialog starts from all of those (the name goes back to "Untitled-1"). The values are stored in the preferences, so they survive a restart.
- With an image on the clipboard, the size comes from the clipboard and mode and depth are still remembered.
- Corrupt remembered values (negative width, text resolution, depth 7, numeric mode) fall back to the defaults, while a valid height is used.
- A failed Create leaves the remembered values unchanged.

Without the remembering, the second dialog shows width 1920 instead of 640. The existing `new_doc_ui` tests, including the clipboard preset test, still pass.

title: Free Transform: edge handles scale proportionally, ⇧ stretches one axis (as Photoshop CC 2019+)
author: kuvshin888
body:
## Problem

In Free Transform (⌘T), dragging a **side (edge) handle** always stretches the layer along one axis, and **⇧ does nothing** on an edge handle. There is no way to resize from a side without distorting the image, and the key Photoshop users reach for has no effect.

Photoshop CC 2019 and later scale proportionally from any handle while *Maintain aspect ratio* is on (the default), and ⇧ toggles to non-proportional scaling. From Adobe's help page [Transform images, shapes, and paths](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/crop-resize-transform/resize-adjust-resolution/transform-images-shapes-and-paths.html): ⇧ while transforming toggles proportional and non-proportional scaling, and to scale non-proportionally you turn *Maintain aspect ratio* off and then drag "a corner or a side handle". PhotoCraft already does this for corners (`transform_tool.rs`: "corner drag scales proportionally (⇧ for free)"); edges were left out.

## Change

| Gesture on an edge handle | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| drag | stretches its one axis | scales proportionally: the opposite edge's handle stays put |
| ⇧ + drag | stretches its one axis (⇧ ignored) | stretches its one axis |
| ⌥ + drag | one axis, about the reference point | proportionally, about the reference point (as corners do) |
| ⌥⇧ + drag | one axis, about the reference point | one axis, about the reference point |

- The dragged edge sets the scale of its axis; the other axis follows by the same factor about the middle of the box. Dragging past the opposite edge flips only the dragged axis.
- **Preferences › General › Use Legacy Free Transform** keeps edges stretching their one axis whatever the keys, as Photoshop did before CC 2019. Corners keep their swapped ⇧, unchanged.
- Unchanged: corners, ⌘-edge skew, the Skew / Distort / Perspective modes, and the Type tool's own transform (it maps edges to skew).
- `corner_mods` is renamed `legacy_mods`, since it now covers edges too. `docs/ui-design.md` and the module …

title: Web: fonts served next to the app, loaded on demand (fonts/manifest.txt, craft-fonts format)
author: kuvshin888
body:
Part of #1615 (it adds the "serve font files next to the wasm and fetch them lazily" half); related to #1135.

## Problem

1. **The web build can't have more fonts than Inter and JetBrains Mono.** A browser offers no system fonts, embedding more would push the wasm over the 24 MiB gate, and nothing can add a font at run time. `crates/text/build.rs` already says the web build keeps no Japanese font "until craft-fonts can be served next to the wasm instead of inside it". A host that embeds PhotoCraft can't give its users the fonts they work with.
2. **A variable font shows only one style.** Most Google Fonts are variable. The style menu lists the faces the database reports, and a variable font reports only its default instance: Montserrat offers just "Thin" and "Thin Italic", although the layout draws any weight its `wght` axis covers. This affects desktop too (any installed variable font).

## Change

### 1. Fonts served next to the app, loaded on demand

To connect fonts, a host puts them next to `index.html` and lists them in `fonts/manifest.txt`, **in craft-fonts' own manifest format**, so a craft-fonts checkout is already a valid font folder and any other font is one line:

```text
site/
├── index.html, photocraft-web-….js, photocraft-web-…_bg.wasm
└── fonts/
    ├── manifest.txt
    ├── montserrat/Montserrat[wght].ttf, Montserrat-Italic[wght].ttf, OFL.txt
    └── lobster/Lobster-Regular.ttf, OFL.txt
```

```text
# family | style | file (relative to the site root) | scripts | licence | licence file | sha256 | source
Montserrat | Regular | fonts/montserrat/Montserrat[wght].ttf | Latn,Cyrl | OFL-1.1 | fonts/montserrat/OFL.txt
Montserrat | Italic | fonts/montserrat/Montserrat-Italic[wght].ttf | Latn,Cyrl | OFL-1.1 | fonts/montserrat/OFL.txt
Lobster | Regular | fonts/lobster/Lobster-Regular.ttf
```

- At start the web shell fetches `fonts/manifest.txt` (a few KB). **No manifest (404): nothing changes**, so existing deployments are untouched.
- Served families are lis…

title: fix(engine): reject invalid new-document parameters

title: Crop tool: rotate the crop frame by dragging outside it (#1792)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1792

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11f861fc-f2b0-457c-ab89-4fc3ce9160a2


## Why
In Photoshop (and Affinity Photo, Pixelmator), moving the pointer just outside the Crop box shows a curved rotate cursor; dragging rotates the crop, Enter rotates the document by that angle and crops to the box, and Esc cancels. PhotoCraft drew a new frame instead, and `image.crop` had no angle.

## Change
- `image.crop` takes an optional `angle` (degrees, clockwise on screen, the frame turned about its centre): the document is rotated with Image Rotation › Arbitrary so the frame is upright, then cropped to it, as one undo step ("Crop"). Handles resize along the turned frame's axes (opposite edge fixed), moving still translates, ↵ commits with the angle, Esc / a new frame starts upright. As in Photoshop, a new frame is drawn after committing or cancelling the pending one.

The shield, thirds and handles draw for a turned frame (also under a rotated/flipped view), and the beyond-canvas preview reaches its corners. No snapping while turning or moving a turned frame.

title: raw: decode Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3 and 4 (vendor-compressed)
author: Gotya-OFFCIAL
body:
PhotoCraft opens Panasonic RW2 files whose sensor data is vendor-compressed (PanasonicRaw RawFormat 4, e.g. the DMC-GX7) from the camera's embedded JPEG preview — a 1920×1440, 8-bit stand-in — with the warning `RW2: Panasonic RW2 raw format 4 (vendor-compressed) is not decoded yet`. This adds a clean-room decoder for the vendor-compressed RW2 stream (RawFormat 3 and 4), so those bodies open at full sensor resolution.

## What the format does

Established by observation of sample files (every step verified by decoding whole frames and comparing against the camera's embedded JPEG, the recorded levels and the borders):

* The payload at RawDataOffset is a fixed-rate stream: 16 bytes per 14 pixels, so a row occupies `width / 14 * 16` bytes and rows are byte-aligned.
* Bits are consumed downward from the top of each 0x4000-byte page, addressed through the same page split the RawFormat 5 stream uses (`(i + 0x4000 - 0x2008) % 0x4000`); fields are read LSB-first from the little-endian 16-bit word at the cursor.
* Pixels arrive in groups of 14 with two predictors carried from one group to the next (even and odd columns). Every third pixel carries a 2-bit scale selector `sh` (0, 1, 2 or 4). The first value of each parity is absolute (8 + 4 bits); the rest are 8-bit deltas around 0x80 scaled by `sh`, wrapping in its low bits.
* The decoded samples sit 15 counts above the recorded BlackLevel tags (measured on the darkest pixels of sample files); the black level is read with that offset.

## Changes

* `crates/raw/src/rw2.rs` — RawFormat 5 is untouched; RawFormat 3/4 decode through a new bit cursor (`Bits`) and a per-row group decoder, run in the same parallel bands. The +15 black offset is applied to the compressed variants. Module docs describe the layout.
* `crates/raw/src/testgen.rs` — `rw2_format4` synthesizes RawFormat 4 files (a mirrored writer deposits each field where the decoder reads it), like the existing `rw2` does for RawFormat 5.
* `crates/raw/tests/vendor_codecs.…

title: Schema dialogs ignore notes after a spec; Selective Color's OK works again
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
**Regression fix:** on current `main`, OK in **Image › Adjustments › Selective Color…** fails with "`reds` must be an array of 4 numbers [c, m, y, k]". The cause predates it, but my #1790 (merged today) turned it into an error. Sorry about that.

## Cause

`filter_dialog::parse_spec` read a command's whole params doc as parameters, including notes after the `{…}` object. Selective Color's spec ends `… "reds":json} (per-range [c,m,y,k] arrays: reds yellows …)`. The note did two things:
- it glued itself onto `"reds"`, so `"reds"` parsed as a **number** field instead of hidden JSON;
- its commas split off a junk field, `"k] arrays"`.

So the dialog showed both a "Reds" and a "K] arrays" number box, and sent `reds: 0`. The old Selective Color parser silently ignored that; since #1790 a wrong-typed key is a `BadParams` error, so OK and the live preview fail.

## Fix

`parse_spec` reads only the spec's leading object. A small `object_body` finds its closing brace, aware of strings and nested brackets, so notes and `→ {…}` results after it are ignored. This also removes a hidden junk field from Image › Mode › Color Table, and the parser is safe for future specs with notes.

## Screenshots

Image › Adjustments › Selective Color…, rendered offscreen with `--example snapshot`:

| Before: junk "Reds" and "K] arrays" fields | After |

| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kayrockscreenprinting/photocraft/bbc13955dd2ddfeb53c6858d4fd8ac5cdb3fbf2a/selective-color-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kayrockscreenprinting/photocraft/bbc13955dd2ddfeb53c6858d4fd8ac5cdb3fbf2a/selective-color-after.png) |

title: Canvas: the CPU canvas pixel grid skips empty pixels, like the GPU canvas
author: Jeremy8776
body:
**Problem.** #1491 made the GPU canvas draw the pixel grid only over pixels with content. The CPU fallback (no usable GPU) still draws a full lattice across empty checker above 500%.

**Fix.** `pixel_grid.rs` gives the CPU path the shader's rule:
- Each pixel owns its left and top edge, so the document's right and bottom edges carry no line.
- A transparent pixel gets no line. A dark pixel gets a white line at 25% strength, a light one a black line at 64% of that, scaled by alpha, as in `gpu_canvas.rs`.
- The grid is built from the composite of the part of the document in view. Runs of equal colour merge into one segment, so an opaque region costs one segment per line, and the total is capped at 60,000.
- Segments are cached per document revision, preview and padded region (snapped to 64 px), so panning inside the padding costs nothing and the work is bounded by the viewport at 500% or more, never by the document.
- The threshold and strength are shared constants, so the two paths cannot drift apart.

**Tests.**
- 14 unit tests in `pixel_grid.rs`: colour rules, merging, the segment cap, short buffers, region snapping and cache reuse.
- Two offscreen render tests in `tests/checker_canvas.rs` on the CPU canvas (the harness now builds the app with or without wgpu): at 600, 800 and 1200% the grid lines are 1 px, spaced by the zoom, at about 64 over black. Over empty checker the pixels are identical with the grid on and off. I checked that the second test fails if transparent pixels are given a line.
- Run locally: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib pixel_grid`, `--test checker_canvas`, clippy for the crate with `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`. I did not run `cargo xtask wasm` locally; CI covers it.

**Known difference.** Where two grid lines cross on the CPU path the pixel is lightened twice (about 112 instead of 64). The previous CPU grid did the same.

title: Filter previews compute off the UI thread; a stale one is cancelled once the slider settles
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Found while testing the app (no existing issue): with **Preview** on, dragging **Gaussian Blur**'s radius toward 1000 px made the window unresponsive. Every filter's live preview except Indexed Color (#1741) ran inline in the canvas draw, so each slider step blocked the frame until that blur finished.

## Change

- **Every filter preview runs on the worker.** With background jobs (the desktop app), all previews go through the `filter_preview_worker` that #1741 added for Indexed Color: one at a time, latest request wins. The frame never waits on a filter. Web, tests and `PHOTOCRAFT_INLINE_JOBS` keep the deterministic inline path (#1676).
- **Stale previews can be cancelled.** Each preview gets a `JobCtx`. `Worker::supersede` cancels a running preview for older values **once the dialog's values have been unchanged for 150 ms** (`SETTLE_MS`). Closing the dialog cancels it too.
  - While a slider is still moving, the running preview finishes and is shown, so the canvas keeps updating during the drag.
  - When the slider stops, an outdated slow preview (a 1000 px blur) stops at its next check instead of holding up the final value.
  - My first version cancelled on every slider step, which meant no preview finished until the slider stopped. The settle delay fixes that.
- **Engine:** `Session::set_inline_job_ctx` runs inline job work under a caller's context. `filter_dialog::preview_document_with` sets it on its private session. Filters already pass their `JobCtx` to the algorithms' checks (`ctx.stage` → `apply_in_with(..., ctl)`), so nothing in the filters changed.

Checked by hand in the desktop app (macOS): dragging Gaussian Blur's radius up to 1000 px keeps the window and slider responsive, updates the preview during the drag, and settles quickly when the drag stops.

## Tests

title: SVG import: refuse deeply nested markup instead of overflowing the stack
author: syd168
body:
## Summary
- An SVG with ~6 000 nested `<g>` elements (70 KB) aborts PhotoCraft with a stack overflow: `roxmltree::tokenizer::parse_element ↔ parse_content` recurse once per nesting level, and the overflow hits before usvg's node limit. A stack overflow is an abort, not a panic, so neither the desktop crash guard nor the MCP/CLI guards can catch it; on the web the tab dies. 2 MB worker-thread stacks die at ~6 000 levels, the 8 MB main thread at ~20 000.
- `crates/io/src/svg.rs` now pre-scans the markup and rejects nesting past `MAX_XML_DEPTH = 512` with an `IoError::Svg` before the parser runs. The scan skips comments, CDATA, processing instructions and the DOCTYPE, and honours quoted attribute values (`>` / `/>` inside quotes).
- `.svgz` can't be scanned compressed, so the importer inflates it itself with a `MAX_INFLATED_BYTES = 128 MB` cap and hands plain XML to usvg. Side effect: a gzip decompression bomb (1.5 MB → 1.5 GB of whitespace, previously 1.57 GB RSS) is refused too. `flate2` moves from dev-dependency to dependency of `photocraft-io`; usvg already pulls it in, so no new crate in the tree.

- [x] New `deeply_nested_markup_is_an_error_not_a_stack_overflow` runs 8 000 levels (plain and gzipped) on a 512 KB stack; on the previous code the test process aborts with "has overflowed its stack", with the fix it passes. Just under the limit still opens.
- [x] New `the_depth_check_skips_comments_cdata_doctype_and_quoted_markup` and `svgz_is_inflated_with_a_size_cap` (valid svgz opens; >128 MB bomb and corrupt gzip are errors).

title: raw: cRAW black level without a tag; measured image areas (D800E, ILCE-7)
author: Gotya-OFFCIAL
body:
PhotoCraft renders the first-generation cRAW bodies (an ILCE-7 — and the A7R/A7S of the same generation) washed out: they write no BlackLevel tag (`0x7310`), so the black level falls back to 0 and the develop carries the 512-count pedestal of the cRAW tone curve into the frame. On a real file that is a flat band — luma p5..p95 = 63..89, against the camera JPEG's 30..117 — with no real blacks. Both bodies also decode their full sensor data, including border pixels the camera's JPEG does not contain.

## Changes

* `crates/raw/src/tiffep.rs` — a cRAW file with no BlackLevel tag gets the black level of its tone curve's black code: 512. The curve's first segment maps code 256 to 512 for any knots (see `src/sony.rs`), and the files' own dark pixels sit on a 512 floor. Files that do write the tag are unchanged; the "assumed 0" warning no longer fires for tag-less cRAW.
* `crates/raw/src/cameras.rs` — an image area can now be measured without a full profile. A small table records the areas measured so far — **Nikon D800E** `(8, 6, 7360, 4912)` of `7424 x 4924` and **Sony ILCE-7** `(12, 12, 6000, 4000)` of `6048 x 4024` — and `apply` crops to it, leaving levels, colour and tone untouched. Both origins are even, so the Bayer phase of the crop is unchanged.
* Tests — a cRAW file whose BlackLevel tag is renamed (hidden) decodes with black 512 and no warning; the image-area table applies by make + model + size only, and only to what was measured.

* **Black level**: the cRAW tone curve maps the black code (256) to 512 for any knots — the first segment is `code × 2` — and the two real ILCE-7 files have the darkest 0.01% of their samples at 510–518: a 512 floor, not 0.

title: No windows ink pressure issue + responsive stylus right click
author: siraxe
body:
## Brush Preset picker: pen right-click opens on press, not release

Fixes the flaky pen barrel-button right click: the picker often didn't appear and had to be spammed (isolate of the press-to-open part of #943).

### Problem

The picker opened on `Response::secondary_clicked()` — egui's "click" needs a clean press **and** release with total movement under the click distance. A pen barrel tap jitters a few pixels, and a pen user naturally holds the barrel while choosing a preset, so the release rarely counted as a click.

### Fix

Open on the press itself (`button_pressed(Secondary)`):

- `canvas_buttons`: press-to-open for the picker; Alt-resize, ⌘/Ctrl layer menu and the Erase preference keep owning the right button as before.
- `show_picker`: the outside-press close skips the one press that opened the picker (`brush_picker_open_press`), so it can't close in the frame it opened.
- `pointer_secondary` (automation path) sets the same flag; new `brush_picker_open_press` field on the app.

### Pen input paths on Windows (context)

Which path the pen takes depends on the Wacom driver's **"Use Windows Ink"** checkbox (read at startup from `%APPDATA%\WTablet\Wacom_Tablet.dat`, the application scope matching this executable, else "All" — `photocraft_tablet::wacom::load`; `PHOTOCRAFT_WINTAB=1`/`=0` forces either way):

- **Ink off (Wintab)**: the driver stops sending pen frames through `WM_POINTER` and synthesizes the mouse itself — the barrel arrives as a real right click. The Wintab reader (`crates/tablet/src/wintab.rs`) only carries pressure/tilt into the `StylusFeed`; the right click needs nothing special from us. This fix is what makes it reliable: the click is acted on at press time instead of depending on a jitter-free release.
- **Ink on (default)**: the pen reaches winit as an emulated touch and its buttons are dropped entirely — no right click reaches the app at all. That needs the `WM_POINTER` window subclass from #943 (`crates/tablet/src/windows.rs` + `pointer…

title: Paste: drop a stale image once the OS clipboard has moved on
author: jason4short
body:
When the OS clipboard no longer held an image (text or a non-image file was copied since, or a format we can't read), the session kept the image we had last mirrored to or imported from it. Paste then pasted that stale image, and the New Document dialog's Clipboard preset showed its size.

`import_os_clipboard` now drops that image once the OS clipboard has moved on, so Paste reports nothing to paste, as it does for an empty clipboard. An image copied only inside the app (when there is no OS clipboard service, or mirroring failed) is kept. Covered in `os_clipboard_bridge`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
