title: fix(ui): correct percentage grid spacing and snapping on rectangular canvases
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Addresses #1876.

Percentage-based grid spacing used the document width for
both horizontal and vertical intervals.

On rectangular documents, this produced square grid cells
instead of proportions based on each document dimension.

Grid snapping also used a single interval, potentially causing
snapped positions to disagree with the intended grid.

## Root Cause

Grid rendering calculated its major spacing using the document
width and reused that value when drawing both axes.

The snapping engine similarly represented grid spacing as a
single scalar rather than independent horizontal and vertical
intervals.

## Changes

### Grid Rendering

- Calculate horizontal and vertical grid intervals independently.
- Use document width for vertical gridline positions.
- Use document height for horizontal gridline positions.
- Apply subdivisions independently to each axis.
- Preserve existing spacing behavior for absolute units.
- Apply low-zoom visibility thresholds independently per axis.

### Grid Snapping

- Support independent X/Y grid spacing in SnapOptions and SnapTargets.
- Update point snapping and rectangle snapping to use the
  appropriate interval for each axis.
- Share percentage-grid spacing calculations between rendering
  and snapping.

### Regression Coverage

Add tests covering:

- Percentage spacing on a 1280×720 document.
- 20% major spacing with two subdivisions.
- Independent X/Y snapping intervals.
- Point and rectangle snapping to rectangular grids.
- Preservation of equal spacing for absolute pixel units.
- Grid spacing derived from the configured preferences.

Expected subdivision intervals for the reported example:

- X-axis: 128 px.
- Y-axis: 72 px.

## Files Changed

- crates/engine/src/snap.rs
- crates/ui-egui/src/rulers.rs
- crates/ui-egui/src/snap_ui.rs

## Validation

Implementation and regression tests have been committed.

Verified:
- Branch exists on the contributor fork.
- Three intended files changed.
- Cross-fork GitHub compari…

title: Fill layers keep their colours in the document's mode (#1905)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1905.

## Problem

In a Grayscale or CMYK document, a new fill layer showed its colours as plain RGB: a blue Color Fill was blue on the canvas, in `document.pixel`, in previews and in `.pcraft` saves of a `Gray/8` document. Flattening, exporting or a PSD round trip then gave the converted grey, so what you saw was not what you got.

A fill layer's colours are meant to be in the document's colour model (`Color` is documented as "a colour value in the document's model", and Image › Mode converts fill colours that way). The commands that create fill layers stored the RGB colour from their params or the swatches as is, so the compositors (CPU and GPU, both through `Color::to_rgb`) drew it unconverted.

## Fix

- `Color::in_mode(mode)`: a colour in another mode's model, converted the way pixels written to a surface of that mode are (`rgb_to_gray`, `rgb_to_cmyk`, `srgb_to_lab`), so a fill layer matches the same colour painted with Edit › Fill. Indexed and Multichannel keep RGB colours, as `to_rgb` reads them.
- `Fill::in_mode(mode)` applies it to a solid colour or every gradient stop (patterns are pixels, untouched).
- Every path that creates or recolours a fill layer stores its colours in the document's mode:
  - Layer › New Fill Layer › Solid Color and Gradient;
  - the Gradient tool's live gradient fill layers (`gradient.fill.create`);
  - gradient fill edits (`gradient.fill.set` / `gradient.fill.stop`);
  - Gradients panel presets (`gradient.presets.apply`, and `gradient.presets.select` on a selected gradient fill).
- The Gradient tool's on-canvas preview of an edit converts the same way, so it shows what the command commits.

RGB documents are unchanged (their colours stay RGB). Lab documents already looked right, but now also store Lab colours, so a later Image › Mode change converts them like any other colour.

## Tests

`crates/engine/src/fill_layer_mode_tests.rs`, at 8, 16 and 32 bits:

- a Solid Color fill layer composites exactly like Edit › Fill with th…

title: Grid: a percent grid has rectangular cells on non-square documents (#1876)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #1876.

## Cause
A grid spacing in percent took the document's **width** as 100% on both axes. `GuidesGridAndSlices::major_px` returned one number, and both `rulers::draw_grid` and `snap_ui::options` passed it `doc.size.width`. On a 1280×720 document, "every 20%" gave 256 px squares instead of 256 × 144 px cells, and Snap To Grid used the same square step. The rulers were not affected: they already take percent per axis.

## Fix
- `major_px` returns `[across, down]` (width for the first, height for the second). Pixels, inches, cm, mm, points and picas give the same value on both axes, as before.
- `SnapOptions.grid_step` and `SnapTargets.grid` carry that pair, so Snap To Grid snaps x and y to their own steps (`SnapTargets::grid_step(vertical)`).
- `rulers::grid_lines` picks the line positions per axis, and an axis whose lines would be closer than 6 screen px at the current zoom gets none (it used to be skipped for both axes together).
- An unusable step (zero, negative, NaN, inf) turns grid snapping off instead of dividing by it.

## Tests
Three of the new tests fail on `main` with the same numbers as the issue (`[256.0, 256.0]` instead of `[256.0, 144.0]`):

| Test | Checks |
|---|---|
| `prefs::percent_grid_spacing_is_per_axis` | `major_px` for 20% on 1280×720, other units unchanged, degenerate sizes stay positive |
| `rulers::percent_grid_cells_follow_the_document_aspect` | 4 + 4 major lines, 9 + 9 with subdivisions 2 (10 columns × 10 rows) |
| `snap_ui::percent_grid_snaps_to_rectangular_cells` | a marquee on a 400×300 document snaps to 40 × 30 steps, not 40 × 40 |
| `rulers::grid_lines_skip_an_axis_that_is_too_dense` | per-axis skipping; zero, NaN and zero-zoom inputs draw nothing |
| `snap::grid_steps_differ_per_axis`, `snap::unusable_grid_steps_are_ignored` | per-axis point and rectangle snapping; bad steps never divide |

Checked by eye with the offscreen `snapshot` example: a 1280×720 document with "every 20%" and 2 subdivisions shows 10 columns and 10…

title: PSD export: pattern fill layers keep their pattern in CMYK and Lab (#1907)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #1907.

## Problem

A Pattern Fill layer in a CMYK or Lab document came back empty after a PSD (or layered TIFF) save and reopen.

PSD export writes a fill layer's rendered pixels next to its fill descriptor, but rendered them with no patterns (`render_fill_content(l, f, canvas, &[])`), so a pattern fill was always written as transparent pixels. On import, a fill layer whose record has pixels keeps them as its rendering (`fill_cache`, "Photoshop's own rendering"). In RGB and Gray, transparent pixels equal the surface default and prune away, so the record was empty and the pattern was re-rendered live. In CMYK and Lab, transparent black converts to non-default channel values (rich black; Lab's neutral a/b), so the tiles were kept, and the reopened layer drew that transparent rendering.

Other readers that composite the stored layer pixels would also have seen an empty layer.

## Fix

The PSD exporter keeps the document's patterns and renders pattern fills from them (`psd_export.rs`, also used for layered TIFF). The stored pixels are now the pattern in the document's format, as for solid and gradient fills.

## Tests

`crates/io/tests/pattern_fill_psd.rs`: a Pattern Fill with an RGB checkerboard (like the default patterns), in RGB, Grayscale, CMYK and Lab at 8, 16 and 32 bits, saved as PSD and as a layered TIFF and reopened. The layer is still a pattern fill, and the composite matches the pattern stored in the document's pixel format (max difference below 0.02). It fails on main. Lab is skipped for TIFF, because Lab documents are saved as a flat TIFF (with a warning).

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-io`; clippy on the changed files; `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo xtask wasm`.

## Note: live rendering in Gray and CMYK

The expected value is the pattern converted to the document's mode (an RGB pattern is grey in a Grayscale document, as Edit › Fill paints it), because that is what the saved file holds. The live compositor still draws an RGB pattern in colour in a G…

title: feat(android): add Android runner with mobile UI, multi-arch CI, and input support
author: krinry
body:

This PR adds native Android runner support for **PhotoCraft** using `eframe` with `wgpu` (GLES fallback) powered by `android-activity`. It includes phone-first adaptations, touch & pointer interactions, in-app file browsing & saving, brand launcher assets, and a multi-architecture CI build pipeline.

---

### 1. `apps/photocraft-android` Runner

title: PSD import: warn when an adjustment layer can't be read (part of #1763)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Part of #1763 (the warning; the reporter's actual Color Lookup parse failure needs their file to diagnose, and this warning will say what it is).

## Problem

When a PSD or PSB adjustment layer's settings can't be read, the importer keeps the block verbatim as `Adjustment::Unsupported`, so it saves back unchanged, but the layer renders as nothing. That happened silently: the layer opened without its effect and with no message. `parse_lookup` also discarded why a Color Lookup failed.

## Fix

- `adjust_map::read_lookup` returns the reason a `clrL` block can't be read:
  - the block is truncated;
  - an unknown version;
  - unreadable settings (the descriptor error);
  - it uses a colour profile (abstract or device link), not a LUT file;
  - empty LUT data;
  - its CUBE/3DL/LOOK LUT can't be read (the parser's error).
  
  `parse_lookup` is unchanged in behaviour (`read_lookup(d).ok()`).
- `adjust_map::label(key)` (menu name of the adjustment) and `adjust_map::unreadable_reason(key, data)`.
- `psd_import`: an adjustment layer that comes in `Unsupported` adds a warning, for example:

  > layer "Teal Look": its Color Lookup settings could not be read (it uses a colour profile (abstract or device link), not a LUT file, which isn't supported yet); the layer is kept as saved but has no effect

  This covers PSD, PSB and layered TIFF, which share the importer.

Out of scope: oversized LUTs dropped by the GPU plan (#1113), and the parse failure itself.

## Tests

- `crates/io/tests/adjust_warnings.rs`:
  - an unreadable Color Lookup layer warns once, naming the layer, the adjustment and the reason, after a PSD and a PSB round trip;
  - an unreadable Levels layer warns without a specific reason;
  - a readable Color Lookup and an Invert open with no warning.
  
  The warning test fails on main.
- `adjust_map::color_lookup_synthetic_block` checks each reason.

title: fix(compose): apply Curves master before per-channel tone records
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Addresses #975.

Levels and Curves previously composed their master and
per-channel tone records in opposite orders.

Levels applied the master record before the channel record,
while Curves applied the channel record first.

This caused equivalent tone adjustments to produce
different output pixels.

## Changes

- Apply the Curves master LUT before each per-channel LUT.
- Align Curves with the existing Levels composition order.
- Preserve Lab behavior, where the master record is ignored.
- Update the composition documentation.
- Add regression coverage for equivalent Levels and Curves
  adjustments.

## Validation

Added a regression test covering:
- Unrounded tone LUTs.
- 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit processing.
- Rendered pixel output through the compositor.
- Lab master-record behavior.

The tests have not yet been executed because the current
environment does not have the Rust toolchain.

Before submission, run:

cargo test -p photocraft-compose
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo xtask test-corpus

The composition order should also be checked against a
Photoshop reference document before claiming Photoshop parity.

## Issue

Addresses #975.

title: codecs: PNG export gives the same bytes on any core count
author: rossaai
body:
## What it does

`parallel_idat` in `crates/codecs/src/codecs/png.rs` split the rows into `available_parallelism() * 4` bands, and a one-core machine used the serial `png` writer instead. Each band is deflated on its own, so the band split decides the bytes. The same image with the same options therefore gave different PNG files on machines with different core counts. The decoded pixels were equal.

This change:

- gives every band a fixed 512 KiB of filtered rows (`BAND_BYTES`), whatever the thread count
- moves the band work into `banded_idat(.., threads)`, which `parallel_idat` calls with the machine's thread count
- runs the banded path on one worker on a one-core machine, instead of returning `None`

## Why it matters

With one output per input, an export can be compared with an earlier one by its hash, cached by hash, and tested against a stored file. We exported one document with `photocraft-cli` on macOS arm64 with 10 cores and in a Linux arm64 container. Inside the container, `available_parallelism()` returned the CPU quota, 3. The filtered scanlines were equal and the deflate streams were not.

## Size and speed

Two 7200x4500 RGB images, made by tiling `docs/images/photocraft-demo.jpg` and `docs/images/photocraft-filters.jpg` 3 by 3, encoded through `photocraft_codecs::encode` from a release build:

| image | level | bytes before | bytes after |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| demo | Fast | 16,243,694 | 16,251,866 |
| demo | Default | 11,786,961 | 11,806,100 |
| filters | Fast | 14,382,089 | 14,386,071 |
| filters | Default | 12,603,747 | 12,620,883 |

The files are 0.05 % to 0.16 % larger. The timings were measured on a shared 10-core machine with a load average between 20 and 37, so they show no clear difference either way. Best of 5, in two rounds: Default took 0.229 to 0.315 s before and 0.213 to 0.301 s after, Fast 0.132 to 0.167 s before and 0.138 to 0.185 s after. The timing program was a scratch binary and is not part of this change.

title: Fix #1905: convert a fill layer's colour to the document's colour mode
author: switch87
body:
A fill layer's colour is authored in RGB, but every layer's pixels live in the
document's colour model: a raster layer's surface is `doc.pixel_format()` and is
read back through `to_rgba` (a Grayscale document's luma, a CMYK document's inks,
quantised to the document's depth). Our own fill rendering (`compose::render_fill`)
skipped that, so a solid blue fill layer in a Grayscale or CMYK document composited
its raw RGB. Only the live canvas was wrong: flatten, PNG/PSD export and a
save/reopen converted it (the PSD export already did — `io::psd_export::fill_pixels`
writes through a `Surface` of the document format).

- New `compose::fill_pixels_to_document_model`: converts RGB fill pixels through the
  document's model (Grayscale luma, CMYK inks via the document profile, Lab) and
  quantises to the document depth, exactly like reading a surface of that format.
  Cached fills are already converted, so unchanged.
- Applied to the CPU fill buffer (`render_content`) and, with the same function, to
  the GPU fill's uniform colour and gradient ramp (`gpu::plan`), so both compositors
  agree.

Verified headless: `#0000ff` in a Gray/8 document is now `0.113725…` (was `[0,0,1]`),
CMYK/8 `[0.223, 0.169, 0.518]`, matching `layer.flattenImage` and `edit.fill`.

Tests: `compose::tests::fill_layer_colour_converts_to_the_document_mode`; GPU parity
now drops a solid fill into the Grayscale and CMYK documents (`gpu/tests/parity.rs`).
compose 173, gpu parity 28 all green; clippy and `xtask layers` clean.

Known limitation (unchanged by this PR): gradient fills convert per pixel on the CPU
but the GPU converts its 4096-entry ramp, so the two differ by the existing LUT
approximation; no parity case covers a gradient in a non-RGB document yet.

Fixes #1905.

title: Brushes: decode imported tips on demand, not at start (#1843)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1843.

**Why.** On start, the brush preset store decoded every imported tip at full resolution, and each tip was then held twice: once in the session's library and once in the store's snapshot of the last sync. A 600-brush library with large 16-bit tips (2.27 GB decoded) cost about 4.5 GB after import and after every restart. Memory now grows with the brushes in use, not with the size of the library.

**Change**
- **photocraft-paint:** new `StoredTile` (key, size, small preview, and the full bitmap once loaded), used by `TipShape::Stored` and `Pattern::Stored`.
  - Rendering uses the full bitmap when it is loaded, otherwise the preview.
  - A loaded stored tip serialises as `sampled`, so tool presets, actions and `brush.get` JSON are unchanged.
  - New `GrayTile::preview` (at most 96 px, box filter, deterministic).
- **Preset store:**
  - Group files record each tip's size and preview (`tips`, `#[serde(default)]`).
  - Opening the store reads previews only. Groups that have been written drop their presets' full bitmaps.
  - Full tips are decoded when a brush is used (picking a preset, strokes, export) and kept in a 256 MB LRU cache.
  - Stores written before this change get their previews made once at the next start, 8 tips at a time, and are rewritten.
- **Errors:** a missing, corrupt or unknown tip returns an error when the brush is used, never a panic.
  - **Behaviour change:** before, a group with a broken tip was skipped at start with a warning. Now the error appears when that brush is used.
- **UI:** the Brushes panel, the picker and Brush Settings draw the stored previews. The tip grid and the "current brush" check match stored tips by key.
- **Tools** (manual only, not run by tests):
  - `crates/io/examples/gen_abr_library.rs` generates a redistributable ABR v6 test library from our own procedural tips. By default that is 600 brushes with 800–2000 px 16-bit tips in 7 files, about 525 MB.
  - `crates/engine/examples/abr_memory.rs` is the memory harness…

title: Patterns paint in the document's colour mode (Gray, CMYK)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Follow-up to #1907 (and the pattern counterpart of #1905).

## Problem

In a Grayscale or CMYK document, a Pattern Fill layer or Pattern Overlay made from an RGB pattern showed in colour. That applies to every built-in pattern and to any pattern defined in an RGB document. The compositors (CPU and GPU) drew the pattern's pixels as they are. What you saw then disagreed with:
- Edit › Fill with the same pattern, which converts as it writes the document's pixels;
- the flattened or exported result;
- the PSD written since #1917, which stores the fill's pixels in the document's mode.

## Photoshop's behaviour (checked by hand)

In a Grayscale document, Photoshop shows an RGB pattern in colour in the Fill dialog's picker but fills in grey. Converting the document back to RGB brings the colours back: patterns keep their own colours and are converted when painted.

## Fix

Patterns are converted when painted, not stored converted:
- `photocraft_compose::pattern::pattern_rgba(pattern, mode)`: a pattern's pixels as they look painted into a document of `mode`. In Grayscale, Bitmap, Duotone and CMYK documents, a pattern in another mode is projected through that mode (`from_rgba` then `to_rgba`, the same conversion Edit › Fill's write and read-back go through). Other modes (RGB, Lab, Indexed) are unchanged.
- CPU: `PreparedPatterns` carries the document's mode (`in_mode`), and its tiles (`Tile::new_in`) use `pattern_rgba`. This covers pattern fills, Pattern Overlay, pattern strokes and bevel textures. `Tile::new` keeps its RGB behaviour for Edit › Fill, brushes and the Pattern Stamp, which convert as they write pixels.
- GPU: the compositor records the document's mode per encode, and `pattern_view` uploads `pattern_rgba` (the cache key includes the mode).

The library and the document's copy of a pattern are never changed, so Image › Mode to Grayscale and back to RGB keeps the pattern's colours.

  - `pattern_fills_paint_li…

title: Fix/zip deflate unbounded limit
author: shmuelbiller1
body:
Fix two issues in PhotoCraft's `.pcraft` ZIP reader that could cause excessive memory allocation or integer overflow when processing specially crafted or malformed archives.

The changes improve the reliability and safety of opening ZIP-based PhotoCraft projects, including archives compressed using DEFLATE.

## Problem

### 1. Excessive memory allocation from untrusted ZIP metadata

Previously, the DEFLATE reader used:

```rust
let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(e.uncompressed);
```

The `uncompressed` value comes directly from the ZIP archive's central-directory header.

A malicious or corrupted ZIP file containing only a small amount of compressed data could falsely claim an uncompressed size of several gigabytes.

This could make PhotoCraft attempt a massive memory allocation before checking the actual decompressed content.

### 2. Integer overflow when reading with an unlimited size limit

The decompression code also used:

```rust
.take(max as u64 + 1)
```

When `max` is `usize::MAX` on a 64-bit system, adding one overflows.

Depending on the build configuration, this can cause a panic or an incorrect decompression limit.

## Changes

- **Safer decompression:** Remove the initial allocation based on the untrusted ZIP header. The output buffer now grows as data is decompressed.
- **Overflow protection:** Replace the size-limit addition with `saturating_add(1)`.
- **Preserved integrity checks:** Continue validating decompressed length and CRC-32 against the archive metadata.
- **Minimal scope:** Limit the changes to PhotoCraft's ZIP reader without altering the project file format.

## Regression Tests

Added a regression test that:

1. Constructs a valid DEFLATE-compressed ZIP entry.
2. Verifies the entry can be read using `usize::MAX`.
3. Verifies normal exact-size reads work.
4. Checks that too-small size limits are rejected.
5. Forges a ZIP entry claiming an uncompressed length of `u32::MAX`.
6. Verifies the forged entry returns a corruption error without reserv…

title: Crop tool: a pending crop stays with its document (#1918)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1918. Part of #1919.

## Why
A pending crop frame was global UI state. After File › New, File › Open, switching tabs or closing the document, the first document's crop box was drawn over whichever document became active, and ↵ cropped *that* document to it.

## Change

It runs from `sync_views` (every frame and after every command), before the canvas makes its default frame, and at the start of `commit_crop`, so ↵ can never crop another document.
- In tiled views the frame is drawn only on its own document's tile.
- While a crop is pending (drawn, moved, resized or turned; not the untouched default frame the tool shows), the menus Photoshop greys are greyed until the crop is committed or cancelled (`crop_ui::blocks`, in `menus::is_enabled` for the menu bar and shortcuts, and in `menus::modal_allows` for the native menu and `ui.menu.invoke`). This follows the item-by-item check in Photoshop 27.11 in the review comment below, and agrees with a check in Photoshop 25.1 (New, Open and Image greyed; nothing greyed for the untouched default frame). What stays available:
  - File: Close, Save, Save As, Save a Copy

title: Crop tool: arrow keys nudge, X swaps orientation, W × H readout (#1919)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #1919 (Crop tool: Photoshop parity, "Keyboard and feedback").

Builds on #1879 (crop rotation, now merged); main is merged in, so the diff is only this change.

## Why
Photoshop's Crop tool nudges a pending crop box with the arrow keys, swaps it between portrait and landscape with **X**, and shows the box's size beside the pointer while you draw or resize it. In PhotoCraft the arrows didn't move the crop box, X always swapped the colours, and there was no size readout.

## Change
- With the Crop tool and a pending frame (no gesture in progress), the arrow keys move the frame 1 document px (⇧ 10 px) instead of the selection or layer. A turned frame moves on the page and keeps its angle. title: ui: Panels::rail and Panels::menu_bar let an embedding app hide the icon rail and the menu bar
author: rossaai
body:
## What it does

Adds two fields to `state::Panels`:

- `rail`: the right dock's icon rail. `right_dock` draws it only when this is on. The dock groups stay, and `dock` still hides the whole dock.
- `menu_bar`: the title bar with the in-window menus. `PhotocraftApp::ui` calls `panels::title_bar` only when this is on.

Both default to `true` and carry `#[serde(default = "yes")]`, so saved settings without them load with both on. `ui.set` accepts them like the other panel flags, because its known keys come from the serialized state:

```json
["ui.set", {"panels": {"rail": false, "menu_bar": false}}]
```

Hiding the title bar hides everything `panels::title_bar` draws: the menus, the brand mark, the document title, the workspace switcher, the search, theme and Discord buttons, and the free gap that drags the window and maximizes it on a double-click. Where PhotoCraft draws its own title bar, on Windows and Linux, its caption buttons go too. The edge resize zones stay.

## Why an embedding app needs it

An app that embeds PhotoCraft's egui UI can switch between a simple view and the full view by setting `app.ui.panels`, `app.ui.dock` and `app.ui.tool`. The toolbar, options bar, status bar, every dock group and the whole dock (`dock`, ⇧Tab, #1388) already have a flag. `dock` hides the dock groups and the rail together. The icon rail alone and the title bar had no flag, so a simple view that keeps some dock groups kept them too. An embedding app that draws its own bar also gets a second menu row.

There is no menu item for either flag. They are state for an embedding app or an agent to set, like `toolbar_double`.

title: Layers panel: the scroll wheel over the blend-mode menu steps through the modes
author: skraus2
body:
The scroll wheel over the Layers panel's blend-mode menu steps to the next or previous mode, as in Photoshop. PhotoCraft took the arrow keys (#1318) but ignored the wheel.

- Wheel down picks the next mode, up the previous one, one per notch, stopping at the first and last mode like the arrow keys. Shift+wheel steps one mode too (no ×10 as on the sliders).
- Each notch is its own `layer.setProps`, so Undo goes back one notch, also when one wheel event carries several notches.
- Notches add up like the sliders' wheel (`wheel_notches`), so high-resolution wheels and touchpads step once per full notch.
- Groups step through their list with Pass Through first. The Background layer's greyed dropdown ignores the wheel.
- While the pointer is over the dropdown, the wheel no longer scrolls the Layers panel.

`widgets::dropdown_wheel_hovered` is an opt-in variant of `dropdown_hovered`; every other dropdown keeps ignoring the wheel.

**Open list.** The issue asks for this "open or closed". Over the open list the wheel used to scroll the list and change nothing. It now steps the mode like over the button; the list stays open and follows the chosen mode instead of scrolling by the wheel's delta. After a wheel step the canvas shows the chosen mode, not the entry under the resting pointer, until the pointer moves to another entry. I asked about this in the issue and haven't heard back, so it is a separate commit; happy to change it if you'd rather have the open list scroll.

title: fix(compose): knock out outer glow behind see-through fill
author: shmuelbiller1
body:
## Fix Outer Glow rendering through transparent layer fills (#1953)

### Problem
PhotoCraft incorrectly renders Outer Glow effects on Photoshop layers with **Fill set to 0%**. Instead of keeping the layer's interior transparent, the glow can fill the entire shape with a solid color, obscuring the artwork underneath.

This causes significant visual differences when importing Photoshop PSD/PSB files, particularly in UI designs, illustrations, and layered artwork.

### Root Cause
The CPU compositor correctly handles transparency knockout for Drop Shadow effects but does not apply equivalent behavior to Outer Glow.

The GPU rendering path has the same omission, allowing the glow to appear inside transparent shapes.

### Solution
- Fixed Outer Glow compositing to respect layer fill transparency.
- Updated both CPU and GPU rendering paths for consistent behavior.
- Reused existing knockout logic to avoid unnecessary complexity.
- Preserved exterior glow effects without filling the transparent interior.
- Maintained normal rendering behavior for fully opaque layers.

### Regression Tests
Added tests covering:
- Outer Glow with 0% Fill.
- Softer and Precise glow techniques.
- Preservation of underlying background colors.
- Correct exterior glow visibility.
- Normal behavior with 100% Fill.
- GPU knockout behavior at 0%, 40%, and 100% Fill.

### Impact
Improves Photoshop compatibility and prevents unwanted visual artifacts when opening and rendering PSD documents containing transparent shapes with layer effects.

**Fixes #1953**

title: Quick Selection: Photoshop's behaviour, measured and fitted
author: Unemars
body:
**Problem.** Quick Selection behaved nothing like Photoshop's. It modelled the stroke's colours, sampled a background behind geodesic edges and flooded everything similar. Its own test shows it: an 80 px drag inside a textured disc of radius 180 px had to select the whole disc (IoU > 0.93). Photoshop, given that very image and stroke, selects only about the stroke (5,285 px; the disc is ~100,000).

**How Photoshop behaves.** Measured on Photoshop 25.4 as a black box. No Photoshop code or assets were used.
- **Method.** I drew synthetic images and stroked them in Photoshop, then read back the exact masks: the selection was stored in an alpha channel and the document saved as Photoshop RAW.
- **Images.** 77 synthetic cases, 3 from this crate's tests, and 25 cases on public-domain paintings from Wikimedia Commons: *Girl with a Pearl Earring*, Ansel Adams' *Tetons and the Snake River*, Monet's *Water Lilies* (1906), *Earthrise* and Hokusai's *Great Wave*.
- **Repeats.** Every case was run three times, holding the button for 1 s. Photoshop keeps computing while the button is down: a 50 ms click can end with an unfinished, smaller result. Results that two runs agree on are used.
- **Determinism.** Away from a threshold, reruns are bit-identical. At a threshold either outcome occurs (a 230 px square: one run in three).

| | Photoshop |
|---|---|
| Brush footprint | always selected, whatever colours it covers |
| Click, 30 px brush, red on blue square | 220 px whole, 240 px only about the brush |
| Same, white on black / 40-level step / 15-level step | 224 yes, 232 no / 182 yes, 200 no / 94 yes, 104 no |
| Brush size | 10 px: 134 yes, 146 no; 60 px: 300 yes, 340 no. The side grows about as √radius: a constant cost per selected pixel |
| 400 px bars | 40 to 120 px wide whole, 160 px not. Clicked 30 px from the end: only the end, cut just past the brush. A 20 px neck doesn't stop it |
| Click 20 px inside a 200 px square's edge | about the brush: the disc runs along the cheap…

title: fix(retouch): sample Proximity Match from original pixels
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fix a source-buffer correctness issue in Spot Healing's
Proximity Match implementation.

Previously, Proximity Match copied translated source pixels
using `copy_within` on the same output buffer being modified.

When translated source and destination regions overlap,
later pixels can sample earlier modifications instead of
the original image.

This can produce repeated values and streaks in the
healed result.

## Changes

### Immutable Source Sampling

- Introduce a dedicated proximity-source copying helper.
- Read all translated source pixels from the original image.
- Write results into a separate destination buffer.
- Prevent earlier repairs from contaminating later samples.

### Bounds Safety

- Validate image dimensions and channel counts.
- Validate translated source coordinates.
- Use checked arithmetic for coordinate calculations.
- Return an invalid result rather than reading outside
  the source region.
- Fall back to content-aware filling when a translation
  cannot be applied safely.

### Regression Tests

Added tests covering:

1. Overlapping source and destination regions.
2. Preservation of original source pixels.
3. Multi-channel image copying.
4. Pixels outside the repair mask remaining unchanged.
5. Invalid negative translations.
6. Extreme coordinate values.
7. Invalid image dimensions.

## Example

Original values:

10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60

Repair positions 1–3 using source pixels one position
to the left.

Expected:

10, 10, 20, 30, 50, 60

The earlier implementation could instead propagate
previously copied values through the output.

## Files Changed

- crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs
- crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds/tests.rs

title: fix(inpaint): bound proximity-match search radii to image dimensions
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Improve robustness of the inpainting proximity-offset search
when given extreme or invalid search parameters.

The existing `best_offset` implementation uses a caller-supplied
search radius and ring size.

Very large values can create unnecessarily expensive searches
and potentially overflow signed integer calculations.

This change bounds those parameters using the actual image
dimensions and avoids integer overflow in distance scoring.

## Changes

### Search Radius Validation

- Clamp the search radius to the image extent.
- Reject zero and negative maximum search radii.
- Cap the radius before constructing search ranges.
- Avoid searches over offsets that cannot be useful
  for the supplied image.

### Ring Validation

- Bound the ring size to the image extent.
- Prevent oversized unsigned values from truncating
  into invalid signed coordinates.
- Preserve normal ring behavior for valid inputs.

### Distance Calculation

- Replace signed integer squared-distance arithmetic
  with floating-point `hypot`.
- Avoid overflow from `dx * dx + dy * dy`.
- Preserve the existing preference for nearby sources.

### Regression Tests

Added coverage for:

- Extremely large search radii.
- Extremely large ring sizes.
- Zero and negative search radii.
- Returned translations remaining within image bounds.

The existing proximity-offset matching tests remain in place.

## Files Changed

- crates/algo/src/inpaint.rs

title: Fix #1918: a pending crop belongs to the document it was drawn on
author: switch87
body:
The crop frame lives in the global `UiState::crop_rect`, and `crop_ui::ensure_frame`
only cleared the *untouched default* frame when the active document changed. A frame
the user drew kept `crop.default_frame == false`, so nothing tied it to a document: it
stayed active, was drawn over whichever document became active next, and pressing Enter
cropped that document to the old box. File › New, File › Open and switching tabs all
landed there.

Photoshop treats a pending crop as modal and blocks those commands; cancelling the crop
first is the same outcome, and it is what the issue asks for ("a pending crop belongs to
the document it was drawn on. It never shows on or applies to another document").

`CropState` gains `frame_doc: Option<DocId>` — the document the current frame belongs to,
set while a frame exists. `ensure_frame` compares it (by document id, not tab index) with
the active document and, on a change, cancels the pending frame; the new document then
gets its own fresh default frame, so committing does nothing until you draw again.

Verified: new `crop_ui::tests::a_pending_crop_does_not_leak_into_another_document` (draw a
frame, add a second document, it becomes active: the frame is gone and the new document
has its own default frame; committing it crops nothing). crop_ui 14 tests green; clippy
`-D warnings` and `xtask layers` clean.

Not in this PR: *blocking* the commands Photoshop blocks during a pending crop (rather
than cancelling on switch) — the issue notes that list still needs checking against
Photoshop.

Fixes #1918.

title: DNG: deflate compression 8 with the TIFF predictors
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Adobe DNG Converter's **default** output — compression 8 (zlib streams) — now decodes.
Previously every deflate DNG answered "Deflate-compressed (floating-point) DNG is not
supported", which put the largest practical DNG share behind an error.

Each tile decompresses against the sample count its geometry declares, so a decompression
bomb cannot grow past the declared tile and a stream that comes up short is an error;
12/16-bit samples unpack through the existing paths; **predictor 1** (none) and
**predictor 2** (horizontal differencing, undone per channel per row, wrapping at 16 bits)
are handled. Predictor 3 (floating-point) and lossy DNG (34892) keep their explicit
unsupported errors.

## Tests

`testgen` grows `DeflateStrips` (delta + zlib via flate2 — the pure-Rust backend
`photocraft-psd` already uses), so the oracle runs in **every** CI without the corpus:
round trips at 12 and 16 bits, both byte orders, LinearRaw (3 samples), with and without
predictor 2 — each against the exact sensor samples — plus a cut-zlib-stream hostile case.

## Note on Sony WB

The branch name carries the research this PR grew out of: the RX0's as-shot white balance
lives in a MakerNote 0x2010 block whose offsets are **unknown even to ExifTool** ("unknown
offsets or values for DSC-RX0/…"), and the candidate offsets we tested (documented Tag2010
offsets, two plausible triples) were disproven against the embedded camera JPEG's channel
means. Sony as-shot WB stays open until a second sample or a reverse-engineered table
shows the layout; findings are recorded so the search can resume.

title: Canvas: zoom is physical at any display scale (#1943)
author: maxm11
body:
Fixes #1943.

## Why

The canvas mapped one document pixel to one egui point at zoom 1.0, so it rendered at
`pixels_per_point` times the chosen zoom: on a 125% display the 100% setting showed 125% (and
Fit, Actual Pixels, cursors, overlays and scrollbars were all off by the same factor).

## Change

`View::zoom` now means **device (physical) pixels per document pixel**, matching its
documentation, and every canvas geometry conversion goes through the new
`PhotocraftApp::canvas_ppp()` / `point_zoom()` (`ctx.pixels_per_point` stored once per canvas
frame):

- `ViewXform` and the GPU `ViewParams` (the shader's device scale is now exactly the view zoom).
- Pan and zoom-about anchoring, so the point under the pointer stays put.
- `fit_view` / `fill_view` / Fit Layer(s) on Screen / Fit Artboard (point-sized areas × ppp).
- Scrollbars, navigator viewport rectangle, preset coordinate mapping, brush/handle/cursor radii,
  the stroke smoothing `zoom` param, and the marching-ants step.
- Every screen-point hit tolerance (`current_zoom()` → `point_zoom()`).
- The GPU pixel-grid threshold now compares physical scale like the CPU path
  (`pixel_grid::shows_at` gets points × ppp; after rebasing onto #1891).

`ui.set zoom` keeps its meaning: 1 = 100% = one document pixel per physical display pixel.

## Verification

Offscreen `snapshot` example (wgpu), 800×600 at `--scale 2`, 200×100 document, `view.actualPixels`:
the white document measures **400×200 physical px before, 200×100 after** in the PNG. The
before/after captures were taken on the same machine with the branch stashed/unstashed.

title: Appearance modes: sync with system, separate dark and light themes
author: luniiya
body: ## What I like having apps on my computer follow the system's light or dark mode, and PhotoCraft didn't have that, so this PR adds it :) Adds an Appearance Mode to Edit -> Preferences -> Interface: Sync with system, Dark or Light. - Separate light and dark theme cards with editor previews, so you pick one theme for each mode. If the system gives no answer, it falls back to Dark. The header button: - The header appearance button cycles Auto -> Light -> Dark, with a monitor, moon or sun icon. - Existing saved single-theme preferences migrate to a fixed Dark or Light mode with their chosen theme. ## Testing - `cargo test -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft`: 2381 passed, 0 failed - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`: clean - Regression tests for the preference migration in `crates/engine/src/prefs/tests.rs` - Scorecard regenerated

title: gpu: write F32_MAX exactly so the compositor shader builds on WebGPU
author: joe2643
body:
## Problem

Since #1722, the web build can't use the GPU compositor on WebGPU. Right after New Document it shows "Switched to CPU rendering" ("GPU error; using the CPU renderer").

`compose.wgsl` line 156 declares `const F32_MAX: f32 = 3.40282347e38;`. That decimal is slightly above `f32::MAX` (3.4028234664e38):
- naga, used by native wgpu and by the WebGL path, rounds it down, which is why native tests pass.
- Chrome's WebGPU compiler (Tint) rejects it: `error: value 340282346999999984391321947108527833088.0 cannot be represented as 'f32'`.

With `pc_compose` invalid, every compositor pipeline is invalid too. The first logged error is only `[Invalid RenderPipeline "fs_content"] is invalid due to a previous error`. The real error is swallowed because, on WebGPU, `first_error`'s error scopes are popped before the error arrives. I found it by hooking `GPUDevice.popErrorScope` and `GPUShaderModule.getCompilationInfo` in the page.

## Fix

`const F32_MAX: f32 = 0x1.fffffep+127f;` is `f32::MAX` bit for bit, the value naga already produced, so native output is unchanged. A new test, `shader_float_literals_fit_f32`, checks that every decimal float literal in the shader is within f32's finite range. Without the fix it fails on line 156.

## Checked

- `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu`: all pass, including `shader_validates` and the GPU compositor tests. `clippy -D warnings` and `fmt --check` pass.
- Chromium 153 with WebGPU on an AMD RDNA3 GPU: every shader compiles without errors. New Document, Add Noise and Gaussian Blur run without a GPU error. Help › System Info shows `Backend: webgpu (other)` and `Image compositor: GPU`.
- v0.5.0 predates #1722 and is unaffected.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Menus: a submenu with every item disabled is disabled too (#1976)

body:

title: Keyboard Shortcuts: import Photoshop .kys sets; first launch takes Photoshop's live set (#1163)
author: texjer
body:
TLDR:

Photoshop keyboard shortcut sets come across: Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts gets an Import Shortcuts… button that loads a `.kys`, opening or dropping a `.kys` does the same, and at the first launch on a desktop with Photoshop installed its live set is imported on its own, so Photoshop hands work here from the start. Covers the ".kys" line of #1163.

## Reading the set

A `.kys` (Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts › Save Set in Photoshop) is XML: `<command kind="static|dynamic" name="Gaussian Blur...">` rows with one or more `<shortcut>Control+Opt+Cmd+G</shortcut>`, then the tool keys. Photoshop's live set is the same XML, kept as `Keyboard Shortcuts.psp` in its per-version settings folder and named after the set the user chose. `kys_import.rs` parses it with roxmltree (already in the tree through egui_extras → resvg → usvg) and `prefs::normalize_shortcut` already understands Photoshop's `Opt`/`Control` spelling.

Photoshop stores only the menu label, so rows match our commands by label, loosely (case, a trailing ellipsis). Where a label sits in several menus (Levels… under Image › Adjustments and Layer › New Adjustment Layer; All under Select, Edit › Purge and View › Show), the command whose default is one of the row's keys wins, then the one that has a default at all, then the first in Photoshop's menu order. Ours are one shortcut per command, so a row's first key is kept, unless one of its keys is already the command's default (Zoom In lists `Cmd++` before `Cmd+=`). Scripts, Bridge, the frames commands and the macOS application menu have no command here and are counted in the message. Tool keys are not imported: the tool letters are fixed.

On a real set of 122 rows: 103 match, 27 become overrides, 19 are counted as not here.

## Applying it

The import fills the open dialog's overrides, so OK applies them the way hand-made changes are (a key moved to a command is taken from its old owner) and Cancel discards them. A key equal to the command's default clears its overrid…

author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Partially addresses #1951.

PhotoCraft persists recorded actions internally, but users
cannot conveniently export their action libraries or import
actions from another installation.

title: Multithreaded web build: WebAssembly threads with a rayon Web Worker pool
author: joe2643
body:
## Summary

This adds a second browser build next to the single-threaded one: the same `photocraft-web` app compiled with WebAssembly threads. It uses one shared memory, and runs PhotoCraft's rayon work on a pool of Web Workers instead of the page's single thread:
- filters, compositing and colour transforms
- resampling, selections and segmentation
- RAW and HEIC decoding
- PNG and `.pcraft` encoding

The existing Trunk build (`packaging/web`) and native builds are unchanged.

```sh
packaging/web-threads/build.sh            # -> dist/web-threads
packaging/web-threads/build.sh --serve    # http://127.0.0.1:8777 with COOP/COEP
```

Docs: `packaging/web-threads/README.md`.

## How it works

- **Gates.** Each parallel step is a rayon branch for native and a sequential branch for `wasm32`. 120 of those gates now read `any(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), target_feature = "atomics")` and its complement, so the threads build takes the rayon branch. Crates that only depended on rayon natively also depend on it for wasm with `atomics`, and heic-rs gets `parallel` there.
- **`std::thread` splits.** Five data-parallel steps use scoped OS threads, which `wasm32-unknown-unknown` can't spawn: PNG `parallel_idat`, `effects::rows_par`, `store::par_compress`, `io::pixels::par_map`/`bands`, and the GPU canvas pixel conversion. In the threads build they hand the same work to rayon. Native keeps the scoped threads. `rows_par` nesting in a tile is safe for the reason its comment gives: map builds never block (#276).
- **The main thread never blocks.** The egui UI runs on the browser's main thread, where `Atomics.wait` traps. rayon's `web_spin_lock` feature makes that thread spin while it waits for a parallel step. Background jobs and the UI preview workers stay synchronous on the web on purpose: run alongside the UI, they would contend for shared caches behind `std::sync::Mutex`.
- **GPU objects.** wgpu objects are `!Send`/`!Sync` with atomics, but egui-wgpu's `callback_resources` requires…

title: Add native layered Paint.NET (.pdn) import
author: SilentYeti
body:
Adds native import-only support for Paint.NET PDN3 documents as editable PhotoCraft layers. Preserves layer order, names, visibility, opacity, pixel alpha and all 14 Paint.NET blend modes.

Imported layers work with PhotoCraft’s existing painting, masks, transforms, duplication, reordering and undo/redo. PDN sources are protected from overwriting; saving creates a native `.pcraft` copy.

### Changes

- Enable opening through desktop, browser, CLI and platform file associations.
- Reject PDN export and warn when PSD export substitutes unsupported blend modes.
- Add synthetic parser tests and real-file import/edit/native-save checks.
- Add the contributor’s requested public GitHub display-name credit.

### Validation

Native desktop/CLI/web compile checks, PDN/color tests, editing/history/native persistence, Save As protection, GPU XOR regression, Clippy and dependency-layer checks pass.

### Limits

Import only: PDN3 bitmap BGRA32 layers, up to 1,024 layers and 1 GiB of decoded pixels. Metadata, print resolution and color profiles are omitted; unsupported layouts return errors.

Wasm, external corpus and full float GPU parity still need CI or suitable hardware.

title: Fix Free Transform preview layer order and frame timing
author: CyanAvatar
body:
When Free Transform starts on a lower layer, its preview is drawn above the entire document. Upper layers, transparency, masks and adjustments therefore stop providing the context needed to position the layer. This change previews the transformed content through the normal document compositor and updates the canvas after pointer input, so pixels and handles show the same frame.

The preview uses an isolated engine session and caches unchanged geometry. Eligible whole-pixel raster translations reuse the existing move helper; scaling, rotation, fractional moves and warp use the existing transform commands. The actual document and its history remain unchanged until commit. Selection, mask/channel and path-only overlays retain their existing behavior.

**Draft:** this is a tested correctness fix and a useful local improvement, with substantial performance work still needed before it is suitable for general release. Implementation was AI-assisted; @CyanAvatar reproduced the problem and tested the local Windows build, confirming correct layering and noticeably smoother movement, scaling and rotation on an 800×450 layered document.

title: Brushes: keep the folder hierarchy of imported .abr files (#1851)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1851.

**Why.** Photoshop CC `.abr` files store their Brushes panel folders in a `phry` section. We skipped that section, so every imported preset landed in one flat group. Photoshop's Import Brushes puts the file's folders, nested, inside a folder named after the file (Adobe community threads: [1](https://community.adobe.com/questions-712/custom-brush-sets-all-load-with-group-folders-is-that-normal-1061295), [2](https://community.adobe.com/t5/photoshop-ecosystem-discussions/brushes-load-automatically-intermediate-folder-added-to-new-groups/m-p/9597011/highlight/true)). This PR does the same.

**Change**
- **psd:** `phry` is parsed into `AbrFile::folders` (one folder path per preset). A damaged hierarchy becomes a warning, never an error:
  - a stray `groupEnd` is ignored, and folders still open at the end close themselves;
  - more or fewer preset entries than presets: extra entries are ignored, missing ones go to the top level;
  - folders deeper than 32 levels merge into their parent at that depth;
  - an unreadable section imports flat;
  - paths are built only for the presets in `desc`, and hold at most 16 MB in total; presets past that import at the top level.

  New `write_v6_folders` writes the section; `write_v6` is unchanged.
- **paint:** new field `BrushPreset::folder`, the nested path inside `group` (serde default).
- **io:** imported folders nest inside the file-name group. A preset skipped for a missing tip doesn't shift the others.
- **Preset store:** stores `folder` per preset. Old stores load flat, without a rewrite. Paths read from disk or from `.pcpresets` are bounded.
- **Commands** (no new ids): `brush.presets.move`, `moveGroup`, `renameGroup` and `deleteGroup` take an optional `folder` path. `importAbr` also reports a `folders` count.
- **Brushes panel and picker:** nested folders draw indented in list and grid view. They are collapsible, accept dropped presets, reorder among their siblings, and have Rename/Delete in the context menu. Pr…

title: fix(gpu): preserve hard gradient stops with CPU fallback
author: raghav2005
body:
Fixes #974.

A gradient with coincident stops can show gray on the GPU canvas where the CPU export is white: the 4096-entry ramp LUT interpolates across the discontinuity. On an Apple M2 Max/Metal adapter, the issue's 8×2 fixture reproduced the reported pixel exactly: CPU `[1, 1, 1, 1]`, GPU `[0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1]` (127.5/255 error).

Return `Unsupported` when a sampled gradient has coincident color or opacity stops, so the existing canvas fallback evaluates the original ramp with the CPU compositor. Cover gradient fills, Gradient Map adjustments, Gradient Overlay, gradient strokes, and inner/outer glows. Matching fill caches, hidden/occluded layers, disabled effects, and ordinary gradients retain their existing GPU path. Fill-stop positions are checked after sorting a copy, matching the CPU's treatment of unsorted fills.

title: Chisel bevel: facets are flat at any edge angle (#1926)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #1926.

## Problem
Chisel Hard/Soft bevels shaded the facets of edges at 30°, 60°, 120° and 150° in regular cross-stripes (a comb along the edge). Edges at 0°, 45°, 90° and 135° were clean.

## Cause
A chisel's height is a linear ramp of the distance to the edge, and that distance was measured to the nearest pixel centre of a thresholded mask. An oblique edge is a pixel staircase, so the distance ripples with its period (0.19 px at 60°), and the shading is its gradient scaled by depth. At 0° and 45° the staircase is regular, hence no stripes there.

## Fix
Three commits, each verifiable alone:

1. **Measure to the edge itself.** A sharp anti-aliased edge pixel (partly covered, touching an empty and a full pixel) places the edge by its coverage along its normal (`edge_offset` inverts the area a straight edge cuts off a pixel). A pixel measures to the line of the edge pixels around the foot of its perpendicular, not to the nearest centre. The GPU compositor takes the same fields through new `FieldKind::BevelInside/BevelOutside`; the glow fields are untouched.
2. **Edge normals from a line fit.** The 3×3 coverage gradient is 1–3° off, systematically. A line fit through the edge points of neighbouring pixels reaches the ideal-normal floor (field ripple 0.0105 → 0.0038 px). The inside field is capped by the plain distance, which fixes up to 0.29 px of overshoot at a circle's pole and on whole-pixel rounded rectangles.
3. **Sparse sharp-edge storage** (perf only, bit-identical). The refinement was memory-bound: a 16-byte `Option` per pixel and two whole-map copies for a few thousand edge pixels. Now a 4-byte slot per pixel plus a short list.

Masks without anti-aliased edges and soft ramps give exactly the old fields (tested bit for bit).

## Result
Worst luma std along the bar, script from the issue (release CLI, 600×200):

| | 45° | 60° | 120° |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chiselHard` main → fix | 0.1 → 0.0 | 21.2 → 0.3 | 4.8 → 0.7 |
| `chiselSoft` main → fix | 0.5 → 0.3…

title: Edit › Fill and Edit › Stroke: the colour opens the Color Picker
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
## Problem

In Edit › Fill, **Contents: Color…** showed a small inline swatch whose click opened egui's compact colour popup. Edit › Stroke's colour swatch (#1477) opened egui's raw colour button popup. Neither used PhotoCraft's Color Picker: the Photoshop-style dialog the foreground and background colours use, with HSB/RGB/Lab/CMYK and hex fields, the gamut warning and the image eyedropper.

## Photoshop's behaviour (checked by hand)

- In Edit › Fill, choosing **Contents: Color…** opens the Color Picker.
- **Cancel** in the picker leaves Contents on Color….
- The Fill dialog shows no swatch of the colour.
- Edit › Stroke's colour swatch opens the Color Picker too.

## Fix

- **Fill › Color…** opens PhotoCraft's Color Picker ("Color Picker (Fill Color)") on the dialog's colour, the foreground at first.

- **OK** writes the colour into that dialog's `color` field. The dialog stays open, and the foreground and background colours are untouched. **Cancel** leaves the dialog as it was.

- `color_picker_ui::open_for_field` adds a "field" target: OK sets a field of another dialog.
- A dialog body asks for the picker with `color_picker_ui::request(fields, title)`. The dialog loop opens it once the body's fields are saved (`open_requested`), so the picker knows the dialog's id.

title: DNG: lossy compression 34892 (baseline JPEG tiles)
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What

Adobe's **lossy DNG** (compression 34892) now decodes. Previously these files answered
"lossy-compressed DNG is not supported".

Each tile is a complete baseline JPEG (8-bit luma at tile size — Adobe stores the CFA as a
plain gray JPEG); zune-jpeg decodes it, the tile geometry must match the header (a mismatch
is an error), and the 8-bit samples widen 0xFF → 0xFFFF like any 8-bit raw read into the
16-bit pipeline. Predictors, black levels and the rest of the develop path are unchanged.
JPEG XL (52546) keeps its explicit unsupported error.

Stacked on the deflate PR (#1971, still open): this branch carries that commit too, so the
compression-8 and 34892 arms land together without a conflict.

`testgen` grows `LossyJpegTiles` — the fixtures encode Q60 baseline JPEG via image-rs behind
the `testgen` feature, so the oracle runs in **every** CI: a smooth-ramp CFA decodes within
a few quantisation steps of the 8-bit source (JPEG is lossy; the test pins the band, not
identity), and a tile cut mid-stream fails cleanly. Full suite: 88 raw tests green, clippy
`-D warnings` clean, wasm32 clean.

title: Compose shader: exact F32_MAX, so WebGPU in Chrome no longer falls back to the CPU (regression from #1722)
author: kuvshin888
body:
## Problem

Since #1722, the web build in Chrome with WebGPU switches to the CPU compositor as soon as a document is drawn: the "Switched to CPU rendering" dialog appears, and the console shows only the follow-up error:

```text
uncaptured wgpu error: [Invalid RenderPipeline "fs_content"] is invalid due to a previous error.
 - While encoding [RenderPassEncoder "pc_compose_pass"].SetPipeline([Invalid RenderPipeline "fs_content"]).
```

The previous error is the shader module itself. Chrome's WGSL compiler (Tint) rejects line 156 of `crates/gpu/src/compose.wgsl`:

```text
pc_compose 156:22 value 340282346999999984391321947108527833088.0 cannot be represented as 'f32'
```

```wgsl
const F32_MAX: f32 = 3.40282347e38;
```

That decimal (the usual printed `FLT_MAX`) is slightly above the real `f32::MAX`, 3.4028234663852886e38. naga rounds it down to `f32::MAX`, so native builds and `shader_validates` pass. Tint applies the WGSL rule that an abstract-float value must be representable in the target type and rejects the module, and with it every compose pipeline (`fs_content`, `fs_mask`, `fs_blend`, …).

Repro: web build of current main, Chrome with WebGPU, File › New. With `?webgl` there is no error (the GL path goes through naga's own output).

wgpu on the web doesn't log shader compilation messages; I got the line above from a page-side hook on `GPUDevice.createShaderModule` → `getCompilationInfo()`.

## Change

- `F32_MAX` is the exact hex literal `0x1.fffffep+127f`, with a comment on why.
- New test `shader_float_literals_fit_in_f32`: every decimal float literal in `compose.wgsl` must fit in an `f32`. `shader_validates` (naga) can't catch this.

## Screenshots

Web build in Chrome (WebGPU, macOS), File › New, then a type layer:

title: Edit › Stroke: whole opaque pixels, Center like Photoshop, and strokes on the canvas edge
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
## Problem

Edit › Stroke didn't match Photoshop's pixels:

- **Center straddled the edge.** It expanded and contracted the selection by w/2, so a 1 px Center stroke was a 2 px band at half opacity, and every odd width left a half-transparent pixel on each side.
- **A selection edge on the canvas border got no stroke.** Distances were measured only inside the canvas, so a selection touching the canvas had nothing to contract from on that side. For example, Select All then Stroke › Inside, the usual way to frame an image, drew nothing.

## Photoshop's behaviour (checked by hand)

- Center puts ceil(w/2) px inside and floor(w/2) px outside: 1 px is all inside, 2 px is 1 + 1, 3 px is 2 + 1.
- Fractional widths round up (0.5 px strokes 1 px).
- Every stroked pixel is fully opaque.
- Select All, then a 3 px Center stroke, draws the 2 px inside part around the canvas.
- Outside corners are rounded, as PhotoCraft already draws them.

## Fix

`extra_cmds::stroke`:
- The width rounds up to whole pixels.
- Center expands by floor(w/2) and contracts by ceil(w/2). On a hard selection, whole-pixel distances give fully opaque bands; feathered selections keep their soft edges.
- The stroke is computed on a copy of the edge mask padded with unselected pixels, then cropped, so the canvas border is a selection edge like any other.

The no-selection path (stroking the layer's opaque pixels) uses the same code.

### Curves

A 6 px Outside stroke of a 14 px circle selection made without anti-aliasing, read pixel by pixel from a Photoshop screenshot, is reproduced exactly by one rule: a pixel is stroked when its centre is less than width + 1 from a selected pixel's centre. Every threshold from 6.71 to just under 7 matches all 26 × 26 pixels, and other rules don't (centre distance ≤ w: 48 pixels off; Chebyshev or Manhattan distance: 72 and 108 off). That is where `selection::expand` gave the fringe partial alpha (100 % at w, fading to 0 at w + 1), so a curve had a soft, too-thin edge.

Th…

title: Add native scratch storage and bounded PSB/EXR viewport streaming
author: vistaero
body:
Large layered PSB files can exceed the merged-image decoder limit or exhaust GPU upload memory, while large scanline EXR files require whole-file and whole-channel allocations. This change imports supported native PSB/EXR files directly into tiled storage and renders visible regions at their original resolution, with configurable RAM and GPU budgets and SSD scratch for cold pixels.

## Integration status

The tested head is `2f52c1502f8a81a15e040d1cfbf27dc07bba628d`, integrating upstream through `d80455ad25fe2f1ed8b493794d9d8be47b23cbaf`. At submission, upstream `main` has advanced by 216 commits to `6ae2a8498cb0085d94d12bcad5d54f1a7b4256d5`. I am submitting the validated implementation now; further synchronization and conflict resolution can happen during maintainer review. Maintainer edits on the fork branch are enabled.

## Changes

- Add compressed, integrity-checked scratch storage shared by document pixels and undo snapshots, with copy-on-write edits and on-demand reloads. Failed reads block edit commits and saves instead of replacing source pixels with display placeholders.
- Coordinate RAM admission and tile eviction using process RSS and available physical memory. Fresh preferences use 90% of physical RAM; existing MiB settings keep their value.
- Stream layered PSD/PSB channel rows and supported flat scanline EXR compression blocks into tiles without allocating whole channels. Preserve source dimensions, depth and HDR values.
- Stream zoom-specific visible pages through two shared workers, retain source-resolution CPU fallback, and bound GPU staging transfers. Retry work after worker capacity is released and keep cache identity stable across tab closure/reordering.
- Publish streamed PSB saves atomically from a snapshot. Save-before-close waits for publication; failures and edits made during a save keep the document open and dirty.

author: Jeremy8776
body:

## Change

- **Delete current state** runs a new engine command, `history.deleteState`. It undoes the current step and forgets that step and every redo state, which is what Photoshop's linear history does. - **Create new document from current state** runs the existing `image.duplicate`.

The crop options bar's Rule of Thirds overlay button, also listed in #1117. PR #1958 is changing the crop tool, so I left it alone. The four options-bar buttons from the same issue (airbrush, smoothing, symmetry) were fixed in #1214.

body:
Refs #1909 (the Thai part; the memory part is handled separately).

## Why
Thai typed in a newly chosen font rendered as .notdef boxes; only text saved by Photoshop looked right. - `thai_in_latin_font_falls_back_to_installed_thai_font`: lays out Thai in Inter with system fonts loaded; no .notdef, and Latin and Thai in the same line use different faces. Skips when no Thai font is installed.

title: Shape tools: a click opens Create Rectangle / Create Ellipse (#1175)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1175.

## Why
In Photoshop, a single click (no drag) on the canvas with a shape tool opens a creation dialog: Create Rectangle (Width, Height, Radii, From Center), Create Ellipse (Width, Height, From Center), Create Triangle and Create Polygon (Width, Height, Number of Sides, Star Ratio, From Center). OK places the shape at the clicked point, or centred on it, with the options bar's fill and stroke. In PhotoCraft a click with a shape tool did nothing: the drag geometry was under 1 px, so `finish_shape` returned early.

## Change
- New `shape_dialog` module with the Create Rectangle / Ellipse / Triangle / Polygon dialogs. Width and height are shown in the ruler unit and stored in document px. Radii and sides start from the options bar. Width, height, From Center and star ratio are remembered per tool (`prefs.dialogs["shape.create.<tool>"]`).
- OK runs the existing `shape.create` command, so the UI only dispatches it. Bad sizes or positions put an error in the status bar instead of panicking.
- `finish_gesture`: a shape-tool gesture that stays within 3 screen px of the press opens the dialog. Drags behave exactly as before. Line and Custom Shape still ignore clicks.
- `vector_ui::create_shape` now holds the fill/stroke params, shared by the drag and the dialog.
- Catalog entries for the new labels and titles in every complete language.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: the `ui.pointer` entry describes how agents use the dialogs.

## Tests

title: DNG: JPEG XL compression 52546 (DNG 1.7, Samsung Expert RAW)
author: ravelund
body:
## What

**JPEG XL–compressed DNG** (compression 52546, DNG 1.7) now decodes. Previously these files returned "JPEG XL-compressed DNG is not supported", and `photocraft-io` fell back to the embedded 8-bit JPEG preview. This is the format Samsung Galaxy phones write for Expert RAW and the camera app's RAW mode. A Galaxy S26 Ultra LinearRaw file (4000×3000, one 16-bit JXL strip) now opens as a 16-bit, correctly oriented document, decoding in about 0.6 s and opening through the CLI in about 1.5 s in release builds.

Each strip or tile is one JPEG XL codestream, bare or in the container format. A new `jxl.rs` decodes it with **jxl-oxide** (pure Rust, MIT OR Apache-2.0), the decoder `docs/architecture.md` already names for JPEG XL. It is pinned exactly (`=0.12.6`) because it parses untrusted files, as `heic-rs` is in `photocraft-heif`. It uses rayon on native builds and stays sequential on wasm.

- **Geometry must match:** the codestream size must equal the segment (whole tile, or the remaining rows for the last strip), and the channel count must equal SamplesPerPixel. A mismatch is an error.
- **Sample depth:** 16-bit samples come back exactly as stored. Lower depths, which jxl-oxide normalises to 0..=65535, are scaled back to the TIFF BitsPerSample range (exact for lossless data).
- **Never crash:** dimensions are checked against `Limits` before decoding, jxl-oxide gets an `AllocTracker` budget capped by `Limits::max_alloc`, and every call runs under `catch_unwind` (as in `photocraft-heif`), so a decoder panic becomes `RawError::Malformed`.

Lossy DNG (34892) and deflate (8) keep their existing arms. #1971 and #2021 edit the same `match compression` in `sensor.rs`, so whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase.

**Also:** a DNG that carries a **ProfileGainTableMap** (DNG 1.6, tag 52525: the local tone mapping Samsung relies on for its default look) now gets a warning that it is not applied, rather than silently rendering darker than the camera. Implementing it is a…

title: Auto-Align Layers: register focus and exposure brackets by intensity when there is nothing to match
author: ragtux
body:
Closes #2064.

`edit.autoAlignLayers` gets a direct, intensity-based registration for layers that nearly coincide (a focus bracket, an exposure bracket, a burst), where feature matching has nothing to match and fails with "couldn't find enough matching detail".

**Algorithm** (`photocraft_algo::direct`): the target is registered to the reference coarse-to-fine on a Gaussian pyramid of the luminance. The cost of a pose is the RMS of the difference between the reference and the target warped by it, the mean removed, over the pixels both cover; the correlation of the two over the same pixels comes back with it (exposure independent: near 1 for a bracket of one scene, near 0 for unrelated pictures). Each level runs a bounded Nelder-Mead search whose simplex starts one pixel of that level wide and stops at a tenth of one. The pose (`Pose`) is a similarity about the centre — shift, scale, rotation — with aspect and shear for an affine fit and two perspective terms for a projective one; `Motion` says which move. The pose is resolution independent, so the engine builds the luminance planes at the search scale (≤ 2048 px across, `DIRECT_SIDE`) and never holds or warps a full-resolution plane; the pose's matrix at full resolution places the layer. Coverage-aware (a layer has no say where its alpha is below ½), `par_map`/`par_rows2` (single-threaded on wasm), no panics, deterministic.

**Engine** (`photo_cmds::register_direct`, `align_cmds`): layers register outward from the reference, each to the previous one aligned, starting from its pose, and come back as planar `Placement`s. A layer whose best pose overlaps its neighbour by less than a quarter of the plane or correlates with it below 0.5 is no fit, and the command fails with the existing "couldn't find enough matching detail" error rather than placing it at whatever pose the search box ended at. so warping, masks, undo and the JSON result are shared with the feature path. Projections map to motions: Reposition → translati…

title: Save in the background so large saves don't freeze the window (#2017)
author: brennanMKE
body:
Fixes #2017.

Saving a large layered document (a layered TIFF, or a PSD big enough to be written as PSB) froze the whole window until the write finished, with no progress, so Windows marks the app "Not Responding". Saves now run in the background with the progress dialog that filters and opens already use.

## Cause

`PhotocraftApp::write_document` called the `export` and `write` services on the UI thread. For a multi-GB document that is the whole encode plus the write, so no frame was drawn until both were done.

## Fix

- **New service:** `Services::save_file` encodes and writes on a worker thread and reports its stage ("Encoding", "Writing") to the job. The desktop app provides it: `photocraft_io::export`, then the same atomic write as before.
- **Save as a job:** `write_document` starts a `file.save` job through `jobs_ui::start_save` when background jobs are on and the service exists. The worker gets a snapshot (`Arc`) of the document, which stays locked against edits until the job ends. The progress dialog appears after 250 ms. The bar stays indeterminate because the encoders don't report progress yet.
- **When it ends:** `PhotocraftApp::saved` sets the path and saved state, fires the Save Document script event, writes Image Assets and shows the warnings, as the synchronous save did. It also works when another tab is active by then.
- **Cancel:** Esc or Cancel while encoding leaves the file on disk untouched. The document stays unsaved.
- **Failure:** a failed save is reported as "Save failed: …". The document stays unsaved.
- **Unsaved-changes prompt:** waits while a save runs. Close or Quit → Save closes the document once the save has finished.
- **Window close during a save:** closing while a save is still writing (for example a saved copy, which leaves nothing unsaved) is held until the save ends, then repeated.
- **Unchanged:** the web build and tests (no `save_file`) still save synchronously, and so does `app.save` on the control channel, which replies on…

A layer with Transparency Shapes Layer off (PSD `tsly` = 0) takes the whole canvas as its effect region (`layer_bounds` → `advanced::shapeless`). ## Problem

title: Selection distance transforms: 7.6-10.6x faster and correct past 4K
author: excited-raccoon
body:
Expand, Contract and Border use a distance transform that scans columns serially. Its f32 parabola intersections also lose precision past coordinate 4096: even a fully selected 6000 x 1 mask can contain nonzero distances.

This replaces the binary column envelope with two nearest-seed sweeps, stores integer vertical distances, and evaluates f64 row envelopes in parallel 32-row bands. Empty and fully selected masks skip the passes. The public function and selection radius/coverage behavior stay the same, with the large-coordinate distance errors corrected. Malformed dimensions return an empty result instead of indexing past the input.

Release medians on an AWS c7i.4xlarge, Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C, 16 vCPUs, 32 GiB RAM, Rust 1.99.0, 16 Rayon workers. Three measured runs after warmup, alternating old/new order:

| Size | Mask | Before p50 | After p50 | Speedup | Changed distances | Largest correction |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 MP | ellipse | 630.74 ms | 83.11 ms | 7.59x | 827,500 | 1 px |
| 24 MP | sparse | 621.81 ms | 71.03 ms | 8.75x | 0 | 0 px |
| 24 MP | dense | 1048.21 ms | 99.73 ms | 10.51x | 2,034,343 | 1.4142135 px |
| 36 MP | ellipse | 994.14 ms | 124.48 ms | 7.99x | 2,431,817 | 1 px |
| 36 MP | sparse | 984.52 ms | 109.94 ms | 8.96x | 0 | 0 px |

title: Dropdowns: the mouse wheel walks the open list (#2061)
author: maxm11
body:
Closes #2061.

## What

A wheel over an **open** dropdown now walks its choices, exactly like the arrow keys already do (#1318), instead of only scrolling the list under a stationary highlight. The value changes as the wheel turns — for the Layers panel's Blend Mode dropdown the live canvas preview follows too — so a user no longer has to scroll to find an item and click it.

- `dropdown`, `dropdown_hovered` and `dropdown_with_tooltips` all take the wheel while their popup is open.
- The wheel is consumed while the pointer is over the list, so the list does not also scroll; the stepped-to row is scrolled into view (`scroll_to_me`).
- Out-of-range wheel steps clamp (`stepped_index`), and the arithmetic uses `i64` so hostile steps can't overflow.

## Tests

- `widgets::tests::mouse_wheel_steps_an_open_dropdown` — wheel down/up steps and clamps at both ends.
- `widgets::tests::mouse_wheel_off_the_list_leaves_the_dropdown_alone` — a wheel off the list doesn't change it.
- `widgets::tests::a_step_through_a_dropdown_never_overflows` — clamp arithmetic, including `i32::MAX`/`MIN`.
- `blend_dropdown_keys_tests::mouse_wheel_steps_the_open_blend_mode_dropdown` — end-to-end through the real Layers panel dropdown with eframe input; the layer's blend mode changes.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` — 1323 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo xtask layers` — no violations.

title: fix(linux): disable unsupported startup notification (#2089)
author: zenjabba
body:
Launching PhotoCraft from GNOME's dock requests startup feedback, but the native runner never completes that handshake. Set `StartupNotify=false` so the launcher stops promising unsupported startup notification and GNOME does not wait for its timeout.

Keep `StartupWMClass=photocraft`: with the pinned egui-winit/winit versions, the X11 class defaults to the executable basename. `ViewportBuilder::app_id` is applied on Wayland and does not change that X11 class.

GNOME dock runtime was unavailable; this is the minimal desktop-entry fix, with no activation-token handshake added. The [Desktop Entry specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry/latest/recognized-keys) defines the startup-notification promise.

Fixes #2089.
