title: Canvas: UI Scale must not magnify the image (#2121)
author: maxm11
body:
Closes #2121.

**No product behaviour change.** The report — UI Scale magnifies the image, so 150% UI Scale draws 100% zoom at 150% — is the bug #1943 fixed in #1978. Interface › UI Scale is egui's `zoom_factor`, folded into `pixels_per_point` together with the display scale. `canvas_view` stores the view zoom as device pixels per document pixel, every point-space conversion divides it by the **full** `ctx.pixels_per_point` (`PhotocraftApp::point_zoom`), and the GPU shader multiplies it back to device pixels. So 100% is one document pixel per *physical* display pixel at any UI scale. The report is from v0.5.0, which predates #1978. This PR is test coverage plus comments, not a fix.

## Coverage

`crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_scale_canvas.rs` renders a black 60 px document through the real app on the **GPU and CPU canvas** at UI Scale 100/125/150/200% and zoom 100/200%, and measures the document's on-screen size from the pixels (like `checker_canvas.rs`). It stays 60×60 / 120×120 physical px at every UI scale.

Unlike a point-space assertion, it fails on either regression:
- canvas stops dividing by `pixels_per_point` → **75×75** at 125% UI Scale (both GPU and CPU tests);
- GPU shader stops multiplying back by `pixels_per_point` → **48×48** at 125% (GPU test; the CPU test is unaffected, as expected).

The tests skip when no wgpu adapter is present (repo convention).

## Comments

`View::zoom`, `PhotocraftApp::ppp` and `canvas_view` now name Interface › UI Scale explicitly, since `pixels_per_point` folds in both the display scale and the UI scale.

## Verification

`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --test ui_scale_canvas` and `--lib` green (the one pre-existing macOS-only `mask_thumbs_ui` label failure also fails on a clean origin/main; it hard-codes `Alt` where macOS paints `⌥`). `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask layers` clean. `cargo xtask wasm` can't run here (no wasm32 std component); the non-test ch…

title: Crop/marquee readout and Properties W/H/X/Y in the ruler unit (cm, mm, in…)
author: llduyll10
body:
## Problem

With Edit › Preferences › Units & Rulers › Rulers set to Centimeters (or mm, inches…), the rulers and the Canvas Size dialog follow the unit, but the lengths shown while working stay in pixels:

- the W × H readout beside the pointer while drawing or resizing a crop frame or a marquee;
- the Properties panel: a layer's Transform W / H / X / Y, and the document's Canvas W / H.

Photoshop shows all of these in the ruler unit, so laying out print work in cm means converting by hand.

## Fix

- `canvas::size_readout` formats the crop and marquee readouts with `UnitsAndRulers::format` at the document's resolution (`readout_in` does the formatting, so it can be tested without an app). Pixels still read `1644 px`.

The Transform fields and the Canvas W / H fields show the value in that unit with its suffix, and a typed value is converted back to px before the same `edit.transform` / `layer.translate` / `image.canvasSize` commands run. The 0.5 px change threshold is checked in px, so a small change in cm still applies.

- New `marquee_tests::size_readout_follows_the_ruler_unit`: px, cm and mm readouts (1644 px at 72 dpi → `58.00 cm`).
- New `layer_props_ui::tests::transform_fields_show_and_take_the_ruler_unit`: cm ↔ px both ways, px unchanged, percent of the canvas.

title: fix(adjust): colourize at 0% saturation greys out (#2326)
author: mroxso
body:
## Problem

With Hue/Saturation ▸ Colourise ticked, dropping the Saturation slider to 0% still left colour in the image (issue #2326). Photoshop removes all colour at 0% saturation, whether or not Colourise is on.

## Cause

The colourise path floored the saturation at 25%: `ss = s.abs().max(0.25)` in the CPU compositor and `ss = max(abs(sat), 0.25)` in the GPU shader. So a 0% slider still produced a 25%-saturated result, and low values (e.g. 10%) were silently raised to 25%.

## Fix

Take the slider literally: `ss = s.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` in both `crates/compose/src/adjust.rs` (the CPU oracle) and `crates/gpu/src/compose.wgsl`, keeping CPU/GPU parity. Hue is unchanged; lightness is preserved as before, so 0% saturation now yields the grey of the original lightness.

## Tests

- New regression test `hue_saturation_colorize_zero_saturation_is_grey` (compose): colourise at 0% saturation is colourless with lightness preserved for several hues, and 10% saturation is honoured exactly (no floor).

title: UI font fallback: Thai and other non-CJK scripts draw in the Layers panel (#2275)
author: maxm11
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2275. A text Layer name in a script the bundled UI fonts lack (Thai, Arabic, Hebrew) showed missing-glyph boxes, even though the canvas rendered it with a fallback font.

**Root cause.** The canvas falls back through the Type tool's font database (`fonts::fallback_candidates`, which carries `THAI_FAMILIES`), but the egui shell's lazy UI fallback (`cjk_fonts.rs`) only knew the four CJK scripts — `missing_char` filtered to `cjk::classify`, so a Thai character never loaded a fallback and stayed tofu.

**Fix.** The UI loader now handles non-CJK scripts too:

- New `FontDb::fallback_face_for(c) -> Option<(family, bytes, face index)>` returns the first installed fallback face (in the same order the canvas falls back) whose charmap covers `c`; ASCII is skipped, bytes are bounded at 128 MB, malformed data yields nothing, never a panic.
- The loader classifies a glyphless character via `served::script_of` (Thai `Thai`, `Arab`, `Hebr`, `Deva`) and registers the returned face's bytes in the egui font stack, deduped per `(family, index)`.
- `exhausted` now waits for the non-CJK scripts as well, and `CjkFontPlugin` only requests a repaint when it made progress (a load, or a newly tried script), so a character no fallback applies to can't spin the frame loop.

CJK behaviour is unchanged: CJK characters still take the locale-ordered script-font path.

## Verification

- Offscreen render (`snapshot --safe-gpu`) of `file.new` + `layer.new.layer {"name": "สวัสดี ภาษาไทย"}`: the Thai name now draws in the Layers panel, Properties header and title bar. (Before: boxes.)

title: fix(cms): parse DeviceLink profiles (LUT channels vs output space, not a 3-ch PCS)
author: mroxso
body:
## Problem

A well-formed ICC **DeviceLink** profile (class `link`) failed to parse with `CmsError::Invalid("invalid ICC profile")`, telling the user their file is corrupt when it is valid and merely unsupported (#2337). This also made the deliberate `Unsupported` path in `link_stages` unreachable: no non-Lab DeviceLink ever got past parsing.

## Cause

`parse_profile` validated every AToB/BToA tag against a hard-coded 3-channel PCS. For a DeviceLink that is wrong: per ICC.1:2010 §10.4 the header's *PCS field* (bytes 20..24) carries the **output colour space**, not a PCS — a CMYK→CMYK press link legitimately carries 4→4 LUTs.

## Fix

- `Profile` gains `link_output: Option<ColorSpace>` — the output space, parsed from bytes 20..24 for the `link` class only (`None` elsewhere).
- Channel validation compares AToB outputs / BToA inputs against the link's output space (falling back to 3 for every other class, and skipping the check when the output space is unknown). Error messages now name both spaces for a link (`Cmyk→Cmyk`).
- `link_stages`: a Lab-input DeviceLink now parses, so the guard is tightened — only links ending in a PCS space (Lab/XYZ) may be linked; others get a clear `Unsupported`, never a silent mis-decode.
- `write::encode` writes the output-space signature into bytes 20..24 for DeviceLink profiles, so a parsed link re-encodes faithfully.

## Tests

- New `devicelink_profiles_parse`: a crafted CMYK→CMYK link (4→4 `mft2` A2B0/B2A0) parses, reports `link_output == Cmyk`, and yields `Unsupported` (not `Invalid`) as a transform source; a link whose AToB output contradicts its output space is still `Invalid`.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-cms` (incl. `system_profiles`, `malformed_profiles_are_rejected_without_panicking`), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-cms --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --workspace`, `cargo xtask layers` green.

title: cms: accept ICC DeviceLinks whose output isn't a 3-channel PCS
author: kavishkashehan726-sudo
body:
A DeviceLink's header PCS field holds its output colour space (ICC.1:2010 §7.2.7), so a CMYK→CMYK link has a 4→4 AToB0. The LUT channel check hard-coded 3 outputs and rejected such files as invalid, so users were told a well-formed profile was corrupt and never reached the "DeviceLink profiles cannot be used" error.

Check DeviceLink LUTs against the header's output space instead, and only let a Lab DeviceLink through link_stages when its tables end in 3 channels, so a Lab→CMYK link gets the unsupported error rather than building a mismatched transform.

Fixes #2337

title: HEIF: decode with heic-decoder instead of heic-rs (correct iPhone colours, 62/63 conformance)
author: Multipad-cyber
body:
Replaces heic-rs 0.1.1 inside `photocraft-heif` with [`heic-decoder`](https://crates.io/crates/heic-decoder) 0.1.0. The crate's API is unchanged, so `photocraft-codecs`, `photocraft-io` and the apps need no changes beyond the dependency.

**Disclosure:** I maintain heic-decoder. Like heic-rs, it is pure Rust, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, MIT OR Apache-2.0, has no C dependencies and builds for wasm. Its HEVC output is bit-exact against HM, the HEVC reference decoder. The numbers below come from running both decoders through `photocraft-heif`'s own pipeline (probe, then RGB/RGBA8 or RGB/RGBA16 output) on the same files.

## Why

### 1. iPhone photos open with the wrong colours today

iPhone HEICs have no `colr/nclx` box. They signal their colour (BT.601 matrix, **full range**, Display P3 primaries) only in the HEVC stream's VUI. heic-rs discards the VUI (`src/hevc/ps/vui.rs`: "every field is discarded") and falls back to BT.709 limited range (`Nclx::default`). As a result, every iPhone photo PhotoCraft opens is off by about 8 levels on average.

Compared with Apple's own decode (`sips` → PNG) of iPhone photos, mean |error| per channel in 8-bit levels:

| | heic-rs 0.1.1 | heic-decoder 0.1.0 |
|---|---|---|
| 5 unrotated 12 MP iPhone photos (personal, not shared) | **7.4 – 8.7** (max 26–28) | **0.08 – 0.11** (max 9–12) |
| `with-exif.heic` (corpus; has an `nclx` box) | 0.24 | 0.30 |

The corpus never caught this because its iPhone-like file carries an `nclx` box. Two new corpus files now cover it (see Testing).

### 2. More files open

| Files | heic-rs 0.1.1 | heic-decoder 0.1.0 |
|---|---|---|
| [Nokia HEIF conformance suite](https://github.com/nokiatech/heif_conformance) | 44 / 63 | **62 / 63** (only `multilayer004`, AVC, fails) |
| Sony a6700 4:2:2 10-bit camera photo ([public sample](https://github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/16018)) | error: "picture is not fully covered by slices" | opens, 4128×6192, HM-exact |
| 12-bit and 4:4:4 pictures | error | open |

title: Linux/BSD: a second launch opens its files in the running window (#1540)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #1540. Covers the single-instance part of #1266.

Opening an image from a file manager (Dolphin's Open With, a double-click) runs `photocraft <path>`, and every launch started its own app and window. Photoshop runs once; a file opened while it's running lands in the existing window as a tab.

**Change** (`apps/photocraft/src/single_instance.rs`, wired in `main.rs`; `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`)
- The first instance listens on a Unix socket. A later launch sends its paths (made absolute against its own cwd), waits for `ok`, and exits. The running window opens them through the existing `OsEvent::Open` path, the same one macOS Apple events use (`drain_os_events`: `open_paths` + `ViewportCommand::Focus`). So Workspace › Open Documents as Tabs applies as for any other open.
- **Socket:** `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/photocraft-<hash>.sock` (per user, 0700; shared by a Flatpak app's instances), else the settings directory. Mode 0600. The hash is of the settings directory, so separate `PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`s (tests, agents, portable copies) stay separate apps.
- **Protocol:** a version header (`photocraft-open-1\0`), then NUL-terminated path bytes (non-UTF-8 paths survive the trip). Connections without the header are ignored, input is capped (1 MiB, 4096 paths), and only absolute paths are taken.
- **Never blocks a launch:** a stale socket (crashed instance) is replaced; no answer within 2 s or any error starts the launch normally. The listener is dropped before the CPU-mode relaunch, which would otherwise hand its files to the exiting process.
- **Opt-out:** `--new-instance` or `PHOTOCRAFT_NEW_INSTANCE=1`. `--control` instances neither forward nor listen. Launches with non-UTF-8 paths start their own window, which reports them as before.
- std only: no new dependency, no `unsafe`.

**Tests** (8 in `single_instance::tests`): hand-off end to end over a real socket; a second listener defers to a live one; relative paths dropped; stale socket replaced; a non-answeri…

title: Raw: Fujifilm lossless compressed RAF decodes natively, X-Trans and Bayer, 14/16-bit (#50)
author: smyrgeorge
body:
Fujifilm's lossless compressed RAF (the `IS` strips written by X-Trans III–V bodies such as the X-T2/X-T3/X-T30/X-T4/X-S10 and by the GFX cameras) now decodes natively instead of falling back to the embedded JPEG preview. Progress on #50.

## What's in the box

- `crates/raw/src/rafc.rs`: the decoder, plus a mirror encoder (behind `testgen`/tests) so synthetic files round-trip and feed the hostile and fuzz-seed tests. X-Trans and Bayer, 14- and 16-bit; blocks decode in parallel (rayon on native, sequential on wasm).
- `crates/raw/src/raf.rs`: routes `IS` strips to it. The lossy variant (stream version 0) and early FinePix files still report `Unsupported`, so `photocraft-io` keeps opening their preview with the usual warning.
- Tests: round trips (X-Trans, Bayer, 14/16-bit, all-zero / all-white / checkerboard extremes), truncation and corruption, a lossy-stream rejection, hostile samples, and a bit-exact corpus test (sums and FNV-1a hashes) for two newly pinned CC0 raw.pixls.us files: X-T30 (X-Trans) and GFX 50S (Bayer). `xtask/src/corpus_pins.rs`, `xtask/pixls.sha256` and `ATTRIBUTION.md` carry the pins.
- Docs: `crates/raw/README.md` (support matrix and sources), `docs/roadmap.md` honest assessment.

## Clean-room sourcing (please check this meets the bar)

No decoder source was read (LibRaw, rawspeed, rawler, dcraw, blitz). The structure follows Fabian Tamp's published prose description of the scheme (<https://capnfabs.net/posts/fuji-raf-compression-algorithm/>: independent vertical blocks, six-row lines collated into colour vectors coded in interleaved pairs with the odd positions lagging, a gradient-adaptive predictor, unary + fixed-length residual codes whose length follows 81 gradient buckets, a 41-zero escape). title: Add Windows MSI auto-updates in About
author: aEboli

Portable and manually copied installations get a link to the official release page.

## How it works

title: Content-Aware Fill workspace, as Photoshop's
author: Unemars
body:
**Builds on #2202.** Its commit, "Content-Aware tools: Photoshop's behaviour, measured", is the first one here. This PR adds the last two commits: "Content-Aware Fill workspace, as Photoshop's" and a one-line rustfmt change that main currently needs.

**Problem.** Edit › Content-Aware Fill… opened a generic parameter dialog. In Photoshop it opens a workspace:
- you paint what may be copied from with the Sampling Brush;
- you change the fill area with a lasso;
- the result shows in a Preview panel;
- you can apply several fills before leaving.

None of that could be done here: the sampling area was Auto, the whole window, or a rectangle typed as numbers.

**How Photoshop's workspace behaves.** Measured on Photoshop 25.4 on a virtual screen. Only what it does was observed, never its code or assets.

| | Photoshop 25.4 |
|---|---|
| Layout | Options bar for the tool. Tools on the left: Sampling Brush, Lasso, Hand, Zoom. The document with the sampling area tinted and the fill area in marching ants. A Preview panel with a zoom field and slider. The Content-Aware Fill panel: Sampling Area Overlay (collapsed), Sampling Area Options, Fill Settings, Output Settings. Footer: reset, OK, Apply, Cancel. |

title: Brush rendering: rayon parallelism, fast-path rasterization, tail throttle
author: cwshields
body:
## Summary

Three independent optimisations for the brush rendering hot path, reducing worst-case per-chunk time from ~37 ms to ~12 ms:

- **Rayon parallelism** — row-level `par_chunks_mut` in `rasterize()`, parallel dab rasterization in `raster_pending()`, and parallel tile blending in `composite()` (all wasm32-gated, same pattern as `photocraft-compose`)
- **Fast-path rasterization** for simple round brushes — eliminates the `to_tip` coordinate transform, pre-computes `inv_range` to avoid per-pixel division, and skips entire rows where `dy² >= reach²`
- **Tail preview throttle** — skips the smoothing catch-up erase+recomposite on odd pushes, halving per-frame tail work with one frame of stale preview (imperceptible at 60 fps)

### Benchmark (release, RGBA8 textured+scattered 200px)

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| worst/chunk | ~37 ms | 12.44 ms |
| mean/chunk | ~16 ms | 8.05 ms |

All depths and colour models show similar improvement (RGBA16 6.97 ms, RGBA32F 7.82 ms, CMYKA8 8.31 ms mean/chunk).

Complementary to #354 (input sampling vs rendering throughput) — zero file overlap.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-paint -p photocraft-engine` — all 1172 tests pass
- [x] `cargo clippy -p photocraft-paint -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo xtask layers` — no violations
- [x] Smoothing pixel-perfect test (`live_stroke_equals_the_commit_at_every_zoom_with_smoothing`) passes
- [x] Manual painting test at various brush sizes and settings
- [x] Verify wasm build (wasm32 target not installed locally; CI will check)

title: Windows: keep the custom title bar's window borderless (#2246)
author: roaldosulejmani
body:
## Problem

On some Windows systems (reported: Windows 10 LTSB, Intel HD Graphics 4600, 1366x768), the custom title bar's window shows black bars at its top-left and the pointer no longer matches what it points at -- hovering the Lasso highlights the Crop tool. Present since 0.5.0 (#2246).

## Cause

winit 0.30 gives an undecorated window `WS_CAPTION | WS_BORDER` and hides the non-client area by spreading the client rect over it (`WM_NCCALCSIZE`, rust-windowing/winit#2419). On affected systems the desktop compositor still reserves that frame for the window surface, so the content is drawn offset by the caption and border (~8, 30 px) while input stays at the client origin: black bars at the top-left, and a pointer offset by the same amount. winit 0.27 omitted those styles for undecorated windows, which is why 0.5.0 (custom title bar, #986) regressed.

## Fix

`apps/photocraft/src/window_frame.rs` strips `WS_CAPTION | WS_BORDER` from the window and has Windows recalculate the frame (`SetWindowPos(SWP_FRAMECHANGED)`), keeping `WS_THICKFRAME` and the window buttons so edge resizing and Aero snap keep working -- restoring winit 0.27's undecorated behaviour. The guard runs every frame from `raw_input_hook` (a new `Services::window_frame` hook), so a style winit restores on a flag change (maximize, restore, ...) is taken off again. Decorated windows (Preferences > Interface > System Title Bar) and non-Windows platforms are untouched.

All Win32 calls go through safe `winsafe` wrappers; no `unsafe` is added.

## Testing

- `apps/photocraft`: `window_frame::platform::tests` pins the style math (caption and border dropped, thick frame and window buttons kept).
- `crates/ui-egui`: `window_frame_tests` pins that the hook runs once per frame and is a no-op when unset.
- Verified on Windows against the live window: without the guard the undecorated window has `WS_CAPTION` (`style = 0x17CF0000`); with it `WS_CAPTION` is gone (`style = 0x170F0000`), the custom title bar sits flush …

title: fix(vector): Stroke Path refuses pixel-locked and fully locked layers (#2388)
author: KausBoss
body:
Fixes #2388.

## What was wrong
Stroke Path only read the destination's **transparency** lock. Brush, Pencil and Eraser strokes therefore painted on a layer whose pixels were locked, or that had Lock All set, including when the lock came from a parent group. Fill Path and ordinary painting already refuse that destination.

## Fix
`path_stroke` now checks `effective_locks` (the layer's own locks plus its groups') for `pixels || all` and returns the same "layer is locked" error as Fill Path. The layer is left unchanged and no history step is recorded. Transparency-lock behaviour, including the Eraser painting the background colour on the Background, is unchanged.

## Tests
- `stroke_path_refuses_a_locked_layer_or_group` in `crates/engine/tests/filter_locked.rs` covers Brush, Pencil and Eraser × pixel lock and Lock All × lock on the layer or on its parent group. It asserts an error and identical pixels. It fails without the fix: Brush returned `Ok` with damage on a pixel-locked layer.
- `stroke_path_still_runs_on_an_unlocked_layer` is the control case.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` all pass.

title: fix(vector): Fill Path stays inside the active selection (#2387)
author: KausBoss
body:
Fixes #2387.

## What was wrong
Fill Path painted the whole work path on the target layer even when a selection excluded part of it. Rectangular, elliptical and feathered selections had no effect on the fill.

## Fix
`path_fill` now multiplies the path's coverage, after anti-aliasing and the fill's own feather, by the active selection mask over the same area. This uses `photocraft_algo::selection::mask_from_surface`, the same read used elsewhere. Soft selection edges therefore scale the fill. With no active selection, behaviour is unchanged and the whole path fills.

## Tests
- `fill_path_stays_inside_the_selection` in `crates/engine/src/vector_cmds/tests.rs` covers hard rectangle, ellipse and feathered (4 px) selections at 8, 16 and 32 bit. It checks that pixels inside are filled, that pixels outside stay at alpha 0, that the fill's alpha never exceeds the selection's coverage along the edge and corners, and that undo restores the layer. It also checks that a fill with no selection still covers the whole path. The test fails without the fix ("outside the selection").
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `panic_hunt -- --ignored` all pass.

title: fix(engine): list running jobs before ended ones in jobs.list (#2395)
author: KausBoss
body:
Fixes #2395.

## What was wrong
`Session::jobs_with_recent` is documented as "Running jobs followed by the last few that ended (newest last)", but its code chained the ended jobs first. As a result, `jobs.list` (control channel, CLI `serve`) and MCP `jobs_list` returned a finished job ahead of a running one.

## Fix
The chain order is swapped: running jobs come first, then the recently ended ones (oldest to newest). This is a one-line change. The job IDs, states and results are unchanged.

## Tests
- `jobs_list_puts_running_jobs_before_ended_ones` in `crates/engine/src/jobs_tests.rs` finishes one gated job, starts a second one on another document, and asserts that `jobs.list` returns `[running, done]` in that order. It fails without the fix.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`, `cargo test -p photocraft-automation jobs` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` all pass.

title: Fix desktop save paths and preserve linked Smart Object edits
author: alirexa
body:
MCP-opened documents retained relative paths as desktop save destinations. When the macOS app started with `/` as its working directory, Cmd+S tried to write at the filesystem root, and Edit Contents could not find relative linked sources. Linked contents saves could embed the source, write edits after Don't Save, or overwrite competing editors without refreshing other open mockups.

This change records canonical desktop document identities while keeping automation I/O within its granted read/write roots. Relative and absolute requests beneath the configured root share the same desktop identity, including symlinked roots; implicit Save remains scoped to the canonical write root. Flat automation exports remain copies and preserve the original layered document's path and dirty state. Relative Smart Object sources resolve beside their owning document, including nested contents editors, and Relink to File opens a picker bound to the original document and layer.

Linked contents save atomically in the original source format and retain their links. Byte hashes reject sources changed since the editor opened or last saved. Each successful save prepares and refreshes all open instances with their individual placement, filters and depth; busy documents or failed renders abort before writing.

The branch incorporates upstream's shared Smart Object identities and current file-picker/save-copy/close-tab behavior. Embedded duplicates share edits, and a surviving duplicate remains editable after the originating layer is deleted. Close All and Quit answer contents editors before dirty parents, close each answered tab immediately, and retain document/revision-scoped Don't Save confirmations. Cancellation keeps unanswered documents open; a failed close retains its editor and prompt. Mockups dirtied by contents saves receive their own confirmation.

## Validation

Updated against upstream main `97136485`.

- Affected-crate unit tests: desktop 94, automation 56, engine 1,209, UI 1,831 …

title: Speed up large feathered mask refreshes
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What changed

Large documents with several feathered masks repeatedly evicted their combined masks from the 512 MiB LRU, forcing expensive full-canvas rebuilds during redraw. This keeps derived mask coverage in U16 tiles (at most 1/65535 quantization error) and raises the accounted cache cap to 768 MiB, enough for five 6336×7920 masks with U8 input and U16 output tiles. The separable box blur now works on contiguous rows, with bounded scoped threads and a blocked transpose; it preserves the sequential arithmetic and falls back if transpose storage cannot be reserved.

## Evidence

- Synthetic 6336×7920 blur: sequential 705.8 ms; parallel 451.2 ms (1.56× faster). This measures the blur component, not a complete redraw of the reporter's PSB.
- Cache accounting regression test verifies five issue-sized entries remain resident.
- Matching parallel/sequential output regression test exercises the threaded path.
- The reported PSB fixture was not available locally for end-to-end reproduction.

title: fix(layers): preserve Background behavior across merge, duplication and canvas resize
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fix three related inconsistencies in PhotoCraft's Background-layer
behavior across Merge Down, Duplicate Layer, and Canvas Size.

These operations should preserve the distinction between a locked
Background and an ordinary editable layer.

## Problems

### 1. Merge Down loses Background locks (#2380)

Merging a normal pixel layer onto Background removes its transparency
and position locks.

Consequently:
- Clear and Cut erase pixels to transparency.
- The resulting Background can be moved.
- Layer From Background becomes unavailable.

### 2. Multi-layer duplication retains Background locks (#2381)

Duplicating Background individually correctly produces an unlocked
ordinary layer.

However, duplicating Background together with other selected layers
leaves Background copy locked, preventing movement.

### 3. Transparent canvas extensions cannot be painted (#2384)

Extending an opaque Background using a transparent Canvas Size
extension preserves its Background classification.

The newly transparent region cannot be painted normally because
the layer's transparency lock remains enabled.

## Implementation

### Merge Down

Preserve the lower layer's editing locks when constructing the
merged raster layer.

This restores Background behavior without unnecessarily locking
ordinary merged layers.

### Duplicate Layer

Reuse the existing shared layer_copy implementation for multi-layer
duplication.

This ensures:
- Background copies become ordinary unlocked layers.
- Other duplicated layers retain their original lock settings.
- Single-layer and multi-layer duplication behave consistently.

### Canvas Size

Convert Background into a normal editable layer when a transparent
extension introduces new canvas area.

Reuse the existing Background conversion behavior.

Opaque extensions and no-op resizes retain the original Background
classification.

## Regression coverage

Added five integration-test functions covering:

- Merge Down onto Background.
- Background iden…

title: Save and export dialogs remember where each document was last saved (#1826)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Closes #1826.

## What

#1866 already starts Save As and export dialogs beside the document. This adds the second half of #1826: after the user navigates a save or export dialog somewhere else, that document's next dialog starts there.

`pick_save` records the folder of every path chosen in a save/export dialog, for the document the dialog was asked for (not whichever is active when the answer arrives), and uses it for the document's next bare-name dialog: exports, Save for Web, an untitled Save As. Precedence:

1. a caller's explicit directory
2. the folder this document was last saved or exported to
3. beside the document (#1866)
4. the shell's default

Save As of a saved document still suggests its own path, as before. The memory is session-only (`PhotocraftApp::save_dirs`, keyed by `DocId`), pruned of closed documents at the next dialog, and ignores the web's download-name answers, which carry no folder.

## Changes

- `crates/ui-egui/src/file_dialog.rs`: `pick_save` consults and updates the per-document folder.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`: the `save_dirs` field.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/file_dialog/tests.rs`: `save_dialogs_remember_where_each_document_was_last_saved` covers the export → remembered folder flow, Save As keeping the document path, cancelled dialogs and explicit directories changing nothing, per-document isolation, the answer landing on the document it was asked for, and pruning on close.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`: 1636 passed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo xtask wasm`: ok

Not included: a global "last save folder" for brand-new untitled documents (Photoshop's behaviour); that would be a separate preference.

title: fix(psd): an unedited save writes Photoshop's Txt2 back unchanged (#2374)
author: vivekprojects-GIT
body:
Fixes #2374 (Photoshop refuses a PSD that PhotoCraft re-saved without edits, but only when the file has type layers).

**Cause.** Since #1517 (optical kerning round trip), every PSD save with type layers rebuilds the document-wide `Txt2` block in `photocraft_text::psd::build_txt2`, even when nothing was edited. The per-layer `TySh` was still written back byte for byte, but the rebuilt `Txt2`:
- replaced everything under `/1` with just the text-object list (`outer.set("1", { /1: slots })`), dropping the other keys Photoshop stores there
- emptied every object that no layer's `TextIndex` names into `<< >>`
- replaced each kept object's style runs (`/0 /6 /0`) with stubs that hold only the auto-kern mode (`/0 () /6 << /0 0 /11 mode >>`). Every other style key in those runs was lost, while the object's other data (e.g. `/21` glyph positions, paragraph runs) still described the original runs.
- re-encoded the whole block: Latin-1 strings were rewritten as UTF-16, and decimals were rounded to 5 places

**Fix.** `build_txt2` now starts from the file's own block:
- the other keys under `/1`, and objects no layer names, are kept as they are
- a kept object (same text) keeps its own style runs. Only `/11` is set on each run, and a run is split where a mode change falls inside it. If the file's runs don't cover the text, generated runs are used as before.
- if the rebuilt content equals the file's block, the original bytes are returned unchanged. So an unedited save writes `Txt2` byte for byte, as it did before #1517.

Optical kerning still round-trips (`build_txt2_round_trips_kerning_modes`, `txt2_carries_optical_kerning` and `crates/io/tests/psd_kerning.rs` are unchanged and pass).

New tests in `crates/text/src/tests.rs`, using a `Txt2` shaped like Photoshop's (`/1 /0` settings, `/1 /2`, full style runs, a Latin-1 string, decimals, an unnamed object):
- `unchanged_txt2_is_written_back_byte_for_byte`: Metrics-only and Optical cases
- `edited_txt2_keeps_the_files_styles_and_o…

title: fix(document): restore layer comps when duplicating documents
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fix layer-comp references when duplicating documents through
Image Duplicate and History → New Document.

Also correct related inconsistencies involving historical states,
nested layers, Last Document State, and merged-only duplication.

## Problem

Both document duplication paths generate new layer IDs but retain
layer-comp records referencing the original IDs.

Consequently, applying a copied layer comp reports missing layers
and fails to restore the recorded visibility, position, and appearance.

Merged-only duplicates also retain layer-comp metadata even though
the original layer structure has been discarded.

## Changes

### 1. Preserve layer-comp references

Introduce a shared helper that:

- Generates fresh identities for copied layers.
- Remaps recorded layer-comp references.
- Handles nested groups and their children.
- Preserves genuinely missing-layer references and warnings.

### 2. Preserve Last Document State

Update Last Document State references to target copied layers.

This allows the copied document to restore its own recorded layout
without affecting the original document.

### 3. Fix merged-only duplicates

When duplicating a flattened document:

- Remove obsolete layer comps.
- Clear stale last-applied-comp references.
- Remove invalid Last Document State metadata.

The original document remains unchanged.

### 4. Add regression coverage

Five new integration tests cover:

- Image Duplicate and History New Document.
- Copies created from earlier history states.
- Nested layers and groups.
- Previously deleted layers.
- Last Document State restoration.
- Merged-only duplication.
- Original-document preservation.

checked upstream main, with no commits behind.

body:
### What happens

Over the control channel, `ui.key` with `ctrl` never matches a keyboard shortcut on Linux or
Windows. The call succeeds, and nothing happens:

```
ui.key {"key": "N", "ctrl": true}       -> {"ok": true}, no dialog
ui.key {"key": "N", "command": true}    -> {"ok": true}, New Document opens
```

Plain keys work either way (`{"key": "M"}` picks the Marquee), so only the Ctrl modifier is
affected. `docs/control-protocol.md` documents `ui.key {key, command?, shift?, alt?, ctrl?}`
without saying that off the Mac a shortcut needs `command`, so `ctrl: true` is the natural thing
to send from Linux, and it fails silently.

### Why

`control.rs` built the modifiers with `command` and `ctrl` as independent fields. Off the Mac they
are the same physical key, and egui expects both to carry the same value:

> `Modifiers::command` — "On Windows and Linux, set this to the same value as `ctrl`."
> `Modifiers::ctrl` — "When checking for keyboard shortcuts, consider using `Self::command`
> instead."

A real Ctrl press arrives with both set, so shortcuts are matched on `command`. A synthetic event
with `ctrl: true` and `command: false` is a state that cannot occur off the Mac, and it matches
nothing.

### The change

One `modifiers_from` helper for both `ui.key` and `ui.pointer`: off the Mac `ctrl` and `command`
are paired, so either flag reaches the same shortcuts; on the Mac they stay apart, with `command`
as ⌘ and `ctrl` as the Control key. Callers already sending `command: true` are unaffected.

### Tested

New unit test covering both platforms, grouped and top-level flags, no modifier, and shift+alt.
Verified by hand on Arch Linux (Hyprland, Wayland, 0.6.0 release build): before the change
`ui.key {"key":"N","ctrl":true}` did nothing; after it, New Document opens, same as
`command: true`.

Gates, on this branch rebased onto main:

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` — 1552 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warni…

title: Quick Selection: 3.5x faster CPU strokes with hybrid graph cuts
author: excited-raccoon
body:
## What this fixes

Quick Selection was spending most of a large stroke in repeated max-flow path
augmentation. Painting across a 24-36 MP document now takes about 0.2 seconds
in the measured raster stroke pipeline, down from about 0.75 seconds.

## Change

- Use FIFO push/relabel for large finite graphs with both terminal directions.
  Exact global distances to both terminals keep discharge and source return moving.
- Keep BK for small graphs and one-terminal graphs.
- Skip fixed/fixed edge weights. Sparse boundary graphs merge five sorted
  source-pixel streams, keeping the original edge order and terminal accumulation.
- Keep the fitted selection energy, brush rules, working resolution and refinement bands.

## Measured results

Release on c7i.4xlarge, 16 vCPUs. Full CPU stroke calls through the editor's
raster sampler, including depth conversion, sampling, distance costs, graph

title: fix(docs): Linux build prerequisites only name Debian packages
author: Erica4fr
body:
### What happens

`docs/development.md` › Prerequisites lists the Linux libraries with Debian package names only:

> Linux needs `libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev
> libgtk-3-dev`

On Arch none of those names exist — `pacman -S` fails on the whole line — and on Fedora they all
need `-devel`. Nothing anywhere else in the repository gives the equivalents, so you are left
translating seven package names before your first build.

Meanwhile the app itself already speaks four distros at runtime: `apps/photocraft/src/linux_libs.rs`
carries a `{soname, debian, fedora, arch, suse}` table, reads `ID` and `ID_LIKE` from
`/etc/os-release`, and prints `sudo apt install`, `sudo dnf install`, `sudo pacman -S` or
`sudo zypper install` as appropriate when a runtime library is missing. This brings the build
instructions up to what the code already does.

Also adds the prerequisites to `book/src/getting-started/building.md`, which currently says only
"Install the stable Rust toolchain" — the book is what the README points to as the documentation,
and on Linux that page sends you into `cargo build` with nothing installed.

### Verified

Package names checked rather than copied: Arch with `pacman -Q` on a working machine (all seven
installed, and the release build succeeds on it), Fedora and openSUSE with `dnf list` and
`zypper info` in clean containers. The runtime table in `linux_libs.rs` covers shared libraries
loaded at run time, not development packages, so the names are not simply copied from it.

title: Open file pickers for Replace Contents, Export Contents and Convert to Linked
author: fabianghe
body:
From the menu, **Layer › Smart Objects › Replace Contents…**, **Export Contents…** and **Convert to Linked…** failed with "pass `path`", because no file dialog was wired to them. You could only use them from scripts. This is the step a template user needs: for example, swapping their own art into a Steam store asset template's smart objects.

## Changes
- **Replace Contents…** opens a file picker. The engine receives the picked file's name and bytes (`smart_cmds::replace_contents_bytes`), so the picker also works on the web build. With #2222's shared contents, every instance updates in one undo step. A file that can't be decoded reports an error and changes nothing.
- **Export Contents…** opens a save dialog that suggests the contents' own file name (e.g. `Layer 1.pcraft`, `Logo.psb`). It writes through `Services::write`, the same path Save a Copy uses.
- **Convert to Linked…** opens a save dialog for where to write the contents, then runs the existing command with that path.
- New engine helper `smart_cmds::contents_of`, which `export_contents` now also uses.
- **Relink to File…** is unchanged; #2416 adds its picker.

## Tests
Three new tests in `ui-egui/src/file_dialog/tests.rs`:
- Replace Contents: cancelling leaves the contents unchanged; picking a file replaces the contents of both instances; a file that isn't an image fails with an error.
- Export Contents: the suggested name, and the path that gets written.
- Convert to Linked: the contents file is written, and every instance is linked to it.

Checks run:

title: Opening card: a long file name no longer pushes Cancel out of the card (#2423)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Closes #2423.

## Problem

While a document opens, the canvas shows an "Opening {name}" card. `open_card` painted a fixed 340×132 card and laid the rows out in it with no height constraint, so a title that wrapped (a long file name, or a long translation of "Opening {name}" or the job message) pushed the percentage and Cancel below the card's bottom edge, onto the backdrop.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/photocraft/pr-assets/2423/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/photocraft/pr-assets/2423/after.png) |

Rendered offscreen at 2× with a gated open job named `a7rv-test_2024_02_17_shot_30_3705_with_an_even_longer_suffix_that_never_ends.psb`.

## Fix

- The title and the message are single-line `Label::truncate()` labels, so a long name ends in "…" and egui shows the full text on hover.
- The card background and border are added as `Shape::Noop` placeholders, the rows are laid out, then the shapes are set from the content rect. The card grows from the 132 pt minimum to fit its rows, so a tall message or button row (long translations) still gets a card. It is centred at the height it needed last frame and settles in one repaint.
- The card's rects are recorded in egui temp data so tests can check the layout (`jobs_ui::open_card_rects`).

## Test

`jobs_ui::tests::the_opening_card_keeps_a_long_name_and_cancel_inside` stages an open tab on a gated job with a short and a long name, and asserts the title is one line, keeps the card's padding, and that both the title and Cancel lie inside the card. On the old layout it fails at the one-line check (the title wrapped to three lines).

## Checks

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`: 1641 passed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo xtask wasm`: ok

title: GPU canvas: re-upload a layer or mask texture when its default pixel changes (#2422)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2422.

`Compositor::sync` decided whether a resident layer or mask texture was stale from its region, kind, format and CMYK space only. Tiles the surface doesn't store are written into the texture only when it is created, as the default pixel. A command that changes a surface's default without touching those absent tiles (Invert on a sparse mask, mask Reveal/Hide All, Fill on an empty layer) left them neither "changed" nor "gone", so the GPU kept the old default there: the staircase of blocks in the issue. The CPU compositor and saved files were already correct.

`Resident` now records the bit pattern of the surface's default pixel, and a different default makes the texture stale, so it is rebuilt with the new default in every absent tile. `default_nonzero` is computed from the same pixel. This is the first option the issue suggests. A rebuild only happens when the default actually changes, which these commands do once, so normal painting is unaffected. The fix is in the shared `sync` path, so layer and mask textures are both covered, in whole-texture and paged rendering.

Test: `changed_mask_default_updates_absent_tiles` in `crates/gpu/tests/parity.rs` renders a layer whose mask stores tiles only in two opposite corners (so the resident texture spans absent tiles between them) with default 0, then with default 1, and compares the GPU against the CPU compositor, unpaged and paged. Without the fix the second render keeps 0 in the absent tiles and fails.

title: Remove tool: an empty layer is a no-op instead of running the fill (#2435)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2435.

With Sample All Layers off, the Remove tool reads only the target layer. On an empty layer the window around the stroke is fully transparent, so there is nothing to remove and nothing to fill from. `run_remove` still ran the whole patch completion on it (15 s for the large stroke in the issue) and `remove` then added a "Remove" history step that changed nothing.

`run_remove` now checks the window it reads from the target layer before the fill. If Sample All Layers is off, the layer has alpha and every pixel in the window has alpha 0, it returns `None` and `remove` answers `{"changed": false}` without calling `s.edit`. The job ends at once, before the fill, and no history step is added.

It is a no-op and not an error to match the other retouch tools: Spot Healing, Blur, Sharpen and Smudge on an empty layer with Sample All Layers off succeed and change nothing (`retouch_ui::tests::sample_all_layers_reaches_the_command` checks exactly that for all five tools, Remove included). `{"changed": false}` is the reply other commands already use for a no-op (`warp_cmds`, `distort_cmds`, `select_extra_cmds`).

What does not change:
- Sample All Layers on: the fill reads the composite, so an empty layer can still take a removal of the image below.
- Targets without alpha (a background layer, a layer mask, a channel) and layers with any content in the window: no change.

Test: `remove_on_an_empty_layer_is_a_no_op_without_a_history_step` adds an empty layer over the test image and strokes it with the Remove tool. The call returns `{"changed": false}` and the history length stays the same. The same stroke with `sampleAllLayers: true` adds one step. Without the fix the first call returns a damage rect and adds a step, so the test fails.

title: OpenEXR/HDR export: linearize grayscale documents too (#2386)
author: itsF4LCON
body:
TLDR:

Fixes #2386. OpenEXR and Radiance HDR export linearized RGB documents but not grayscale ones, so an sGray `#808080` was written as 0.502 instead of the linear 0.216 that the same RGB colour gets. The import side then read a grayscale EXR's `Y` as untagged sGray, so PhotoCraft's own round trip hid the error, while every other reader saw it too bright.

The cause is in `flat::export_flat`: the EXR/HDR branch converts through `convert_rgb`, which returns `None` for gray layouts, so gray samples were written as stored. Import only tagged `ColorMode::Rgb` files as linear.

Changes:

- `io/flat.rs`, export: a gray image is converted from its profile (sGray when untagged) to linear gray as 32-bit float, as RGB already is to linear sRGB. The RGB and gray paths share the transform code (`convert_from`). A grayscale EXR keeps its single `Y` channel; HDR has no gray layout, so the codec writes R=G=B as before.
- `io/flat.rs`, import: an untagged grayscale OpenEXR is tagged linear gray. OpenEXR's `Y` is linear luminance by spec, so files from other apps open correctly too, not just PhotoCraft's.
- `cms/builtin.rs`: `linear_gray()`, a gray profile with a linear tone curve. It's a plain function next to `srgb()` rather than a `Builtin` variant, so it doesn't appear in the profile lists or settings.
- `engine/color_cmds.rs`: the open policy already keeps 32-bit documents tagged linear sRGB without a mismatch prompt; linear gray is now kept the same way. Without this, opening a grayscale EXR would start asking about a profile mismatch, which it didn't do before.
- `book/src/formats/raster-formats.md`: notes linear gray for grayscale OpenEXR.

Tests:

- `io/tests/flat.rs`, `gray_exr_and_hdr_store_linear_light`: decodes the exported bytes and checks that the stored samples are the linear value, for grayscale and an RGB control, in EXR and HDR, at 8/16/32-bit. It fails on main with the issue's numbers (`0.502` vs `0.216`).
- `io/tests/flat.rs`, `gray_exr_round_trips`: a graysca…

title: fix(codecs): exports drop the source's EXIF thumbnail (#2147, #2373)
author: vivekprojects-GIT
body:
Fixes #2147 and #2373: exported images show the original, unedited photo as their thumbnail (macOS Finder, Android's browser, Instagram's file picker), while opening the file shows the edit.

**Cause.** Exports copy the source's EXIF, patching only Orientation and the resolution (`export_exif`). Camera JPEGs, and files saved by most editors, keep a small JPEG thumbnail in EXIF IFD1, which IFD0's next-IFD pointer names. Finder, Android and upload pickers show that embedded thumbnail rather than decoding the image, so an edited photo kept its original preview. #2373 describes exactly this: a photo saved in black and white still had a colour thumbnail.

**Fix.** `export_exif` now unlinks IFD1 by clearing IFD0's next-IFD pointer (`exif_without_thumbnail` in `crates/codecs/src/resolution.rs`).
- Nothing else moves, so every other offset in the block stays valid. The rest of the EXIF (camera, lens, exposure, date and so on) is kept.
- Readers then build the thumbnail from the image itself.
- Every writer that embeds EXIF goes through `export_exif`: JPEG, PNG, WebP, and the PSD EXIF resource. They are all fixed by this one change.
- An EXIF block without a thumbnail, or one that doesn't parse, is returned unchanged (borrowed).

**Tests** (`crates/codecs/tests/resolution.rs`), little- and big-endian:
- `exports_drop_the_source_exif_thumbnail`:
  - IFD1 is unlinked with and without a resolution rewrite, and with an `Exif\0\0` prefix
  - only the 4 pointer bytes differ from the input, and the length is unchanged
  - a thumbnail-free EXIF stays borrowed
  - JPEG, PNG and WebP exports carry no IFD1
- `thumbnail_removal_never_panics_on_truncated_exif`: every truncation of the block

The first test fails on `main`, and the second passes on both.

Checked: `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

Not in scope: XMP can also carry a legacy `xmp:Thumbnails` image. I haven't seen Finder …

title: Image Size: Photoshop's resampling, measured
author: Unemars
body:
**Problem.** Image Size's resampling was not Photoshop's.
- Bicubic was Catmull-Rom (a = −0.5). Photoshop's is sharper.
- Bicubic Smoother, Bicubic Sharper and Automatic were missing. The interpolation preference's Bicubic Sharper opened the dialog on Lanczos.
- Bilinear and every bicubic shrank differently from Photoshop. Shrinking by more than 4× in particular did not match.

On 225 probes compared with Photoshop 25.4 (16-bit, in levels of 32768), the mean error per method was 240–550. On hard edges the error reached 14,700, nearly half the range. In 8-bit RGB the mean error was 3–13 levels.

**How Photoshop resamples.** Photoshop 25.4 was measured as a black box: synthetic 16-bit images went through Image › Image Size by script, and the results were read back exactly. Every method except Preserve Details' enlargement turned out to be linear. Each method was therefore taken apart through its response to single pixels. No Photoshop code or assets were used.

| | Photoshop 25.4 |
|---|---|
| Position | Output pixel i reads x = (i + 0.5)/s − 0.5. Its fraction is rounded to 1/128 pixel. At the canvas edge, x stops at the first or last pixel centre. |
| Nearest Neighbor | Input pixel floor((i + 0.5)/s). |
| Bilinear | A tent that is never widened. Below half size, each output pixel is the plain average of the input pixels floor(i/s) … floor((i+1)/s) − 1. |
| Bicubic | The Keys cubic with a = −0.75, widened by 1/s when reducing. |
| Bicubic Smoother | Keys stretched ×1.15. a = −0.625 when enlarging, −0.625 − 0.5·(1 − s) when reducing. |
| Bicubic Sharper | Keys stretched ×1.05. a = −1 when enlarging, −1 − 1.6·(1 − s) when reducing. |
| Below ¼ | The bicubic filters first average the image down to four times the target, then filter at ¼. |
| Two axes | Two passes, the smaller scale first. The image is clipped between them, and 8-bit images are rounded too. The bicubic filter is designed for the height's scale (the width's when the height stays) and serves both axes. So h…

title: Google Fonts: install fonts from inside PhotoCraft (Find More tab, Resolve Missing Fonts download)
author: kntrttm
body:
Draft: the font index hosting and the network-access policy are still open in #1135. The index URL and sha256 are unpinned, so a build without `PHOTOCRAFT_FONT_INDEX_FILE` reports "the Google Fonts index is not configured in this build". Nothing goes online by default.

## What this adds
- **Index (no network):** `cargo xtask fonts-index` builds a schema-1 JSON index from a pinned `google/fonts` checkout. It reads METADATA.pb, sha256-hashes every file, and records axes and PostScript names (including fvar named instances). `photocraft_text::catalog` validates the index (rejecting the whole thing on any bad path, sha, size, weight or URL) and provides search and PostScript lookup.
- **Engine commands:**
  - `type.fonts.catalog`
  - `type.fonts.install`: a background job with progress and cancel
  - `type.fonts.installed`
  - `type.fonts.remove`: refuses a font in use unless `force` is given
  - `type.resolveMissingFonts` now lists `downloadable` fonts and takes `{download: true}`
- **New L6 crate `photocraft-fontfetch`:**
  - Downloads with ureq + rustls (no tokio, no OpenSSL), HTTPS only.
  - Timeouts, a hard size cap, and cancel.
  - Tries jsDelivr first, then raw.githubusercontent.com.
  - Stores fonts app-privately in `config_dir()/Fonts/Google/<slug>/`, with the licence file and a manifest, swapped in atomically.
  - Installed fonts are registered from disk at startup, with no network.
- **UI:**
  - A Find More tab in the font picker, modelled on Photoshop's Adobe Fonts tab: search, category and language filters, per-row progress and cancel, and a note on variable fonts.
  - A consent card shown on first use.
  - A Resolve Missing Fonts dialog with "Download from Google Fonts".
  - Preferences › Type › Manage downloaded fonts.
  - All new strings are translated in the 12 complete catalogs.

## Safety
- **Opt-in:** `type.allowOnlineFonts` is off by default. MCP and control clients cannot enable it; the guard is in automation. The CLI needs `--allow-online-fonts`,…

title: fix(ui): keep menus responsive on documents with thousands of layers
author: m6502
body:
## Problem

  With a PSD of 3,593 layers open (800×480, nested 8 deep), every menu ran at 1–2 fps. While a menu is open, the menu bar rebuilds its 809 items each frame, and that took about 700 ms.

  Each item's enabled/checked check looks up the active layer several times (`menus::is_enabled`, `enable_rules::disabled`, `with_mask_target`, the engine's `enabled` closures). `Document::layer` built the whole layer list through `walk()`, allocating a path per layer, for every one of those lookups: about 265 µs
  each, roughly 2,600 times per frame.

  ## Fix

  - **Direct layer lookup** (`crates/doc`): `Document::layer` and `path_of` search the tree without building the layer list.
  - **Menu item cache** (`crates/ui-egui`): an open menu reuses its items between frames. They are rebuilt when `native_menu::state_hash` changes, or on a frame with a click or key press, the same policy the macOS native menu already uses. Nothing is kept once the menus close, and the hash is only computed while one
  is open.
  - `state_hash` now also covers a running background job, since that greys commands on its document.

  ## Numbers

  Release build, on the 3,593-layer PSD:

  | | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | One `Document::layer` lookup | 265 µs | 23 µs |
  | One `menu_items` build | ~700 ms | ~87 ms |
  | Frames while a menu stays open | one build each | reuse the last build |

  ## Tests

  - `layer_lookup_agrees_with_walk`: `layer`, `layer_mut` and `path_of` match `walk()` at every depth and miss cleanly.
  - `an_open_menu_reuses_its_items_until_the_state_changes`: no rebuild on idle frames, a rebuild when a document opens under the open menu, nothing kept after closing.

  Ran: `cargo test -p photocraft-doc -p photocraft-ui-egui` (57 + 1,552 unit tests and all 20 UI integration test files pass), `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on both crates, `cargo xtask layers`.

  ## Not done

  - `cargo xtask wasm` was not run locally: the wasm32 target is not installed o…

title: Fix false contours in the pixel grid at high zoom
author: ssh-den
body:
The pixel grid creates false contours in smooth image regions because
its color abruptly switches from white to black at luminance 0.55.
Nearby pixels receive opposite overlays, exaggerating small tonal
differences into visible patches.

This follows #1891, which aligned the CPU grid with the GPU grid's
content-alpha behavior after the earlier grid work in #1491. The
luminance-dependent color rule was shared by both rendering paths.

### Changes

- Use a uniform white overlay on both CPU and GPU canvases.
- Draw CPU grid strokes at one physical pixel rather than one egui
  point, matching the intended thickness on scaled displays.
- Preserve the existing zoom threshold, transparency handling and
  caching.

### Validation

- UI crate tests: 1,649 passed, 8 ignored.
- Regression coverage: CPU/GPU, display scales 1x/2x, 8/16/32-bit
  images, fractional and integer zoom.
- 711.9% is a regression test input from the reported screenshot;
  production code contains no special case for that zoom.
- Desktop release build, layer checks, wasm checks and quick
  performance checks passed.
- Offscreen CPU/GPU snapshots inspected at both display scales.
- Changed-file formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

Repository-wide formatting fails in unchanged `prefs_ui.rs`.
Strict clippy fails on existing warnings in `affinity` and unchanged
UI code; no reported warning points to the modified files.

Selection outlines and Smart Guides may have similar coordinate
rounding issues, but are outside this PR's scope.

title: Tests: one integration-test binary per crate (#2204)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #2204 (proposal 3: one integration-test binary per crate). Proposals 1, 2 and 4 are in #2414; the two PRs don't conflict and can merge in either order.

## Why
Every `tests/*.rs` file links its own test binary, which costs seconds of link time each: ~13 s CPU per io binary and ~39 s per ui-egui binary (measured in #2204). This follows https://matklad.github.io/2021/02/27/delete-cargo-integration-tests.html.

## Change
- `crates/<crate>/tests/*.rs` moved (`git mv`, so history follows the renames) into modules of one `tests/it` binary per crate: io 47 files, engine 32, ui-egui 20, codecs 19, psd 7, format 6, raw 6, automation 5, cms 3, gpu 3.
- Each old file stays its own module file (`tests/it/<name>.rs`). `tests/it/main.rs` only declares the modules, so the tests read the same as before (echelon's concern in #2204).
- Shared helpers (`common/`, `support/`) became modules of the binary. In each file, `mod common;` became `use crate::common;`.
- **GPU lock:** ui-egui and gpu now have one shared `support::gpu_lock()` instead of a private lock per file, because per-file locks would not serialize across files in one process. Every test that creates a wgpu device or a `.wgpu()` harness takes it. Several took no lock before (checker_canvas, arbitrary_rotation_preview, full_res_preview, drag_preview_canvas, …). The last two are the files #2204 saw crash with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` under `cargo test` on Windows.
- **Separate binaries:** engine `text_gamma.rs` (process-wide text gamma) and `mask_cache_purge.rs` (exact byte counts of the process-wide mask cache) stay separate, with the reason at their top.
- **New test names:** tests now carry a `<module>::` prefix. Commands in AGENTS.md, docs, the book, READMEs and test comments use `--test it <module>::` (e.g. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test it panic_hunt -- --ignored`).
- **Scorecard:** xtask scorecard paths and the scorecard notes point at `tests/it/`; docs/scorecard.md is regenerated.
- **AGENTS.md rule…

title: Fix clipboard copy/cut/paste in the type tool's custom text editor
author: seldoms
body:
## Summary
- The type tool uses a custom text editor (not egui::TextEdit), so egui-winit never sends `Event::Copy`/`Cut`/`Paste` — it only does so when a standard text field has focus
- Cmd+C/X/V arrived as plain key presses that neither the type tool nor `shortcut_dispatch` handled (the type tool passed them through; `shortcut_dispatch` filtered them as `TEXT_OWNED`), so clipboard operations were completely lost while editing text
- When the custom text editor is active and no egui::TextEdit has focus, convert Cmd+C/X/V key presses into `Event::Copy`/`Event::Cut`/`RequestPaste` so the type tool's existing clipboard handlers see them

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a document, select the Type tool, create/edit a text layer
- [ ] Select some text, press Cmd+C — text should be copied to clipboard
- [ ] Press Cmd+V — clipboard text should be pasted into the text layer
- [ ] Select text, press Cmd+X — text should be cut to clipboard
- [ ] Verify Cmd+C/X/V still work normally in other contexts (image paste, panel search fields, etc.)

title: Let Edit > Fill and the fill keys fill an adjustment layer's mask (#2456)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2456.

With an adjustment layer's mask targeted, Edit › Fill (Shift+F5 / Shift+Backspace) and the fill keys (⌥⌫, ⌘⌫ and their ⇧ variants) were refused with "active layer is an Adjustment layer, not a pixel layer", although `routed()` already sends them to the mask target and `fill_cmds::fill` writes to it through `target_surface`.

The cause: the mask-target precondition override (`mask_target_enabled`) only covers the ids `edits_mask()` lists (Image › Adjustments and the filters), so `edit.fill` fell back to `has_pixel_or_channel`.

Changes:
- `edits_mask()` also lists `edit.fill` and `fill_key_cmds::IDS`, the same ids `routed()` sends to masks. With `"target":"mask"` they now need only a layer mask, exactly like ⌘I Invert on an adjustment layer's mask (#780). Without a mask target nothing changes: Fill on an adjustment layer is still refused.
- The `target` param docs of `edit.fill` and the fill keys now list `"mask"`, as the other routed commands' docs already do (`"pixels"|"mask"|"quickMask"|{"channel":i}`).

Test: `fill_works_on_an_adjustment_layers_mask` (engine, next to the #780 Invert test) makes a Curves layer, checks that Fill is still disabled without the mask target and enabled with it (also `edit.fillForeground`), then fills the mask black and white. It fails on `main` at the `is_enabled_with` assertion and with the reported error on `execute`.

title: Keep surrounding spaces when renaming a layer (#2459)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2459.

`layer.renameLayer` stored `name.trim()`, so renaming a layer to `"black skin bw "` lost the trailing space, while `layer.new.layer` keeps the name as given. Photoshop also keeps spaces in layer names, so actions that select a layer by its exact name failed after a PhotoCraft rename.

The command now stores the name unchanged. An empty or all-whitespace name is still rejected with the same `missing \`name\`` error as before.

Test: `rename_layer_keeps_surrounding_spaces` renames a layer to `" black skin bw "` and checks the exact name, then checks that `"   "` is rejected and leaves the name unchanged.

title: Skip distant TSL-off stroke layers during composition
author: Elvis33LE
body:
## What changed

Layers with `tsly=0` and only enabled, local stroke effects no longer allocate and composite across the full canvas. The compositor derives the affected bounds from the source content bounds plus stroke reach and skips unrelated tiles/bands. Knockout, Blend Interior, Blend If, enabled masks, clipped layers, non-local effects, and mixed/non-stroke effects retain the existing path.

This addresses the tall-document slowdown in #2102. On a 1920×103675 synthetic document matching the report, the release benchmark changed from 23.015s to 2.453s (3 layers, 9.4× faster) and from 40.500s to 4.978s (10 layers, 8.1× faster). Reproduce with `cargo run --release -p photocraft-compose --example bench_tsly_stroke`.

## Correctness and validation

Added exact pixel-equivalence tests comparing a full render with tiled and banded rendering across U8/U16/F32, Outside/Inside/Center strokes, four blend modes, three fill opacities, and Blend If on/off. Advanced blending and masks are explicitly verified to reject the optimization.

Passed: `cargo test -p photocraft-compose`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask test-corpus`, and `cargo xtask perf --quick`.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` reports an existing formatting difference in `crates/ui-egui/src/prefs_ui.rs` on the base branch; the changed Compose files are formatted. The quick performance run also reports several unrelated layout/move scenarios over budget on this Windows machine.

Fixes #2102

title: Ruler units keep their own decimal places (#2434)
author: bitshiftza
body:
Closes #2434.

## Problem

Document sizes were shown with one decimal place whatever the unit, so a 1234 px side at 300 ppi read `4.1 in` instead of `4.113 in`. Millimetres, centimetres and picas lost a place too.

Image Size in inches, 1234 × 800 px at 300 ppi:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/photocraft/pr-assets/2434/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/photocraft/pr-assets/2434/after.png) |

There were two separate culprits: the dialogs' value fields always used the shared one-decimal formatter, and `Unit::decimals` (which the Info panel readout uses) had its own wrong values, giving millimetres one place and inches two.

## Fix

`Unit::decimals` now follows Photoshop: whole pixels, one place for points, two for millimetres, centimetres and picas, three for inches.

New `prefs::fmt_decimals` rounds half away from zero and then drops trailing zeros, which is the "double rounding" the issue asks for: a value is never shown with more precision than it has, so `0.7995 in` reads `0.8`, never `0.799` or `0.800`, and a whole number keeps no trailing `.0`. It guards the zero-decimal case, so `550 px` cannot lose its zero to the trim.

Everything that shows a length in a unit now takes its precision from that one place:

- the Info panel, through `UnitsAndRulers::format`
- Image Size and Canvas Size, New Document, and the shape dialog, through the new `widgets::value_field_prec` and `widgets::unit_decimals`
- `widgets::fmt_num` and `fmt_num2` delegate to `fmt_decimals`, so the generic one- and two-place formatters stay in step

Percent keeps its single place. It was not in the report and reads better coarse, so I left it alone rather than guess.

## Tests

`prefs::tests::ruler_units_round_to_their_own_decimal_places` covers each unit's places, half-away-from-zero rounding on both signs, the trailing-zero trim, the `-0` and `550` guards, and the Info panel readout end to end. It fails on …

title: Free Transform: keep the layer's place in the stack (#2439)
author: Geljic
body:
Fixes #2439.

Ctrl+T on a layer that sits under other layers drew the moving pixels over the whole document, so the layer jumped to the top while the box was open. Photoshop keeps it in its place: the layers over it still cover it while you move, scale or rotate it.

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs`): the layers covering the moving one are composited **once**, on their own, when the session starts (and again if an edit changes the document while the box is open). That image is drawn over the moving pixels, and the canvas under the box leaves those layers out. The box itself still moves on the existing GPU mesh preview, so dragging, scaling and rotating cost the same per frame as before: no re-composite per frame.

Which layers cover it (`covering`): from the top of the stack down, the *plain* ones, meaning Normal layers that aren't adjustments, and Normal or Pass Through groups of them. Searching stops at the first layer that isn't plain (an adjustment layer, or Multiply, Screen and the other blend modes). That layer and everything under it stay in the canvas under the box exactly as today, because they depend on what is under them and drawing them over transparency would be wrong. So the preview is never worse than now:
- plain layers over the target (the common case): correct stacking;
- an adjustment or blend-mode layer at the top: unchanged from today's behaviour.

Clipping groups move as a whole. The layers clipped to the target stay with it under the box. Groups that hold the target are searched into, unless they use a blend mode other than Normal or Pass Through.

Not covered (left for follow-ups, as in #2439's second point): the moving layer's own blend mode in the preview, and adjustment/blend-mode layers above it applying to the moving pixels. Both need the moving pixels inside the compositor.

**Relation to #1999.** That draft fixes the same issue by compositing the transformed layer through the document compositor. It handles every blen…

title: Layer commands accept an explicit layer with none selected; Deselect Layers is a no-op when nothing is selected (#2457)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2457.

The issue reports two problems. This PR fixes both.

**1. An explicit `"layer"` is refused when no layer is selected.**
`Session::precondition` now accepts `layer.hideLayers`, `layer.showLayers` and `layer.renameLayer` when their `"layer"` param names a layer that exists in the active document. This applies to both `execute` and `is_enabled_with` / `disabled_reason_with`. The commands already find their layer through `layer_param`, so only the availability check changes. The rule follows the existing param-aware checks: `mask_target_enabled` (a mask target enables a command) and `smart_cmds::target_enabled` (a smart filter command checks the layer named in `"layer"`, not the active one). If the param is missing or names an unknown layer, these commands still use the old check, so `{"layer": 999999}` or `{}` with nothing selected still fails as before.

**2. Deselect Layers fails when nothing is selected.**
`select.deselectLayers` now needs only an open document (`has_doc`, as `select.allLayers` uses). When nothing is selected it does nothing and adds no history step, as in Photoshop.

**Tests:** I extended `layer_multi_cmds::tests::toggle_and_range_selection`. A second Deselect Layers succeeds and the history length stays the same. Then, with no layer selected, Hide Layers, Rename Layer and Show Layers run on an explicit layer. An unknown layer id fails, and so does a call with no `"layer"` param. These new assertions fail on `main`.

title: TGA: a 32-bit Targa opens with its alpha as "Alpha 1", as in Photoshop (#2225)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #2225 (the TGA part; PNG transparency already opens as Photoshop opens it).

Opening a 32-bit Targa turned its alpha into layer transparency. That hid the colours of transparent pixels, and since #2157 only an alpha channel becomes a Targa's alpha on save, so a TGA opened and saved again lost its alpha.

**Photoshop's behaviour, measured** on Photoshop 27.11 (Windows, scripted over COM; input files built byte by byte, results read from Photoshop's document and lossless PSD layer bytes):

| file | Photoshop opens it as |
|---|---|
| 32 bpp, 8 alpha bits; red; alpha 255 left / 0 right | opaque **Background** + **"Alpha 1"** = 255 / 0; colour red everywhere, nothing transparent |
| 32 bpp, alpha gradient 255→0 | same; Alpha 1 = 255 / 125 / 0 at x = 0 / 32 / 63 |
| 32 bpp, **0** alpha bits in the descriptor, same bytes | same: the 4th byte still becomes Alpha 1 |
| 24 bpp | Background only, no channel |
| Photoshop's own 32-bit save (alpha channel 255/128) | round-trips: Alpha 1 = 255 / 128 |

(The same harness first reproduced #2157's Save As measurements on 27.11, to make sure it reads Photoshop correctly.)

**Change**
- `io::flat::import_flat`: a Targa decoded as RGBA (every 32-bit Targa, whatever the alpha bits) opens as a locked, opaque Background with the stored colours, plus an "Alpha 1" channel with the alpha. Banded; no full-size float copy. 24-bit and grayscale Targas are unchanged.
- **Image sequences keep working:** video layers (`load_frames`) treat a frame's alpha as transparency, as footage does in Photoshop (Interpret Footage). For `.tga` frames, the new `io::tga_alpha_channel_to_transparency` moves the channel back before flattening; without it, a transparent TGA sequence would turn opaque.

**Tests**
- `tga_32_bit_opens_its_alpha_as_a_channel_like_photoshop`: the measured byte layouts (8 and 0 alpha bits, and 24 bpp).
- `tga_transparency_reopens_as_alpha_1`: replaces the `tga_rgba8` round trip, which expected transparency back.
- `tga_writes_the_…

title: Crop tool: W x H x Resolution mode resamples the crop to a size and resolution (#2443)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2443. (Part of #1919)

## Why
Photoshop's Crop tool has a "W x H x Resolution" mode: the width and height fields take units (4 in, 10 cm, 1024 px) next to a resolution in px/in or px/cm. The frame keeps W:H while you draw it, and committing resamples the crop to exactly that size and sets the document resolution. The preset menu also has built-in sizes (4 x 5 in 300 ppi, 1024 x 768 px 92 ppi, …) and Front Image (I), which copies the active document's size and resolution. PhotoCraft only had ratio presets.

## Change
- `image.crop` takes optional `targetWidth`/`targetHeight` (px), `resolution` (ppi) and `resample`. After the crop (also a turned crop) the area is resampled to exactly that size and the resolution is set, in the same undo step. Image Size's resampling and its megapixel budget are now shared helpers (`resample_doc`, `check_resample_budget`); Image Size's behaviour and error message are unchanged. Bad params return errors, nothing panics.
- Crop options bar (new `crop_size.rs`): "W x H x Resolution" in the preset menu, with unit-aware W/H fields (in, cm, mm, px, pt, pica; a bare number keeps the field's unit), a resolution field with px/in or px/cm, Photoshop's 8 built-in size presets, Front Image (menu or `I`), Clear, and ⇄/X swapping W and H. The frame holds W:H while drawn or resized. Commit passes the target to `image.crop` and resamples with the Image Interpolation preference.
- Empty resolution: physical units convert at the document's resolution, which is kept. W or H empty: plain crop, no resampling.
- New `ToolOptions` fields have serde defaults, so older settings still load. Translations added for the new labels (plus the missing Russian "Swaps height and width", which was failing `every_tl_literal_is_translated` on main).
- Scorecard TOOL-214-9 note updated; it stays partial (saved presets missing).

## Tests
- Engine: 8- and 16-bit crop to a target size and resolution (exact size, pixels, one undo step, undo restores); turned crop plus …

title: Float the layer mask, not the layer, when the mask is targeted (#2468)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2468.

With the layer mask targeted (mask thumbnail clicked), ⌘-dragging a selection (⌘⌥ to copy, Move tool drag, arrow nudges) floated and moved the layer's pixels instead of the mask's.

- `select.float` now takes `"target": "mask"`: `CutParts` splits the layer's mask by the selection instead of its pixels, the floating preview and `select.drop` put the piece back into the mask. Without `copy`, the hole takes the background colour, as on the Background layer and as the eraser does on a mask.
- The mask's untouched area (its default white or black) moves too: on a mask the cut covers the selection over the whole canvas, not only the painted pixels.

title: Control: timeout errors name the likely causes (#2489)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Fixes #2489

The control protocol's `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout"}` covered two opposite situations with one string: a command genuinely still running, and a request that sat queued because the window was not drawing frames (display asleep, fully occluded — on Wayland the frame update, and with it the control drain, only runs on compositor frame callbacks). An agent cannot tell "wait longer" from "check your display".

Review hardening: the text no longer hardcodes the deadline it reports. A new `control::REPLY_DEADLINE` constant drives the serve thread's clock, and `timeout_error()` builds the message from it — one source for the number and the wording, with a test asserting the text matches the constant. Both timeout sites (the transport thread's `recv_timeout` fallback and `drain_control`'s expired-request rejection) return the same message. `docs/control-protocol.md` documents the semantics and the Wayland frame-callback behavior.
