title: Eraser: Block mode (#2770)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2770

Depends on #2694 (its commit is included; this PR's own change is the last commit).

## What changed
Photoshop's Eraser has Mode: Brush / Pencil / **Block**. #2694 added Pencil; Block was missing because the paint engine had no square dab. Block erases a hard, aliased square of 16 **screen** pixels, so its size in document pixels is `16 / zoom` (taken at stroke start); Size, Hardness, Opacity and Flow don't apply.

- **paint**: `BrushSettings.square` (together with `aliased`) rasterises every pixel of the dab's whole-pixel grid square, ignoring angle and roundness. Serialised only when true, so existing brushes and presets are unchanged.
- **engine**: `paint.pencil` takes `"block": true`. The brush becomes a fresh square, aliased, full-opacity, full-flow brush of `brush_cmds::block_size(zoom)` = `round(16 / zoom)` px (clamped 1..5000), from the stroke's existing `"zoom"` param; colour, erase, smoothing and seed still come from the resolved brush. A `zoom` that is not a positive number returns an `Err`. The params doc lists `block` and `zoom`.
- **ui**: the Eraser's Mode dropdown gains Block. In Block mode the Eraser commits `paint.pencil` with `"block": true` (live and on release), shows the block's square cursor on the pixel grid, and greys out the brush preset/Size, Hardness, Opacity and Flow.

## Tests
- `pencil_tests::the_eraser_in_block_mode_erases_a_16_screen_px_square`: a soft, 5 px, 50 % opacity, 30 % flow Eraser in Block mode clicked on an opaque layer clears exactly a 16×16 square at zoom 1 and an 8×8 square at zoom 2, with no partial alpha, through `paint.pencil` with `"block": true`.
- Without the square dab in `paint/src/render.rs`, the test fails with `left: (208, 16, 16) right: (256, 16, 16)` (a round aliased disc instead of the square).

cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-paint --lib -- render brush
cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ig…

title: fix(compose, gpu): round dithered gradient fills to the document dept…

title: Batch: a failed step inside a called action fails the file and the script (#2779)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2779

## Root cause
`actions.play` returns `Ok` with a `failed` entry when a step inside the called action fails. Action playback (headless and desktop) promotes that to a failure with `actions_cmds::nested_failure`, but two other step runners didn't:

- `automate_cmds::run_steps` (File › Scripts › Browse and Script Events) only treated `Err` as a failure, so the script reported `"ok": true` and ran the later steps.
- `file_cmds::batch` (File › Automate › Batch, and Run Droplet, which goes through it) ran each file in a fresh scratch session with no actions, so any batched action that calls another action failed on every file with `no action named …`.

## Fix
- `run_steps` checks `nested_failure`, records the error on that step and stops.
- `batch` gives each scratch session a copy of the caller's actions list and playback stack, and turns a nested failure into a per-file error (the file goes to `errors` and isn't saved, like any other failing step). Copying the playback stack means an action that batches itself is caught as a recursive call instead of recursing without end.

## Relation to #2746 / #2761
Both PRs change the `steps.retain(...)` filtering at the top of `batch` and `create_droplet`. This PR only changes the per-step result handling inside the batch closure and `run_steps`, so the diffs don't overlap.

## Tests
- `automate_cmds::tests::a_failed_step_inside_a_called_action_fails_scripts_and_batch`: a script stops on a failing nested action call; Batch plays a called action and reports a failure inside one as a file error; an action that batches itself returns instead of overflowing. Without the fix it fails (`ok` is `true`).

## Commands
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --lib -- batch script droplet actions`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`
- `cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-engine -- --check`
- `cargo check -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --ta…

Now the new text takes the style of the first character it replaces, and the first paragraph's settings, which is what Photoshop does. Independent of #2783 (that PR fixes the same problem for the in-app File › Automate › Batch); this one only touches the CLI.

**Root cause**

title: Layers: Layer via Copy duplicates every selected layer (#2777)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2777

## Root cause
`layer.new.layerViaCopy` (`layer_via` in `crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs`) always worked on the active layer only. Without a pixel selection it duplicated just that layer, and it never checked the layer selection. `layer.duplicate` already had a multi-layer path (`layer_multi_cmds::duplicate_selected`), but Layer via Copy didn't use it.

## Fix
With no pixel selection and more than one layer selected, Layer via Copy now calls `duplicate_selected`: every selected layer is copied in a single undo step, each copy goes directly above its original, and the copies become the new selection. Copies are made with `layer_copy`, the same function Duplicate Layer uses, so smart objects still share their content (#2222). The copies stay in place, as with single-layer Layer via Copy. The history step is named "Layer Via Copy". `duplicate_selected` now takes the history label as a parameter and also returns `"layer"` (the new active layer) next to `"layers"`.

When there is a pixel selection, nothing changes: Layer via Copy still copies only the selected pixels of the active layer.

## Tests
- `edit_cmds::tests::layer_via_copy_duplicates_every_selected_layer`: selects two layers with no pixel selection and runs Layer via Copy. It checks that both layers are copied, each copy sits above its original, the copies are selected and it is one undo step. It then undoes, sets a pixel selection and checks that only one new layer is created. Without the fix it fails (`left: 4, right: 5`: only the active layer was copied).

title: Droplets: carry the actions their Play Action steps call (#2794)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2794

Depends on #2783: this branch is based on it (the per-file batch sessions get the caller's actions and playback stack there). Until #2783 merges, the diff here also shows its commit; the change for this issue is the last commit.

## Root cause
`file.automate.createDroplet` wrote only the chosen action's own steps. A Play Action step (`actions.play`) inside it names another action that the droplet file didn't contain. `photocraft-cli droplet` and the droplet's `.command` shim run `file.automate.runDroplet` in a fresh `Session` with no actions, so every file failed with `no action named …`.

## Fix
- `actions_cmds::called_actions` collects the actions the steps call, followed transitively through nested Play Action steps, with a seen-set and the 16-level playback cap. They come out in list order. Index references (`{"action": 1}`, which the panel's play button records) are rewritten to names so they resolve without the rest of the list.
- `createDroplet` saves them under `"calledActions"`. It doesn't use `"actions"`, because the CLI's `batch --actions` (#2792) reads that key as an action set.
- `runDroplet` passes them to `file.automate.batch` as `calledActions`. The per-file sessions then play from that list instead of the caller's. The list is parsed as data and capped at 4096 actions; a bad value is a `BadParams` error.
- Droplets without the key behave as before. Self-calls are still caught at playback by the existing recursion check.

## Tests
- `automate_cmds::tests::droplets_carry_the_actions_their_play_steps_call`:
  - A droplet whose action plays `Outer`, which in turn plays `Rotate` by index, embeds only `Rotate` and `Outer` and no `actions` key.
  - In a fresh `Session` it processes every file.
  - A droplet built from a self-calling action fails each file instead of looping.

title: View: Pattern Preview tiles the document around the canvas (#1067)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1067.

View › Pattern Preview could be checked but did nothing: `view.patternPreview` only toggled a flag that nothing read. In Photoshop, Pattern Preview shows the document repeated as a seamless tile around the canvas, so what leaves one edge shows up at the opposite one. That's how tileable textures are made.

## Change
- New `pattern_preview.rs` works out which copies cover the visible canvas. It caps them at 31 per axis, centred on the view, so a tiny document zoomed far out stays cheap.
- GPU canvas: each copy is another paint callback over the same document texture, offset by whole document sizes in the tile shader (`ViewParams::offset`, in the spare view-uniform slots `d.xy`).
  - Nothing is composited again, and seams are exact.
  - The checkerboard is anchored per copy, so every copy looks the same.
  - Copies are keyed by slot, so panning reuses the same uniform buffers.
- CPU canvas: the checkerboard and texture drawing moved into `paint_cpu_document`, which also draws each copy with a shifted view mapping (flip and rotation included).
- The drop shadow is off while tiling. The selection, guides and transform handles stay on the document itself.

## Tests
- Unit tests for the tile layout: view filled by the document, fit view, zoomed out, panned, cap and recentring, hostile input (zero size, NaN/inf, inverted rects, huge values).
- New `tests/pattern_preview_canvas.rs` (wgpu kittest harness): a 200×100 document with a red band on its left edge. With Pattern Preview on, the pixels right of, below and diagonal to the document show the matching copy, on both the GPU and the CPU canvas. With it off, they show the pasteboard. Before this change it fails with `got [40, 40, 40]`.

title: Spot Healing: Content-Aware dab no longer scans every patch in full (#2771)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2771

## Root cause

A Content-Aware Spot Healing dab spent about 70 % of its time (`perf`) in `photocraft_algo::inpaint::onion_peel`, the initial fill at the coarsest pyramid level of `inpaint::complete`. For every hole pixel it computed the full 7×7 sum of squared differences against **every** valid source patch, with no early exit. The pyramid shrinks the hole to about four patches across, and the sampling window is about 4× the dab. So the coarsest level is always about 100² with ~10 000 sources and ~600 hole pixels, which made a dab cost ~200–450 ms whatever its size. The sampling window was already bounded; the problem was this exhaustive initialisation.

## Fix (results are bit-identical)

- **`onion_peel`**: still an exhaustive scan that picks the same source, the first minimum in source order, but most candidates are rejected early:
  - The target's known offsets and samples are gathered once per front pixel.
  - An upper bound on the best error comes from the filled neighbours' sources (shifted, as in PatchMatch propagation), or from every 16th source at the hole's edge.
  - A candidate's sum is abandoned once its mean exceeds that bound or reaches the best so far.
  - Sums keep the original order and only grow, so the winner, ties included, is unchanged.
- **PatchMatch `vote`**: the weight `exp(-cost / 2σ²)` is computed once per target, not once per covered pixel (49×).
- **PatchMatch `dist`**: a fast path for target patches fully inside a level with no void pixels: row slices, same summation order.

Content-Aware Fill, Remove, Patch and Content-Aware Move go through the same code, so they get faster too.

## Before / after

`retouch_bench` (a single-size focused variant), release, 6016×6016 8-bit, one single-dab stroke through `Session::execute`. The machine was heavily loaded (load average 27–52), so these are best of 3 alternating rounds × 5 dabs:

| Content-Aware dab | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 50 px | 178 ms | 63 ms |
| 100 px | 190 ms …

title: Pencil: 1 px lines step pixel by pixel, no doubled corners (#2139)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2139

## Root cause
The path walker spaced every brush's dabs by distance (Spacing × diameter, 0.25 px for a 1 px Pencil). The aliased Pencil snaps each dab to the pixel grid (`render::grid_center`), so along a sloped line the x and y pixel boundaries were crossed by different dabs: the dab sequence went `(x, y) → (x+1, y) → (x+1, y+1)` instead of stepping diagonally. That left an L-shaped doubled pixel at every step of the staircase, the uneven, thick look in the reporter's comparison.

## Fix
`crates/paint/src/dynamics.rs`: when the tip is aliased and its dabs are at most one pixel apart (`size × spacing ≤ 1`, e.g. 1–4 px Pencils at 25 %), `PathWalker` steps each segment pixel by pixel instead: one dab per pixel along the major axis, on the line between the pixels holding the segment's ends, placed at the pixel's dab centre (0.5 offset for odd diameters, 0 for even, matching `grid_center`). That is a Bresenham line. Larger or spaced-out Pencils, anti-aliased brushes, speed spacing (Spacing unchecked, with timestamps) and the airbrush keep the old distance walk. A non-finite or absurdly long span (> 10⁷ px) falls back to distance spacing, so there is no new panic or hang path.

Before / after, 1 px Pencil from (2.5, 2.5) to (22.5, 9.5):

```
before                        after
..##......................    ..##......................
....###...................    ....###...................
.......###................    .......###................
..........###.............    ..........##..............
............####..........    ............###...........
...............####.......    ...............###........
..................###.....    ..................###.....
.....................##...    .....................##...
```
Before: 24 pixels, with the runs overlapping by a column at 3 steps. After: 21 pixels, one per column.

2 and 3 px lines also come out regular. Freehand strokes with dense input points look practically unchanged. Each segment is now a…

title: Web: File › Open opens every selected file (#2802)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2802

## Root cause
The web build's file dialog service (`apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs`) always called `rfd::AsyncFileDialog::pick_file()` and ignored `FileDialogRequest::Open { multiple, .. }`. `FileDialogAnswer::Contents(name, bytes)` could also hold only one file, so the shell had no way to receive more than one. The desktop build uses `pick_files()` and opens each path in its own tab.

## Change
- `crates/ui-egui/src/file_dialog.rs`: new `FileDialogAnswer::ContentsMany(Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>)`. File › Open opens each file as its own document and reports a file that fails to open without stopping the rest, as the desktop's multi-path open does. Single-file pickers (Place, presets, scripts) take the first file if they are ever given this variant.
- `apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs`: when the request has `multiple` set, use `pick_files()`, read every file and answer with `ContentsMany`. Single-file requests behave as before.

Dropping several files onto the web page already opened all of them, so it is unchanged.

## Tests
- `file_open::tests::the_web_opens_every_selected_file`: answering File › Open with three files (one broken) opens the two good ones as separate documents and shows an error notice for the broken one. It fails when only the first file is opened (`left: ["one.png"]`, `right: ["one.png", "two.jpg"]`).

## Commands
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- the_web_ file_dialog` (25 passed)

title: select.cryptomatte: click an object, select its coverage
author: Elvis33LE
body:
The Cryptomatte picker on top of the merged #2180 codec — the Arnold/V-Ray/Redshift workflow: click an object in the render, get its exact selection.

**`select.cryptomatte {x, y, layer?, tolerance?, mode?}`**

- Reads the ID at the clicked pixel of the active document's **source EXR** (the Cryptomatte layer by name, default the first; the document must have been opened from a saved `.exr`, everything else says so).
- Builds the selection from every pixel that ID **covers** — partial coverage becomes a partial mask, so an edge falls between both objects instead of hard-cutting. `tolerance` groups near-identical IDs (default 0: exact).
- Returns the ID, the **manifest's object name**, the pixel count and the layer used — the name is what a status-bar line or MCP caller shows.
- `mode` replace/add/subtract/intersect combines like the marquee tools; clicking a pixel with no samples deselects in replace mode (Magic Wand behaviour).

Everything is a command, so the control channel, CLI and MCP drive the same selection headlessly; the UI picker panel can follow as a thin shell.

**Tests** (synthetic 4×4 file: `cube` at coverage 1 on the left half, `sphere` at 0.5 on the right, manifest naming both): exact pixels and name for a full-coverage click, 0.5 mask at the half-covered pixel, add/subtract arithmetic (0.5 − 0.5 → 0.25), layer-by-name, and a hostile-param sweep (missing, non-numeric and out-of-bounds coordinates, unknown layer and mode — all `Err`, never a panic). `panic_hunt` green; engine suite 1161 green; clippy/fmt clean.

On `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, three constants were dead code because their only users are native-only:

Fixes #1946.

In Photoshop's layer name and value fields, as in native Windows and macOS text fields, a drag selection in a single-line field follows only the pointer's horizontal position. PhotoCraft followed the vertical one: drifting a few points above the field selected everything to the start, and below it everything to the end. egui's `TextEdit` picks the character under the pointer with `Galley::cursor_from_pos`. title: Tools: remember tool options between launches (#2814)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2814

## Root cause
`ToolOptions` (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`), which holds the options-bar settings, was only serialized for Tool Presets. Nothing saved it at exit or restored it at launch. The preferences file kept the engine preferences, the panel layout (`panelLayout`) and the brush picker view (`brushPicker`), but not the tool options. So unticking Move > Auto-Select (the setup asked for in #2706), setting a marquee Feather, choosing a crop ratio and so on only lasted until the next launch. Photoshop remembers each tool's options between sessions.

## What is persisted and where
- `Preferences::tool_options` (`toolOptions` in the prefs JSON): a new shell-owned `Value`, like `brushPicker`. It holds only the `ToolOptions` fields that differ from their defaults, so if a default changes in a later release, users who never touched that option get the new one.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/tool_memory.rs`:
  - `persist` runs every frame after the panels, next to `brush_picker::persist`. It waits until the pointer is up, so a slider drag doesn't write on every step. When nothing changed it costs one struct compare. Options set through the control channel or by a tool preset are remembered too.
  - `restore` runs in `prefs_ui::load` at launch and applies the saved values field by field.
- Per-document state (crop rect, polygon in progress and the like) lives outside `ToolOptions` and is not saved. Brush tips and sizes belong to the session brush, which #2516 handles separately. There is no Reset Tool / Reset All Tools command yet, so nothing needed to change there.

## Compatibility and robustness
- Old preference files have no `toolOptions` key, so the defaults apply, as before.
- If `toolOptions` is not an object, it is ignored with a log warning.
- An unknown key is ignored.
- A field that doesn't read back keeps its default, logs a warning and leaves the other fields alone. That covers a wrong type and a number outside the `f32` range (it would become infinity).

title: Options bar: Reset Tool and Reset All Tools (#2825)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2825

## What changed
- Right-clicking the tool icon at the far left of the options bar opens a context menu with **Reset Tool** and **Reset All Tools**, as in Photoshop.
- **Reset Tool** (`tool.reset`) puts the current tool's options back to their defaults.
- **Reset All Tools** (`tool.resetAll`) asks first, with Photoshop's text ("Reset all tools to their default settings?", OK/Cancel), then resets every tool's options. The question is an ordinary dialog, so `ui.inspect` shows it and `ui.dialog.confirm` / `ui.dialog.cancel` answer it. `{"confirmed": true}` skips it for agents that have already asked.
- Both are shell UI commands (`menus::UI_COMMANDS`), so the control channel (`engine.execute` / `ui.menu.invoke`) can run them.
- Resetting only changes `ui.tool_options`, `ui.selection_mode` and the per-tool brush state. #2822, which remembers tool options between launches, picks the change up without extra code.

## Which fields belong to which tool
`ToolOptions` is one struct, not one per tool, so `tool_reset::reset_options` maps each tool to its fields:
- Move: `move_auto_select`, `move_target`, `move_show_transform`
- Marquees: `feather`, `anti_alias`, `marquee_*`. Lasso and Polygonal Lasso: `feather`, `anti_alias`. Magnetic Lasso: those plus `magnetic_*`
- Magic Wand: `tolerance`, `anti_alias`, `contiguous`, `sample_all_layers`. Quick/Object Selection: `sample_all_layers`, `enhance_edge`
- Crop: `crop_*`. Eyedropper: `eyedropper_*`. Zoom: `zoom_scrubby`. Pencil: `pencil_auto_erase`

author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2835 (scorecard row BUG-207-4)

## Root cause
`edit.transform` only transformed an alpha channel or the Quick Mask when the caller passed an explicit `"target"`. The Free Transform box in the UI does pass one, but nothing else did:
- `edit.transform` called without `"target"` (by agents, MCP or actions) ignored the Channels panel and transformed the active layer.

title: Docs: claim an issue with an "I'm working on this." comment (#2418)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2418.

Several issues got two competing PRs (9 in the last 300, see #2418) because agents start coding without checking whether someone else already has. Contributors already use a plain `I'm working on this.` comment as a claim; this PR tells agents about it and backs the comment with a draft PR, which is what other agents actually find. No bot, workflow, labels or permissions needed.

## Change
`AGENTS.md` › *4. Picking work*: new **Claiming an issue** subsection.
- Check the issue is free: no `I'm working on this` comment under 72 hours old, and no open PR, searched by number and by feature keywords.
- Claim before writing code: open a draft PR from an empty WIP commit with `Fixes #N`, and comment `I'm working on this.`
- Push progress to the draft often, so others can see the claim is alive.
- Re-check before every push and before marking it ready. If a competing PR is further along, hand over.
- If you stop, delete your claim comment, close the draft and delete the branch.
- A claim expires after 72 hours with no new commit, PR or update.

`docs/contributing.md`: a one-line rule pointing to that section.

## Why a draft PR and not only a comment
- A comment alone gets overlooked: #3368 was claimed 12 minutes before #3412 was opened for the same fix.
- A draft shows up in the issue's *Development* sidebar and in `gh pr list`, which is what agents search.
- Searching only by issue number misses work: #2867 was already covered by the long-open #884.
- When two people collide, the one further along should keep it (#3437 vs #3506).

## Tests
Docs only, so there's nothing to test.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Tests: save-dialog expectations build their paths with Path::join, so they pass on Windows (#2745)
author: mroxso
body:
## What

Fixes #2745: `file_dialog::tests::save_dialogs_remember_where_each_document_was_last_saved` fails on `windows-latest` because it compares the suggested path against hard-coded `/` strings, while `pick_save` builds it with `Path::join` (which uses `\` on Windows).

## How

The five expectations that go through `dir.join(name)` are now built the same way the behaviour builds them: a small `joined(dir, name)` helper returns `Path::new(dir).join(name).to_string_lossy()`. The remaining literal comparisons are untouched because those paths never pass through `join`:

title: Dropdowns: press, drag onto an option and release to choose it (#2735)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #2735.

A dropdown took two clicks to change, for example Levels › Channel. Pressing the box, dragging onto an option and releasing chose nothing. Menus got this gesture in #775 (PR #837); the dropdowns were left out.

**Cause:** egui's `ComboBox` opens its list on a whole click (press and release), and its rows only respond to clicks. As @switch87 found, forcing egui's popup open from outside didn't stick in their attempt. In egui 0.36, a popup opened during a pass counts as open for that pass (`OpenPopup::new` sets `open_this_frame`), so it survives `Memory::end_pass` when it's opened with the id egui uses for the box's list.

**Change:** `press_menu::PressCombo` adds the gesture around egui's own widget, so the look, ids, keyboard and wheel behaviour are unchanged:
- `PressCombo::after(&response)`: a primary press on the box opens the closed list and starts the gesture. egui draws the list from the next frame.
- `PressCombo::chosen(ui, &item)`: a row is chosen when it's clicked, or when the press-drag that opened the list is released on it. In the second case the list closes.
- `PressCombo::before(ui, salt)`: a plain click ends that same press with the pointer still on the box, and egui would toggle the list shut on it. So the list is closed just before the box (using `primary_clicked()`, known before any widget runs), and egui's toggle reopens it in the same frame with no blink. That frame uses `PopupCloseBehavior::IgnoreClicks`. A plain click therefore still leaves the list open for a second click, and clicking the box again closes it.
- Used by `widgets::dropdown` (and its hovered and wheel variants, so Levels, the Layers blend mode and the other dialog dropdowns), `dropdown_with_tooltips`, the font family picker (which keeps `CloseOnClickOutside` for its search field), the kerning presets, the Gradient Map presets, the shape stroke choices and the credits sort.

title: Tools: Freeform Pen and Curvature Pen (#1054)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1054

## What changed
The Pen flyout (P, Shift+P cycles) now has **Pen, Freeform Pen and Curvature Pen**. `ui.set {"tool": "freeformPen" | "curvaturePen"}` selects them and `ui.inspect` reports them. Both tools share the Pen's options (Path or Shape mode, stroke) and its commit path. A finished path becomes a new shape layer in Shape mode. Otherwise it's added to the targeted vector mask or becomes the work path. Each finished path is one History step, and individual Curvature clicks add none.

- **Freeform Pen:** a drag draws freehand and shows a live trace. On release the trace is fitted with cubic Béziers within the options bar's **Curve Fit** (0.5–10 px, default 2 px). Turns sharper than 60° stay corner anchors. Releasing on the start point closes the path. A plain click draws nothing.
- **Curvature Pen:** each click adds a smooth point, and the path passes through every point. Inner anchors get collinear handles parallel to their neighbours' chord, each a third of the distance to that neighbour (Catmull-Rom with chordal scaling, so uneven spacing doesn't overshoot). Dragging a point moves it. Double-clicking a point toggles it between corner and smooth, so double-clicking empty canvas places a corner, as in Photoshop. Clicking the first point closes the path. Enter or Esc finishes it and Backspace or Cmd/Ctrl+Z removes the last point, as with the Pen. A dashed preview shows the curve the next click would make. Clicks snap like the Pen's.

## Algorithm
- `photocraft_vector::trace::fit_trace(points, tolerance, closed)` reuses the least-squares cubic fitting that Make Work Path already uses, with Newton reparameterisation and splitting at the worst point (P. J. Schneider, "An Algorithm for Automatically Fitting Digitized Curves", *Graphics Gems*, 1990). Corner detection now also works on open polylines, with a window of ±2 × tolerance. A run that is straight within the tolerance becomes one straight segment, because end tangents estimated from jittery sampl…

title: CI: run panic_hunt in the Linux test job
author: 1Git2Clone
body:
Runs `panic_hunt` in CI. AGENTS.md says it "must stay green", but it's `#[ignore]`d and no workflow ran it, so a command that panics or hangs on bad params could merge without anyone noticing.

It's a new step in the Linux test job, right after Test. The Test step has already compiled the binary (ignored tests are built, just not run), so the step asks cargo where it is (`--no-run --message-format=json`, same flags as Test, so nothing rebuilds) and runs it: **19–20 s** on the runner, ~18.7 s of it the test ([fork run](https://github.com/1Git2Clone/photocraft/actions/runs/38089610063), [rerun after rebasing onto 009bef76](https://github.com/1Git2Clone/photocraft/actions/runs/38131055452)). `cargo test --test panic_hunt` would have taken 4.5 min instead: selecting a single test target drops the other crates' dev-dependency features, so the whole graph recompiles.

Linux only: the commands are platform-independent. The step has a 10 min timeout as a backstop; each command already has its own 4 s timeout.

#2997 makes `panic_hunt` rerun a command that times out before calling it hung (the first `type.create` scans the system fonts), which keeps this step from flaking on a loaded runner. The two don't conflict.

If #2933 merges first, the step's `cargo test ... --no-run` should use the same `--lib --bins --tests` selection as its nextest Test step, so it still finds the binary without rebuilding.

title: Actions: toggle, reorder and delete single steps (#2855)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2855 (part of #219, scorecard row AUTO-219-2)

## What changed
Photoshop's Actions panel has a check column: an unchecked step is skipped by playback, Batch and droplets. PhotoCraft could already reorder steps by dragging (`actions.move` with `step`) and delete a single step (`actions.delete` with `step`, trash button), but every step always ran.

- **Model:** `Action` gains `disabled: BTreeSet<usize>`, the 0-based steps that are switched off. It's `#[serde(default)]` and left out of `actions.json` when empty, so older files load unchanged. `actions.move` and `actions.delete` remap it so the flag stays on the step it belongs to. Added `Action::new` and `Action::enabled_steps`.
- **Command:** new `actions.toggle {action, step?, enabled?}`. With `step`, it flips or sets one step (pending recorded steps included, flushed first, as `move` and `delete` already do). Without `step`, it switches every step like the action's own check mark: all on unless all already are. A bad action, a bad step index or a bad `enabled` type returns `Err`.
- **Playback:** `actions.play` (headless), the desktop playback path and `action_steps` (the steps handed to File › Automate › Batch and Create Droplet) skip unchecked steps. `from` still counts recorded step indices, and `failed.step` reports the original index. `actions.get` now also returns `disabled`.
- **Panel:** each step row has a check box in the icon column, and an unchecked step's label is dimmed. The action row shows "2/3 steps" while some steps are off. New string "Include in playback" is translated in all 16 catalogs.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: a row for `actions.toggle`, and `actions.get`'s new field.

## Note for other open PRs
`Action` gets a new field, so struct literals `Action { name, steps }` need `disabled: Default::default()` (or `Action::new(name, steps)`). I updated every literal on `main`. Open PRs that add literals will need the same one-line change after this merges: #2800, #2441, #1991.

title: perf: repeated Select Subject answers from the last mask (#2865)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2865 (scorecard row P29, part of #211).

## Root cause
`select.subject` reran the whole pipeline on every call: sampling the composite at working resolution, SLIC superpixels, the saliency optimisation, GrabCut, then the full-resolution band re-cut (which composites again tile by tile). Running it again on an unchanged document cost as much as the first run.

## Technique
The session keeps Select Subject's last result (`smartselect_cmds::SubjectCache`):
- **Key:** the pixels it was computed from, checked with the existing `layer_multi_cmds::same_pixels` (tile-pointer comparison, the one `Session::edit` already uses for damage) against a **weakly** held document, plus the sampled target (composite, or the active layer with `sampleAllLayers: false`). Selection-only edits such as Deselect keep the entry valid; any pixel or compositing change makes it miss.
- **Each call still applies the mode** (replace/add/subtract/intersect) to the current selection, as one history step, exactly as before.
- After the selection edit, the weak pointer follows the new document (same pixels), so a short history doesn't turn the next repeat into a miss.
- `apply` now borrows the region, so a hit doesn't copy the mask.

Results are bit-identical: a hit returns the very mask the first run computed.

## Before / after
`perf_scenarios --only "Select Subject"` (release, 6000×4000 photo, 5 timed repeats after one warm run), alternating binaries, load average 15-22 on 16 cores:

| run | before p50 / p95 | after p50 / p95 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 315.8 / 370.7 ms | 8.95 / 9.26 ms |
| 2 | 260.2 / 299.3 ms | 6.91 / 8.39 ms |
| 3 | 272.7 / 277.7 ms | 8.44 / 8.92 ms |

The committed baseline (Apple M4 Pro) has 559 / 693 ms. The first run is unchanged.

`perf/budgets.toml`: P29 is met, but I left `enforce = false` (with a note): with the committed baseline still at 693 ms, `enforce = true` renders P29 as **BUDGET BROKEN** in `docs/scorecard.md`. It can be enforced once `cargo xtask perf --update-…

title: perf: Select › Modify › Feather/Smooth on 24 MP within budget (#2873)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2873 (scorecard rows P26 and P27, part of #211)

## Root cause
The blur itself (`selection_blur`) was already parallel and independent of the radius: 9 ms for Smooth and 15 ms for Feather on 24 MP. Most of the command was serial glue around it:

- `selection_cmds::modify` copied the mask into a padded buffer (`pad_mask`, per sample with bounds checks) and copied the result back out (`crop_mask`, a `flat_map` collect). It did this even with zero padding, the usual case of a selection clear of the canvas edge. That was two single-threaded passes over 24 M floats.
- `selection::combine` built a full-canvas byte buffer, scanned it again to check for emptiness, then copied it into tiles one tile at a time on a single thread.

## Change
- `modify`: with no padding, the mask is used as it is. With padding (a selection touching the canvas edge), it pads and crops row by row with `copy_from_slice`/`fill` instead of per sample.
- `combine` / `mask_to_surface`: a new `surface_from_masks` fills the GRAY8 selection tiles in parallel (`par_map`, serial on wasm), straight from the f32 mask a row at a time. There is no intermediate byte buffer. Empty tiles are dropped, as before. Fully selected tiles now share one copy-on-write tile (`Surface::solid_tile`), so the inside of a large selection also stops costing 64 KB per tile.

The blur algorithms are unchanged.

## Numbers
Release build, `perf_scenarios --cpu --only "Select > Modify"`, 6000×4000. Before and after binaries were run alternately on a shared 16-core machine where four other builds were running. Load average was 13–23, so the absolute numbers are noisy; the paired ratio is the reliable part.

title: perf: duplicating a layer recomposites only where the copy draws (#2883)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2883 (scorecard P8/P9, part of #209).

### Where the time went
`perf_scenarios --only "duplicate 12 MP"` (release, Linux, RTX 5090):

- `layer.duplicate` itself: **0.1–0.3 ms**. The copy was already cheap: `Layer::duplicate` clones the surface's map of `Arc<Tile>`s, so the copy shares every tile with its source, and the history step holds the old document by `Arc`.
- The canvas refresh afterwards: **everything else**. `Session::edit` reports no damage (`last_damage = None`) for any edit that changes pixels, so after a duplicate the canvas recomposited the **whole 20 MP document** (`gpu-full`, 19.96 MP), not just the 12 MP the copy draws in. Re-uploading the copy's tiles to the GPU (204 tiles, new layer id) was a small part of it.

### Change
Duplicate Layer (single and multi-selection) now reports the pixels it can change, using the `step_damage` walk (layers paired by id, tiles compared by pointer) extended to **bounded additions** (`insert_damage`). A layer that only the new document has contributes its `photocraft_compose::change_bounds` when it is self-contained:
- not an adjustment layer, or a pass-through group holding one (`change_bounds` returns `None`);
- not a new clipping base: an unclipped layer whose upper neighbour is clipped makes everything recomposite, as before;
- no video layer and no excluded channels inside it.

Anything else still recomposites everything. That includes document-level changes such as the canvas growing for an artboard copy (`doc_pixels_equal`). Undo and redo keep `step_damage` unchanged. Results are identical: only the recomposited area shrinks (12.4 MP instead of 19.96 MP in the scenario, including the effect reach).

### Before / after
Release `perf_scenarios`, before = upstream/main 5a1f6eef, after = this branch, run alternately on the same machine. Other builds kept the load average between 40 and 60, so the absolute numbers are noisy; the table pools 10 alternating pairs (30 repeat samples each).

title: Accelerate large canvas brushes with tiled rasterization and GPU compute
author: bastova
body:
Large brushes previously rasterized dense masks and replayed live strokes on pointer release. This change bins large dabs into sparse ordered coverage tiles, composites native pixels in parallel, and lets the normal paint command adopt a matching live preview without replay.

Native builds also use bounded wgpu compute for dense computed-tip batches, sharing the canvas device. Small batches and unsupported tips retain CPU rendering. Wet Edges keeps the corrected upstream stroke-depth path. GPU coverage is read back before native-format compositing, preserving ICC conversion, saves and undo/redo. Coverage/readback buffers are capped at 32 MiB; the display still allocates a full canvas/mip texture.

### Measurements

Apple M5, release build:
- Dense 24-point, 1,000 px hard-brush raster batch including transfers and completed GPU work: CPU median 15.141 ms → GPU 6.955 ms (2.18×).
- CPU-optimized 20,000² RGBA8 canvas with a 1,000 px soft brush, 180 samples: painting + completed GPU compositing median 5.264 ms, p95 7.351 ms; commit 0.450 ms. This is a different workload from the dense GPU batch comparison and excludes physical input, presentation and scanout.

Reproduction commands, thresholds, precision tolerances and remaining limits are in `docs/brush-performance.md`. GPU arithmetic has bounded floating-point differences; CPU serial/parallel regression cases remain bit-identical.

### Validation

Passed before rebase:
- Full tests for paint, gpu, engine and ui-egui, including Metal tests.
- Final targeted GPU coverage/native-pixel parity (RGBA8/16/32f, CMYK8, Gray16), unsupported-tip/device-loss fallback, and live-stroke save/undo/redo at 8/16/32 bits.

title: fix(engine): preserve Frame from Layers undo under history limits
author: Imkkey
body:
Problem
Frame from Layers records a grouping edit and a mask edit, then calls purge_last to fold them into one history entry. If the second edit trims history to one state, the original snapshot is already gone and purge_last removes the remaining undo.
Reproduction:
1. Create a document containing a layer.
2. Set Preferences → Performance → History States to 1.

Fixes #2871.

## Root Cause

The canvas cursor dispatch checks the active Free Transform session but does not account for the transform controls displayed by the Move tool before a transform session begins.

## Changes

- Display the appropriate horizontal, vertical, and diagonal resize cursors.
- Display a rotation cursor when hovering over the rotation region.

- Preserve normal Move cursor behavior inside the transform box.

title: fix(brush): interpolate pen pressure across Shift-click connecting strokes
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Shift-clicking with a pressure-sensitive brush connects the previous stroke to the new click with a straight line.

However, the connecting line uses the new click's pressure at both endpoints.

This prevents pressure-sensitive size and opacity from transitioning naturally between the two points.

Fixes #2827.

## Root Cause

The editor stores only the previous stroke's endpoint coordinates.

When creating a Shift-click connecting stroke, it inserts the previous coordinates with the current click's pressure.

Consequently, both stroke endpoints receive identical pressure values.

## Changes

- Preserve the pressure value alongside the previous stroke's endpoint coordinates.
- Initialize connecting strokes with the previous endpoint's recorded pressure.
- Preserve the new click's pressure at the destination.
- Allow the existing brush dynamics interpolation to transition pressure between endpoints.
- Maintain the existing single-stroke undo/history behavior.
- Preserve document-specific stroke tracking.
- Keep the rubber-band line preview compatible with the updated endpoint representation.

## Regression Coverage

Added tests covering:

- Different starting and ending pen pressures.
- Correct endpoint coordinates.
- Multiple consecutive Shift-click connections.
- Pressure continuity between successive connections.
- One undo step per connecting stroke.

## Validation

- Added focused regression tests.
- Reviewed the pressure propagation and brush stroke construction paths.
- Rust tests and interactive pressure-sensitive drawing checks have not been executed.
- CI pending.

Fixes #2827.

title: perf: keep resident GPU tiles and convert 32-bit tiles directly for brush dabs on large documents (#2900)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2900 (scorecard rows P13 and P16, part of #209).

## Root cause

I timed each dab in two parts, the `paint.stroke` command and the GPU canvas refresh. The command takes about 0.4 ms. The refresh is the cost, and the slow dabs are the ones that paint past the layer's stored tiles. `Compositor::sync` keys a layer's resident page by its region, which is the layer's tile bounds inside the page cell. When that region grows, the page counts as stale: the texture is recreated and **every stored tile of the layer in that cell is converted and uploaded again**. Refresh time rose with that count: 1 tile took about 3 ms, 8 tiles took 14–20 ms on the 32-bit document. In P16 the dabs walk diagonally across a mostly empty layer, so almost every timed dab grew the bounds.

32-bit tiles also went through the general conversion: decode the tile into a float buffer, then `to_rgba` and `f32_to_f16` per pixel. `to_rgba` + `read_region` were about 60 % of CPU samples in the 32-bit dab loop.

## Change (`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`)

- **Keep the overlap when only the region moved.** The kind, format, CMYK profile and default pixel must be unchanged. The new texture gets the old texture's overlap through a GPU copy, and the tile map entries inside the overlap carry over. The existing incremental pass then uploads only new or changed tiles, and writes the default pixel where tiles went away. The copy goes in its own small submission. Queued tile writes run at the start of the next submit, ahead of the frame's encoder, so a copy recorded in that encoder would overwrite freshly written tiles with old texels. Resident textures now also have `COPY_SRC`.
- **32-bit float fast path.** RGB/gray F32 tiles convert straight from their samples to RGBA16F, next to the existing 16-bit table path. The bytes are the same as the general path.

Pixels are unchanged. The new test checks that the grown pages match a compositor that uploads everything afresh, bit for bit.

title: Layers: Combine Shapes merges the selected shape layers (#2400)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2400.

## Why
Layer › Combine Shapes › Unite / Subtract Front Shape / Intersect Shape Areas / Exclude Overlapping Shapes only changed the path operations between the components of the active layer. With two shape layers selected, each holding one rectangle (the reported case), the active layer had a single component, so nothing happened. In Photoshop these commands merge the selected shape layers into one.

Measured in Photoshop (two overlapping rectangle shape layers, black "Rectangle 1" below, grey "Rectangle 2" above, both selected):
- Unite Shapes: one layer left, named "Rectangle 2" with its grey fill, in the top layer's place; its path has both components with the Combine (add) operation.
- Subtract Front Shape: same layer, the bottom component keeps Combine, the upper one becomes Subtract.

## Change
- With two or more shape layers selected (and no `layer`/`subpath` param), the four Combine Shapes operations merge them into the top-most layer in one history step. That layer keeps its name, fill, stroke and stack position. The bottom layer's components keep their operations, every component of the layers above takes the chosen one in stacking order, and the other layers are removed.
- Merge Shape Components with several shape layers selected merges them the same way (each layer combined) and then bakes the result (the baking code moved unchanged into `bake_components`).
- Selected non-shape layers are left alone; a locked shape layer refuses the merge with an error. With one selected layer, or an explicit `layer`, the behaviour is unchanged.

title: perf: marquee selections on large documents are built row by row (#2888)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2888 (part of #211).

## Root cause

- **Elliptical Marquee:** `select.rect` with `ellipse: true` tested every pixel of the bounding box on one thread (4 corner tests, plus 16 sub-samples on the edge) and stored each one with `Surface::write_pixel` (tile lookup and copy-on-write check per pixel). Fully selected tiles weren't shared either.
- **Add, Subtract, Intersect** (rectangle and ellipse): the local `combine` in `commands.rs` read both selections over the whole canvas into `f32` buffers, mapped them and wrote the result back. On 24 MP that's about 290 MB of temporaries.

## Technique

New module `crates/algo/src/selection/marquee.rs`:

- `ellipse_surface(r, clip, anti_alias)` works a row at a time. A row is a run of fully selected pixels with edge pixels at each end, and the run is bounded analytically in `f64`. The bounds are widened by a margin that covers the `f32` tests' rounding, then checked with the exact `f32` tests: the run's two end pixels must be full and the pixels just outside must be empty. If either check fails, the whole row is evaluated exactly. This is enough because along a row the full pixels form one interval, since each test is monotonic in the distance from the centre. Only the edge pixels get the original per-pixel coverage test, and they keep the same 4×4 supersampling. Row spans and tiles are computed in parallel with `par_map`, so wasm runs them serially. Fully selected tiles share one `Arc` tile, and only tiles that hold something are created.
- `combine_surfaces(a, b, area, f)` maps two GRAY8 selections tile by tile in parallel through a table of all 256×256 byte pairs. It gives the same bytes as the decode, `f` and encode steps did, since the table is built with them. A tile that `f` passes through unchanged (for example Add or Subtract where the new shape has no tile) stays shared with the old selection. Fully selected results share one tile, and no buffer is allocated for the whole canvas. Non-GRAY8 inputs fall back to the…

title: perf: pasting a layer recomposites only where it draws (#2901)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2901 (scorecard rows P10/P11, part of #209).

**Depends on #2884**: this branch is stacked on it and uses its `note_insert` / `insert_damage`. Only the second commit (`ade7e0a7`) belongs to this PR.

### Root cause

`edit.paste` (shared by Paste in Place) inserts the pasted layer through `Session::edit`, which reports no damage for an edit that changes pixels (`last_damage = None`). So every paste recomposited the **whole 20 MP document**, although the pasted layer only draws in its own 12 MP. Paste Into / Paste Outside paste through `edit.paste` and then add the layer mask in more coalesced edits, which also reported no damage.

### Fix

Capture the document (an `Arc` clone) before the paste and call `layer_multi_cmds::note_insert` afterwards, as Duplicate Layer does in #2884: a self-contained added layer contributes its `change_bounds`. A layer that isn't self-contained (a new clipping base for clipped layers above it, video, excluded channels) still recomposites everything. The composite is unchanged; only the region that gets recomposited is smaller.

Covered: Paste, Paste in Place, Paste Into, Paste Outside.
Not changed: New from Clipboard (it creates a new document, which needs a full render anyway), paste into a targeted mask or channel (`paste_to_target`, `channel_clip::paste`: they change a mask or channel and still recomposite everything), and undo/redo of a paste (`step_damage` without bounded additions, still a full recomposite, not timed by P10/P11). The layer-based paste paths in #2653 and #2686 (`paste_layers`) insert through their own `Session::edit` and would need the same `note_insert` call.

### Before / after

`perf_scenarios --only "paste 12"`, release, Linux, RTX 5090. Median of 5 alternating before/after runs on the GPU, 3 on the CPU. The machine was shared with other builds (load 10–20), so treat the numbers as approximate.

title: Camera Raw: Shadows/Highlights inside raw development, Whites/Blacks and the D4 look measured from Photoshop
author: Unemars
body:
**Problem.** Camera Raw's Shadows, Highlights, Whites and Blacks were guesses, and on raw files they acted in the wrong place.
- Shadows and Highlights were exposure changes weighted by smoothstep masks of a guided-filter base; Whites and Blacks were fixed smoothstep offsets. On ten public-domain photos (NASA image library) they differed from Photoshop 25.4's Camera Raw Filter by 2.7–36.8 levels of 255 on average.
- When a raw is opened, Photoshop's Camera Raw applies these sliders inside the raw development. PhotoCraft applied them to the developed pixels, after the camera's tone curve, so on a Nikon D4 NEF the effect of Shadows +100 correlated with Photoshop's at only 0.68 (Highlights −100: 0.55).
- The D4's default development (fitted to the camera's JPEG, #1475) was 0.29 stop off Photoshop's opening of the same files (median), up to 0.9 stop lighter in the shadows.

**How Photoshop does it.** Photoshop 25.4 was measured as a black box: images and NEFs were opened through Camera Raw by script with set sliders, and the 16-bit results read back. No Adobe code, profiles or data were used, only rendered output.

*Raw opens* (29 NEFs from one D4 body, private files not included; about 350 opens):
- **Shadows and Highlights act before the tone curve, in linear light.** Mapped back through each image's default curve, the gain of Shadows +100 at exposure −1 equals the one at exposure 0 (correlation 0.985–1.0).
- **The gain is local and follows the image.** log₂ of the gain is `slider / 100 · C(B − anchor)`:
  - `B` is an edge-preserving base of the log₂ luminance (guided filter, radius 32, ε 1 stop², on a copy 1232 px on its long side). Whole areas move together; edges stay sharp.
  - The anchor follows the frame, which is why exposure changes nothing. Shadows: the log₂ power mean (p = 1.5) of the linear luminance. Highlights: the mean of the log₂ luminance.
  - The change is linear in the slider (+50 is half of +100). Each direction has its own curve `C`.

title: Raw: lossless-JPEG tiles respect the allocation limit (#2897)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #2897.

**Why:** camera raw import checked only the whole image plane against `Limits`. Tile sizes come from TILE_WIDTH/TILE_LENGTH (up to 65536 each, whatever the image size), so an untrusted DNG/TIFF with a tiny image and huge lossless-JPEG tiles could allocate decode buffers past the configured `max_alloc`.

**Change** (`crates/raw/src/sensor.rs`)
- `read_plane` checks each strip or tile buffer with `limits.check(tile w, tile h, samples * 2)` before decoding it, and returns `RawError::LimitExceeded` if it is too big. This covers the lossless-JPEG and Sony quad-tile buffers, and also the deflate and uncompressed tile buffers, which had the same gap.
- The lossless-JPEG frame budget (up to 4x the tile) is capped at `max_alloc / 2` samples, so its intermediate never goes over one buffer's limit.
- Valid DNG strips and tiles, and Sony quad tiles, decode as before (strips are never larger than the already-checked image).

**Tests**
- New unit test `sensor::tests::lossless_jpeg_tile_respects_alloc_limit`: an 8x8 DNG with 256x256 lossless-JPEG tiles returns `LimitExceeded` under a 4 KiB limit and decodes with default limits. It fails on main (verified by reverting the fix with the test kept).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-raw --lib --tests`: all green (lib 55 passed, integration binaries 28, 4, 7, 0, 10, 9 passed).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-raw --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Not included / not verified**
- A limit on the combined size of all tiles decoding in parallel (each buffer is limited, the total is not; the issue asks for the per-buffer invariant).
- Corpus tests not run locally (CI runs them).

title: PSD: bound parse-time merged-image ZIP validation by the decode budget (#2898)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
`validate_planes` checked ZIP merged-image data against the uncapped layout size, while `decode_planes` caps it at `MAX_DECODED_BYTES`. So parsing could inflate data for a layout that decoding would reject anyway, and a stream too short to ever reach the declared size was fully inflated before being reported. This makes the two paths use the same limits.

ZIP validation now rejects a stream that can't reach the declared size at deflate's ~1032:1 maximum ratio, without inflating it (the same bound `filter_effects.rs` uses). Layouts past `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` are not inflated at parse time; decoding them still returns `LimitExceeded`, the same as for Raw and RLE data. Streams within budget are still inflated to the end, so the Adler-32 check still runs, and large PSBs within the budget load as before.

Added `zip_validation_respects_decode_budget`, which covers the over-budget skip, the length check, the 1 MiB cap past the expected size, and checksum failures. Checked with `cargo test -p photocraft-psd`, clippy, fmt, `xtask layers` and `xtask wasm`.

Closes #2898.

author: 1Git2Clone
body:

The Windows tests go from **~35–40 min to ~13 min** and the Linux test job from **~34 to ~16 min**, with no paid runners. Every step below was measured on my fork, three runs per change.

## Times

`windows-latest` hands out different CPUs (EPYC 7763, 9V45, 9V74, Xeon 8370C/6973P), and the newer ones build ~35 % faster, so a single run compares machines, not changes. The fork times compare only jobs on the most common CPU, the EPYC 7763, all with a warm dependency cache, like main's.

| | Upstream main | This branch (fork) |
|---|---|---|
| Windows tests (slowest job) | [35.2 min](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38119131293) | [12.8 min](https://github.com/1Git2Clone/photocraft/actions/runs/38119303394) |
| Linux test job | [33.8 min](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38119131293) | [16.2 min](https://github.com/1Git2Clone/photocraft/actions/runs/38120272104) |
| Linux with craft-fonts / without heif | inside the test job | [14.4 / 3.7 min](https://github.com/1Git2Clone/photocraft/actions/runs/38120272104) |

Step by step on Windows (EPYC 7763):

title: Linux: a late first appearance reply repaints the idle window (#2798)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
On Linux with Sync with system, the appearance worker only requested a repaint for later `SettingChanged` signals. If the portal's first `Read` reply came back after the 250 ms startup wait, the value was stored but an idle window kept its dark fallback until something else caused a frame.

The first read and later signals now go through the same publish step, which repaints the registered egui context whenever the value changes. The thread and wait setup moved into a small `start()` helper so the new test can hold back the first result past the startup wait and check that a repaint happens, without D-Bus.

Checked with `cargo test -p photocraft`, clippy, fmt and `xtask layers`. Not tried against a real desktop portal.

Closes #2798.

title: Open GIMP XCF files: layers, groups, masks, blend modes, channels and selection
author: diegochagas
body:
Closes #1076.

## What changed

PhotoCraft opens **GIMP XCF** files (`.xcf`, `.xcf.gz`), read only, through a new reader in `photocraft-io` (`crates/io/src/xcf.rs`, ~900 lines) written from the [public XCF specification](https://developer.gimp.org/core/standards/xcf/) and from files GIMP 3.2 writes; no GIMP code. Save suggests `.pcraft`; exporting as `.xcf` fails with a message, as PDN does.

- **Read:** XCF versions 0 to 26 (32-bit pointers up to 10, 64-bit after; newer files open with a note); uncompressed, RLE and zlib tiles; 8/16/32-bit integer and 16/32/64-bit float precisions (32-bit integer opens as 16-bit, floats as 32-bit float with HDR values kept; linear-light precisions get a linear sRGB or linear gray profile); RGB and grayscale as such, indexed through its colour map as RGB.
- **Layers:** any size and position (off-canvas too), opaque layers as locked-transparency layers, groups rebuilt from `PROP_ITEM_PATH` (nested, Pass through), names, opacity (`FLOAT_OPACITY` over `OPACITY`), visibility, offsets, layer masks applied or disabled, lock alpha/content/position, colour tags, GIMPhoto's `gimphoto-clipped` parasite as a clipping mask.
- **Blend modes:** the 2.10 set and the legacy set mapped to Photoshop's; Addition → Linear Dodge, Dodge/Burn → Color Dodge/Burn, HSV/LCH/luma modes to the HSL-based ones with a note, and the seven with no counterpart (Behind, Grain extract/merge, Color erase, Erase, Merge, Split) as Normal with a note naming the layer.
- **Image:** ICC profile (`icc-profile` parasite), resolution, guides, the comment (as document text metadata), extra channels as alpha channels, the saved selection as the selection.
- **Reported, not applied:** GIMP 3 layer effects (the layer opens unfiltered), paths, floating selections; text, vector and link layers open as their pixels.
- **Never panics:** every read is bounds-checked; canvases ≤ 300,000 px a side and 1 GiB of pixels, ≤ 8,192 layers, ≤ 1,024 channels, nesting ≤ 64, payloads ≤ 64 MiB, gzip…

author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #1481.

**Why**
In Photoshop, with a pop-up list open (for example the Layers panel blend modes), typing a letter jumps to the next item that starts with it, and the same letter again cycles through the matches. Letters typed quickly match a longer prefix, and Enter chooses the item. In PhotoCraft a letter did nothing in the list, and a tool shortcut fired underneath instead: M switched to the Marquee tool.

**Change**

title: Text fields: right-click edit menu (#2921)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2921 (scorecard row UI-217-8, part of #217)

## What changed
Right-clicking in any text field now opens a small edit menu at the pointer: **Undo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Delete, Select All**. It works in the layer rename field, number fields being typed into, and dialog and panel fields. The items act on that field's text and selection:

- A right-click inside the current selection keeps it, so Copy and Cut take it. Before this, egui moved the caret to the pointer on any press. A right-click elsewhere in the field puts the caret there, as on Windows.
- Cut, Copy and Delete are disabled when nothing is selected.
- Esc closes only the menu: the field keeps its focus and a layer rename stays open.
- Clicking a menu item doesn't take the field's focus (a layer rename would otherwise commit). A press anywhere else closes the menu and still does what it normally does.
- The right-click belongs to the field and never opens the canvas, tool or layer-row menus.
- Field keyboard shortcuts are unchanged.

**How:** `crates/ui-egui/src/text_field_menu.rs` adds an egui plugin, so every `TextEdit` gets the menu without a wrapper.
- Its end-of-pass hook opens the menu on a secondary press in the focused field. Its begin-pass hook closes it. Its input hook removes Esc while the menu is open.
- The app draws the menu at the very start of `ui()`, before any field. The menu can't be drawn inside a plugin hook: a widget under the pointer calls back into the locked plugins and deadlocks.
- A chosen item gives the field back its focus and pushes the matching input into that pass: egui's `Copy`/`Cut` events, Cmd+A, Cmd+Z or Delete. The field handles it later in the same pass, after the app shortcuts have already run.
- Paste sends `ViewportCommand::RequestPaste`, the same clipboard path Cmd+V uses in a field. It works on web too.
- While the menu is open, `surrender_focus_on` is `Never`. The previous value comes back when the menu closes.

**Not covered:** spelling suggestions. The spell …

title: Add FITS read/write (astronomy images)
author: dmoulton
body:
## Summary

Adds FITS (Flexible Image Transport System), the standard astronomy image format, as a flat format you can open and save: `.fits`, `.fit` and `.fts` in File › Open, Save As and the batch commands. Astrophotographers can now edit stacks from Siril, PixInsight or DeepSkyStacker, and frames from capture software, without converting to TIFF first.

**Why a built-in codec and not a plug-in:** plug-in ABI v1 is filter-only, and `docs/plugins.md` lists plug-in-provided file formats as not in v1. So FITS is a codec in `photocraft-codecs`, built in like Netpbm, with no new dependencies.

## Behaviour

**Reading** (`crates/codecs/src/codecs/fits.rs`)
- The image in the primary HDU, or the first `IMAGE` extension when the primary HDU is empty.
- `BITPIX` 8, 16, 32, 64, -32 and -64, with `BSCALE`/`BZERO` and integer `BLANK`.
- `NAXIS3 = 3` opens as RGB. Any other plane count opens the first plane as gray with `DecodeWarning::MorePages`.
- Rows follow `ROWORDER`, bottom-up by default (the FITS convention; Siril and DS9 do the same).
- Values that fit stay exact: unsigned 8-bit as U8, integers in 0..=65535 as U16 (for example a camera's `BITPIX = 16`, `BZERO = 32768`). Everything else becomes F32: values at most 2 are taken as already normalised (Siril, PixInsight), larger ones are divided by 65535 when they fit in it (DeepSkyStacker) and by the maximum otherwise. NaN and blank pixels read as 0.
- Other header cards are kept as `Metadata::text`: string values unquoted, `COMMENT`/`HISTORY` by their text, `HIERARCH` keywords by their long name. Cards that describe the data layout are dropped, because after decoding they no longer describe the pixels.

**Writing**
- Gray or RGB; U8 (`BITPIX = 8`), U16 (`BITPIX = 16`, `BZERO = 32768`) or F32 (`BITPIX = -32`, 0..1). Bottom-up rows, with `ROWORDER = 'BOTTOM-UP'`.
- Text metadata becomes header cards. Names that aren't valid FITS keywords use `HIERARCH`, or a `COMMENT` card when they don't fit in one card.
- `caps()` declare…

title: Type: Edit › Paste, Copy and Select › All work on the text being typed (#2893)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2893

## Root cause

Two things made pasting into a type layer fail for the reporter (macOS, v0.6.0):

1. **⌘V.** With the native macOS menu bar, AppKit takes ⌘V as Edit › Paste's key equivalent, so a text edit never got the paste. This is already fixed on `main` by #2568 (commit 0a189375), which is not in v0.6.0.
2. **Edit › Paste from the menu** (still broken on `main`, on every platform). While editing type, `menus::invoke` routes only `edit.cut` through the type editor (#1355). `edit.paste` still ran the pixel paste, which has nothing to paste when the clipboard holds text. `edit.copy` copied rendered pixels, and Select › All selected the canvas instead of the characters.

## Fix

While a type edit is active (`app.ui.text_edit`):
- **Edit › Paste** sends `ViewportCommand::RequestPaste`. The clipboard text arrives as a `Paste` event the next frame, and the type editor uses it to replace the selection, the same path as ⌘V. It is enabled while typing.
- **Edit › Copy** copies the selected characters through the new `type_tool::copy_selection`, which the clipboard Copy event and `cut_selection` now share. It is enabled only when characters are selected, like Cut.
- **Select › All** selects every character, like ⌘A.

Keyboard shortcuts already had this behaviour (`TEXT_OWNED` in `shortcut_dispatch.rs`). Only the menu rows were wrong.

## Tests

`native_menu::tests::copy_and_paste_type_from_native_menu` drives native menu clicks during a type edit. It checks that:
- Select › All selects `Hello`.
- Copy and Paste are enabled.
- Copy emits `CopyText("Hello")` and leaves the pixel clipboard alone.
- Paste emits `RequestPaste`, and the `Paste("World")` event that follows replaces the text, with no layer added and no error.

Without the `menus.rs` change the test fails at the Select › All assertion. With only the Paste arm removed it fails at `Edit > Paste asks the window for the clipboard text`.

title: PSD: don't inflate an over-budget ZIP merged image at parse time (#2926)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2926

## Root cause

`validate_planes` (run by `ImageData::read` inside `PsdFile::from_bytes`) used `layout.total_bytes()`, which has no cap, as the only bound on its zlib loop. A file declaring a merged image larger than `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` (e.g. a 300000² PSB) with a ZIP/ZIP+prediction stream was inflated at parse time up to the declared size plus 1 MiB, far past the decode budget. Yet `decode_planes` refuses that layout with `LimitExceeded` before it touches the stream, so all that work led to the same error.

## Fix

When the declared size is over `MAX_DECODED_BYTES`, the ZIP stream is kept verbatim and not inflated, the same way an unknown compression method is handled. Decoding still reports `LimitExceeded`. Streams within the budget are validated as before, including the Adler-32 checksum, and the Raw and RLE paths are unchanged. Parse-time work on any ZIP merged image is now bounded by `MAX_DECODED_BYTES + 1 MiB` of output.

The issue suggested refusing the file outright. I chose to skip the stream instead, because refusing would break layered PSBs that open today. `psd_import` only decodes the merged composite when something needs it, and only warns when that decode fails. So a layered file whose composite is over the budget (but whose layers are within it) still opens. Before this change such a file also opened, but only after inflating more than 8 GiB.

## Tests

- `compression::tests::zip_over_budget_is_not_decompressed_at_parse`: feeds garbage zlib bytes with an over-budget layout. Validation passes, which proves nothing was inflated. Decode returns `LimitExceeded`. A layout within the budget still rejects the garbage.
- `file::write_tests::over_budget_zip_merged_image_opens_without_inflating`: patches a layered ZIP PSB to 300000². `from_bytes` succeeds, the layers are there, and `decode_merged` returns `LimitExceeded`.
- `tests/malformed.rs::huge_declared_dimensions_small_data`: its ZIP half used to expect a parse error. It now expects `LimitExc…

author: davidmann4
body:
Part of the #204 dead-settings sweep.

**Why**
In Photoshop, Preferences › File Handling › Image Previews (Always Save / Never Save / Ask When Saving) decides whether PSD and PSB files carry a thumbnail image resource. That is resource 1036: a 28-byte kJpegRGB header followed by JFIF data, at most 160 px on the long side, as described in Adobe's PSD spec. title: PSD: cap the layer tree in psd_to_document; layered TIFF checks group depth (#2940)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2940

## Root cause

When you open a PSD/PSB file, `import_stages` runs the `group_depth` preflight and rejects nesting deeper than `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` before conversion. Two other paths skipped that check:

- The public `psd_to_document` (and `psd_to_document_with`) called `file.layer_tree()`. That builds the whole `LayerNode` tree, as deep as the file nests its groups (up to about 16,000 levels). `Ctx::build` capped the tree only after that, and dropping it was still recursive at the file's full depth.
- Layered TIFF (`tiff_layers::import_layered`) calls `psd_to_document` with no preflight at all.

## Fix

- **photocraft-psd:** new `PsdFile::layer_tree_max_depth(n)`. It builds the tree iteratively, like `layer_tree`. A group nested `n` or more groups deep keeps its own node but not its children, so the tree is never more than `n + 1` levels deep. Walking it or dropping it recursively is therefore bounded. `layer_tree()` now just calls it with `usize::MAX`, so its behaviour doesn't change.
- **psd_to_document_with** builds its tree with `layer_tree_max_depth(MAX_GROUP_DEPTH)`. That is the cap `Ctx::build` and `apply_link_groups` already apply: a group at the cap keeps no children. The imported document and its warnings are the same as before.
- **Layered TIFF** now rejects nesting past the cap with the same `layer groups nested deeper than 100` error as a PSD. The check lives in a new helper, `psd_import::check_group_depth`, which the PSD path now uses too.

## Tests

- `psd/tests/tree.rs::layer_tree_max_depth_drops_deeper_children` checks a 3-deep nesting at caps 0, 1, 2 and `usize::MAX`. It fails when the cap check is removed.
- `io/tests/tiff_layers.rs::layered_tiff_nested_past_the_cap_is_rejected` builds a TIFF whose 37724 layer data nests 101 groups, and expects the limit error. At 100 groups the file still imports. Without the new check in `import_layered`, the test fails: before this change the 101-level file imported.

title: Speed up large-radius Unsharp Mask with guarded FFT convolution
author: optimalbytee
body:
Large-radius Unsharp Mask repeatedly filtered and copied large tile halos, making full-resolution application and the existing slider preview slow. This change adds native FFT convolution using the existing `rustfft` dependency and the original discrete Gaussian coefficients, plus a streamed separable fallback that preserves the original tap order.

The FFT path handles radius 64–1000 and at least 65,536 output pixels when the threshold is zero or negative and the amount is nonzero. Positive thresholds, unstable samples, unsupported geometry and insufficient scratch use the exact path. Wasm retains exact processing. Alpha, hidden colour, selections, edge policy, cancellation and command/history behavior are preserved. Smart Sharpen, High Pass and shared blur math are unchanged; no dependencies or unsafe code are added.

### Performance and numerical accuracy

Measurements supplied by the handoff: Windows x86-64, Ryzen 7 9700X, eight Rayon workers, normal release profile. Full-operation medians from three alternating before/after pairs following two warmups:

| Workload, amount 150 / threshold 0 | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 MP RGBA8, radius 300 | 19.869 s | 533.823 ms | 37.22× |
| 24 MP RGBA8, radius 1000 | 79.472 s | 777.857 ms | 102.17× |
| 24 MP RGBA16, radius 300 | 19.315 s | 550.603 ms | 35.08× |
| 24 MP RGBA32f HDR, radius 300 | 19.352 s | 574.254 ms | 33.70× |
| 36.15 MP RGBA8, radius 300 | 27.833 s | 849.792 ms | 32.75× |

The existing 4K radius-1000 preview computation improved from 12.035 s to 113.038 ms at factor 2, and from 55.979 s to 408.382 ms at factor 1. Those preview runs used baseline-then-candidate ordering and include proxy creation, scaled parameters, engine command/history and CPU flattening. They exclude scheduling, egui frames and GPU presentation; these are not measured event-to-screen times or Linux results.

title: control: allow requests that operate an open Camera Raw dialog
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
`ui.menu.invoke` rejects Camera Raw's documented `ui.set`/`ui.commit`/`ui.cancel` payloads while the Camera Raw dialog is open. Consequently, a native RAW import can open its adjustment dialog but automation cannot finish it. This is also reported as unaddressed in [#2919](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2919).

Allow a request that operates the existing Camera Raw dialog through its own modal gate. It must contain only the `ui` object; other dialogs, discard confirmation, crop restrictions and command authorization still apply. Native menu clicks and ordinary engine-command behavior are unchanged.

Reproduced in the native app on Apple M1 Pro after confirming the embedded-profile prompt and verifying that no other dialog remained: Camera Raw continuation still returned `menu command is unavailable while a modal dialog is open`.

title: Select and Mask: Refine Edge Brush (#2972)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2972
Part of #214 (scorecard TOOL-214-1)

**Depends on #2970** (stacked on its branch: the brush lives in the Select and Mask view-mode module `select_mask_view.rs` that #2970 adds). Until #2970 merges, the diff here also shows its commit; the change of this PR is the last commit.

## What changed
Select and Mask had no Refine Edge Brush. Photoshop's brush paints where edge refinement happens: brushing over hair or fur picks up detail beyond the Radius band, and Alt-painting restores the original edge.

- **Engine** (`select.refineEdge`): new `refineStrokes` param, `[{"points":[[x,y],…],"size":px=30,"mode":"add|subtract"}]`, applied in painting order. Agents and actions can drive and record it like any other param.
- **Algorithm** (`photocraft-algo`, new `matting/brush.rs`): strokes are rasterised into a signed coverage map. Added areas are treated as unknown. Each pixel's coverage comes from projecting its colour onto the line between the mean known foreground and background colours nearby: normalised convolution over a box the brush's size, reaching four times as far where nothing is near (one fg/bg colour pair per window, after Levin et al.'s colour-line model). Restored areas keep the original edge. The tiled `refine_mask` grows its box and halo to cover the brush, so the result does not depend on tiling. Works at 8, 16 and 32-bit float depth.
- **Never crash**: non-array or malformed strokes, non-finite points, sizes outside 1–5000 px, more than 4096 strokes or 100k points, and strokes that sweep more than 2^28 px all return `BadParams`.
- **Dialog**: new controls: Refine Edge Brush (R), Mode (Expand Detection Area / Restore Original Edge; Alt swaps them), Size (`[` / `]`) and Clear Brush Strokes. With the brush on, dragging on the canvas under the dialog draws a brush ring and paints into the dialog's `refineStrokes` field. The live preview (scaled to the proxy), Show Edge (which now includes the painted area) and OK all use those strokes.

title: Pixel grid: fade the line colour across mid-tones instead of flipping at one luma
author: Jeremy8776
body:
## What

The pixel grid picked a white or a black line per pixel with a hard cut at luma 0.55. On an image whose tones sit near that value (a mid-tone texture, skin, terracotta), neighbouring cells fall on either side of the cut, so the grid shows bright lines, dark lines and different line strengths in patches. The patch boundaries trace the 0.55 contour of the image, which reads as outlined blobs over the picture.

Measured on a screenshot of such an image: lines were lighter than their cell for 99% of cells below luma 0.54, 67% between 0.54 and 0.56, and 2% above 0.56.

## Change

The line is now a white layer and a black layer weighted by a smoothstep over luma 0.35 to 0.75. Dark and light pixels keep the existing white and black lines; mid-tones get a faint line that varies smoothly. The change in a mid-tone pixel's value across the 0.51 to 0.59 luma range drops from about 0.2 to about 0.07.

- GPU canvas: the fragment shader in `gpu_canvas.rs`.
- CPU canvas: `pixel_grid.rs` (`light_share`, `cell_color`). The share of black is rounded to eighths so noisy mid-tone pixels still fall into a few colours and equal-colour runs keep merging into long segments.

## Tests

- Unit tests in `pixel_grid.rs`: the fade across the whole luma range has no jumps, mid-tone lines are near-identical, non-finite input reads as dark.
- `checker_canvas.rs`: a GPU render test at 800% over flat greys 0x87 and 0x90 (either side of the old cut) asserts a faint line, and over 0x60 and 0xd0 asserts a clear one. It fails on the old shader (a line 30 levels off its pixel at 0x87).
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and rustfmt are clean; `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --test checker_canvas` passes.

Not run locally: wasm, the corpus, `panic_hunt`. Nothing was checked visually beyond the render test's pixel values.

---

title: Tests: panic_hunt reruns a timed-out command before calling it hung (#2994)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2994

**Root cause.** `panic_hunt` gives each command 4 s on a fresh 24×16 document. The first `type.create` also starts the process-wide text engine (`photocraft_text::shared()`), which scans every system font once. On a machine with a load average of about 35 on 16 cores, that first call took 5.2 s and 3.5 s in two instrumented runs. Every other `execute` stayed under 0.3 s. So the test reported `type.create` as hung whenever the scan went over 4 s.

**What changed** (test only). A command that times out is run once more on a fresh session. A real hang reproduces, and one-time lazy setup doesn't (the rerun waits for the setup to finish). So a timeout now counts only if both runs time out. The deadline stays at 4 s, which is still more than 10 times what any command needs. It is now a named `DEADLINE` constant, and the message says `hung (>4s, twice)`. The failure message already named the command and params.

**Evidence**
- 6 plain runs on upstream/main at load 28–35: all passed, in 25–40 s each.
- 2 instrumented runs (logging any `execute` over 300 ms): only `type.create <- {}`, at 5177 ms and 3489 ms.
- Fails without the fix: with the deadline temporarily set to 1 s, the old single-run check fails with `type.create [hung] <- {}` and `type.fonts [hung] <- {}`. `type.fonts` waits on the font scan that the abandoned `type.create` thread is still running. With the rerun, the same 1 s deadline passes.

**Commands**
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` (passes, 15.7 s)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt -p photocraft-engine -- --check`
