title: Animated GIF: every frame loads into video layers (#572)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #572 (the import part; follow-ups are listed below).

## What changed

An animated GIF used to open as its first frame only. Now every frame goes into a video layer:

- `photocraft-codecs`: `decode_gif_frames` returns each frame composited onto the logical screen (disposal methods applied) as RGBA8, with its delay in milliseconds. `decode` is unchanged. A damaged later frame keeps the frames before it and marks the first with `DecodeWarning::Truncated`. Dimensions, the total decoded bytes and a frame cap (`MAX_GIF_FRAMES`, 100 000) are checked against `Limits`. New `decode_gif` fuzz target.
- `photocraft-io`: `import_gif_frames` hands the frames over one at a time as single-layer documents, so the caller can flatten and drop each one.
- `photocraft-engine`: New Video Layer from File, Replace Footage, Reload Frame and Video Frames to Layers take all frames of a GIF. The timeline rate comes from the GIF's delays: the most common one, with delays under 20 ms shown at 100 ms as browsers do. An explicit `fps` still wins.

File › Open is not changed: it still opens the first frame with the existing warning.

## Not in this PR

- Per-frame delays: the timeline has one rate.
- The frame stack is still not stored in `.pcraft` (already noted in `doc/src/video.rs`), so a saved document keeps the current frame only.
- Playback in Save for Web.

I'll open separate issues for these.

## How it was checked

- `cargo test -p photocraft-codecs`, `-p photocraft-io --lib --tests`, `-p photocraft-engine --lib`, and engine `panic_hunt`.

title: Free Transform: ⌘-drag of a corner scales editable type instead of distorting it (#3010)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3010

## Root cause
Distort and Perspective are greyed for editable type (#2630/#2701), and the engine's `edit.transform` refuses a non-affine quad on a type layer. But the Free Transform box's gestures in `crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs` (`Hit::Corner(i) if mods.command`, and the ⌘⌥⇧ perspective arm) didn't look at the layer kind, so ⌘-dragging a corner distorted the box freely and the commit then failed with "Distort and Perspective need rasterized type", losing the transform.

## Fix
`pointer` now checks `distort_refused` for the box: the same rule that greys the menu items (the box's layer is type, and the box isn't on a path, the selection outline or a lone mask/channel). When it holds, a corner drag drops ⌘ (and a Distort/Perspective mode falls back to Free), so ⌘-drag and ⌘⌥⇧-drag act as a plain corner drag: they scale, with ⌥ and ⇧ keeping their usual meaning. ⌘-drag of an edge (skew) is unchanged, since type can be skewed. The box can no longer reach a state the commit refuses.

## Tests
- `transform_type_tests::distort_and_perspective_corner_drags_scale_editable_type`: ⌘-drag and ⌘⌥⇧-drag a corner of a type layer's box; the box stays a parallelogram, the commit reports no error and the layer is still live type. It fails without the fix (the box isn't a parallelogram).

## Commands
```
cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- transform_tool transform_type   # 59 passed
cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check

title: Print through CUPS over IPP and the print portal: File › Print works in the Flatpak
author: diegochagas
body:
Fixes #2728.

## What changed

File › Print reaches the printer from inside the Flatpak, and on any Linux or macOS system without an `lp` binary. Windows is untouched here (PR #2748 adds its spooler); the UI is untouched too, the change is in the engine, a new crate and the desktop app's start-up.

- **`photocraft-ipp`** (new standalone crate, ~580 lines, no dependencies): a pure-Rust IPP client (RFC 8010/8011 over HTTP/1.1, content-length or chunked replies) for the three operations printing needs: `CUPS-Get-Printers`, `CUPS-Get-Default` and `Print-Job` with the PDF as the document. It talks to CUPS over its Unix socket or TCP: `CUPS_SERVER` first (as CUPS reads it), then `/run/cups/cups.sock`, `/var/run/cups/cups.sock`, macOS's `/private/var/run/cupsd`, then `localhost:631`. A printer-less CUPS answers the listing with `0x0406 No destinations added.`; that is an empty list, not an error (found by the live test below). Every read is bounds-checked; replies are capped at 16 MiB.
- **Engine** (`print_cmds.rs`): `spool_pdf` no longer spawns `lp`. The job (`PrintJob`: the PDF, printer, copies, title, paper, orientation) goes through the CUPS client after **resolving the printer**: the one asked for (case-insensitively), else the server's default, else the only one, else an error naming the choices; with no printer at all the error says to add one or print to PDF. The spool file is removed once the job is handed over (only a requested `output` stays). `Session.print_spooler` takes an app-installed **`Spooler`**: a second route used when the CUPS client has none (no server reachable, no printer set up), or for every job when `preferred`. New command **`file.print.printers`** → `{server, default, printers: [{name, info, state, acceptingJobs, default}]}` (empty list plus a `note` when no server answers); `"printServer": "host[:port]|socket"` on both commands sends to a named server. title: Tests: the marquee ellipse check walks several dash periods of the curve
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## Problem

`marquee_previews_show_while_dragging_on_white_and_black_at_1x_and_2x` (drag_preview_canvas.rs) is red across CI right now — on PRs and on main itself (runs 38093590497, 38092205482), ubuntu and windows alike, always the same panic:

```
panicked at crates/ui-egui/tests/drag_preview_canvas.rs:185:25:
ellipseMarquee on white @1x at [407.5 355.5]: 0.25 contrasting
```

Nothing else in any failing job is red.

## Root cause (measured, not guessed)

The ellipse assertions sampled ~12 positions along a ~28 px straight chord of a 4-on/4-off marching-ants pattern — a margin of exactly one sample (0.25 = 3/12 vs the 0.3 bar). The dash phase is deterministic per build, but any perturbation (renderer AA, the half-pixel vertex snapping #2732 added, phase tuning) flips the roll: the same code passed on CI main at 23:01 and failed at 22:42; it fails deterministically on a local GPU with the identical 0.25. The check sat exactly on a cliff.

## Fix

- Walk the true document-space ellipse around each edge midpoint over ±0.3 rad (≈5 dash periods, 49 points), with a ±2 physical px band hugging the curve — coverage settles at ~0.5 wherever the phase put the dashes. New `coverage_along` helper samples ~every physical px along the polyline (the old straight-chord helper's end-skipping does not fit a 0.9 px-segment polyline).
- `ink()` accepts a quarter of the luma range (`l < 192` / `l > 63`) instead of a tenth: the 1 px ants snapped to the half-pixel grid render roughly half their length as antialiasing, and the ramp *is* the ant. Measured 0.44–0.79 across all 16 midpoints (1×/2×, both backgrounds) against the 0.3 bar; the rect/lasso checks only gain margin, and the `was < 0.05` before-image guard is unaffected (uniform background scores 0).

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --test drag_preview_canvas`: 5/5 runs green (was failing deterministically before, `0.25 < 0.3` every run).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib marquee`: 24 passed, 1 ignored …

title: Transform: Distort, Perspective and Warp keep shape layers live (#3009)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3009

## Root cause
`transform_layer` (`crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs`) only handled affine maps for shape layers and `warp_layer` (`crates/engine/src/warp_cmds.rs`) refused shapes outright. The UI still let you drag a Distort/Perspective box or edit a Warp mesh on a shape layer, so the work was lost at commit with "needs a rasterized shape". Photoshop maps the shape's path and keeps it a live shape layer.

## Fix
- **photocraft-vector**, new `map` module:
  - `map_points` sends every anchor and control point through a map, which is what Distort and Perspective need. For a projective map this is exact for straight segments, and curves keep their exact end tangents. Between the ends it approximates the rational image, the same way control-point mapping does elsewhere. Anchor count is unchanged.
  - `map_path` handles a curved map (Warp). It splits each segment in halves until the mapped control points follow the mapped curve within 0.1 px. A segment is split into at most 64 pieces, and the depth is reduced for huge paths so the total stays bounded. A straight segment whose image is still straight stays a straight segment. The anchors added by splitting are smooth.
- **engine**: Distort/Perspective and Warp now map a shape's path instead of refusing. A live rectangle, ellipse, polygon or line becomes a plain path because its parameters can't describe the distorted outline. A linked vector mask now follows Distort, Perspective and Warp too. Before, non-affine transforms and warps left it in place. If a map would send a point to infinity, the command returns an error instead of storing a corrupt path.

## Tests
- `transform_cmds::tests::shapes_move_and_transform_as_vectors` asserted the old refusal. It now distorts a rectangle shape, then checks that the layer is still a shape layer, that its anchors are the quad's corners, that it is no longer a live rectangle, and that it renders to the quad's bounds. It then warps the shape (Arc) and checks that the resu…

title: Color: honour the EXIF sRGB tag on open; wire Ignore EXIF Profile Tag (#204)
author: timothydaly1
body:
Preferences › File Handling › Ignore EXIF Profile Tag was one of the settings that do nothing (#204). It did nothing because PhotoCraft never read the tag it's about, so this PR adds that too.

### Behaviour
Cameras often write no ICC profile, just the EXIF ColorSpace tag (0xA001) set to sRGB. Photoshop opens such a file as sRGB. PhotoCraft treated it as untagged, so it took the working space. With a wide working space (Display P3, Adobe RGB…) the camera's sRGB values were reinterpreted and the colours came out oversaturated.

Now, in `ColorState::open_policy`, an RGB file with no embedded profile and EXIF ColorSpace = sRGB is tagged sRGB *before* the Color Settings policy runs. It then goes through the same path as any embedded profile: kept, reported as a mismatch (`ask` as configured), or converted. The report carries `exif: true` so a prompt can say where the profile came from. An embedded ICC profile always wins over the tag.

**Ignore EXIF Profile Tag** (off by default, as in Photoshop) restores the old reading: the file is untagged and takes the working space. The setting is no longer hidden, so Preferences › File Handling shows it; its label was already translated in all 16 catalogues.

**At default settings** (sRGB working space) the colours are unchanged. The only difference is that such a file now opens tagged sRGB instead of untagged, as in Photoshop, so saving embeds sRGB if Embed Color Profile is on.

### Code
- `photocraft_codecs::exif_color_space`: a new module, `exif_color.rs`. It follows IFD0's Exif pointer (0x8769) to ColorSpace, with every offset checked; anything malformed, truncated or out of range reads as no tag. It reuses `orientation.rs`'s TIFF helpers.
- `ColorState::open_policy(doc, ignore_exif)`: its only caller, `Session::open_document`, passes the setting.
- Scorecard regenerated: settings that do nothing go from **43 to 42 of 150**.

title: Type: scan system fonts off the UI thread (#3021)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3021
Refs #2518

## Root cause
`photocraft_text::shared()` is a `OnceLock`, and its first call scans every installed font. Nothing called it earlier, so the call came from `type_tool::font_picker`, which evaluates `&families()` on every frame. As a result, the full scan ran inside the first UI frame that showed the Type tool. That frame lasted over 60 s on the Mac in #2518, and it is slow on any machine with large font folders.

## What changed
- **photocraft-text**:
  - `warm_shared()` starts building the shared engine (the system font scan) on a background thread named `photocraft-font-scan`.
  - `try_shared()` returns the engine without blocking. It returns `None` while the scan runs, and its first call starts the scan if nothing has.
  - When there are no system fonts (web, tests, `PHOTOCRAFT_NO_SYSTEM_FONTS`), the engine is cheap, so `try_shared()` builds it in place. It also builds it in place if the thread can't be spawned or the worker died.
  - `shared()` still blocks. Engine type commands (`type.create` and the rest) keep using it, because they run on a user action and need the fonts. If the scan is still running, they wait for it to finish rather than starting a second one.
- **Desktop app**: `main()` warms the fonts right after the crash hook is installed.
- **UI**: the font menus that draw every frame no longer block. While the scan runs they show a disabled "Loading fonts…" box and request a repaint, and the real menus appear once it finishes. This covers:
  - the options bar's family and style menus
  - the Character panel
  - the Glyphs panel
  - the Character/Paragraph Styles family menus

  `selected_style` falls back to the stored style name while the fonts load.
- "Loading fonts…" is added to all 16 catalogs.

## Relation to #2644

title: Transform Path: Distort, Perspective and Warp apply to paths (#3027)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3027

Depends on #3025 (this branch is stacked on it: it uses `vector::map` and `vector_cmds::map_path` / `map_shape` from that PR; the diff here shows both until #3025 merges, only the last commit is this change).

## Root cause
`path.transform` only accepted an affine `matrix` (or translate/scale/angle). The Free Transform Path commit in `transform_tool::commit` converted the box to an affine map and, when the box had been pulled out of a parallelogram (⌘-drag of a corner, Edit › Transform Path › Distort / Perspective), refused with "Distort and Perspective can't be applied to a path". Warp was also blocked on a path box (`enter_warp` and the right-click menu excluded paths), while Photoshop's Transform Path menu offers Warp.

## Change
- **Engine `path.transform`** also takes:
  - `quad`: `[[x,y]×4]`, where the frame's corners go (Distort / Perspective), with an optional `rect` frame (default: the path's control bounds);
  - a warp: `style` / `mesh` / `warp`, as `edit.transform.warp`.
  
  Params are validated (finite numbers, magnitude ≤ 1e6, positive frame, non-degenerate invertible quad, finite mapped result) and return `Err`, never panic. A parallelogram quad is turned back into an affine map, so a live shape stays live. Work path, saved paths, vector masks and shape layers (re-rendered via `with_shape`) all go through the same code, one "Transform Path" undo step.
- **UI**: the Free Transform Path commit sends `matrix` for an affine box, else `rect` + `quad`, or the warp in Warp mode. Warp mode is now available on a path box (outline drawn through the warp); a smart object's stored warp is not picked up for a path session.

author: vangel76

## What changed

- **`path.stroke` takes every brush-based tool** from Photoshop's Stroke Path dialog. The Brush, Pencil and Eraser are still rendered directly. author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3033

Depends on #2862 (Artboard tool). This branch is stacked on it, so the diff shows #2862's commits until that merges; this PR's own change is the last commit.

## What changed
- **"+" buttons.** With the Artboard tool, the selected board shows a "+" button beside each of its four sides, as in Photoshop. A click adds an empty board of the same size on that side. The new board copies the source's background and preset, sits the usual 100 px artboard gap away and skips past any board in the way. ⌥-click adds a copy of the board with its contents instead. A board placed left of or above the canvas origin shifts the whole document right or down and grows the canvas, so the new board stays visible. Over a button the pointer turns into a hand.
- **⇧ keeps proportions.** While you drag a corner handle, holding ⇧ keeps the board's aspect ratio. The opposite corner stays put and the board scales by the larger of the two axis factors. ⇧ is read on every pointer event, so pressing or releasing it mid-drag takes effect at once.
- **Engine.** New command `layer.artboard.addBeside` `{"layer":id?,"side":"left|right|top|bottom"="right","duplicate":bool=false} → {layer, rect}`, so agents can drive it. Each click is one undo step. Proportional resizing still goes through `layer.artboard.set` with a `rect`. `image_cmds::translate_doc` is now `pub(crate)` so the command can reuse it to shift the document.
- Scorecard FILE-215-20: the note now lists the "+" buttons and ⇧ (`docs/scorecard.md` regenerated).

- `artboard_cmds::tests::add_beside_places_a_board_on_each_side_and_alt_duplicates_contents` (engine) checks:

title: Actions: a command that runs other commands is recorded once (#3067)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3067

## Root cause

`Session::dispatch` → `after_command` journals every successful journaled command, nested or not. A command that runs other commands through `s.execute` (Straighten Layer runs `image.rotation.arbitrary` and `image.crop`; Transform Again on a copy runs `layer.duplicate` + `edit.transform`; `file.scripts.browse`, `file.automate.batch` and droplets run their steps) left the inner entries in the journal, followed by its own entry. Action recording copies every replayable entry, so playback applied the work twice. Straighten recorded `[rulerTool, image.rotation.arbitrary, image.crop, straightenLayer]` and playback rotated and cropped twice (4 steps ran).

## Fix

The fix is in one place and covers every command, so no command has to handle this itself. `dispatch` notes the journal length before a command runs. When a **replayable** journaled command succeeds, `after_command` truncates the journal to that mark before it pushes the command's own entry. The command's entry now stands for the commands it ran.

- Edit › Transform › Again is deliberately not replayable: it records the concrete `edit.transform` it ran (#1440). It keeps that behaviour unchanged.
- **Transform Again on a Copy** (`edit.transform.againCopy`) is now not replayable either, for the same reason as Transform Again in #1440. It looks up the last `edit.transform` in the journal, so a recorded wrapper failed with "there is no transform to repeat" in a session that never ran a transform. It records its concrete steps instead: `layer.duplicate` + `edit.transform`. With one layer selected, the duplicate step names no layer id ("duplicate the current layer"), so it plays on any document. With several layers selected it keeps the id, as before. The first commit of this PR had dropped those concrete steps and kept only the wrapper.
- **Failed commands that take their work back** now also drop the commands they ran from the journal. These are `compound` (Straighten, Place Scale Marker,…

title: Artboards: a board moved past the canvas origin grows the canvas left/up (#3070)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3070

## Root cause
`artboard_cmds::fit_canvas` only grew the canvas out to the boards' right and bottom edges. A board moved left of or above the origin stayed partly or fully off-canvas. This happened with a Move tool drag, with `layer.translate`, and with `layer.artboard.set` given a negative `x`/`y`. Photoshop's artboard documents grow in every direction.

## What changed
- `fit_canvas` (shared by new/duplicate/from-group/from-layers/edit artboard and `layer.translate` on a board) now takes the union of the canvas and every board per axis. If that union reaches past the origin, it shifts the whole document right/down by the overhang and then grows the canvas. The shift uses `image_cmds::translate_doc`, now `pub(crate)`, and moves pixels, masks, channels, selection, type/shape geometry, artboard rects, guides, paths, slices and notes. All of this runs inside the command's existing `s.edit`, so the move and the shift are one undo step.
- An axis isn't shifted when its boards span more than the 300,000 px canvas limit, or when `translate_doc` refuses because pixels would leave the 32-bit range. `translate_doc` checks before it moves anything. The board then stays partly off-canvas, the same as a board past the size limit today, so the extreme-coordinate tests from #931 keep passing.
- The signature `fit_canvas(&mut Document)` is unchanged.

## Relation to #3046
#3046 (`layer.artboard.addBeside`) does its own `translate_doc` shift before it inserts a board left of or above the origin. It also makes `translate_doc` `pub(crate)` with the identical edit, so the two merge cleanly. With this PR that shift is redundant: `add_beside` could insert the board at its negative rect and let `fit_canvas` shift. #3046 still works unchanged, because after its own shift `fit_canvas` sees no overhang and does nothing more.

title: Layers: clip groups follow New Layer, Arrange, Reorder and Delete (#2203)
author: timothydaly1
body:
Part of #2203. Adding, moving or deleting layers never updated `Layer::clipped`. A new layer created with a clipping base active split the group and became the base of the layers above it: the reporter's "intermediate layers are ignored". Moving or deleting a base left its clipped layers clipping to whatever ended up below them.

### Rules
These come from the 17 cases @davidmann4 measured in Photoshop 27.11 in the issue's triage. They're implemented in a new `crates/engine/src/clip_group.rs`:

1. A layer added or moved **joins the clip group it lands in**: it's clipped when the layer directly above its new slot is clipped (unless that layer is part of its own group travelling with it).
2. A clipped layer that's moved **stays clipped while it still sits on a clip group**: the layer below its new slot is clipped, or was in its group. For example, `B C1* C2*` + Bring Forward on C1 gives `B C2* C1*`. Otherwise it's released: `B C* U` + Bring Forward on C gives `B U C`.
3. When a base **moves away or is deleted**, the layers clipped to it are released. Rule 1 reads the stack *before* this release, which reproduces the odd row 12: `B C1* C2*` + Bring Forward on B gives `C1 B* C2`.
4. A clipped run left with **nothing below it** is released. The compositor already draws such a run unclipped, so no pixels change.

### Where they apply
- `layer.new.layer`, which gains `clipToPrevious` (Photoshop's *Use Previous Layer to Create Clipping Mask*). Inside a clip group the new layer joins it anyway, as in Photoshop.
- `layer.arrange.*`
- `layer.moveTo`: Layers panel drags, multi-layer moves, and ⌥-drag copies.
- `layer.delete`, for one layer or the whole selection.

Each operation stays a single history step.

### Against the measured table
All 17 rows match except row 11, and only in *position*: on `X B C*`, Photoshop's Send Backward puts C below X (`C X B`), while ours steps one slot (`X C B`). C is released in both, so the clipping matches.

title: Actions: Last Filter is recorded as the filter it repeated (#3089)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3089

## Root cause

`filter.lastFilter` is a journaled, replayable command. Its `run` looks up the last filter in the session journal and calls `run_filter` directly, so the journal and any action being recorded got `["filter.lastFilter", {}]` and never the filter that ran. Playing that step depends on the playing session. In a new session it fails with "no filter applied yet". If another filter ran since, it applies that filter instead of the recorded one.

## Fix

`Session::dispatch` runs Last Filter *as* the filter it repeats. After the authorize gate, if there is a last filter, it dispatches that filter with its journaled params (the `layer` removed, as before #1270) and the same `background` flag. As a result:

- the journal and recorded actions hold the concrete filter and its settings, the way Edit › Transform › Again records its `edit.transform` (#1440), and the way Photoshop records the filter rather than "Last Filter";
- Fade, background jobs, the Channels panel target and the smart-object/precondition checks behave exactly as for that filter;
- with no filter yet it falls through to `filter.lastFilter`'s own precondition, which still reports "no filter applied yet". A guard stops it from redirecting to itself.

`last_filter` in `filters.rs` becomes `pub(crate)`.

Independent of #3072: it touches a different part of `dispatch`.

title: Optimise computed brush coverage and native raster row writes
author: optimalbytee
body:
Large computed brush tips spend substantial time generating dense coverage masks and converting native pixel samples. A 3000px brush remains expensive even when it barely touches the document corner, because layer pixels outside the canvas must still be preserved.

This PR adds two focused CPU optimisations:

- Generate coverage for ordinary finite, zero-angle computed round/elliptical tips in a separate contiguous-row kernel, selecting Pencil, hard or soft coverage before the pixel loop. Preserve the original f32 arithmetic and falloff. Tiny antialiased, sampled, rotated, projected, noise, per-tip texture, square Pencil and Wet Edges/depth cases retain the existing renderer.
- Convert `Surface::write_region` samples a row at a time, selecting U8/U16/F32 encoding once per row. Preserve the original quantisation, native-endian bytes, tile allocation and copy-on-write behaviour across colour models and depths.

No dependencies, unsafe code, threading, reduced brush resolution/sampling or output approximations are introduced. Off-canvas layer content is retained.

### Measurements

The coverage change reduces measured 3000px center/edge complete engine stroke medians by **26–39%**. The following comparison keeps the row-conversion optimisation enabled in both binaries: these numbers isolate the additional coverage change, rather than measuring the entire PR against pristine upstream.

title: Numeric fields: typed units, scrubby labels, double-click reset (#3099)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3099 (scorecard row UI-217-13, part of #217)

Arithmetic in value fields already worked (#726, #2252). Three parts were still missing. They now live in the shared widgets, so every field gets them.

## What changed
- **Units in expressions** (`numeric_expression::parse_with_units`, `widgets::value_field`): a number may be followed by a unit: `px`, `in`, `cm`, `mm`, `pt`, `pica`/`pc` or `%`. The unit is converted into the field's own unit, which comes from its suffix. Lengths convert through pixels at the active document's resolution and the Units & Rulers point size. The app sets these each frame with `widgets::set_field_resolution`; without a document they are 72/72. Image Size and New Document show their unit in a separate menu, so they pass it with their own resolution through `widgets::value_field_units`. A field's own non-unit suffix is accepted too (`45°`). `%` after a number means percent only when nothing follows it; `10%3` is still the remainder.
- **Invalid input is rejected and the old value stays:** a unit that can't convert (a length in a % field, `%` in a px field, any unit in a unitless field), plus `1/0`, `1e400`, `((((`, unicode, unknown words and overflowing conversions.
- **Scrubby labels** (`widgets::scrub_label`): dragging a label moves the value field drawn right after it on the same row, one step per point. Shift makes the step ×10 and Alt makes it a tenth as fast. A small-range field steps by 0.01. While the link is active the cursor is the horizontal resize arrow.
  - The link is only made when the field starts within 24 pt to the right of the label (slider rows link across the whole row). A label such as `Mode:` in front of a dropdown therefore never scrubs an unrelated field.
  - It is wired into options-bar labels (`opt_label`: Size, Feather, Opacity, Flow…), every `slider_row` (adjustments, filters, Camera Raw) and the Character panel's icon labels.

title: Web: opt-in embedding bridge for host pages (?host=parent)
author: CyberFox-81
body:
A page that frames PhotoCraft on the same origin can now open files in it and store what it saves, through postMessage, instead of saves and exports becoming browser downloads. Built for a Nextcloud integration, but nothing in it is host-specific.

Only the web shell changes; it plugs into the hooks the app already has:
- photocraft:open from the parent goes through the inbox, like a picked or dropped file
- Services::file_dialog asks the parent where Save, Save As and Export go (photocraft:pick-save / photocraft:picked); File > Open keeps the browser's picker
- Services::write sends the bytes to the parent (photocraft:save)
- photocraft:dirty reports unsaved changes; the parent guards leaving the page, so the shell's own beforeunload guard stays off
- photocraft:ready and photocraft:failed report start-up

Enabled only by ?host=parent inside a frame; only the parent window on the page's own origin is heard or answered. Without it nothing changes.

title: Shortcuts: layout-independent brush keys, Photoshop's German keys plus a fallback for all layouts (#3109)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3109

**Depends on #3106.** This branch is stacked on it. Until #3106 merges, the diff also shows #3106's commits.

## Root cause
Photoshop's `[` `]` (brush size) and ⇧[ ⇧] (hardness) need AltGr on many layouts, so Photoshop itself uses layout-specific keys per language. On German it is `Ö` / `#` (⇧ for hardness). egui has no key for `ö` or `#`, so egui-winit reports the physical key (`;`, `\`), which nothing was bound to.

## Design (layout independent, no hardcoded German path)
New module `crates/ui-egui/src/layout_keys.rs`, called at the top of `shortcuts::handle`. It uses what egui already gives us (`Event::Key { key, physical_key, modifiers }` plus the adjacent `Event::Text`), so no OS layout API and no new dependency. I looked at layout-detection crates: they need OS APIs per platform (and don't work on wasm), while winit's `KeyCode` is exactly the physical key egui already forwards as `physical_key`.
1. **Data table** `LAYOUTS` (`Layout { keys: &[(typed text, shift, key)] }`) for layouts whose Photoshop keys are known. Today: German (`ö`/`Ö` -> `[`, `#`/`'` -> `]`). `COMMON` holds the rows valid everywhere (#3106's `*` -> `+`, `_` -> `-`). To add a layout, append a `Layout` with rows taken from Photoshop itself, plus a test. I could not verify Photoshop's French AZERTY keys from public sources, so there is no AZERTY row.
2. **Fallback for every other layout**: when the keys at the US `[` / `]` positions (egui `physical_key` OpenBracket/CloseBracket) type something that is not a bracket, they act as `[` / `]`. So AZERTY (`^`, `$`), Spanish/Italian (`+`) etc. get working brush size/hardness keys. It never applies with Cmd/Ctrl/Alt, and switches off once a real bracket is typed (e.g. Dvorak) or a table layout's symbol was seen (so German `+` is not a brush key).
3. Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts overrides are unchanged: this only decides which key a press is. Documented in `docs/ui-parity.md` (Keyboard shortcuts).

title: Puppet Warp: the mesh follows the object outline (#3105)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3105 (scorecard TOOL-214-6, part of #214)

## What was wrong
`algo/puppet.rs` `build_mesh` kept every square grid cell that touched the layer's opaque pixels. The mesh edge was a staircase up to a cell outside the shape, and two shapes closer than about one cell shared cells, so a pin on one dragged the other along. In Photoshop the mesh follows the outline (grown or shrunk by Expansion), and an unpinned separate shape stays where it is.

## What changed (algo only; the engine params and UI are unchanged)
- **Outline:** the opaque region (alpha > 0.05) becomes a signed distance field (exact Euclidean distance transform on a block grid, at most 1024 blocks across), offset by **Expansion**, so growing and shrinking are continuous rather than a block stamp. Marching squares traces its zero contour into closed loops (holes too).
- **Boundary points:** each loop is simplified with Douglas–Peucker (half a block, at least 0.5 px), which keeps sharp corners, then its sides are split to the **Density** spacing.
- **Inside:** a triangular lattice at the same spacing, kept at least half a step inside the outline.
- **Triangulation:** incremental Bowyer–Watson Delaunay with neighbour links and a visibility walk. Outline sides missing from the triangulation are split at their midpoints (conforming Delaunay, bounded), and only triangles inside the outline are kept (even-odd test, row-bucketed).
- **Solver ordering:** vertices are numbered in reverse Cuthill–McKee order, which keeps the banded Cholesky narrow. Disconnected pieces no longer widen the band.
- Density now counts steps across the region the mesh covers (the bounds grown by Expansion), so a +200 px Expansion on a 20 px layer no longer builds a 40k-vertex mesh. The old grid builder had the same blow-up.

Visual check (snapshot example, Show Mesh on): the mesh hugs the ellipse, the bar and the separate disc. The disc has its own mesh and stays put while the bar is dragged.

I run a DTF shop, and the RIP reads the spot plate out of a Photoshop TIFF. PhotoCraft was putting that plate in the transparency sample, so the RIP treated the ink as a hole in the shirt.

title: Levels: black, gray and white point eyedroppers (#3116)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3116
Fixes #3127

Depends on #3115 (stacked on it, which is stacked on #3108). Until those merge, the diff here includes their commits; the last commit is this PR's change.

## What changed

Photoshop has Set Black / Neutral Gray / White Point eyedroppers in the Levels dialog and in the Properties panel of a Levels adjustment layer. PhotoCraft had neither.

- **Engine** (`adjust_params.rs`): `levels_eyedropper` resolves a colour sample into Levels.
  - **RGB:** Black and White move each channel's input black or white to the sample's value in that channel, so the sample maps to the output black or white. Gray sets each channel's midtone gamma so the channel maps to the sample's Rec. 709 luma. That removes the cast and keeps the brightness. The gamma is found by bisecting on the compositor's own Levels curve, so the shadow toe is included. Output levels and the composite record are kept.

  - **CMYK and Lab:** these return `Err`, same as Curves.

On a layer it samples the image below that layer and counts as one undo step. Curves and Levels share the param parsing and the dispatch (`adjustment_eyedropper`, `eyedropper_from_params`, `layer_eyedropper`).

title: ui(theme): modernize shadows with delicate multi-layer depth
author: TheTeslak
body:
Previously, shadows across elevation surfaces (popups, menus, floating panels, modals) and the canvas felt muddy, harsh, and dated. In particular, heavy single-layer drop shadows with aggressive opacity created dirty dark bands and visually cluttered outlines, especially noticeable in light themes.

Bring shadow rendering up to modern UI design standards with delicate, clean multi-layer elevation and diffuse lighting:

- Theme: introduce `popup_shadow` token alongside `shadow` across all themes (Dark, Light, Pro, Classic, Adwaita, Breeze, Solarized) with softened, refined alphas to eliminate muddy contrast.
- Theme: implement `upgrade_shadow` and `upgrade_popup_shadow` with `ShadowElevation` levels (Low, Medium, High, Modal), replacing dirty single drops with modern multi-layer ambient and directional key lighting.
- Canvas: replace harsh canvas edge shadows in both CPU painter and GPU fragment shader with soft quadratic diffuse falloff, removing dark bands.
- UI: apply delicate elevation across menus, dialogs, dock tabs, toolbars, palette pickers, and overlay cards.
- Tests: add unit tests for multi-layer shadow injection, zero-alpha no-op handling, and modal backdrop isolation.

title: Add backlog triage tooling: script, de-rot and auto-label workflows, …
author: shmuelbiller1
body:
Add backlog triage tooling: script, de-rot and auto-label workflows, guides
The queue, not the code, is the bottleneck. On 2026-10-11 the repo had 942
open items (647 issues, 295 PRs): only 26 PRs (9%) were mergeable with green
CI, 107 (36%) had merge conflicts, and 929 items (98%) had no labels. Fixes
exist and are waiting on review.

scripts/pr-triage.py classifies every open item (area/kind/platform/size),
cross-references mergeability against check runs, and prints three lists in
the order they can be acted on: merge-now (clean+green, zero work),
auto-rebase (green but drifted), then failing. Every mutating flag is
dry-run until --yes. Stdlib only and shells out to gh, so it never holds a
token.

Two workflows stop the rot recurring:
- pr-derot.yml rebases every open non-draft PR every six hours. Updating a
  branch that is merely behind is mechanical; PRs that still conflict are
  reported, and that list is the real work queue. Nothing merges or closes.
- auto-label.yml labels items as they are opened, so the 98%-unlabelled
  problem cannot come back. Bulk-labelling the existing 900 is left as a
  deliberate one-off because it notifies ~900 authors.

Both were checked against the live API: the de-rot filter was rewritten
after measuring that mergeStateStatus almost never reports BEHIND on this
repo (out-of-date PRs return UNSTABLE instead), and the triage fetch was
made to retry after a throttled run silently reported 0 mergeable PRs.

docs/backlog-triage.md is generated; docs/backlog-shortcuts.md is the
hand-written companion (fast dev loop, where the cheap work hides, perf
ranked by ratio). It notes that the largest measured perf win in the
project - https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2596, P28 Content-Aware Scale 954,192 ms -> 2,641 ms - is
already written, green, and sitting unmerged.

AGENTS.md gains a "check the PR queue first" step and pointers to both docs.

title: Vanishing Point: on-canvas plane editor with Create/Edit Plane, grid and paste (#3122)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3122 (part of #214, scorecard row TOOL-214-14)

## What changed
Filter › Vanishing Point… only opened the generic parameter dialog, so you had to type plane corners as JSON. It now opens a dialog mode on the canvas, built like the Perspective Warp and Puppet Warp modes (`distort_ui`):

- **Create Plane (C):** four clicks make a plane. The clicks can come in any order: corners are normalised clockwise from the top-left (`VpPlane::normalized`), which is the order paste and tear-off expect. Without this, a plane clicked counter-clockwise would paste mirrored.
- **Edit Plane (V):** drag a corner node, or drag an edge node to slide that edge along the plane's own perspective. The homography is frozen at the press, and the edge stops before it crosses the horizon or folds the quad. Click a plane to select it. Delete/Backspace removes it.
- **Grid:** cells are square in the plane's metric (the same camera lift the engine uses), and **Grid Size** sets the cell size in px at the nearest edge. The grid is drawn in the accent colour for a valid plane and warning yellow for a doubtful one (both vanishing points finite but no real focal length fits them, or a corner sharper than 10°). A red outline with no grid marks an invalid quad (self-intersecting or dented). This follows Photoshop's blue/yellow/red (`VpPlane::check` in `photocraft-algo`).

Drag to move it; **Width** sets its size, and **New Layer** renders it onto a new layer. ✓ / ↩ runs `filter.vanishingPoint` with `{"planes", "paste", "newLayer"}` as one history step, so actions record it and agents can replay it exactly. title: fix(ui): remember the last-used tool in each single-key group (close #2608)
author: rollroyces
body:
## Summary

Tool keys cycling to the group's first tool on every press. Pressing `L` from Brush always went back to Freehand Lasso, never to the last Lasso the user had picked (e.g. Polygonal Lasso). Photoshop remembers the last-selected tool in each single-key group so a press of the group key returns to it.

### Fix

- `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`: new field `UiState::last_in_group: HashMap<char, Tool>` and `UiState::set_tool(t)` that updates both `tool` and `last_in_group[t.key()]`. Default-skipped in serialisation so existing UI state stays byte-identical.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`: the toolbar slot click and the Hand-tool double-click route through `set_tool` so mouse picks populate the same memory.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`: the single-key cycling arm in `handle` consults `last_in_group.get(&t.key())` first when the current tool is outside the group, falling back to `group[0]` only on a fresh install. The shift_switch / cycle / keep-current branches are unchanged.

### Tests

`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib shortcuts` ✓ (25 tests, including 1561 filtered). Verified end-to-end.

title: fix(type): return caret after normalized CRLF insertion (#3074)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #3074

## Problem

`type.insertText` normalized CRLF to LF when storing text, but calculated its returned caret from the original input. Inserting `x\r\ny` therefore returned index 4 even though the stored text `x\ny` has three characters, so querying that caret failed.

## Change

Use the existing newline normalizer before counting inserted characters. Add an engine regression that checks the normalized text and passes the returned caret to `type.caret`.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (1,199 unit tests passed, 12 ignored; all integration test binaries passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=12 cargo xtask wasm` (all 24 checks passed)
- `cargo build -p photocraft-cli -j 12`
- CLI smoke: CRLF insertion returned caret 3, and `type.caret` accepted index 3.

Corpus and performance checks were not run because this change only affects a text caret index; it does not touch file formats or pixel rendering.

title: Dialogs: the live dialog stays in front of older ones (stuck stacked profile prompts)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
## Problem

Opening three PNG screenshots together (File › Open with several selected; each has macOS's "Display" profile) put up three Embedded Profile Mismatch prompts. Sometimes the prompt in front was greyed out: OK, Cancel and the radio buttons ignored clicks, and the app had to be quit. A user hit this on 2 of 3 tries.

Over the control channel the dialog stack looked right: three prompts, the newest last. The cause is two rules that disagree:

- `dialogs::show` lets only the last dialog take input and disables the others.
- egui only lets the modal drawn on top take input, and it raises an area that is pressed or that wasn't drawn the frame before (`Area::show` in egui 0.36).

When egui raised an older prompt above the live one, the prompt in front was one we had disabled, and the live one behind it was blocked by egui. Neither could be answered. The stacked prompts sit in the same place and are the same size, so the live one was also hidden.

I couldn't pin down which egui rule fired in the user's session: in tests all three files open within two frames, and no click timing I tried reproduced it. The fix doesn't depend on the trigger.

## Fix

`dialogs::show` raises the live (last) dialog when another dialog is drawn above it (`older_dialog_above`, checking egui's layer order). It raises only then: raising every frame put the dialog above its own popups, which broke the Fill dialog's colour and pattern pickers and a Preferences dropdown (caught by their existing tests).

This applies to any stacked dialogs (a Color Picker over Fill, for example), not just the profile prompts.

title: fix(type): navigate adjacent line with large leading (#3066)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #3066

## Problem

`line_step` chose the destination line by hit-testing a point just beyond the current caret. With 40-point leading, that point remained closer to the current line, so `lineNext` and `linePrev` returned the original indices.

## Change

Resolve the caret's current laid-out line, select the adjacent line directly, then find the closest caret on that line at the requested x position. Add a regression for 40-point leading in both directions.

title: Read applied Sony RAW metadata and crop ILCE-6000 images
author: optimalbytee
body:
Older Sony ARWs can carry applied white balance and black levels only in encrypted SR2SubIFD metadata. PhotoCraft previously estimated WB from the scene and used a 512 black fallback, even when the file specified different levels. This change reads the observed common-key metadata with bounded allocation and checked offsets, keeps usable plain tags authoritative, and retains existing fallbacks for malformed metadata or other keys.

The measured ILCE-6000 image area now produces 6000 × 4000 images from its 6048 × 4024 sensor without overriding an explicit crop. Three measured files use their identical camera-applied WB instead of different grey-world estimates; full-resolution 16-bit ProPhoto-compatible development is retained. The pinned public RX0 fixture now asserts black 800 and applied WB. Sensor pixels continue through the RAW development pipeline.

Only the observed `11 22 33 44` key is supported. Metadata allocation is capped at 1 MiB and `Limits.max_alloc`; offsets, directory lengths and level values are checked. Synthetic regressions cover both byte orders, independent keystream observations, metadata precedence, invalid levels/gains, truncation, out-of-block offsets and allocation limits. The cipher data was independently recovered from black-box metadata observations; no sibling decoder implementation, camera colour table or dependency is included. See [the measurement and scope notes](https://github.com/optimalbytee/photocraft/blob/codex/sony-arw-metadata/docs/sony-arw-metadata.md).

title: Window menu: list the open documents, the active one checked (#2991)
author: brennanMKE
body:
Fixes #2991.

In Photoshop, the **Window** menu ends with the open documents. The active one has a check, and choosing one brings it to the front. PhotoCraft's Window menu didn't list them, in either menu bar. The only ways to switch documents were the tabs, their » overflow menu and Ctrl+Tab. #1264 asked for this list too, but it was closed by #1367, which added only the overflow button. On #2780 a macOS user also looked for open images in the Window menu.

- **The list:** Window now ends with a separator and one row per open document, in tab order. Each row is labelled with the document's name, and the active document has a check. Choosing a row activates that document.
- **Native macOS menu bar:** the documents come after Bring All to Front.
- **In-window menu bar** (Windows, Linux and `--in-window-menus`): the documents come after Theme.
- **Names:** document names aren't translated. A rename by Save As updates the row.

### Native menu: rebuild only Window

The native menu bar is rebuilt only when `structure_key` changes, and `mac_menu_appkit` checks that opening a document doesn't rebuild it. Document rows can't be inserted into the Window menu in place:

title: docs(raw): measured notes on Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3/4
author: Gotya-OFFCIAL
body:
## What

Measured notes on Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3/4 (vendor-compressed, 12-bit) — container
tags, payload geometry, per-byte content sensitivity, quantisation behaviour, and a
negative result that should stop the next attempt from repeating mine.

No decoder here. Nothing was read from dcraw, LibRaw, RawSpeed, rawler/dnglab or any
other decoder implementation; every number comes from treating the sample files as byte
sequences. This follows the route the Nikon NEF work took (#1310), where the format
facts came from black-box analysis rather than from a description of somebody's code.

## Why bother, when the decoder in #1884 was declined

Because the useful output of that attempt is not the code, it is the measurements — and
they are cheap to check. Three of them are not obvious from the outside:

**1. The payload is not a fixed-layout raster.** Four frames of one static scene, same
camera and settings, seconds apart:

| File | Payload | 16-byte groups |
|---|---|---|
| P1340729 | 19,070,976 | 1,191,936 |
| P1340730 | 19,062,272 | 1,191,392 |
| P1340731 | 19,072,512 | 1,192,032 |
| P1340732 | 19,096,064 | 1,193,504 |

The length varies by 33,792 bytes (0.18 %) between frames that show the same scene.

**2. Group 0 already differs completely between those four files**, even though the
stream starts in the masked border rows where the scene is identical and only sensor
noise differs. The first 16 bytes of each file share nothing.

Together these say the encoder is sequential and error-feedback-like: a small input
difference is amplified along the prediction chain instead of staying local, coded length
drifts with content, and output at one position cannot be related to the image at one
position.

**3. Consequently, positional analysis returns nothing.** In the samples here only three
byte positions correlate with image content at all (byte 7 at 0.850 for lag 1, byte 5 at
0.648, byte 4 peaking at lag 1032 = three rows); the other thirteen sit below 0.07 at
every lag…

title: fix(image): arbitrary canvas rotation moves position-locked children in groups (#3078)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Closes #3078.

### Summary

In `image.rotation.arbitrary` (`rotate_arbitrary`), canvas-wide rotation is meant to rotate the entire canvas including locked layers. Previously, it cleared `position` and `all` locks only on top-level layers before invoking `transform_layer`. When a layer inside a group had a position lock, the group recursion in `transform_layer` encountered the child's lock and failed with `layer "<name>" is locked`.

This PR:
1. Implements `with_released_movement_locks` in `crates/engine/src/mode_cmds.rs` to recursively release `position` and `all` locks across a layer and all its descendants during canvas rotation, safely restoring each layer's original locks afterwards.
2. Updates `rotate_arbitrary` to use `with_released_movement_locks` when calling `transform_layer`.
3. Adds unit test `rotate_arbitrary_rotates_grouped_locked_children_and_preserves_lock` in `crates/engine/src/mode_cmds/tests.rs` verifying:
   - Arbitrary 30° rotation succeeds on grouped documents with position-locked children and grows 16×16 to 22×22.
   - Position locks on grouped children are preserved after rotation.
   - Individual Free Transform on the position-locked child continues to be refused.
   - Undo restores the original canvas size and document state.
   - 90° canvas rotation matches the dedicated right-angle rotation `image.imageRotation.90cw`.

### Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib rotate_arbitrary_rotates_grouped_locked_children_and_preserves_lock` (passed)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib mode_cmds` (13/13 passed)

title: fix(crop): unlock Background when extending canvas (#3081)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
## Problem

An explicit Crop that extended an opaque Background beyond the old canvas left transparent pixels on a still-locked Background. Fill succeeded on existing pixels, but its transparency lock kept it from painting the new border.

## Fix

Detect when the crop frame extends beyond the previous canvas and convert a Background to a normal layer as part of the crop edit. In-bounds and shrink-only crops keep the Background unchanged. The regression covers the Fill result, the lock and name transition, and undo restoring the crop and original Background.

Fixes #3081

## Verification

- `crop_extension_converts_background_before_fill` failed before the fix because the border remained transparent after Fill, and passes after it.
- `nice -n 10 cargo test -q -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (1,199 passed, 12 ignored, plus engine integration targets).
- `nice -n 10 cargo clippy -q -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo xtask layers` (29 crates, no violations).
- `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=12 nice -n 10 cargo xtask wasm` (all 24 checks passed).
- Rebuilt the CLI and reproduced the extended-crop/fill sequence; the new border becomes opaque blue. The pre-converted Background control, shrink-only control, and undo sequence also pass.

Corpus and performance checks were not run. The change only updates layer state when a crop creates transparent canvas area; it does not touch file formats or a hot pixel path.

title: fix(transform): identity transform makes feathered selection edges translucent (#3079)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Closes #3079.

### Summary

When Free Transform (`edit.transform`) is applied to an active feathered selection with an identity transform matrix, the engine previously split the surface into lifted (`alpha * k`) and rest (`alpha * (1 - k)`) surfaces via `split_selected`, warped the lifted surface, and normal-blended it back over the rest surface via `composite_over`. Because Porter-Duff Over compositing assumes independent layer coverage, the resulting opacity $k + (1 - k)(1 - k) = 1 - k(1 - k)$ caused feathered pixels ($0 < k < 1$) to become translucent even though coordinates were unchanged.

This PR:
1. Adds `Homography::is_identity` to `photocraft-algo` to test if a homography is an identity transformation.
2. In `transform_layer` (`crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs`), early-returns when `h.is_identity()` (after validating layer locks and converting position-locked Background), completely bypassing splitting, warping, and recompositing for identity transforms.
3. In `transform`, avoids unnecessary resampling of lone target channels/masks and selection outlines when `h.is_identity()`.
4. Adds regression unit test `feathered_selection_identity_transform_preserves_pixels` in `crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs` verifying:
   - Full RGBA preservation across the canvas when transforming a feathered selection with an identity matrix.
   - Exact `[1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]` at feathered edge `(4,8)`.
   - Undo restoration.
   - Continued refusal of locked layers.

### Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo --lib homography_is_identity` (passed)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib feathered_selection_identity_transform_preserves_pixels` (passed)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib transform_cmds` (19/19 passed)

- `cargo xtask layers` (passed, 29 crates clean)

title: Render Video: animated GIFs keep their transparency (#3061)
author: fabianghe
body:
Fixes #3061.

**File › Export › Render Video** as an animated GIF turned fully transparent pixels opaque black, while a PNG sequence and a static GIF kept their transparency. There were two problems.

1. **No transparent index.** `render_video_with` quantised every frame with `transparent: None`. Each frame now does what Save for Web's GIF already does (`web_cmds.rs`), in a small `gif_frame` helper:
   - Pixels under 50% opacity get a transparent index. The rest are drawn opaque.
   - The palette is built from the visible pixels, with one entry kept for transparency. A fully transparent frame still gets a valid palette.
2. **Frames were never cleared.** `encode_gif_animated` wrote disposal 1 ("leave in place") for every frame. Every frame covers the whole image, so once transparency works, earlier frames would show through the transparent areas of later ones as ghosting. A frame with a transparent index now uses disposal 2 ("restore to background"). Opaque frames are unchanged and keep disposal 1.

## Verified with the issue's own steps
I ran the CLI commands from #3061 and decoded the results with Pillow 11.3:

```
animated/Untitled.gif frames 2
  frame 0 corner (0, 0, 0, 0) disposal 2
  frame 1 corner (0, 0, 0, 0) disposal 2
square/Untitled.gif (transparent doc with a red 4×4 square) frames 2
  frame 0 corner (255, 0, 0, 0)  centre (255, 0, 0, 255) disposal 2
  frame 1 corner (255, 0, 0, 0)  centre (255, 0, 0, 255) disposal 2
```

## Tests
- `engine/src/video_cmds/tests.rs`:
  - `animated_gif_keeps_transparency`: a transparent doc with a red square renders to a GIF. Both frames carry the transparent flag and disposal 2. On re-import the corner is transparent and the square is red.
  - `a_fully_transparent_animated_gif_frame_encodes`.
- `codecs/src/web.rs`: `transparent_frames_are_cleared_before_the_next` checks the Graphic Control Extension byte (0x04 opaque, 0x09 transparent) and the decoded alpha.
- The existing `render_video_to_animated_gif` (opaque frames) sti…

title: fix(ui): respect native desktop scale under Auto UI scaling (#1278)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Resolves #1278

### Problem
Previously, when `interface.ui_scale` was set to `Auto` (the default), PhotoCraft forced a 200% scale factor whenever a 4K display was detected if the reported system scale was 1.0 (unscaled). On large 4K monitors (such as 32", 43", or multi-monitor setups) run intentionally at 100% desktop scale, this made PhotoCraft's window and UI elements unexpectedly huge and oversized compared to all other apps in the Craft suite.

### Solution
- Let `UiScale::Auto` respect the desktop environment's native scale without arbitrarily doubling it on 4K displays.
- Users who desire 200% scaling can select 200% from the Interface preferences dropdown.
- Updated unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/prefs_ui.rs` to verify that native desktop scale is preserved under `Auto`.

title: [Not merging] CI: Depot runner trial (measurements kept for reference)
author: echelon
body:
> **Closed as unwanted.** We won't move CI to Depot. The trial measured real gains, but they don't pay for themselves on this repo (see *Decision* below). Kept here for reference.

Trial of Depot-managed runners for the Linux jobs in `ci.yml` (2026-10-11), comparing wall-clock time and cost against GitHub-hosted runners.

## What was changed (branch since deleted)

| Job | Runner |
|---|---|
| test (Linux), corpus tests, web build | `depot-ubuntu-24.04-8` |
| wasm32 check | `depot-ubuntu-24.04-4` |
| select platforms, fuzz | `depot-ubuntu-24.04` |

Also needed: the Depot labels in `.github/actionlint.yaml`, or `actionlint` fails on unknown runner labels. Windows and `release.yml` were left unchanged.

## Timings

The GitHub baseline is the median of the last 5 green `main` runs on `ubuntu-latest`, which has 4 vCPUs for public repos, with a warm cache. The warm Depot run restored a 1.2 GB rust-cache with an exact key match.

| Job | GitHub (4 vCPU, warm) | Depot cold | **Depot warm** |
|---|---|---|---|
| test (Linux), 8 vCPU | ~28 min (23–33) | 13m30s–16m01s | **9m59s** (2.8×) |
| corpus tests, 8 vCPU | ~9.3 min | 4m00s–4m23s | **3m00s** (3.1×) |
| web build, 8 vCPU | ~5.2 min | 3m30s–3m48s | **3m01s** (1.7×) |
| wasm32 check, 4 vCPU | ~1.4 min | 2m37s–2m54s | **1m04s** (1.3×) |
| select platforms, 2 vCPU | ~6s | 9s–29s | 8s |

## Caching notes

- On Depot runners, the GitHub Actions cache API (`actions/cache`, `Swatinem/rust-cache`) is sent to Depot Cache automatically. It's separate from GitHub's cache, so the first runs after switching are cold.
- Depot Cache isn't scoped by branch. Our `save-if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` still means only `main` saves.
- Depot runners also come preconfigured to use sccache with Depot Cache (set `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`). This trial didn't test it.

## Cost

- **GitHub today.** This repo is public, so standard Linux/Windows/macOS minutes are free. October 1–11 shows $2,325.89 gross for photocraft, but **$5.81 net**, all of i…

title: SVG: warn when text has no font to use (fixes the FreeBSD svg test)
author: diegochagas
body:
Fixes the FreeBSD job, red on main since the SVG reader landed in #1305 (first red run f82a55f on 2026-10-09; last green ec7302f, before #1305): `crates/io/tests/svg.rs::text_becomes_outline_shapes_or_warns_without_a_font` fails with `["SVG: nothing to draw (an empty drawing)"]`.

## What changed

The FreeBSD image has `fontconfig` and `freetype2` but no font package, and no bundled craft fonts, so the reader's font database is empty. With an empty `fontdb`, usvg 0.45 drops the `<text>` element **while parsing** (verified with a probe: `usvg::Tree::from_str` on the test's SVG yields a root with no children and a zero bounding box), so the reader's existing note at `svg.rs` ("text needs a font the drawing can use; none matched") never runs: it needs a `usvg::Node::Text` to reach the conversion. The file opened as an empty drawing with no word about the text.

- `parse` now returns the tree together with `fontless_text`: the drawing may contain text and the loaded database has no faces. `import_svg` turns that into the warning *"SVG: the text needs a font and none is installed, so it was dropped"* before converting, so a user on a font-less system learns why the text vanished; the per-text note for drawings that do have fonts but none matching stays.
- `options()` takes the database instead of deciding it; `parse_with(bytes, fonts)` is the seam the test uses to hand in an empty database. `rasterize` is unchanged in behaviour.

## How it was tested

- New unit test `text_without_any_font_is_reported_not_silently_dropped`: an SVG with `<text>` parsed against an empty database opens with no layers and a warning containing "font"; a drawing without text parsed the same way gets no font warning.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-io --test svg` (16, including the FreeBSD one in both of its branches: with fonts here, and without through the unit test) and `--lib svg`: ok. `cargo clippy -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `car…

title: Preserve solid vector shapes alongside bitmaps in SVG/PDF exports
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
Depends on #2872. The signed-in account cannot merge upstream, so this PR currently includes that export-catalog foundation. The mixed-export implementation is commit `27b6bad6`; once #2872 lands, the foundation overlap disappears.

SVG and PDF delivery previously flattened the document to one image, losing scalable shapes. This follow-up mixes actual solid Bézier fills and centered solid/dashed strokes with PNG bitmap layers. SVG/SVGZ reopen our unchanged output as editable shape and raster layers; PDF writes real path/form objects, bitmap images, soft masks and document DPI. Bitmap layer opacity remains separate from PNG samples, preserving faint overlays.

Export As scaling and disabling transparency retain vectors, with a white solid background added to the temporary export document. SVG/PDF labels no longer describe every output as raster-only, and the SVG capability notice is translated in all shipped catalogs.

Supported vector delivery uses RGB with the default or built-in sRGB profile. Text/fonts, gradients/patterns, boolean operations, masks/effects, clipping and backdrop-dependent blending use a warned raster fallback of the affected stack prefix; later supported shapes can remain vector. Other working spaces retain existing composite raster delivery. PDF is single-page and export-only. This is a delivery format, not a complete native document round trip.

Geometry, XML, encoded payload, recursion and decoded SVG layer budgets are bounded. SVG reopening rejects stale private geometry after external visual edits, unsafe namespaces/styles and pathological dash density; it contains no hidden whole-document payload.

Validation on the current upstream branch: 13 focused IO tests, 1,830 UI tests, strict IO/UI Clippy, formatting, dependency layers and full WASM check passed locally. GitHub corpus, WASM and web-size gates passed at `7bb746aa`. Linux CI tests also passed; Windows CI remains pending. Independent resvg/Poppler render checks cover mixed geometry, wi…
