title: fix: macOS Monterey crash on Intel Iris Pro (disable wgpu indirect validation)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3107 (macOS Monterey startup crash on Intel Iris Pro GPU)

The app crashed with "Compiler encountered an internal error" → "WGPU error: Parent device is lost" on Intel Iris Pro (device ID 0x0d26, Metal GPUFamily 1) running macOS Monterey 12.7.6.

## Root Cause

wgpu 30 compiles two internal compute shaders for indirect draw/dispatch validation by default. Metal's shader compiler crashes on these shaders on Intel Iris Pro, resulting in `RequestDeviceError(Device(Lost))`.

Both `--safe-gpu` and `PHOTOCRAFT_CPU_CANVAS=1` failed because macOS has no software graphics adapter—the CPU fallback still opens the window through Metal, hitting the same compiler crash.

## Fix

One line in `apps/photocraft/src/gpu_startup.rs`: disable wgpu's `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` flag. PhotoCraft never uses indirect draw or dispatch calls, so this validation is unnecessary.

Applied on all platforms (not macOS-only) to remove the same driver-crash risk on other GPUs.

## Testing

- Added regression test `device_creation_skips_indirect_validation_shaders`
- All 20 `gpu_startup` tests pass
- Sabotage test confirmed (removing fix causes test to fail)
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` clean
- Environment override `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` re-enables validation

## Risks

- **Not tested on Intel Iris Pro hardware** — waiting for reporter confirmation
- Future trap if indirect calls added later (code comment guards against this)

## Workaround

Reporter can test before merge: `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=0 photocraft`

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: fix(type): exclude text inside hidden groups from automatic hit testing
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Automatic `type.hitTest` can return text layers inside hidden groups.

Although the text layer itself is marked visible, it should not be
automatically selectable when one of its parent groups is hidden.

Fixes #3075.

## Root cause

The automatic hit-testing path checked each text layer's own
visibility flag without considering the visibility of its ancestors.

## Changes

- Check visibility along the complete layer path.
- Exclude text when any containing group is hidden.
- Preserve explicit hit-testing of a named hidden text layer.
- Add a regression test covering nested groups, visibility changes,
  and explicit targeting.

## Validation

- Verified the committed changes against the upstream baseline.
- Added a focused regression test.
- Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

title: fix(type): use the correct line at soft-wrap caret boundaries
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

At the beginning of a wrapped line, `type.caret` can report the
preceding line even though the caret geometry belongs to the next
visual line.

The same boundary error affects `type.navigate` with `lineStart`
and `lineEnd`.

Fixes #3068.

## Root cause

Adjacent visual lines can share a character offset.

The previous line-index lookup selected the first matching range,
while caret geometry could correctly resolve the following line.

## Changes

- Prefer the following visual line when resolving a shared caret
  boundary.
- Make line-edge navigation use the same line selection.
- Preserve pointer-based hit-testing by determining the visual line
  from the pointer's position.
- Add text-layout regression coverage for wrapped lines, forced
  breaks, and ordinary paragraph breaks.
- Add engine-level regression coverage for caret and line navigation.

## Compatibility

The change preserves existing character indices and text content.

It corrects line identity without changing the document format or
introducing additional history steps.

## Validation

- Verified the committed changes against the upstream baseline.
- Added focused text-layout and engine regression tests.
- Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

title: fix(crop): retain partial aspect-ratio input while typing
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Entering a custom crop aspect ratio can be frustrating because the
first numeric field resets to zero before the second field is filled.

This prevents users from reliably entering ratios such as 4:5 or 16:9.

Addresses the numeric-input problem reported in #3145.

## Root cause

The options bar reconstructs the numeric fields from the committed
crop-ratio value on every UI frame.

However, it only commits changes when both values are greater than
zero.

When a user enters the first number while the second is still zero,
the first number is discarded on the next frame.

## Changes

- Retain incomplete numeric input in transient UI state.
- Restore the first number while the second is being entered.
- Apply the crop aspect-ratio constraint only when both values are
  positive.
- Discard stale input when selecting another preset.
- Reset the transient input state when Clear is selected.
- Add regression coverage for incomplete input and preset changes.

## Scope

This change addresses custom aspect-ratio entry.

The separate crop-handle snapping, undo behavior, and requested
ratio information display mentioned in #3145 are not changed.

## Validation

- Verified the committed changes against the upstream baseline.
- Added a focused regression test for draft-value restoration.
- Rust tests, interactive UI testing, and CI have not been executed.

title: fix(masks): preserve off-canvas alpha in From Transparency
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Layer > Layer Mask > From Transparency loses mask coverage for pixels
temporarily positioned outside the document canvas.

Moving a raster layer partially off-canvas, converting its transparency
to a mask, and moving it back can leave previously visible pixels hidden.

## Root cause

The conversion intersects the raster surface's content bounds with the
document bounds before transferring alpha into the mask.

This excludes valid off-canvas pixels that still belong to the layer.

## Changes

- Transfer alpha across the raster layer's complete content bounds.
- Preserve mask coverage outside the canvas.
- Leave the existing alpha-to-mask conversion behavior unchanged for
  pixels inside the canvas.
- Add a regression test covering off-canvas coverage and restoration at
  8-, 16-, and 32-bit document depths.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Regression test added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests, platform checks, and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3043

title: fix(layers): remap linked-layer groups when copying between documents
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Copying linked layers into another document can accidentally associate
them with unrelated layers already linked in the destination.

Both documents may independently use the same linked-group identifier.
Subsequent linked-layer operations can then affect layers that were
never intended to be linked together.

## Root cause

Cross-document copying duplicates layers while preserving their
document-local link-group identifiers.

The destination may already use those identifiers for different groups.

## Changes

- Remap copied link-group identifiers to unused destination identifiers.
- Preserve relationships between copied layers belonging to the same
  source group.
- Keep separate copied groups distinct.
- Preserve existing destination link relationships.
- Add regression tests for identifier collisions, independent groups,
  and undo/redo of the copy operation.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Two regression tests added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3045

title: fix(history): preserve an empty layer selection across undo and redo
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

When all layers are intentionally deselected, creating a new layer and
then undoing the creation unexpectedly selects the Background layer.

The restored layer target no longer matches the state immediately
before the edit.

## Root cause

History restoration only recognizes targets with an existing active
layer.

A valid empty target falls through to the normal active-layer repair
logic, which selects the top available layer.

## Changes

- Recognize an intentionally empty layer target during history
  restoration.
- Restore no active layer and no selected layers when that state was
  recorded.
- Clear the corresponding layer anchor.
- Preserve existing fallback behavior for invalid or deleted targets.
- Add a regression test covering deselection, layer creation, undo,
  redo, repeated undo, and ordinary selected-target restoration.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Regression test added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3042

title: fix(layers): select Shift ranges in visible panel row order (#3041)
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Shift-click range selection produces incorrect layer membership around
expanded groups.

For example, selecting the range between a layer and an adjacent group
can unexpectedly include the group's children. Selecting from the group
to a child can omit intermediate displayed rows.

## Root cause

Range selection uses Document::walk(), whose traversal order differs
from the Layers panel's visual order around nested groups.

## Changes

- Calculate selection ranges using the Layers panel's top-to-bottom
  ordering.
- Place group rows directly above their children.
- Respect collapsed groups when calculating visible ranges.
- Preserve programmatic access to hidden group children by falling
  back to expanded ordering when an endpoint is not visible.
- Add a regression test covering forward and reverse selection ranges
  across groups and child layers.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Integration regression test added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3041

title: fix(io): preserve group fill opacity in OpenRaster exports
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

OpenRaster export can lose the visible effect of group fill opacity.

A group with 50% fill opacity may reopen at full opacity even though
its exported merged preview reflects the intended transparency.

## Root cause

The exporter writes group opacity independently from fill opacity.

For raster layers, fill opacity can be applied directly to the exported
pixels. Groups have no equivalent single pixel payload, so that
conversion does not preserve their fill contribution.

## Changes

- Combine group fill opacity with serialized group opacity.
- Keep raster-layer opacity separate because raster fill opacity is
  already applied to the exported pixels.
- Clarify export warnings to distinguish the two conversion paths.
- Add regression tests for group fill opacity, combined opacity values,
  and OpenRaster round-trip behavior.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Two regression tests added but not executed locally.
- OpenRaster runtime round trips, cargo tests, and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3048

title: fix(video): preserve transparent pixels in animated GIF exports
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Render Video can turn transparent pixels into opaque pixels when
exporting an animated GIF.

Transparent source frames may consequently produce an opaque black
background, despite retaining transparency in other export formats.

## Root cause

Animated GIF export quantizes frames without reserving a transparent
palette entry and passes no transparent index to the GIF encoder.

## Changes

- Detect frames containing transparent pixels.
- Reserve an additional palette index for transparency when needed.
- Pass that index through pixel quantization and animated GIF encoding.
- Retain the existing palette behavior for fully opaque frames.
- Add regression tests covering transparent animated GIF frames and
  the fully opaque control case.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Two regression tests added but not executed locally.
- Animated GIF runtime decoding, cargo tests, and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3061

title: fix(vector): pivot explicit path transforms on target layer (#3062)
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Numeric path transformations can use the wrong pivot when the command
explicitly targets a layer other than the active layer.

Scaling the target shape may consequently move it far from its
expected position.

## Root cause

path.transform correctly resolves the layer being modified but
independently resolves the pivot through the active layer's path.

The transform target and pivot can therefore refer to different
shapes.

## Changes

- Resolve numeric-transform bounds from the explicitly targeted layer.
- Support both shape paths and vector-mask paths.
- Preserve existing behavior when no explicit layer is provided.
- Leave the explicit transformation-matrix path unchanged.
- Add regression tests for scaling an inactive shape layer and using
  an explicit matrix.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Two integration regression tests added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3062

title: fix(vector): preserve scaled live-line thickness during endpoint edits
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

After uniformly scaling a live line shape, editing an endpoint without
changing its position can unexpectedly reduce the line's thickness.

A four-pixel line scaled by two becomes eight pixels thick, but a
subsequent endpoint edit regenerates the path using the original
four-pixel weight.

## Root cause

The affine transformation updates the live line's endpoints without
updating its stored weight.

Later edits regenerate the line geometry from inconsistent live-shape
parameters.

## Changes

- Update live-line weight when applying positive axis-aligned scaling.
- Account for the line's direction when calculating the perpendicular
  width scale.
- Preserve the original weight for translation-only transforms.
- Keep the line editable after transformation.
- Add regression tests for uniform scaling, subsequent endpoint edits,
  translation, and horizontal/vertical nonuniform scaling.

## Validation

- Source and affected diff reviewed.
- Three integration regression tests added but not executed locally.
- Cargo tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #3063

title: fix(history): read locked history sources (#3076)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Fixes #3076

## Problem

History Brush and Fill with History read a selected historical layer through the write-target helper. When that snapshot had pixel locks enabled, the helper rejected the read and both commands reported that the target did not exist.

## Fix

Add an immutable target-surface lookup for history reads. It reads layer pixels, masks, alpha channels, and Quick Mask without applying write-lock checks, and both history consumers use it. Current destination edits continue through the existing lock-checked write path.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (1,202 passed, 12 ignored, integration targets passed)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib history_ -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` (25 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -j 12 -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`
- `cargo xtask layers` (29 crates) and `cargo xtask wasm` (24 checks)
- CLI repro: both commands restore pixels from the locked source state; state-0 controls pass; both commands still reject a currently locked destination.

Corpus tests were not run because this engine-only change does not touch the file-format crates covered by the opt-in corpus suite. No performance benchmark applies to this history lookup.

title: Fix Windows image clipboard imports (#2629)
author: imSlicedBread
body:
## Summary
Fixes #2629 by importing Windows `CF_DIB` clipboard images when the existing `arboard` image reader cannot decode the clipboard. If both formats are present, PhotoCraft prefers the DIB image only when it preserves transparency lost by the primary image.

title: GPU memory budget: read installed RAM on Windows
author: dhiorns15
body:
`gpu_canvas::physical_memory()` had no Windows implementation, so it returned `None` on every Windows machine. The wgpu compositor's memory budget then assumed 16 GB of RAM and capped layer textures at a quarter of that (4 GB):

- **Large machines** got too little. On a 62 GB PC with the default 8 GB Memory Usage, the budget was 4 GB instead of the full 8 GB allowance.
- **An 8 GB laptop with an integrated GPU** got too much: 4 GB of textures in RAM it shares with the system, where a quarter of the real RAM is 2 GB.

This reads installed RAM with `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` through `winsafe`, the safe binding the desktop app already uses (same pinned `=0.0.29`, `kernel` feature only; no `unsafe`). macOS, Linux and FreeBSD are unchanged.

**Tests**
- New: `gpu_canvas::tests::windows_reports_installed_ram` (Windows only). It fails before the fix, which returns `None`.
- Clean: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: fix(actions): avoid replaying Browse script edits twice
author: Ni-zav

## Summary

Fix action recordings that execute Browse script commands twice during playback.

## Problem

Recording a Browse script captures both the commands executed inside

During playback, the recorded commands run individually before the
Browse command runs them again.

For example, a script containing one 90-degree rotation can produce

title: fix(masks): bake feathered coverage when applying a layer mask
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Preserve softened mask edges when applying a feathered layer mask.

Fixes #3044.

## Problem

Applying a feathered layer mask removes the mask but sharpens its edge.

The resulting layer no longer matches the appearance displayed before
Apply.

## Root Cause

The Apply command reads mask coverage through `LayerMask::values_into`,
which handles mask density but does not perform feathering.

The compositor applies feathering separately.

## Changes

- Use the compositor's combined-mask coverage for enabled feathered
  pixel masks.
- Bake the softened coverage into the raster layer's alpha.
- Avoid baking an independent vector mask that remains attached.
- Preserve the existing path for masks without feathering.
- Add regression coverage for 8-, 16-, and 32-bit documents.
- Add a disabled-mask regression test.

## Validation

- Source and commit diff reviewed.
- Two regression tests added.
- Rust tests and CI have not been executed yet.

title: fix(compose): resolve Dissolve coverage across adjustment, effects, a…
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Correct Dissolve blending in adjustment layers, layer effects, and
clipped layers.

Fixes #3050.
Fixes #3051.
Fixes #3052.

## Problem

Dissolve should resolve partial opacity into spatially distributed
pixel coverage.

Several compositor paths instead interpolate colors continuously,
producing uniform gray where the output should contain separate
opaque source and background pixels.

The affected paths include:

1. Adjustment layers using Dissolve at partial opacity.
2. Layers using Dissolve with enabled layer effects.
3. Clipped layers using Dissolve.

## Root Cause

These specialized composition paths bypass the standard Dissolve
coverage calculation.

They apply ordinary opacity interpolation even when the selected
layer blend mode is Dissolve.

## Changes

### Adjustment Layers

- Resolve adjustment opacity and mask coverage using the existing
  deterministic Dissolve threshold.
- Select either the adjusted or original color at each pixel.
- Preserve the backdrop alpha.

### Clipped Layers

- Apply binary Dissolve coverage to clipped content.
- Preserve the clipping base's alpha.
- Keep Normal blending behavior unchanged.

### Layer Effects

- Resolve layer opacity as coverage when combining the completed
  effect stack with its backdrop.
- Avoid continuously interpolating the effect stack under Dissolve.
- Preserve continuous interpolation for other blend modes.

## Tests

Added regression tests covering:

- Dissolve adjustments producing binary coverage.
- Clipped Dissolve matching an unclipped control over an opaque base.
- A redundant Color Overlay preserving Dissolve coverage.
- Normal blending continuing to produce continuous opacity.

## Validation

- Source and commit diff reviewed.
- Three regression tests added.
- CPU compositor tests, GPU parity checks, and CI remain pending.

title: raw: charge the lossless-JPEG intermediate and segment-sized buffers against max_alloc (#2925)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #2925

## What's wrong

`read_plane` charged the assembled image plane against `Limits` (`limits.check(width, height, samples * 2)`), but every per-segment buffer is sized from the **segment**, not from the image: tile geometry comes from `TILE_WIDTH` / `TILE_LENGTH`, which the file declares itself and `segments()` only bounds at `1 << 16` per axis. So an 8×8 image in a DNG that declares one 512×512 lossless-JPEG tile passes the plane check (128 bytes) and still allocates the whole 512 KiB intermediate — the "checked before allocating" promise in `crates/raw/src/lib.rs` did not hold for that buffer.

## What changed

- One `limits.check(s.w, s.h, samples * 2)` per segment, **before** the compression dispatch: a segment has to be a plausible buffer on its own. That bounds every branch that sizes a buffer from segment geometry (uncompressed, deflate, lossy JPEG, JPEG XL, lossless JPEG), which is remediation 2 in the issue.
- In the lossless-JPEG branch the decoder's sample cap becomes `min(geom, (max_alloc - scatter) / 2)`:
  - `geom` is unchanged (`s.w * s.h * samples * 4`, the existing headroom), so nothing that decoded before is refused because of geometry;
  - a frame the entropy stream declares is now bounded by the budget too, not only by the segment (remediation 1);
  - `scatter` reserves the `Quads` scatter buffer out of the same budget, so output + scatter stay inside one `max_alloc`.

Legitimate strip/tile layouts are unaffected: real strips are clamped to the image, real tiles are smaller than it, and both are far below any default budget.

## Tests

`crates/raw/tests/hostile.rs` — the two `LimitExceeded` assertions failed before the change; the remaining assertions are non-regression checks on fixtures that were already valid:

- `lossless_jpeg_intermediate_is_charged_against_max_alloc`: the same file decodes under default limits, is refused under a 64 KiB budget the image itself fits into, still decodes under a 4 MiB budget that holds the intermedia…

title: fix(compose): preserve Dissolve coverage for adjustments, styles and clipping
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Keep smart-filter mask coverage aligned with smart objects during
document-wide geometry operations.

Fixes #3077.

## Problem

Image Size, Canvas Size, and Crop can leave selection-derived
smart-filter masks at incorrect positions.

The problem becomes particularly visible when a smart filter is
hidden and shown again, triggering a fresh render using the displaced
mask.

Consequently, filtering may affect the wrong portion of the image.

## Root Cause

The shared surface traversal used by canvas geometry operations
processes smart-object appearance caches but omits their
smart-filter mask surfaces.

The mask therefore retains its old coordinates or dimensions while
the associated content moves or resizes.

## Changes

- Include smart-filter mask surfaces in the shared layer-surface
  traversal when mask processing is enabled.
- Treat those surfaces as masks rather than color pixels.
- Resample smart-filter masks during Image Size operations.
- Translate smart-filter masks during Canvas Size and Crop.
- Preserve existing smart-object and filter structures.
- Retain the existing distinction between mask and color-surface
  interpolation.

## Tests

Added three integration regression tests:

1. Image Size preserves selection-derived smart-filter coverage
   after resampling.
2. Canvas Size preserves filter coverage after a right-anchored
   canvas extension.
3. Crop preserves filter coverage after translation.

Each test exercises smart-filter re-rendering by hiding and
showing the filter.

## Validation

- Source and commit diff reviewed.
- Three regression tests added.
- Rust tests, rendering comparisons, and CI remain pending.

title: Help > System Info: the details a bug report needs, in sections
author: dhiorns15
body:
**Builds on #3189**, which it needs for the Windows RAM line. Until that merges, this PR also shows its one commit, "GPU memory budget: read installed RAM on Windows".

Help › System Info used to be ten flat lines:
- "windows x86_64", with no Windows version or build;
- raw names like `dx12 (discreteGpu)`;
- nothing on the CPU, memory, fonts or pen input, or where the log file is.

Most issues here are picked up by agents working from what the reporter pasted, so the report now answers the usual first round of questions itself. It's grouped into sections:

| Section | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Application | version, build profile and target, install kind (Installed, Portable, AppImage, Flatpak, Snap, Built from source), UI language, uptime |
| System | OS name and build, CPU, threads, installed and available RAM. Windows: from the registry, named 11 for builds 22000 and up because `ProductName` still says "Windows 10". macOS: `sw_vers`, plus Rosetta. Linux: os-release, kernel and session |
| Graphics | adapter with its PCI `vendor:device` id; type and API in plain words (Dedicated GPU, DirectX 12); driver; the backend chosen at launch, only when it differs from the preference; startup fallback; compositor; GPU memory budget |
| Displays | the window's display, UI and OS scale, window size, monitor profiles |
| Pen input | where pen data comes from on this platform, and what has arrived this session (pressure, tilt, rotation, eraser end) |
| Fonts | craft-fonts bundle, family count, and the fallback fonts actually found (the Thai, CJK and emoji coverage) |
| Session | each document's size, mode, depth, layers, undo states and pixel memory (never its name); PhotoCraft's memory use; Memory Usage limit; plug-ins |
| Files | settings, log and crash-recovery folders |

**Privacy.** Document names, document paths and pixels are never included. The home folder is written `~`, so the report can be pasted into a public issue as is.

title: fix(shapes): preserve transformed outline on unchanged live geometry edits
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3064.

Reapplying unchanged rectangle dimensions after a nonuniform
transformation should not alter the existing rounded corners.

## Root Cause

A transformed live shape retains its parameter values, but its
vector path can contain geometry that those values cannot fully
represent.

The shape editing command regenerated the path whenever geometry
parameters were supplied, even when those parameters were unchanged.

This discarded the transformed corner geometry.

## Changes

- Compare the requested live-shape parameters with existing values.
- Preserve the current vector path when geometry is unchanged.
- Regenerate the path when geometry parameters actually change.
- Preserve the existing PSD vector data on unchanged edits.

## Regression Coverage

Added tests across 8-, 16-, and 32-bit documents covering:

- Nonuniformly scaled rounded rectangles.
- Reapplying unchanged rectangle dimensions.
- Reapplying unchanged corner radii.
- Applying an actual corner-radius change.
- Restoring geometry through Undo.

## Validation

Regression tests added. Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

author: Ni-zav

## Root Cause

The paragraph-style implementation treated the preceding paragraph

## Changes

- Preserve formatting when inserting text into the empty paragraph.
- Handle the synthetic terminal paragraph marker when importing
  PSD text data.

## Regression Coverage

Added tests covering:

- Formatting the empty paragraph after a trailing newline.
- Preserving the previous paragraph's alignment and geometry.
- Inserting text into the previously empty paragraph.
- Retaining paragraph formatting through PSD text serialization.

## Validation

The restoration commands unconditionally replace frames with

This works for blank video layers but destroys the displayed

title: fix(masks): preserve feathered coverage when applying layer masks
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3044.

Applying a feathered layer mask currently removes the soft edge,
producing a visibly harder transition than the original rendering.

## Root Cause

The Apply Layer Mask command multiplies layer alpha by the raw
mask values.

However, normal rendering uses feathered mask coverage calculated
by the compositor.

The difference causes the feathering to disappear when the mask
is applied.

## Changes

- Use the compositor's existing feathered-mask calculation.
- Bake the resulting coverage into the layer's alpha.
- Preserve the original rendering when removing the mask.
- Exclude retained vector masks from the baked pixel-mask coverage
  to avoid applying vector coverage twice.
- Preserve the existing behavior for unfeathered masks.

## Regression Coverage

Added tests across 8-, 16-, and 32-bit documents covering:

- Feathered pixel-mask rendering.
- Applying the mask.
- Comparing rendered pixels before and after Apply.
- Checking that the mask is removed.
- Restoring the original mask through Undo.

## Validation

Regression tests added. Rust tests and CI have not been executed.

title: Tests: one GPU harness at a time in every GPU test binary (WARP crash)
author: dhiorns15
body:
On Windows, the GPU UI test binaries crash with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (0xc0000005) whenever two of their tests run at once:
- On `main`, `arbitrary_rotation_preview` crashed in 3 runs out of 4.
- `color_managed_canvas`, `crop_default_mode`, `drag_preview_canvas` and `full_res_preview` crash at random.
- Every one of them passes with `--test-threads=1`.

**Cause.** egui_kittest prefers a CPU adapter, which on Windows is **WARP over DX12**, so every kittest GPU test there runs on it. A ProcDump crash dump puts the fault inside `d3d10warp.dll`, with two WARP devices rendering on parallel test threads; the NVIDIA driver's threads in the dump are idle.

| `WGPU_BACKEND` (5 parallel runs each) | crashes |
|---|---|
| `dx12` (WARP) | 5 / 5 |
| `vulkan` | 0 / 5 |
| `gl` | 0 / 5 |

Bare egui harnesses with no PhotoCraft code crash the same way (1 run in 5), so this is WARP rather than our code. The app itself has a single device, used only on the UI thread. GitHub's Windows runners have no GPU, so CI runs on WARP as well.

**Fix.** Three binaries already serialized their GPU tests with a per-binary lock, for the same class of driver bug:
- Mesa llvmpipe and RADV (#194);
- libvulkan with both NVIDIA and lavapipe installed.

That lock now lives once, in `photocraft_testkit::gpu_lock`, with all the known reasons documented. Every test in the 12 GPU test binaries that had no lock takes it on its first line. Under nextest each test is its own process, so the lock costs nothing there.

**Tests**
- After the fix, the 7 multi-test binaries ran 5 times each in parallel: 35 out of 35 clean. Before, most runs of the 5 binaries above crashed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --tests`, run twice: all 23 binaries pass, with no crash.
- `photocraft-testkit`: new tests showing a panicked holder doesn't block the next test, and holders take turns.
- Clean: clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`.

title: automation: doc.place reads a file through the read root (#2810)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #2810

`file.placeEmbedded` takes an ambient path, so the automation boundary refuses it ("use capability-scoped document methods") and an agent had no way at all to place a file into the open document.

Both halves of the counterpart already exist, so this connects them:

- `AuthorizedWorkspace::read` resolves a path beneath the read root — it is what `doc.open` uses in workspace mode — and
- `photocraft_engine::file_cmds::place_bytes` is public and places bytes that are already in memory.

`doc.place` reads through the root and calls `place_bytes`, so the existing `cap-std` rules stay the only path rules: no new scope logic to get wrong, and `file.placeEmbedded` keeps its refusal. Trusted-local callers keep the ambient command, as everywhere else.

- **JSON-RPC:** `doc.place {path, scale? (percent), fit?, center?, index?}` next to `doc.open` in `methods`, documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.
- **MCP:** `doc_place`, annotated additive (it only adds a layer); bridge mode forwards to `engine.execute {command: "file.placeEmbedded"}`, because a bridge app reads its own paths like any other command.

title: Moving type keeps its rendering: Artboards to Files no longer drops PSD text
author: fabianghe
body:
## What happens
`commands::translate_layer` **re-renders a type layer on every whole-pixel move**. For type that came from a PSD, this replaces Photoshop's rendering with PhotoCraft's own:
- paragraphs re-wrap;
- text set in a font that isn't installed disappears completely.

**Found with:** File › Export › **Artboards to Files** on a real Steam store asset template (a free PSD from Noblesteed Games, 20 artboards). `artboard_document` moves each board to the origin with `translate_layer`. The "How to use this template" board lost its big **"Hello!"** title, which is set in JetBrains Mono, and the step list re-wrapped. The same path runs for:
- the Move tool commit (`move_layers`) and arrow nudges;
- applying a layer comp's position;
- moving artboards;
- copying layers.

## The fix
- A whole-pixel move now **shifts the rendered pixels**, the same way smart objects (`shift_smart`) and the Move tool's live preview (`layer_multi_cmds::shift_shown`) already do.
- It also moves the TySh position with a new `photocraft_text::psd::translate_tysh`. That changes only the transform's tx/ty bytes (offsets 34 and 42). The text, styles, warp and trailing bounds are in text space, so they stay byte for byte as Photoshop wrote them, and PSD export still writes the right position.
- Type with no rendered cache yet is still rendered, as before.

## Measured on the template (PhotoCraft export vs Photoshop's own composite)
| | Before | After |

| Artboards identical to Photoshop | 16 of 20* | **17 of 20** |

\* The two other boards that differ, Main Capsule and Header Capsule, have 6 and 26 pixels off by 1 level on smart objects. That rounding is identical before and after this change. title: Preserve 16-bit Affinity pixels and recover source-backed raster layers
author: grlessa
body:
An RGB16 TIFF opened and saved in Affinity 3.3.0 currently imports with an empty pixel layer: its complete raster grid references the embedded original (`Sta*=5`), which the reader does not recover. Independently, decoded native 16-bit tiles are quantized to 8 bits. This change recovers wholly source-backed RGB8/RGB16 layers as editable raster layers and retains 16-bit pixels and masks through import, resampling and the tested native/PSD saves.

Recovery requires the exact complete byte-tile grid in all four channels. Mixed source-backed/edited grids continue using their stored tiles with warnings; the original is never substituted over raster edits. Missing or corrupt originals warn; mismatched dimensions, colour model or depth are rejected. Recovered embedded ICC profiles explicitly warn that they were not applied. Placed images remain smart objects and the Affinity source remains read-only.

Twelve original synthetic regressions cover Stored/Zlib/Zstd containers, exact 16-bit steps across byte tiles, mask coverage, mixed-depth promotion, premultiplied-alpha interpolation, edited grids, malformed/mismatched originals, profile warnings, smart objects, and `.pcraft`/PSD round trips. Seven of the initial eight regressions fail against pre-fix `3e000bc`. An original 1024×16 RGB16 TIFF saved in Affinity 3.3.0 imports all 65,536 RGBA16 samples exactly. The application-made file is used locally only; no proprietary application code, resources or application-made documents are committed. The README records the added black-box validation separately from the original reader provenance.

title: fix(masks): Apply sharpens a feathered layer-mask edge (#3044)
author: buivanvu94
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3044.

When applying an enabled pixel layer mask ("Layer › Layer Mask › Apply"), `apply_mask` in `crates/engine/src/layer_menu_cmds.rs` called `mask.values_into(r, &mut m)` which only takes mask density into account, completely omitting `mask.feather`. During composition, the compositor applies Gaussian blur for feathered masks via `photocraft_compose::masks::combined_mask`. Applying a feathered mask stripped the feather blur and baked a hard edge into the layer alpha, noticeably sharpening the transition.

This PR:
- Updates `apply_mask` in `photocraft-engine` (`crates/engine/src/layer_menu_cmds.rs`) to evaluate feathered pixel layer masks using `photocraft_compose::masks::combined_mask` across the canvas, matching the compositor's rendering, before multiplying layer alpha pixels.
- Preserves raw mask evaluation when `feather == 0.0` or when the mask is disabled.
- Adds regression unit tests across sample depths (8/16/32-bit) and for the exact issue reproduction sequence, verifying that the post-Apply composite preserves soft edge pixels within 8-bit rounding tolerance, restores identically upon undo, and keeps unfeathered masks sharp.

title: 8-bit documents: soft, low-flow brush strokes are dithered instead of banded
author: tanish2k09
body:
Brush phase 6c of the owner-approved overhaul.

## Why

Strokes composite in float (an f32 stroke buffer over the pre-stroke pixels), and then `write_region` rounds each pixel to 8 bits. A soft, low-flow stroke's gradient then collapses into visible bands. The audit measured a soft 120 px brush at flow 5 % / opacity 30 %: 35 distinct levels across the stroke against 119 at 16-bit, with concentric bands showing once contrast is stretched.

## What

`StrokeRenderer::composite` (`paint/src/render.rs`), for 8-bit targets only:
- Every pixel the stroke changes gets the same offset `(hash2(x, y) − 0.5) / 255` on all channels before quantisation. That covers normal, other blend modes, Dissolve and the eraser.
- Fractional values round up or down in proportion, so the bands become grain finer than one level.
- **Exact colours never change.** The offset stays strictly within ±0.5 of a level, and `write_region` clamps then rounds half-up, so a value already on a level rounds back to itself. Pixels the stroke doesn't touch aren't dithered.
- **Deterministic.** The offset depends only on the pixel's position, so the live preview (which re-composites from the pre-stroke pixels each step), the commit and a journal replay produce identical pixels.
- Channels share one offset, so there's no colour noise.

16-bit and float documents are unchanged. Photoshop doesn't dither brush strokes; this goes beyond it, on purpose.

## Tests

- `brush_tests::an_8bit_soft_stroke_is_dithered_instead_of_banded` compares row averages along a straight soft, low-flow stroke against a float render. Along the stroke every pixel of a row has the same true value, so plain rounding puts the whole row on one wrong level. **Main: 0.49 levels off (failed). This PR: < 0.15.**
- `brush_tests::dithering_never_moves_an_exact_colour_or_an_untouched_pixel`: solid paint keeps its exact 8-bit colour; untouched pixels stay identical.
- The existing live-equals-commit pixel tests (engine) pass unchanged.
- Gates: paint…

title: Liquify: the brush fades to nothing at its edge at every Density (#2606)
author: dhiorns15
body: Fixes the tearing in #2606. **Cause.** A Liquify dab's strength was `(1 − Density) + Density · (1 − t²)²`, so at the brush rim it stopped at `1 − Density` instead of 0: - half strength at the default Density 50; - full strength (a hard-edged disc) at Density 0. Forward Warp therefore moved the pixels just inside the brush and left the ones just outside, tearing the image along every dab's circle. A dab lands every fifth of the radius, so along a stroke those tears stack into the sawtooth edges and stripes in the issue's screenshot. Density was also backwards: 0 gave the strongest, flattest brush. **Fix.** A new `liquify::falloff` blends `(1 − t²)³` at Density 0 (effect in the centre, feathered) toward `(1 − t⁴)²` at Density 100 (full effect across most of the brush). Both curves are 1 at the centre and reach 0 at the rim with a flat slope, matching how Photoshop describes Density. Every Liquify brush tool, and Freeze/Thaw, uses it. **Before / after** Left: before · right: after. One Forward Warp stroke (size 200, pressure 100, a 360 px drag) on a grid, at Density 0, 50 and 100. **Notes** - Liquify still moves pixels rather than smudging them, as Photoshop's does. The issue's "smudge" request is about the tool itself, not this bug. - Saved Liquify strokes replay through the same code, so an existing Liquify smart filter re-renders with the smooth falloff. - Where a drag squeezes content hard there is still some moiré: the source isn't prefiltered when it's minified. That's separate from this fix and I've left it for a follow-up. **Tests** - New: `the_brush_fades_to_nothing_at_its_rim_at_every_density` covers the curve (1 at the centre, 0 and flat at the rim, falling all the way, Density widening the core, NaN and out-of-range values). - New: `forward_warp_leaves_the_brush_rim_in_place`: the outer 3 % of the brush …

title: Native brush outline and crosshair cursors on macOS, X11 and Wayland (#1343)
author: tanish2k09
body:
Part of #1343 (cursor lag), done jointly with @jerrykimo's #968.

## What
The brush outline and the crosshairs (Precise, crosshair-while-painting, the big-tip hotspot) were OS cursor bitmaps only on Windows (#1160). On macOS, X11 and Wayland the app painted them into the canvas, so they trailed the hardware pointer by render + present + compositor latency and "jumped to catch up" on slow frames, which is what the #1343 reports describe. The latency-surface experiments didn't perceptibly help, which fits: the outline was the lagging thing, not the strokes.

`tool_cursor` now uploads the bitmap on every desktop root viewport (eframe/egui-winit 0.36 upload `cursor_image` through winit `CustomCursor` on all of them). The web build and immediate viewports keep the painted path.

- **macOS sizing (from #968):** winit takes an `NSCursor` image's size in logical points, so on macOS the bitmap scales only with the UI zoom (`native_scale`); Windows, X11 and Wayland take physical pixels.
- **Size cap off Windows:** 255 px, because X servers and hardware cursor planes commonly cap at 256 and fall back to software cursors (or reject the image) past that. #968 used 128. A larger tip keeps today's fallback: the painted full-size outline plus a small OS crosshair at the hotspot. Windows keeps 2048.
- **Out of scope:** the Pencil's square stays painted (it snaps to the pixel grid, and a cursor hotspot can't follow that). The pipette stays painted too (an SVG icon; it's a follow-up and could come from #968's pipette bitmap). The Hand bitmap stays Windows-only, because the other platforms draw their own hands.

Credit: @jerrykimo is co-author (the cross-platform approach and the macOS point sizing in #968).

title: Control-channel document events and `app.capabilities`
author: emmertex
body:
> **Stacked on #3244** (which includes the earlier PRs in this series): this branch contains their commits. Please review only the commits after them; it will be rebased once #3244 merges.

### Summary
- `events.subscribe {events?}` on the TCP control channel pushes `document.opened`, `document.saved`, `document.closed` lines (`{"event", "params": {path, format, docId}}`, no `id`) on the same connection, always in opened → saved → closed order. Saves are reported even without changes; copies/exports are not.
- The server shares the socket between replies and events, starts forwarding only after the subscribe reply, lifts the idle read timeout for subscribers, one subscription per connection, max 64.
- `app.capabilities` returns `{app, version, protocol, features, events}` so callers feature-detect (`saveInPlace`, `events`).
- `photocraft --version --json` prints the same object without opening a window. Older builds stop at `--version` and print the plain line, so launchers can run this probe against any release.
- Documented in `docs/control-protocol.md` › Events. MCP notifications and `photocraft-cli serve` events are follow-up work.

### Motivation
Tools that hand a file to an editor need to know when it was saved (to re-read it) and when the user is done, without polling or relying on window focus.

### Test plan
- `doc_events` unit tests (order, filters, Save As path on close, dead subscribers, limits, bad names) and an app-level test through `control::handle`.
- `control_server` test: reply before events, events have no id, second subscribe refused, connection keeps serving.

title: Menus: a submenu stays open while the pointer heads for it (#1218)
author: brennanMKE
body:
Fixes the submenu part of #1218.

In the in-window menu bar (Windows, Linux, and macOS with `--in-window-menus`), moving from a submenu's row toward one of its lower items crosses the rows below. Unless the pointer moved in a straight line, the submenu closed on the way, and the crossed rows lit up or opened their own submenus. In the report's example, going from Image › Mode to 16 Bits/Channel crosses Adjustments.

## Cause

egui's `SubMenu` keeps an open submenu only while `is_moving_towards_rect` is true: the pointer's current direction, averaged over the last 0.1 s, must point straight into the popup. A bowed path, or any pause of more than about 0.1 s, fails that test. egui then closes the submenu, and the next frame opens the submenu of the row under the pointer. `menu_nav` also moved the highlight to every row crossed.

## Fix

macOS and Photoshop judge this with a triangle. `menu_nav::Nav::row` now does the same for submenu rows:

- **The triangle:** from the point where the pointer left the row to the submenu's near edge, with 24 pt of slack above and below.
- **While the pointer is inside it:** if egui closes the submenu, `MenuState::open_item` is restored straight after the row is drawn. Later rows therefore can't open their own submenus.
- **Highlight:** the row stays lit, and the rows crossed don't light up.
- **When the submenu switches:**
  - when the pointer rests on another row for 0.3 s;
  - when it moves outside the triangle (straight down, or back to the left);
  - on a click or a key, as before.

  When the submenu lets go, the row under the pointer takes the highlight.
- **Keyboard:** ↑ and ↓ move the highlight as before; the pointer's hold no longer overrides them.

The change is about 130 lines in `menu_nav.rs`, with no change to egui. Nested submenus get the same behaviour, since each level runs the same code.

title: test(paint): pin the retouch dab footprint to the Full Size ring
author: switch87
body:
Closes #1761.

This is the regression test @theriseandfallofitall asked for: one that pins "changed radius ≈ size/2, inside the Full Size ring".

`crates/paint/src/retouch.rs` gains `footprint_stays_inside_the_full_size_ring`. For a single dab of radius 10.5 px it walks the whole `footprint` rect at hardness 1.0, 0.5 and 0.0, measures each painted pixel's distance from the centre using pixel centres (`x + 0.5`, `y + 0.5` — the same sampling `footprint` and `render.rs` use), and asserts:

- **nothing paints past `radius + 0.5`** at any hardness. The half pixel is the anti-aliased edge of `dab_coverage`, which returns 0 from `d >= radius + 0.5`. This is the invariant that a larger-than-cursor brush would break.
- **something does paint** at every hardness, so the test cannot pass by painting nothing.
- **a hard tip reaches the ring** (`hardness == 1.0` → farthest painted pixel is beyond `radius`). Softer tips are deliberately *not* held to that: `dab_coverage` blends the AA edge with the hardness falloff, so at hardness 0.5 coverage reaches 0 at `radius` itself and the farthest painted pixel sits at ~10.12 px. That matches @vangel76's probe (10.12–10.27 px for Spot Healing at hardness 50) and is the falloff working as intended, not a defect.

That last point is why the test is written this way rather than asserting "changed radius ≈ size/2" flat: at a soft tip the ring is the 50 % contour, so painting past it is correct and only the Full Size tip pins the outer bound.

Verification:

```
cargo test -p photocraft-paint --lib          85 passed
cargo clippy -p photocraft-paint --all-targets -- -D warnings   clean
cargo fmt -p photocraft-paint -- --check      clean
```

The test lives in the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `retouch.rs`, next to `coverage_matches_apply_stroke_bounds`, and follows its style. No production code is touched.

title: Type: fall back to installed Khmer, Lao and Burmese fonts (#218)
author: RaccoonPie-314
body:
## The bug

Khmer (and Lao / Burmese) text renders as `.notdef` boxes even though the OS has a font for the script — #218, scorecard item TYPE-218-3.

## Root cause

Not detection, and not shaping. Each layer tested separately:

| layer | result |
|---|---|
| detection | `FontDb::load_system_fonts()` finds *Khmer Sangam MN* |
| loading + shaping | laying the same text out with that family gives real clusters, coeng subscripts included |
| **selection** | the fallback stack never contains a Khmer-capable family |

`fallback_candidates()` is a list of family names filtered against what is installed (`FontDb::refresh_generics`). It carried Thai, CJK, Arabic and Hebrew entries, but nothing for Khmer, Lao or Burmese. `layout.rs` builds each run's CSS family list from exactly that stack plus a trailing `sans-serif`, which resolves to Inter — so an installed Southeast Asian font could not be reached from a Latin-only face, and every cluster became `.notdef`.

## Changes

**photocraft-text** — `KHMER_FAMILIES`, `LAO_FAMILIES` and `MYANMAR_FAMILIES` join `fallback_candidates` next to `THAI_FAMILIES`. The web build's served-font path gets the matching `Khmr` / `Laoo` / `Mymr` script codes, character ranges and `km` / `lo` / `my` languages, so a host serving `Noto Sans Khmer` works there too.

**photocraft-ui-egui** — the UI's lazy loader had one non-CJK slot (Thai: `Sources::thai`, `thai_tried`, `is_thai`, `thai_font_files`). It becomes a `LazyScript` slot table fed by `script_font_files(mac, win, noto_stem, family)`, so the three scripts are data rather than a third and fourth copy of the same state machine. This half matters on its own: tab titles, layer names and panel labels were tofu for the same reason but through a different stack than the canvas.

Family names follow Microsoft's [script and font support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/globalization/fonts-layout/font-support) table (`Khmer UI` / `Lao UI` on Windows 8, `Leelawadee UI` from 8.1, `Myanmar Text`) and th…

title: Windows installer: refuse Windows 7 and 8 with a clear message (#2310)
author: dhiorns15
body:
Closes #2310.

**The problem.** PhotoCraft can't run on Windows 7 or 8. Since Rust 1.78 the standard library calls `ProcessPrng` in `bcryptprimitives.dll`, which only exists on Windows 10 and later, so Windows refuses to start the program before any of our code runs:

> The procedure entry point ProcessPrng could not be located in the dynamic link library bcryptprimitives.dll.

`docs/gaps.md` already lists Windows 7 as out of scope, and `docs/releasing.md` says the builds are for Windows 10+. The MSI, though, installed on Windows 7 anyway, leaving people with that cryptic error.

**The change**
- **Installer:** the MSI now stops on Windows 7 and 8 with "PhotoCraft needs Windows 10 or later. This version of Windows can't run it."
  - A registry search sets `WINDOWS10ORLATER` from `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\CurrentMajorVersionNumber`. That value exists only from Windows 10 on, in both the 32-bit and 64-bit registry views, so the x86 MSI gets the same check.
  - The rule is `<Launch Condition="Installed OR WINDOWS10ORLATER">`, so repair and uninstall still work on any Windows.
  - MSI's own `VersionNT` isn't used: it has reported both 603 and 1000 on Windows 10 (it's 1000 on the Windows 11 PC I tested on).
- **README:** the Windows downloads section now says Windows 10 or later is required. The portable zip can't check anything, because Windows rejects the exe before it runs.

**Verified locally (WiX 5.0.2, as in CI)**
- `package.ps1 -Arch x64 -SkipBuild` builds the MSI and passes its ICE50 validation.
- Read back from the built MSI:
  - `LaunchCondition`: `Installed OR WINDOWS10ORLATER` with the message.
  - `AppSearch` and `RegLocator`: the search, which runs at sequence 50, before `LaunchConditions` at 100.
  - The property is listed in `SecureCustomProperties`.
- Running `AppSearch` in a Windows Installer session, with nothing installed: on Windows 11 the property is `#10` and the condition is true. With the property cleared, as on Windows 7…

title: Edit > Copy takes a targeted layer mask, so masks travel between layers and documents (#2928)
author: vbasky
body:
Part of #2928: the copy & paste half. The ⌥-drag half belongs on the mask-drag start that #3118 is landing, and this branch deliberately does not touch that plumbing.

## Root cause
Copy never knew about the targeted mask. With a mask targeted, ⌘C copied the layer's pixels (or refused on a pixel-less layer), so a mask could never be moved to another layer or document. Paste was ready all along: pasting into a targeted mask has worked since #1035, and the session clipboard is shared between documents.

## What changed
- `edit.copy` honours `"target":"mask"`: the mask's values, as a grayscale clip — inside the selection, or the whole canvas when there is none, as Photoshop copies a mask whole. An untouched Reveal All / Hide All mask copies at its default value, so plain masks transfer too. Pasting then **replaces** the target mask (the request in #2928).
- `edit.copy` joined `routed()`/`edits_mask()`: the ⌘C dispatched while the Layers panel targets a mask carries the target, and Copy is enabled on adjustment and fill layers (which have no pixels of their own) exactly while their mask is targeted. ⌥-viewing a mask targets it as for every other routed command.
- Agents can drive it directly: `edit.copy {"target":"mask"}` → `edit.paste {"target":"mask"}`, in the same or another document; different canvas sizes centre the paste like any other paste.

## Tests
- `copy_with_the_mask_targeted_takes_the_mask_as_grayscale` — copy → paste into another layer's reveal-all mask at 8/16/32 bits, values and bounds, one undo step on the paste, none on the copy.
- `an_untouched_mask_copies_the_whole_canvas_at_its_default` — a never-painted Reveal All mask still transfers.
- `mask_copy_takes_only_the_selection`, `mask_copy_needs_a_mask_and_fails_gracefully` (no doc / no mask → Err, clipboard untouched; enablement on a pixel-less adjustment layer), `a_copied_mask_travels_to_another_document`.

title: PNG export: Indexed Color keeps the document resolution (#3047)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3047

## Root cause
Indexed Color documents are exported to PNG through a dedicated palette encoder (`encode_png_indexed`, used by `export_mode_specific` in `crates/io/src/flat.rs`). Unlike the ordinary PNG encoder, it never set `pixel_dims`, so no `pHYs` chunk was written and the file reopened at 72 ppi.

## Fix
- `photocraft_codecs::encode_png_indexed` takes an optional `dpi` and writes `pHYs` (metres, rounded like the RGB path) when both axes are positive and finite.
- The flat exporter passes the document resolution under the same `embed_metadata` rule as the ordinary PNG encoder.
- Save for Web PNG-8 passes `None` (unchanged behaviour; its PNG-24 path also only writes metadata on request).

## Tests
- `crates/io/tests/modes.rs::indexed_png_keeps_the_document_resolution`: a 300 ppi Indexed document exports as a palette PNG (colour type 3) and reopens at 300 ppi. Fails without the fix (reopens at 72 ppi), passes with it.

## Commands
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-io --test modes --test flat --test png_text_metadata`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-codecs --lib -- png`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --lib -- web`
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs -p photocraft-io --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --lib -- -D warnings`

title: ui: keep the Color panel knob in the corner it was dragged to
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #3228

## Cause

The Color panel's SV field rebuilds its `Hsva` from the stored colour every frame, and the colour lives as RGB. At the bottom edge the value is 0 — black — and black reads back as `s = 0`, so the frame after the drag that put the knob in the bottom-right corner the knob was drawn at `x = s = 0`: bottom-left. The colour round-trips correctly, the field position does not survive it.

The field already remembered the *hue* for a degenerate colour ("Keep hue stable for greys"), but not the saturation.

## Fix

Remember what the field was actually showing — hue **and** saturation — in the same temp entry, and restore both only where the colour itself cannot carry them:

* **black** (`v` ≈ 0): neither hue nor saturation survives the RGB round trip, so restore both — the knob stays in the corner it was dragged to;
* **a grey** (`s` ≈ 0): the saturation really is zero, which is where the knob belongs, only the hue was undefined — restore the hue alone;
* **any other colour**: untouched.

## Tests

* `field_hsva_keeps_black_where_it_was_and_leaves_a_real_colour_alone` — the three cases above.
* `dragging_to_the_bottom_right_keeps_the_knob_there` — a real drag through the harness into the corner: the field picks black there, keeps the dragged saturation, and the next frame draws the knob in that corner.

Verified locally: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib color_tests` (19 passed), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`. The full crate suite runs in CI.

title: Interface: an Enable Animations preference (#3273)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3273. Part of #217 (scorecard row UI-217-10).

## What changed

PhotoCraft had no way to turn UI animation off. Menus, popups and collapsing sections always fade or slide over egui's `animation_time`, and scroll areas glide to their target. #217 asks for a toggle, and #1218 asks for the same thing as a reduced-motion mode. #3251 fixes that issue's submenu part and leaves this out.

- **New preference:** Preferences › Interface › **Enable animations** (`interface.enableAnimations`, on by default). It is saved with the other preferences, and agents can set it with `prefs.set`.
- **What off does:** `prefs_ui::sync_animations` sets `animation_time` to 0 and `scroll_animation` to `ScrollAnimation::none()` in both the dark and the light style. A system appearance switch therefore keeps the setting.
- **On:** it puts egui's defaults back.
- **Theme changes:** the setting is re-checked every frame, like `sync_tooltips`, because a theme change rebuilds the style. It writes only when the value differs.
- **Prefs audit:** the field is read, so the count of settings that do nothing stays at 43 (now of 151).
- **Translations:** the label "Enable animations" is in all 16 catalogs.
- **Scorecard:** UI-217-10 moves from `missing` to `partial`. Animations are done. The Home screen already lists recent files (#2691). Still open: the canvas pattern toggle (#2317 / #2264) and an option to hide the Home screen recents.

## Tests

`enable_animations_off_stops_fades_and_scroll_glides_and_is_remembered` (in `prefs_ui.rs` tests):
- A saved `false` applies on the first frame after a restart (both styles: `animation_time` 0, no scroll animation).
- It survives a theme change.
- `prefs.set` to `true` restores egui's defaults.
- A hand-edited value of the wrong type doesn't crash, and animations stay on.

Without the `sync_animations` call the test fails: `left: [0.2, 0.2]`, `right: [0.0, 0.0]`.

title: Vanishing Point: tear off planes and clone in perspective (#3280)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3280

**Depends on #3133.** This branch is stacked on it, so the first commit here is #3133's. Review the last commit only.

## What changed

**Tear-off planes** (`crates/ui-egui/src/vp_ui.rs`)
- Ctrl/Cmd-drag an edge node, with Create Plane or Edit Plane, to tear off a plane at 90°. Dragging the torn plane's far edge node sets its depth, and Alt-dragging it sets its angle.
- A torn plane is stored in its torn-off form (`from`/`edge`/`angle`/`depth`). Its corners are recomputed from its parent after every edit, the same way the engine builds the scene, so it follows the parent. It is drawn and validated like the other planes. On OK it is sent to `filter.vanishingPoint` as `{"from", "edge", "angle", "depth"}`.
- Deleting a parent plane keeps its torn planes as drawn planes.

**Stamp tool (S)**
- Alt-click a plane to set the source, then drag to clone in perspective.
- Options: Diameter, Hardness, Opacity and Aligned (later strokes keep the first stroke's offset). Cmd/Ctrl+Z inside the window removes the last stroke.
- The canvas shows the strokes as they are painted. The preview uses the same anchored frame as the engine and paints the strokes in pieces. Only the painted area recomposites, through a new `vp_ui::damage` hook in `canvas::damage_since`.

title: Rulers: stay level and fully ticked on a rotated view; guides turn with the image (#3233)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3233
Fixes #3277

## Root cause

- **Rulers (#3233):** `draw_rulers` computed the visible range with `xf.to_doc` of the ruler's end points and placed ticks with `xf.to_screen(px, 0).x` (or `.y`), both through the *rotated* view. With a rotation, a document axis no longer runs along the screen axis, so the ticks were squeezed into a short stretch (none at 90°) and the rest of the ruler was empty, as in the issue screenshot.
- **Guides (#3277, found while fixing this):** `draw_guides` drew a vertical guide as a screen-vertical line through the screen position of `(pos, 0)` (likewise for horizontal ones). On a rotated view that line no longer marks the guide's document coordinate, while hit-testing and snapping still use it.

## Fix

- Rulers are screen chrome and stay level: they now measure with the view minus its rotation (`ruler_xform`). Zoom, flip and pixel aspect stay the same, so the ticks never stretch, and 0 is anchored at the screen position of the document origin as the rotated view draws it. Tilted guides therefore meet the rulers near their numbers. Unrotated views are unchanged.
- Guides belong to the document (as in Photoshop) and turn with the image: `guide_segment` draws the document line x = pos (or y = pos) across every document point the clip rect shows. Unrotated, that is still the clip's full height/width.
- Ruler labels left of / above the origin read without a minus sign (`ruler_label` prints the absolute value), as in Photoshop 2026 ("1000 500 0 500 1000"); this applies to every view, and `rotated_view_keeps_full_rulers` now checks it (fails with the old signed labels: tick -800 labelled "-800").

Before (issue) vs after: the rulers are fully ticked at -119°, and a vertical guide at x = 500 and a horizontal one at y = 300 now cross the rotated image at those coordinates (checked with the `snapshot` example).

Verified against Photoshop 2026: rulers stay level at zoom scale, anchored at the document origin's screen position; guides turn w…

title: Smart Filters: distinct editors, shared disclosure and stable alpha
author: abc2cb
body:
Double-clicking a Smart Filter row currently reopens its parameter dialog, with no separate target for that filter's blending. The shared mask is only a placeholder, and the layer disclosure does not hide Smart Filters. This change gives the filter name and right-hand Blending Options icon separate double-click targets, displays the real shared mask, and uses one disclosure for layer effects and Smart Filters without changing document pixels or history.

Blending Options edits the selected filter's Mode and 0–100% Opacity, with temporary Preview, a bounded CMS-aware image viewport, OK, Cancel, and Undo/Redo. The UI sends 1% as 0.01. Parameter editors reopen stored values and update the existing filter instead of appending a duplicate; Invert has no invented parameter editor and Camera Raw keeps its dedicated editor. Captured document/revision/filter identity and a bounded weak document snapshot guard reject stale editors, including reopening the same saved document with the same IDs.

Native QA also reproduced an existing Smart Filter opacity defect: translucent alpha 128 became 129 at 1% and 160 at 50%. Smart Filter strength now interpolates premultiplied input/filtered results, preserving coverage for alpha-preserving filters. Normal mode also interpolates actual coverage changes; non-Normal modes retain source-over semantics when the filtered surface changes alpha, preserving input-only and output-only pixels around blur edges. This does not alter global layer compositing.

The PR builds on merged #2229 and #2739. Their implementations are not duplicated: current Smart Object source APIs, cached stages and background jobs are retained. Six new localization keys are supplied in all 16 catalogs. Behavior and storage limits are documented in `docs/smart-filters.md`.

title: fix(io): smooth PSD gradients no longer overshoot their stops (#3028)
author: Sir-Starch
body: Fixes #3028 ## Problem The Gradient Map in the issue (0% `#cacaca`, 27% `#1c1c1c`, 53% `#1c1c1c`, 72% `#949494`) renders far too dark in the middle: the 27%-53% stretch should be a flat `#1c1c1c`, but PhotoCraft dips well below it. ## Cause The PSD importer bakes Smoothness into dense stops in `gradient_bake::eval` (Catmull-Rom blended with linear). The tangent at each stop comes from its neighbouring stops. For the segment between the two equal-coloured stops, both end colours are the same, yet each end tangent is non-zero (it is taken from the neighbouring stops, `#cacaca` on one side and `#949494` on the other), so the Hermite curve undershoots the plateau. On the issue's file the output at t = 0.396 was 0.034 (9/255) instead of 28/255. The stop positions and colours are parsed correctly; only the interpolation is off. ## Fix Clamp each interpolated channel to the range of the segment's own two end colours (in the method's interpolation space: sRGB, linear light or Oklab). Smoothness still eases the ramps, but it can no longer invent a colour outside the segment, so a plateau stays exactly flat. It is a small change in `eval`. `bake` is shared, so this also applies to gradient fills, gradient overlays and smoothed opacity stops read from PSD files, not only to Gradient Map. Any smooth segment whose Catmull-Rom curve used to leave its endpoints' range is now bounded by it. ## Result Measured on the issue's PSD, per pixel against Photoshop's embedded composite (red channel; the render is grayscale): | | max error | mean error | pixels off by more than 8/255 | |---|---|---|---| | before (`main`) | 19 | 4.48 | 205 263 | | after | 6 | 1.66 | 0 | The pixel the issue's dark band centres on, (445, 506), was `9` against Photoshop's `28`; it is now `28`. title: Decode Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3/4 (vendor-compressed sensor data)
author: Gotya-OFFCIAL
body:
# Decode Panasonic RW2 RawFormat 3/4 (vendor-compressed sensor data)

`crates/raw/src/rw2.rs` only handled RawFormat 5 (uncompressed); everything else fell back to the embedded 1920×1440 JPEG preview with a `raw-fallback` warning. This adds a full sensor decoder for RawFormat 4 — the compressed variant used by e.g. the DMC-GX7 (4816×3464, 12-bit) — and maps RawFormat 3 to the same row layout.

## What it does

RawFormat 4 stores 14 Bayer pixels per 128-bit block: two unchanged 12-bit seeds, then four groups of three 8-bit differences plus a 2-bit shift code (`{0,1,2,4}` left shift). Each difference predicts against the previous same-colour pixel; a zero difference copies the immediately preceding sample. Rows stride `(w·9 + 2·(w/14))/8` through 16 KiB strips with an XOR-0x3FF0 page interleave and a split rotation; near a page boundary the 16-bit read window wraps inside the strip instead of crossing into the next one.

## Provenance / licensing

Implemented independently for this project — no code was copied from GPL/LGPL decoders. The bitstream layout was derived from sample files (Panasonic DMC-GX7) and verified bit-exact against LibRaw's `raw_image` output via the rawpy bindings:

- 4816×3464 DMC-GX7 samples: **0 mismatches / 16,682,624 pixels** (two separate files)
- the row/stride/page model and predictor recurrence are documented from observation in `rw2.rs` comments

## Verification

- `cargo test -p photocraft-raw` — all green, incl. new `rw2_format4_round_trip_is_exact` (synthetic encoder → exact round-trip) and `rw2_format4_crosses_pages`
- end-to-end on the real GX7 files: full-resolution develop into 4592×3448 16-bit ProPhoto RGB, no fallback warning
- raw sensor layer bit-exact vs LibRaw (see above)

## Notes

- Colour calibration for Panasonic bodies is still absent (pre-existing behaviour, still warned) — the RAW decode itself is the fix here.

title: ui: Dust & Scratches previews at full resolution, as it applies
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #3265

## Cause

`full_resolution_preview` in `crates/ui-egui/src/filter_dialog.rs` decides which live previews run on the reduced proxy and which run at full resolution, and Dust & Scratches was not in `FULL_RESOLUTION_PREVIEW`.

Its `radius` *is* a pixel param, so `preview_factor` clamps the proxy factor to `radius / 1` — but only that. At the default radius the preview happens to land on full resolution; at a practical radius it previews at the document's full factor (k = 4 on a 24 MP document), on an image where downsampling has already averaged away the specks the filter exists to remove, with a radius that then covers k times the area it covers in the result, upscaled back for display. Hence the blocky preview in the report, and a preview that shows nothing removed.

`OK` always applied at full resolution — the result was never wrong, only the interactive feedback was.

## Fix

Add `filter.noise.dustAndScratches` to `FULL_RESOLUTION_PREVIEW` and name it in the category comment next to the other per-pixel noise filters.

## Test

The issue asks for one on the intended preview-quality path, so `("filter.noise.dustAndScratches", {"radius": 4, "threshold": 0})` joins `fixed_size_filters_preview_at_the_scale_they_apply`, which already asserts both that `preview_factor` comes out as 1 and that the shown preview is what OK applies.

Verified: with the list entry removed the test fails with `left: 4, right: 1` at the `preview_factor` assertion — the defect itself; with it, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` (1828 passed), `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `fmt --check` and `cargo xtask layers` are all clean.

title: Codecs: decode PNM straight into the budgeted output buffer (#2938)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2938

## Root cause
`Limits::max_alloc` budgets the decoded pixel buffer, and `Limits::check` charged exactly that before decoding. But the PNM decoder then collected every sample into a `Vec<u32>` first (4x the output of an 8-bit image; for 16-bit, `Image::from_u16` added a further `u16` → byte copy, so roughly 8 bytes per 2-byte sample at peak). PFM did the same with a `Vec<f32>` next to the output bytes. None of that scratch was covered by the budget.

## Fix
This takes the first option from the issue: keep the intermediate in the budgeted output type. A small `Samples` writer reserves the output bytes with `try_reserve_exact`, so a failed allocation becomes `LimitExceeded`. It checks each value against `maxval`, rescales it the same way as before and appends it in native-endian order. P2/P3/P5/P6/P7 build the `Image` from those bytes with `from_raw`. PFM writes native-endian `f32` bytes straight into the output rows, still bottom-to-top. The ASCII reservation stays bounded by the file length (#1110). The decoded values don't change.

## Tests
- New `crates/codecs/tests/pnm_peak_memory.rs`, Linux only and in its own process. It resets the peak RSS through `/proc/self/clear_refs`, decodes a 4096² 8-bit P5 (16 MiB of output) and asserts that the peak grew by less than 2x the output. Without the fix it fails: `decoding a 16777216 byte image raised peak RSS by 84189184 bytes`. With the fix it passes, and it was stable over repeated runs. Where the kernel doesn't allow `clear_refs`, the test skips.
- The existing value tests in `malformed.rs` (maxval rescaling for 8 and 16 bit, PFM bottom-up and endianness), `limits.rs` (bomb headers, #1110 reservations) and `roundtrip.rs` still pass.

## Commands

cargo clippy -p photocraft-codecs --all-targets -- -D warnings

title: Format: admit the declared .pcraft canvas before loading it (#2935)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2935

Also the load-time half of #2934 (the GPU destination-texture budget follows in a separate PR).

## Root cause

`store::load` read the manifest and handed `m.document.size` straight to `Loader::document`, which copied it into the `Document`. `LoadOptions` bounded manifest, blob and decompressed bytes, but nothing bounded the declared canvas. A few bytes of JSON could declare a canvas of any size, up to `u32::MAX` × `u32::MAX`, and the CPU reduction, thumbnails and display textures then work in proportion to that area.

## Fix

- `LoadOptions` gains `max_canvas_side` (default `MAX_CANVAS_SIDE` = 300000: Photoshop's PSB limit, the same as the PSD header check and `file.new`) and `max_canvas_pixels` (default `MAX_CANVAS_PIXELS` = 300000², the full PSB canvas).
- The default admits every canvas the app lets a user create: `file.new`, Canvas Size, Image Size with Resample off and PSB import all reach 300000 × 300000. A lower area cap (an earlier revision used 2^32 = 65536²) would let a user create and save a document that then refuses to reopen. Callers that handle untrusted files (previewers, batch jobs) can lower either budget.
- `store::load` calls `admit_canvas` right after reading the manifest, before any tile or blob is decoded. It rejects an empty canvas (`Corrupt`), a side over the limit and an area over the limit (`LimitExceeded`, with the declared size in the message).
- Loading stays proportional to the file, not to the declared canvas: layers, masks and channels are sparse tiles read from the bundle under the byte budgets, so a 300000² manifest with no content allocates nothing for its area (the test checks the tile count).
- A compile-time assert in `engine/src/document_preset_cmds.rs` ties `file.new`'s `MAX_DIMENSION` to the loader's defaults, so the two can't drift apart again.
- The fuzz target and `book/src/security/parser-hardening.md` are updated to match.

title: GPU canvas: price the display textures before building them (#2934)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #2934

The load-time half (a `.pcraft` canvas above 300000 px per side or 4 gigapixels is refused) is #3295. This PR adds the GPU-side budget the issue asks for, which also covers documents that arrive by other routes (PSB, Canvas Size, `file.new`).

## Root cause

`DocTextures::new` built a full-resolution, mipmapped texture set covering the whole canvas in `DEFAULT_TILE` tiles. The only limit was the side length of each texture, so the size of the canvas alone decided how much GPU memory was committed. A 300000×300000 canvas asks for about 480 GB, and an admitted 65536² canvas asks for about 23 GB. `fits_budget` only covers resident layer pages, not this destination set.

## Fix (`crates/ui-egui/src/gpu_canvas.rs`, `canvas.rs`)

- `canvas_texture_bytes(size, tile, bpp)` prices the set in closed form, over at most four distinct tile shapes and every mip level, with saturating arithmetic. Any declared size costs O(1) to price. The result matches `texture_info`.
- `canvas_budget(ram)` returns a quarter of physical memory, assuming 16 GB when RAM is unknown, and never goes below `MIN_GPU_BUDGET`. This is the same RAM cap `memory_budget` uses. The value is stored in `Resources` and can be changed with `GpuCanvas::set_canvas_budget`.
- `DocTextures::new` returns `None` and creates nothing when the set is over budget. All three callers handle that: `upload_full_as`, `composite` (which returns `Unsupported`) and `upload_composite`.
- `GpuCanvas::refresh` returns kind `REFRESH_OVER_BUDGET` and drops any stale set. `ensure_gpu` checks `fits_canvas` before the per-frame memory-budget walk, and returns `false` on that kind just as it does for `"lost"`. The document is then drawn on the reduced CPU canvas (at most `MAX_TEXTURE` per side), so a large document still displays.

## Tests

- `gpu_canvas::tests::canvas_texture_bytes_price_every_tile_and_mip_level` (no GPU needed): the closed form equals a tile-by-tile sum for several sizes and tile sides. 300000² is over any b…

title: Move tool: double-click type on the canvas to edit it (#1132)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Closes #1132.

Since Photoshop CC 2019, double-clicking a type layer on the canvas with the **Move** tool starts editing its text, with no manual tool switch. PhotoCraft only did this from the Layers panel's type thumbnail.

With the Move tool selected, a double-click on type now:
- picks the topmost visible type layer under the pointer, using the Type tool's own hit test, and makes it the active layer;
- opens an edit session with the caret on the glyph under the pointer;
- switches to the Type tool (Vertical Type for vertical text).

A double-click anywhere else does nothing. ⌘ held over another tool (the temporary Move) doesn't trigger it. An open transform box keeps its double-click, which commits the transform.

### Changes
- `type_tool::edit_at`: starts an edit at a document point, reusing `hit_layer`, `begin_edit` and `hit_offset`. A PSD type layer is re-rendered inside the edit session, as when you click into it with the Type tool.
- `canvas.rs`: calls `edit_at` on a Move tool double-click when no transform box is open.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: adds a row to the Move tool table.

### Testing
- New test `type_tool::canvas_tests::move_tool_double_click_on_type_edits_it`. It double-clicks a glyph while another layer is active and checks:
  - the Type tool takes over;
  - the caret sits on that glyph;
  - the type layer becomes active;
  - no history step is added;
  - typed text lands at the caret;
  - a double-click off the text stays with the Move tool.
- The test fails without the `canvas.rs` change, with the tool staying Move.
- The type tests' harness steps a quarter second per frame, which is past egui's 0.3 s double-click delay, so this test uses a 60 fps harness (`fast_harness`).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`: 1834 lib tests plus all integration test files pass.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` are clean.
