title: Brush Settings: a response curve per dynamic control (#3294)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3294 (scorecard TOOL-213-11; part of #213)

## What changed
The global pen curve (Preferences › Tools › Pressure Curve) existed; each brush dynamic had no own response to its control. Now every `Dynamic` (Size, Opacity, Flow, Roundness, Scatter, Count, Texture Depth, Foreground/Background, …) carries a response curve for its Fade / Pen Pressure / Pen Tilt / Stylus Wheel / Rotation input, applied after the global pen curve.

- **paint**: new `ResponseCurve` (`crates/paint/src/curve.rs`): the global curve's monotone cubic (Fritsch–Carlson), moved down from the engine as a fixed-size `Copy` type so a dab evaluates it without allocating. Same sanitising (non-finite dropped, clamped, sorted, deduped, ≤16 points, monotone outputs). Serialises as its point list. `Dynamic.curve` (defaults to linear); `dynamics::dynamic_value` applies it wherever a control value is read (scalar dynamics, base diameter, scatter, foreground/background). Angle Jitter and the direction controls ignore it.
- **engine**: `prefs::PressureCurve` is now `photocraft_paint::ResponseCurve` (one implementation, existing prefs tests unchanged and green). `tools.setBrush` takes it through the existing deep merge, e.g. `{"shapeDynamics":{"size":{"control":"penPressure","curve":[[0,0],[0.5,0.2],[1,1]]}}}`; the curve is always in the brush JSON, so the Brush Settings diff can set it back to linear, actions record it and presets keep it.
- **ui-egui**: each Control row gets a curve button (lit while the curve isn't linear) that opens the same editor as Preferences › Tools (drag/add/remove points, Linear/Soft/Hard). `pressure_curve_ui::edit_points` is the shared editor. New string "Response curve" in all 16 catalogs.
- **io**: ABR import keeps a linear curve.
- **scorecard**: TOOL-213-11 → done; `docs/scorecard.md` regenerated.

## Tests

title: Brush: smooth edges on large hard round strokes (#3240)
author: dhiorns15
body: Closes #3240. **Cause.** At Photoshop's default 25 % spacing, neighbouring round dabs sit a quarter of their width apart. Where their circles cross, a hard edge is notched by `r − √(r² − (s/2)²)`, about 3 % of the radius. For a 400 px tip that's **6 px**, which is the scalloped edge in the issue; at 100 px it's 1.3 px. **Fix.** The painting tools take shorter steps when a plain, full-Flow round tip's Spacing would notch the edge by more than half a pixel. That covers Brush, Pencil and Eraser, in both the live stroke and the committed one. - A softer rim hides a notch up to a fifth of its width, so the step can stay longer as hardness drops; by about 85 % hardness nothing changes. - At full Flow the extra dabs only add coverage along the edge. The stroke's pixels inside are identical, and the tests check that. **Left exactly as before** (same dabs, same pixels), because for these extra dabs would change the look: - Flow below 100 %: the overlap rings of a low-Flow stroke are how it builds up. I tried compensating each dab's flow instead; it kept the centre density, but the stroke's ends looked different, so I dropped it. - Sampled tips, roundness below 100 %, scattering, random size/roundness/opacity/flow/colour jitter, Fade, per-tip texture, Dual Brush, Wet Edges, Noise and Build-up. - Tools that pick up or sample per dab (Smudge, Mixer Brush, the retouching tools): `StrokeRenderer::smooth_edges()` is opt-in and they don't call it. **Numbers** (a 1000 px drag, release build) | Tip | Edge ripple | Dabs | Time | |---|---|---|---| | 400 px, hardness 100 % | 6.06 → **0.17 px** | 11 → 36 | 12 → 27 ms | | 100 px, hardness 100 % | 1.26 → **0.17 px** | 41 → 71 | 3 → 4 ms | | 1000 px, hardness 100 % | (bumps) → smooth | 5 → 23 | 35 → 100 ms | | 400 px, hardness 90 % | 4.38 → 2.43 px | 11 → 12 | same | | 400 px, hardness ≤ 75 % or Flow 30 % | unchanged | unchanged | same | **Before / after**

body:
Fixes #3298 (part of #213, scorecard row TOOL-213-8)

## What changed

**W/H link.** The Clone Source panel now has Photoshop's chain button (Maintain aspect ratio) beside W/H. With it on, setting only W (or only H) scales the other field by the same factor. The engine handles this, so agents and actions can drive it:

title: Fix/curved stroke splineFix faceted strokes on fast curves: add a midpoint Bézier spline stage before smoothing
author: Marpuriganesh
body: ## Problem Fast circular strokes come out faceted, like a polygon with visible corners instead of a round curve. This happens with smoothing off and with smoothing on (shown here at 10). | Before | After | | :---: | :---: | | || | Faceted curves (Brush, smoothing 10) | Round curves (same brush and settings) | ## Cause The engine only sees the pointer events the platform delivers, roughly one per frame, so a fast circle is only about 10 points per loop. Those points were joined with straight lines and dabs were spaced along that polyline, so every event became a corner. Smoothing doesn't fix this: both modes (exponential and pulled string) move the brush toward each new point in a straight line, which adds corners of its own. ## Change A new `Spline` stage in `crates/paint/src/dynamics.rs` turns the sparse points into a smooth path before smoothing and dab spacing: input -> Spline -> Smoother -> PathWalker -> dabs - Midpoint quadratic Bézier: for consecutive points p0, p1, p2 it draws a curve from mid(p0,p1) to mid(p1,p2) with p1 as the control point. Pieces start where the previous one ended, so there are no gaps or jumps. - The stroke start is passed through unchanged. A straight lead-in runs from the first point to the first midpoint, and a straight run from the last midpoint reaches the last input point exactly. - Every `StrokePoint` field (pressure, tilt, rotation, wheel, time) is interpolated along the curve, so pressure dynamics and time-based behavior (speed spacing, airbrush build-up, smoothing) keep working. - Curve pieces are sampled into chords of about 2 px, capped at 64 per piece. - A stroke of two points stays one straight segment, as before…

title: fix(format): persist the Save As filename in .pcraft manifests (#3312)
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Fixes native .pcraft files retaining the previous document name after Save As.

Fixes #3312.

## Root Cause

The document is serialized before the session updates its name following a successful save.

As a result, the saved manifest contains the original filename even though the session displays the new one.

## Changes

- Create a temporary document snapshot with the destination filename before native serialization.
- Apply the correction to disk-based saves and byte encoding.
- Preserve the original document until the write succeeds.
- Leave unrelated export formats unchanged.

## Tests

Added regression coverage for:
- Native Save As and reopening.
- Consecutive saves under different filenames.
- Saving back to an existing native file.
- Native byte encoding without modifying the source document.

Tests have not yet been executed.

title: fix(format): share identical tiles when loading .pcraft
author: predic8
body:
Fixes #3315.

`.pcraft` saves deduplicate tiles by content hash, but load decoded and charged each reference separately. Large solid documents failed with `LimitExceeded` on reopen, and smaller ones lost tile sharing (huge RAM use).

`Loader` now caches decoded tiles by (hash, pixel format) for the duration of a load. Repeated references reuse one `Arc<Tile>` without refetching, re-decompressing or re-charging `max_total_bytes`.

Test: `identical_tiles_are_loaded_once_and_shared` reloads 1600 references to one tile under an 8 MiB budget and checks they share one `Arc`. `cargo test -p photocraft-format`, clippy and `cargo xtask layers` pass.

author: LloydNicholson

title: Group effects follow their children's effects, not just their pixels (#3274)
author: alexanderalber
body:
Fixes #3274.

## Why
A group with an effect (e.g. Drop Shadow) around a layer with its own outside Stroke showed the stroke cut off at the child's pixel bounds on the canvas, and the group's shadow followed the cut shape. The exported PNG looked right.

The group's effect region (`compose::effect_region`, `gpu::bounds::effect_region`) and the empty-tile check (`compose::empty_in`) were computed from `layer_bounds`, which for a group is the union of its children's *pixels*. The children's own effect reach was missing, so everything past it was clipped: on the GPU by the effect passes' clip, on the CPU when rendering tiles away from the pixels (a whole-document render, as in export, happened to cover it).

## Change
- New `photocraft_compose::effect_source_bounds`: `layer_bounds`, except that a (non-artboard, non-shapeless) group's visible children count grown by their own effect margin, recursively.
- Used by `compose::effect_region`, `compose::empty_in` and `gpu::bounds::effect_region`. Other `layer_bounds` callers are unchanged (`composite_bounds` already includes child margins; the gradient/pattern frame `sb` stays on the pixels).

## Tests
- New `group_effects_reach_past_children_effects` (compose): a 6 px outside stroke on a child, a 2 px drop shadow on its group; 1×1 renders check the stroke left of and below the pixels, the shadow below the stroke, and white past it. Fails without the fix.
- New case in `layer_effects_on_groups_clipping_and_fills` (gpu parity): a child with an 8 px stroke in a group with a drop shadow. With only the GPU half of the fix reverted it fails (max diff 41.99/255); with the fix it passes. Run on an RTX 3090, so the GPU path really executed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --lib --tests`: all passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`: clean.
- `cargo xtask test-corpus`: 2680 passed, 0 failed, 24 igno…

title: Color panel: HSB on sRGB values, like Photoshop (#3323)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Closes #3323.

The Color panel converted the foreground to and from hue, saturation and brightness with egui's `ecolor::Hsva`, which works in **linear light**. Photoshop's HSB works on the sRGB-encoded values, and so does PhotoCraft's own Color Picker dialog. As a result, in the panel:
- the colour field's left edge halfway down was drawn as **188** grey, not 128, which is what the issue reports;
- a 50% grey (128) read as about **22%** Brightness on the HSB sliders, where Photoshop shows 50%.

### Changes (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`)
- `srgb_hsva` and `hsva_srgb` now use the Color Picker's `rgb_to_hsv` and `hsv_to_rgb`, so the panel and the dialog give the same numbers for the same colour.
- A new helper, `hsva_color32`, does the drawing. The colour field, the hue strip, the HSB slider tracks, the swatch and the stored-HSB check all use it instead of `Color32::from(Hsva)` and `Hsva::to_srgb`. `Hsva` is now only a container for the four numbers.

Picking in the field already used the same HSB as the drawing, so what you click and what you see still agree. Both now follow Photoshop's sRGB HSB.

### Testing
- New test `panels::color_tests::color_panel_hsb_is_srgb_like_photoshop`:
  - grey 128 has Brightness 50%;
  - HSB with S 0% and B 50% gives sRGB 0.5, and the field paints it as `Color32::from_gray(128)`;
  - a saturated colour gets the same H, S and B as the Color Picker dialog.
- It fails without the change; the grey's Brightness came out at about 0.22.
- The existing round-trip test `srgb_hsva_roundtrip` still passes.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`: 1932 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` are clean.

#3228 (the field's knob jumping at the bottom-right corner) touches the same function. It's a separate fix that someone else has claimed, and this PR doesn't change the knob.

title: Moving a shape keeps its rendering: Artboards to Files matches Photoshop
author: fabianghe
body:
Follow-up to #3218, which fixes the same problem for type. This one is for shape layers.

## What happens
`vector_cmds::translate_vectors` **re-renders a shape layer on every move**. For a shape from a PSD, this replaces Photoshop's anti-aliasing with PhotoCraft's own. The same path runs for:
- File › Export › **Artboards to Files**, which moves each board to the origin;
- the Move tool commit (`move_layers`) and arrow nudges;
- applying a layer comp's position;
- moving artboards;
- copying layers.

**Found with:** a real Steam store asset template (a free PSD from Noblesteed Games). With #3218 applied, every remaining difference between PhotoCraft's "How to use this template" artboard and Photoshop's own composite was inside its two shape layers, a rounded rectangle and an ellipse.

## The fix
- A whole-pixel move now **shifts the rendered pixels**, through one `vector_cmds::shift_shape` helper.
- `layer_multi_cmds::shift_shown` (the Move tool's live preview) already did this. It now calls the same helper, so the preview and the committed move always agree.
- Rules kept from that preview code:
  - The render is cut at the canvas, so a shape reaching past it still renders again. So does a fractional move.
  - The path moves either way, so PSD export writes the new position: `psd_raw` is only reused while it still decodes to the path.
  - `fit_canvas` still re-renders shapes when an artboard move grows the canvas (#2389 / #2623). Its test passes unchanged.

## Measured on the template (with #3218)
The "How to use" artboard has **no pixel off by more than 2 levels** (out of 255) from Photoshop's composite. Before, both shape layers differed, with pixels up to 83 levels off at their edges.

## Tests
New tests in `engine/src/vector_cmds/tests.rs`. They are kept out of `artboard_cmds/tests.rs` so this PR and #3218 don't conflict.
- `moving_and_exporting_imported_shapes_keeps_their_rendering` (8, 16 and 32 bit). The test uses a shape whose cache is deliberately not what …

title: Let `[` shrink the brush to 1 px (#3229)
author: myangaa1
body:
Fixes #3229.

`[` steps the brush size down by 25 %, rounded: from 2 px that is 1.6, which rounds back to 2, so the key never reached 1 px and pixel artists had to type the size in the brush settings. `]` already grows by at least a pixel (`.max(size + 1.0)`); `[` now shrinks by at least a pixel the same way (`.min(size - 1.0)`), still clamped to 1 px.

One line in `size_step` (`crates/engine/src/brush_key_cmds.rs`). Both `[` paths (the UI shortcut and the `tools.decreaseBrushSize` command) go through it.

Tests: `size_step(2.0, false) == 1.0`, every size from 2 up shrinks on `[` and grows on `]`, and the command test walks 3 → 2 → 1 → 1.

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` (1214 passed) and `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` pass.

title: MCP: command_batch says it is not atomic, and the docs explain recovery
author: KnottyDyes
body:
Agents read the `command_batch` tool description rather than `docs/mcp.md`, and the description only said the batch stops at the first error. An agent can take that for a rollback.

- The description says the steps run in order and that earlier successful steps stay applied: it is not an atomic transaction and nothing is rolled back.
- `docs/mcp.md` gives the `stop_on_error` default and a recovery recipe: inspect with `doc_inspect`, undo with `edit.undo` once per history entry (undo does not reverse files written to disk), or experiment on a copy made with `image.duplicate` or `history.newDocument`.
- A test checks the listed description.

title: Format: reopening a .pcraft shares deduplicated tiles again (#3315)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3315

## Root cause
Saves deduplicate tiles by content hash: a solid fill shares one `Arc<Tile>`, so a white 300000² canvas stores a single tile. The loader did not do the same in reverse. `Loader::surface` (crates/format/src/convert.rs) called `LoadFetch::tile` (crates/format/src/store.rs) once per tile *reference*. Each call decompressed the tile, re-checked its hash, charged `max_total_bytes` again, and copied the bytes into a fresh tile at that coordinate. As a result:
- A solid canvas above about 65536² (8-bit), 46341² (16-bit) or 32768² (32f) saved fine, but reopening it failed with `LimitExceeded("bundle expands beyond 17179869184 bytes")`.
- Smaller canvases reopened but lost the sharing. A solid 30000² 32-bit document grew from about 1 MB to about 14 GB in memory.

## Fix
During a load, `Loader` now keeps the tiles it has already decoded, keyed by sample type and content hash. Each distinct tile is decompressed, hash-checked and charged against the budget once. Every later reference gets the same copy-on-write `Arc<Tile>` through `Surface::put_tiles`, so the reopened document keeps the sharing the save had. An edit splits the tile off as usual (`Arc::make_mut`).

Hostile-input protections are unchanged:
- `max_total_bytes` still bounds the distinct decoded bytes.
- An extra reference costs one map lookup and one `Arc` clone. The number of references is bounded by `max_manifest_bytes`, as before.
- Invalid hashes still fail in `LoadFetch::tile`. The cache only holds tiles that were verified.
- If a cached hash is referenced again with a different tile length, the load fails as corrupt instead of putting a wrong-sized tile into the surface.
- Duplicate-coordinate and coordinate-range checks run before the cache lookup, as before.

## Tests
- `roundtrip::solid_fill_reopens_with_one_shared_tile`: a solid 2048² RGB document at 8, 16 and 32-bit saves and reopens with a budget of one tile. The reopened document equals the original, and all 64 tiles are one …

title: Color panel: HSB over the encoded values, not linear light (#3323)
author: myangaa1
body:
Fixes #3323.

The Color panel's field, hue strip and Hue/Saturation/Brightness sliders used egui's `Hsva`, which is HSV over *linear* RGB. Half-way down the field, and at 50 % brightness, that is linear 0.5 = sRGB 188, a light grey, where Photoshop (and PhotoCraft's own Color Picker dialog) show 128. Grey 128 read back as 21 % brightness in the sliders.

The panel now keeps HSB over the sRGB-encoded components (a small `Hsb` in `panels.rs`, built on the dialog's `rgb_to_hsv` / `hsv_to_rgb`), so the panel and the dialog agree: the midpoint is 128, 50 % is 50 %, and the field and sliders shade evenly. The hex/RGB readout and the remembered hue for greys work as before.

Before / after (Pro theme, foreground red; snapshot example, measured along the field's left edge): the grey ramp was 253 → 144 over the visible field and 208 at its middle; it is now a straight 250 → 0 ramp with 128 at the middle.

Tests: `srgb_hsb_roundtrip` and `color_panel_hsb_is_in_gamma_space` (grey 128 ⇄ B 50 %, (255, 128, 0) ⇄ H 30° S 100 % B 100 %, and the panel equals the dialog). `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests` (1850 passed) pass.

Not changed: `widgets::hue_stops()` (the hue slider tracks shared with Hue/Saturation, Camera Raw and the brush Hue Jitter slider) still mixes in linear light; it only affects the look of those tracks, not any value, so I left it for a separate change if wanted.

title: Type: free Warp, Distort and Perspective on live type, which stays editable (#3321)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3321. Depends on #3008 (stacked on it: the first commit here is #3008's branch; review the last commit).

## Better Than PS
Photoshop limits live type:
- Edit › Transform › Warp takes only the warp styles (Warp Text).
- Distort, Perspective and the split warps are greyed until the type is rasterized, and then the text can no longer be edited.

PhotoCraft now keeps all of them on the live type layer as non-destructive transforms. The text stays editable.

## What changed
- **doc**: `TextLayer.distortions: Vec<TypeDistortion>`. Each entry is a custom `Warp` (the same mesh model as `edit.transform.warp` and smart-object warps) or a projective 3×3 map (Distort / Perspective).
  - Each one is stored in the document space it was made in: `frame` = the layer's `transform` at that moment.
  - So a later move, scale, rotate, Image Size or crop carries it along exactly.
  - `is_valid()` checks for finite values, an invertible frame and a well-formed mesh capped at 193×193 points. There are at most 16 distortions per layer.
- **text**: the renderer bends the glyph outlines through Warp Text, then the distortions. This works on vectors, by subdividing segments (no resampling).
  - Bounds follow automatically, since the cache is the rendered result. The CPU and GPU compositors, thumbnails, Rasterize, Create Work Path and Convert to Shape all see it.
  - Editing the text re-renders under the same transform. A custom warp continues outside its box, so longer text doesn't collapse at the edge.
- **engine** (new `type_distort.rs`):
  - `edit.transform.warp` on a type layer:
    - With no free transform yet, a style (or none) is the Warp Text, as in #3008. A custom mesh replaces the Warp Text.
    - Otherwise the warp replaces the trailing free warp (none removes it), or goes on top of a trailing Distort.
  - `edit.transform` with a non-affine `quad` on type pushes a projective map. It is merged into a trailing one, which is exact.

title: fix(presets): never overwrite preset or actions files that failed to load
author: tms-h
body:
## Summary

Keep brush preset group files and `actions.json` intact when they fail to load, instead of overwriting them on the next save.

## Problem

When a brush group file can't be loaded, the preset store skips it with a warning. That happens when the file is corrupt, written by a newer version (`version != 1`), or has missing tips. The comment at the skip says the file is "left on disk untouched".

But the next sync writes the group's file name again, with only the presets currently in memory. Saving a single new brush therefore replaces the whole skipped file, and every preset in it is lost. For example, a user who downgrades PhotoCraft loses their ungrouped presets on the next brush save.

`actions.json` has the same behaviour. A file that fails to load (corrupt, too large, or an unsupported version) loads as an empty list, and the next action change rewrites it with only the new actions.

## Root Cause

- `open` drops a group file that fails to parse or has missing tips (`preset_store.rs:617`, `:668`) without remembering it. `sync` then sees no loaded entry for `group_file_name(group)` and calls `write_group` (`:867`).
- `load_actions` (`:695`) returns the same empty list for "unreadable" as for "no file", so `sync_actions` (`:1012`) can't tell them apart.

## Changes

- Record the names of group files skipped at load. `sync` leaves those files unchanged and adds a warning instead of writing them.
- `load_actions` returns `None` when `actions.json` exists but couldn't be loaded. A missing file still means an empty list, as on a first launch. `sync_actions` then leaves the file unchanged and adds a warning.
- Two regression tests on `MemBackend`, one per file type. Each seeds a `version: 2` file, saves a brush or records an action, and checks that the file is byte-for-byte unchanged and a warning was raised.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib preset_store`: all pass. Each new test fails with its fix reverted and passes with it.

title: Tests: bad-layer-id checks use an id that can't exist (#3343)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3343

## Root cause
Layer ids come from one process-wide counter (`NEXT_ID` in `crates/doc/src/lib.rs`). `LayerId`, `DocId` and `SmartContentsId` all draw from it, and `ensure_ids_above` raises it whenever a test loads a file. A full `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` runs about 1,200 tests in one process, so the counter passes 9999. Many "no such layer" checks used small sentinels (`"layer": 9999`, `999_999`, `99_999`, `LayerId(9999)`, `"reference": 9999`, `"to": 9999` …). When a layer that the test itself just created gets that id, the command succeeds and the `is_err()` assertion fails. Which test gets the id depends on thread scheduling, so CI fails at random. This is the failure in `type_extra_cmds::tests::vertical_orientation_renders_columns_inside_the_canvas` (tests.rs:112).

I confirmed it locally with a throwaway test (not committed): after `photocraft_doc::ensure_ids_above(9998)`, the next `type.create` gets layer id 9999, and `type.orientation.vertical {"layer": 9999}` then returns `Ok`.

## What changed
This is a test-only change. Every bad-layer-id sentinel in the `photocraft-engine` tests (lib and `tests/`) and the `photocraft-ui-egui` lib tests is now `u64::MAX`, which the counter never reaches. That's 28 files. Commands read the id with `as_u64`, so `u64::MAX` still reaches the lookup and fails with `no such layer LayerId(18446744073709551615)`, not with a parameter error. I checked the error text for the affected commands with a throwaway test. The adversarial `panic_hunt` params are unchanged, because they don't assert `Err`. Document indices, job ids and style indices are not drawn from this counter, so they stay as they are.

## Commands
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --lib`: 1219 passed, 12 ignored
- `cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-engine --test eraser_locked --test rasterize_selected_layers --test selection_layer_commands`

title: CR2: decode Canon sRAW/mRAW (subsampled lossless JPEG small/medium raw)
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Canon sRAW1/sRAW2/mRAW open now instead of refusing: `09.canon.sraw1.cr2` from raw.pixls.us develops into its 3872×2574 image where it previously fell back to the embedded JPEG preview with "Canon sRAW / mRAW is not supported yet".

**What the files are:** a lossless JPEG whose first component samples at 2×2 (sRAW1/mRAW) or 2×1 (sRAW2) with 1×1 chroma — a subsampled MCU of 4 or 2 luma values plus centred Cb/Cr, decoded through a chain predictor (the luma samples chain through each other, all sharing the luma Huffman table; dcraw's assignment).

**The decode** (`ljpeg::decode_sraw` + the sRAW branch of the CR2 reader, clean-room from the public lossless-JPEG spec and dcraw's published algorithm):
- MCU-interleaved lossless scan with the chaining predictor and per-component restart semantics,
- luma placement per 2×2/2×1 block, Cb/Cr centred at 1<<14 shared per block,
- chroma upsampling the way dcraw does it (odd rows then odd columns average their neighbours, +1 >> 1; the last row/column replicate),
- Canon's fixed YCbCr→RGB matrices per body generation, with the firmware-version hue rule (MakerNote 0x0007 `Firmware Version 2.1.2`, dcraw's `ver > 1.0.0.6` check for the 5D Mark II),
- the per-file `sraw_mul` scale record from the ColourData block (dcraw's walk off the white balance, G == 1170),
- the 16-bit difference category fixed at **−32768** per T.81 H.1.2.2 — our reader had **+32768**, which no CFA file ever hit.

The sensor is 3-sample linear RGB (no CFA), white 16383, and the file's as-shot white balance applies as with the CFA path.

**Verification:** pixel-exact against an instrumented dcraw (public-domain reference) — the first six converted RGB values of the 5D Mark II sRAW1 file match bit for bit: (497,704,190), (496,702,193), (484,683,186), (480,676,187), (488,688,191), (492,694,193). title: CMYK documents keep their inks: export, PSD merged image and Flatten (#2220)
author: SBaksa
body:
Fixes #2220.

A CMYK document's composite went CMYK → RGB → CMYK through the profile: TIFF and JPEG exports came out as sRGB RGB (#2220), and even where the colour model survived, exact inks didn't. K-only black (C0 M0 Y0 K100) came back as four-colour black (about C18 M11 Y12 K91), which matters for print (K-only type and line art). The same loss happened in a CMYK PSD's merged image, and in Flatten Image, Merge/Stamp Visible and Copy Merged.

### What changes
- **TIFF/JPEG export** of a CMYK document is always CMYK with the document's own profile. TIFF keeps transparency; JPEG is composited over blank paper.
- **`compose::cmyk`** (new) mixes the layers on their ink values wherever the stack allows, so opaque pixels keep their exact inks:
  - **Content:** pixel, type, shape and smart object layers; solid and gradient fills (through #2628's `render_cmyk_fill`); masks; isolated and pass-through groups; clipping groups; knockouts.
  - **Blend modes:** every separable mode, applied to each ink's brightness as the RGB compositor applies it per channel. That includes #2552's Fill rule for the special eight and Dissolve's noise.
  - **Adjustments:** Invert, Posterize, and Levels/Curves recorded on the CMYK channels.
  - **Layer effects:** shadows, glows, strokes, colour and gradient overlays, satin, and bevel without texture. These run through the existing compositor on two stand-in RGB documents whose channels hold the brightness of C, M and Y, then of K. That is exact because everything allowed there works channel by channel, and a property test checks it: random effect stacks rendered with the inks in different channels must agree.
- **Fallback:** anything else keeps the RGB composite, converted back through the document's own profile, with a warning in the export result. That covers channel-mixing modes (Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity, Darker/Lighter Color), channel-mixing adjustments, pattern effects, effects on adjustment layers, Blend If, channel restrictions a…

title: fix(gpu): request CPU fallback for gradient stops closer than a LUT entry (#3053)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Closes #3053.

### Summary

The GPU compositor samples gradient ramps into a 4096-sample lookup table (LUT) and linearly interpolates adjacent entries. When gradient stops are closer than one LUT interval (`1.0 / 4095.0`, ~0.000244), linear interpolation cannot represent the steep transition without introducing significant error (up to 0.5 per RGB channel), exceeding the 1/255 CPU parity tolerance.

Previously, `check_gradient_stops` only caught strictly coincident stops (`w[0] == w[1]`).

This PR:
1. In `crates/gpu/src/plan.rs:check_gradient_stops`, checks whether adjacent stop positions are closer than `1.0 / 4095.0`, requesting fallback to the CPU compositor just like coincident stops.
2. Adds unit regression test `close_distinct_gradient_stops_request_cpu` in `crates/gpu/tests/parity.rs` verifying that close distinct stops (such as 0.4999 and 0.5 from #3053) request the CPU fallback and meet parity contracts.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity close_distinct_gradient_stops_request_cpu` (passed)
- `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity` (38/38 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean)
- `cargo xtask layers` (clean)

title: Window: a window saved while minimized reopens at the minimum size, not 160 × 64
author: KattKnight
body:
On Windows, PhotoCraft can reopen as a 160 × 64 strip on every launch.

**Cause.** eframe saves the window's size on exit. If the window is minimized at that moment, Windows
reports a 160-pt-wide window with almost no height, and eframe's own clamp only raises it to 64 pt.
On the next start eframe restores that size, and `with_min_inner_size(760 × 480)` isn't applied to a
restored window, so the window stays 160 × 64. It stays that way, because each exit saves the small
size again. Found while driving the app over the control channel: `ui.screenshot` and `ui.inspect`
both reported a 160 × 64 window, and `ui.ron` held `inner_size_points: (160, 64)`.

**Fix.** A `window_builder` hook (`at_least_min_size` in `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`) grows a
restored window that is smaller than the minimum size up to it, keeping its centre. A window at or
above the minimum, or a maximized one, is unchanged. The rest of `ui.ron` (panel layout) is kept,
unlike `ui_state::sanitize`, which removes files that would crash startup.

**Tests.**
- New `a_window_saved_while_minimized_reopens_at_the_minimum_size`: the saved 160 × 64 window opens
  at 760 × 480 and stays centred, a too-narrow window only grows wider, and normal sizes are unchanged.
- Live, with the broken `ui.ron`: before, 160 × 64 for the whole run; after, 760 × 480. Without a
  saved layout, 1440 × 900 as before.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft`, rustfmt: clean.

title: Copy takes every selected layer, Paste recreates them (#2478)
author: DomiLuebben
body:
Fixes #2478.

## Problem
With several layers selected and no pixel selection, Edit › Copy only copied the active layer's pixels, so Paste made one layer. Photoshop copies all selected layers and pastes them back as layers.

## Fix
`copy` in `crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs` now puts the selected layers on the session clipboard as whole layers: those that no selected group already carries (`layer_multi_cmds::top_level`), bottom-to-top, in a scratch document. `paste_layers` already recreates a list of layers (it loops over `copies.layers`), so Paste needed no change. The OS clipboard still gets the merged pixels, as for a group.

- A pixel selection keeps the old behaviour: the active layer's selected pixels, as one layer.
- A single selected layer behaves as before (`takes_whole` is untouched).
- The Background in the set pastes as an ordinary, unlocked layer, like Duplicate Layer makes it.
- `Copy` is enabled whenever several layers are selected, even if the active one is a group.

## Tests
`edit_cmds::tests::copy_and_paste_several_selected_layers` (both layers' bounds, order, one undo step, pixel selection still copies one layer) and `copying_the_background_with_another_layer_pastes_an_ordinary_layer`. Both fail without the change. `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib` passes (1234 tests) and `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. `cargo clippy -D warnings` on Rust 1.95 reports one `collapsible_match` in `color_to_alpha_cmds.rs`, which is on `main` already and not touched here.

Not covered: layers selected in different groups paste flat above the active layer, not back into their groups.

title: Content-Aware tools: faster, cancellable at once, same pixels (P21, P22, P49)
author: Unemars
body:
**TL;DR:** the Content-Aware tools from #2202 (Fill, Spot Healing, Patch, Content-Aware Move) get their time back without changing a pixel, and a cancelled 24 MP fill stops within tens of milliseconds. The P49 row, which #2575's nightly found over its 200 ms budget, fits again. It is also faster than main with #2805, which sped up the same onion peel and votes meanwhile.

**Problem.** #2202 made the fill match Photoshop's, and the new perf nightly (#2575) caught what it cost on a Ryzen 5 3600X:

| Scenario | Before → after #2202 (p50) | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| P21 Content-Aware Fill 10 MP | 105 → 537 ms (5.1×) | 1500 ms |
| P22 Spot Healing 10 MP | 54 → 130 ms (2.4×) | 500 ms |
| P49 Cancel Content-Aware Fill 24 MP (max) | 136 → 566 ms (4×) | **200 ms** |

**Why it was slow:**
- **Cancel (P49).** Long stretches of the 24 MP job never looked at the cancel flag: Auto sampling's min cut (~300 ms), the window copy and mosaic, the pyramid, the onion-peel initialisation and the colour-adaptation votes. Freeing full-size buffers (match field, costs, a 560 MB gain/bias buffer, two or three 280 MB window copies) added to the wait too, at about 80 µs per MB.
- **P21 / P22.** Colour adaptation (on by default since #2202) had no early out, the onion peel searched every source exhaustively, and PatchMatch kept only 2–7 threads busy on the small pyramid levels.

**Change.** Same algorithm, same floating-point order, so every result stays bit for bit what it is on main:
- **Solver bounds.** The solver works over the hole's bounds grown by a patch: match field, costs, votes and the per-target tables are kept only there, since nothing outside changes or is matched.
- **Votes.** A vote computes each target's weight and match centre once and writes into one buffer instead of a `Vec` per pixel. It walks only the offsets inside the image, with the channel count and colour adaptation fixed at compile time. The sums and their order are unchanged.
- **Colour adaptation.** It reuses each p…

title: Linux: say so when no file dialog can open (#3354); read ldconfig on non-English systems
author: DomiLuebben
body:
Refs #3354 (does not fix the reporter's environment, but makes the failure visible).

## 1. No file dialog: tell the user instead of doing nothing
`rfd` opens the XDG file chooser portal through `libdbus-1` (loaded at run time) and falls back to `zenity`. When neither works, for example in a minimal labwc/Void session without a portal backend, it only logs the failure and answers "nothing picked". The app took that for Cancel, so File › Open / Save / Export did nothing and said nothing.

- `apps/photocraft/src/file_dialog_probe.rs` looks once, on a background thread at start-up, for the three pieces: `libdbus-1.so.3` in the linker cache, the portal's `FileChooser` interface on the session bus (a `version` property read, 5 s timeout), and `zenity` on `PATH`.
- When a dialog comes back empty and none of them is there, the shell answers with the new `FileDialogAnswer::Unavailable(message)`. `ask_file` turns that into an error, so the status bar says what to install (xdg-desktop-portal with a backend, libdbus, or zenity) and suggests dropping or pasting a file meanwhile.
- The probe only explains an empty answer; it never blocks a dialog. Anything it can't tell counts as present, so a system where dialogs work never sees the message. Linux only; other platforms compile an empty `start()`.

## 2. `ldconfig -p` was unreadable on non-English systems
`linux_libs::read_ldconfig` accepted the listing only if its first line contained "libs found in cache". On a German system the header is "5522 Bibliotheken im Cache … gefunden", so the cache counted as unreadable and the start-up library check silently fell back to a directory search. `ldconfig` now runs with `LC_ALL=C`, and any listing that starts with a count is accepted. The probe above reads the same cache.

## Tests
- `file_dialog_probe`: no message when a portal, zenity or an unknown answer is present; messages for a missing portal and for missing libdbus; `PATH` lookup.
- `file_dialog::tests::an_unavailable_dialog_is_re…

title: feat(api): add file path to document.inspect
author: Mr-Pearce
body:
This PR adds the active document's absolute file path to the JSON response of the `document.inspect` engine command.

Motivation
Currently, external tools interacting with the engine via JSON-RPC receive the document's name, but not its location on disk. Exposing `DocState.path` is highly beneficial for automation workflows and RPC clients.

As a concrete use case: I am using this to build an external tool that listens to file saves, triggers headless .tga exports via photocraft-cli, and automatically routes the updated color and spec-map textures directly into a local game directory (e.g., iRacing's paint folder) for instant 3D rendering updates. Knowing the active document's path is strictly required to resolve relative exports or match the file watcher events.

Changes

Mapped doc.path to the `"path"` field in the inspect::document JSON output (crates/engine/src/inspect.rs).

Updated the info helper in `apps/photocraft-cli/tests/orientation.rs` to strip the `"path"` field prior to structural equality assertions, as the round-trip test saves temporary documents to distinct paths.

title: feat(ui): Motion Blur and other filter angles get the angle dial (#3152)
author: Kartik8Dwivedi
body:
## Summary
Motion Blur's Angle is now a dial you can click or drag, with a degree field next to it, as in Photoshop. Drop Shadow already had this dial; it is now a shared widget, and the filter dialog uses it for the other direction angles too.

## Root cause
`filter_dialog::body` drew every numeric range param with `widgets::slider_row`, so the angle was a straight slider. The only dial was private to `layer_style.rs` and fixed to -180..180.

## What changed
- New `widgets::angle_dial_row(ui, label, &mut angle, range)` in `widgets/angle_dial.rs`, moved out of `layer_style::angle_row`:
  - The dial points within -180..180, and its result is clamped to the param's range. The field accepts the whole range, so Motion Blur keeps a 270° value.
  - The field is the dialogs' `value_field`, so Angle gets the opening focus with its text selected (#1757), plus Tab order and arrow steps.
  - Arrow keys on the focused dial wrap round only when the range is the dial's own -180..180 (Drop Shadow). On a wider range they step on, so 270° goes to 271°, not -89°.
  - Clamping uses `max`/`min`, not `f32::clamp`, so a malformed (reversed) range cannot panic.
- Layer Style (Drop Shadow and the other effects) uses the shared widget with -180..180.
- The filter dialog uses the dial for direction angles measured counter-clockwise from three o'clock, the dial's convention (checked against each algorithm): Motion Blur, Emboss, Oil Paint, Lighting Effects, Relight and Global Light.
- These keep the slider:
  - Twirl, Rotate Arbitrary, Crop, Lens Correction and the Blur Gallery filters, whose angle is an amount of rotation;
  - Flame, whose 0° points up.

## Tests
- `dialogs::tests::motion_blur_angle_dial_sets_the_angle_by_click_and_drag` (kittest, real dialog) checks:
  - the Angle field opens focused;
  - a click above the centre gives 90°;

title: feat: add SVG Paste As and external smart-object editing
author: Skyfuller1303

Copying SVG from VectorCraft previously entered PhotoCraft through the bitmap clipboard path. This adds a Windows Paste As dialog with Layers, Smart Object, Pixels, Path, and Shape Layer, then supports editing an embedded SVG Smart Object in VectorCraft, Illustrator, or an explicitly selected executable.

Confirmation executes `edit.pasteVector` as one undoable edit; cancel makes no edit. Layer > Smart Objects > Edit Contents opens an editor chooser for embedded SVG. Stable saved snapshots are read on a background worker, then validated and applied through `layer.smartObjects.updateSvg`. Document ID, layer, shared contents ID, and expected source fingerprint bind each update to its original target. All shared instances update atomically in one undo step; placement, perspective/warp, filters and masks remain intact. Source stays SVG through `.pcraft` save/reload. Unchanged saves add no history, and deleting the last object produces transparent contents.

title: Make magnetic lasso edge direction polarity-independent
author: imSlicedBread
body:
Fixes #3337.

The live-wire cost treated edge tangents as directed vectors. When the strongest image channel changes and reverses the gradient, the same straight edge receives a high direction penalty, which can pull the Magnetic Lasso off the boundary.

Compare tangents as unoriented axes so either gradient polarity follows the same edge. Add unit and synthetic-image regressions for a high-contrast contour crossing a polarity change.

title: Actions: replay tests for crop, filters, selections and styled text on a second document (#3410)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3410 (scorecard AUTO-219-4, part of #219)

## What was missing
Action replay was only tested for new layer + rect select + fill and for an explicit transform. Nothing checked that a recorded crop, filter, selection sequence or styled type layer replays on a second document with the same result.

## Change
Tests only, in a new file `crates/engine/tests/action_replay.rs` (`actions_cmds.rs` is untouched, since several open PRs change it). Each case builds three identical documents: a gradient background plus a layer with two rectangles. It records on A, plays on B and runs the same commands directly on C. Each test then checks:
- B == C and A == C: canvas size, every layer compared in full (pixels, style, type content and its rendered cache) and the selection mask. Layer ids are left out because they are counted across the whole session.
- `failed` is absent, `ran` equals the number of steps, and history grows by one step per played step.
- The result differs from the untouched document, so a test can't pass without doing anything.

Cases, each at 8/16/32-bit:
- `replayed_crop_matches_direct_crop_at_each_depth`: `image.crop`
- `replayed_gaussian_blur_matches_direct_blur_at_each_depth`: `filter.blur.gaussianBlur` radius 3.5
- `replayed_selection_operations_and_fill_match_direct_at_each_depth`: elliptical `select.rect`, add, subtract, `select.modify.feather`, `select.inverse`, `edit.fill`
- `replayed_styled_type_layer_matches_direct_at_each_depth`: `type.create` with font, size, colour, tracking, underline and name

author: guoyinchen

title: Properties: a new adjustment or fill layer shows its settings, not its mask (#3369)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3369.

**Why:** In Photoshop, a new adjustment or fill layer targets its layer mask, so painting edits the mask right away. The Properties panel still shows the layer's own settings, such as the Curves graph. It switches to the mask controls only when you click the mask thumbnail. PhotoCraft targeted the mask correctly (#2166), but Properties then showed Density/Feather, so you had to click the layer before you could edit the adjustment you had just made.

**Change**
- New UI state `properties_layer` (serde, readable over the control channel): the adjustment or fill layer whose settings Properties shows even though its mask is targeted.
- It is set when `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.*` / `layer.newFillLayer.*` succeeds. The mask stays targeted, so painting, Invert and Delete still act on the mask.
- It is cleared when you click the mask thumbnail, target the pixels, select another layer or set `ui.set {maskTarget}`. Properties then shows the mask controls again.
- The single check sits in `mask_props_ui::targeted()`, which both Properties views use: docked (Pro) and floating (Studio).

**Tests**
- New kittest test `a_new_adjustment_or_fill_layer_shows_its_settings_until_the_mask_thumbnail_is_clicked` (Curves and Solid Color), with real clicks:
  - after creation, the mask is targeted and Properties shows the settings;
  - a row click keeps the settings view;
  - clicking the mask thumbnail shows Density.
  - It fails without the fix.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib`: 1920 passed. One type-tool test (`options_font_family_preserves_peer_faces_and_batches_layer_flags`) failed once while the machine was under load; it passed on reruns and passes on main.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

**Not verified**
- Not checked visually in the running app.
- The Studio floating Properties is covered only through the shared `targeted()` path.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across PhotoCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for PhotoCraft.

title: Fix Color Balance tonal ranges and slider axes
author: imSlicedBread
body:
Fixes #3423.

Color Balance sliders represent the Cyan–Red, Magenta–Green, and Yellow–Blue axes. The CPU and GPU paths treated them as independent RGB offsets, and the tonal masks used encoded-value Rec.601 luma. This made an sRGB gray value of 128 fall outside the Shadows range.

Use document-decoded linear Rec.709 luminance for the tonal masks, map each slider to its RGB opponent axis, and keep the CPU and GPU implementations aligned. A regression test covers the reported Shadow adjustment on neutral gray with Preserve Luminosity both enabled and disabled.

I reproduced the reported adjustment in Photopea on neutral 8-bit sRGB gray; PhotoCraft’s previous shadow mask left the pixel unchanged.

Checks:
- cargo test -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu
- cargo clippy -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo fmt -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu -- --check
- cargo xtask layers
- cargo xtask wasm

Contributor credit: @imSlicedBread.

title: File > Save As / Save a Copy / CLI can write PDF (#3401)
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #3401 (the Save As side; PDF read stays tracked by #2541).

## What changed
- **The PDF writer moved below the seam.** The print path's one-page writer (Flate image XObject, ICCBased profile, marks, text) was engine-local and unreachable from the export dispatch, so it now lives in `crates/io/src/pdf.rs` (L4). `print_cmds` re-exports the same names — behaviour is byte-identical, and the whole print suite still passes unchanged.
- **New `pdf::export`**: the document flattened to one page — RGB, Grayscale or CMYK at 8 bits, composited over paper white (zero ink for CMYK), the embedded ICC profile travelling as an ICCBased colour space, page size = pixels × 72 ÷ document resolution (so a 300 ppi 3000×2000 doc prints as 10×6.67 in). Anything the format can't hold is a warning, not a silent loss.
- **One dispatch point**: because Save As, Save a Copy, `file.export`, Export As and the CLI's convert/batch all route through `photocraft_io::export` by extension, a `.pdf` name now just works everywhere: desktop, control channel, MCP, actions and `photocraft-cli`. PDF joined the Save As filter list after PSD (second, as Photoshop's own dialog ranks it).

## Refusal paths (Rule 9)
Lab/Indexed/other modes → `convert … to RGB first (Image > Mode)`; zero-sized documents → an actionable error; bad `ExportOptions` are ignored, not panicked on. `panic_hunt` untouched (no new command ids; the dispatch change is additive).

## Tests
Six new io tests: a structural oracle (startxref → the xref table; every recorded offset really precedes its `n 0 obj`), inflate-and-compare pixel content (white paper, a 50% red-over-white blend, per-mode channel counts), dpi → MediaBox maths, ICC bytes round-tripping through the profile object, and refusal of other modes through both `pdf::export` and the general dispatch.

`cargo test -p photocraft-io` (134) · engine lib (1244) · ui-egui lib (1926) · app crate · clippy `-D warnings` · fmt · `xtask layers` · `xtask wasm` — all green.

title: PSD gradients: read the interpolation method Photoshop writes; add Smooth
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Gradient fills and gradient effects read their interpolation method from `gs99`, a key Photoshop doesn't write. Photoshop 27.11 stores it as the enum **`gradientsInterpolationMethod`** (`Perc`, `Lnr `, `Smoo`, `Gcls`), so **every Perceptual, Linear or Smooth gradient opened as Classic**. No file in the corpus contains `gs99`, while 14 files contain `gradientsInterpolationMethod`.

It shows once a gradient fill is re-rendered (any edit). Measured on gradient fill layers saved by scripted Photoshop 27.11, against Photoshop's own composite in each file, after changing the fill's angle:

| Method | `main` (max error) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Classic | 1 | 1 |
| Perceptual | 31 | 1 |
| Linear | 74 | 1 |
| Smooth | 30 | 2 (two stops) |

Smooth, Photoshop's default method since 2024 (also Gradient Map's default), had no model at all.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: two-stop gradients on three colour pairs, sampled every 4–8 px, plus three- and four-stop gradients.
- **Perceptual, Linear, Classic:** the existing `gradient_bake` model is right once the method is read.
- **Smooth:** runs straight across each segment in Oklab with its own easing. The curve is the same for every colour pair, and Smoothness doesn't change it. It fits no simple formula, so it's kept as a measured 17-point table (`SMOOTH_EASE`).
- Midpoints: Photoshop applies `Clrs[i].Mdpn` to the segment **ending** at stop `i`. PhotoCraft already reads them that way.

## Change
- `io::blocks::gradient_method`: reads `gradientsInterpolationMethod`, with `gs99` kept as a fallback; used by gradient fills and gradient effects.
- `io::gradient_bake`: a `Smooth` method (`Smoo`), interpolating in Oklab with the measured easing.

title: Color Balance: Photoshop's per-channel levels and gamma curves
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Color Balance added a share of each slider, weighted by the pixel's lightness, and then (with Preserve Luminosity) rescaled to the old luma. That isn't what Photoshop does. On the corpus's Photoshop-made file `photoshop/adjustments/rgb8/color-balance.psd` (all three tones moved, Preserve Luminosity on), `main` is up to **43 levels off on 99% of the pixels**.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: a gray ramp and 16 pure colours through each slider at ±25, ±50 and ±100, with Preserve Luminosity on and off, plus two and three tones and two sliders at once (86 cases). Every slider is a **levels-and-gamma curve on each channel**:

- **Preserve Luminosity off:** a slider moves only its own channel. Midtones is gamma 2^−a. Shadows is gamma 2^(−a/2), after a black point at 0.39·|a| when lowered. Highlights is gamma 2^(−a/2), after a white point at 1 − 0.39·a when raised.
- **Preserve Luminosity on:** midtones is gamma 2^(−a/2) on the slider's channel and 2^(a/2) on the other two. Shadows and highlights go by the *differences* between a tone's sliders: each channel gets a black point at 0.39·(max − own) for shadows and a white point at 1 − 0.39·(own − min) for highlights.
- **Order:** highlights, then shadows, then midtones.

(`a` = slider / 100. Shadows −100 maps 99.6 of 255 to black, and highlights +100 maps 155.5 to white, hence 0.39.)

## Results

| | measured cases within 1 level | worst | corpus file: worst / mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 0 / 86 | 128 | 43 / 20.9 |
| #3434 | 0 / 86 | 150 | 54 / 24.6 |
| **this PR** | **85 / 86** | 9 | **4 / 1.4** |

#3434 (opened today) fixes the same issue a different way: linear-light tonal masks, checked against Photopea. I ran its branch through the same Photoshop measurements so the two can be compared directly. The one case here off by more than 1 is midtones +100 below about 28 of 255, where Photoshop flattens the steepest gamma near black (up to 9 levels).

title: Warp presets: Photoshop's Bezier control grids instead of approximations
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

The 15 warp presets (Edit › Transform › Warp, smart object warps, **Warp Text**) were closed-form approximations of each style's look, and up to **70 px off** Photoshop's. For example:
- **Arc** kept its centre fixed and pulled the ends in. Photoshop keeps the inner edge's corners and raises the middle.
- **Flag** waved the opposite way, at about a third of the height.
- **Squeeze** shrank the height. Photoshop pinches the sides in.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted renders on Photoshop 27.11 of a grid image whose colours encode each pixel's own position, 102 cases: every preset at bend ±50 and ±100, both distortions, vertical orientation, and square, wide (256×96) and tall (96×256) boxes. **Every preset is a single bicubic Bezier patch** (least-squares fits land within 0.5 px), with this control grid:
- **Arc:** each row is a circular arc of b·π around one centre, and the inner edge keeps its chord. **Arch, Bulge, Arc Lower/Upper and Shell** are built from the same arcs. The arcs stay circular in pixels on any box.
- **Flag, Wave, Fish, Rise, Fisheye, Inflate, Squeeze, Twist:** control points move linearly with the bend, in box units.
- **Distortion:** vertical scales the top and bottom rows about their midpoints and blends the rows between; horizontal scales each column. **Vertical orientation** swaps the axes and the two distortions.

## Results
- All 102 cases land within **1 px (median)** of Photoshop's pixels (95th percentile ≤ 2 px).

title: Crop tool: switching to another tool commits the pending crop (#3368)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3368.

**Why.** With an edited Crop frame, picking another tool (from the toolbar or by its key) left the crop pending and never applied it. In Photoshop, switching to another tool commits the crop silently. An untouched default frame is just dropped.

**Change.**
- `crop_ui::frame()` is the per-frame crop sync that every tool switch passes through (toolbar, shortcut keys, tool presets, control channel). It now commits an edited frame through the existing `canvas::commit_crop`, the same path as ↵, once the current tool is no longer Crop.
- It commits with the tool briefly set back to Crop, so the default mode leaves the view upright after a turned crop.
- The untouched default frame (canvas or selection bounds) is still dropped. The frame stays pending while a crop gesture is in progress, or while the pen's eraser end stands in for the Crop tool.
- Held tools (Space, Ctrl/Cmd) never change the current tool, so they don't commit.

title: Automation: --font-dir and type.registerFonts for headless sessions (#3393)
author: funkvay-star
body:
Fixes #3393

Headless sessions could only use bundled and installed fonts. This adds two ways to load fonts from a file or folder:

- `--font-dir <dir|file>` (repeatable) on `convert`, `info`, `run`, `batch`, `serve` and `mcp`: trusted launch configuration, loaded before anything opens so PSD font matching sees it.
- `type.registerFonts {path}` → `{families, files, skipped}`. Over `serve` and headless MCP the path resolves under `--automation-read-root`.

Fonts go into the process-wide text engine, so `type.fonts`, type layers and PSD import in every session of the process see them.

### What changed
- **text**: `FontDb::register_font_path` (file, or folder 8 levels deep) and `register_font_files` (bytes already read). Limits: 256 MiB per file, 4096 files, 1 GiB total, checked before reading. Bad files are skipped and reported; registering the same file twice adds no faces; WOFF/WOFF2 get a clear error.
- **engine**: `font_cmds.rs` with `type.registerFonts`. No menu, no history step, not recorded in Actions (`journal: false`, like `type.fonts`).
- **automation**: `AuthorizedWorkspace::read_font_files` walks the read root through cap-std (links can't escape) with a running byte total. Errors name the client's path, never the host root. Still refused inside `actions.play` steps and on the desktop control channel.
- **cli**: `--font-dir` on six subcommands. Missing paths or font-less folders exit 1; skipped files are `warning:` lines on stderr, so stdout stays clean; refused with `mcp --bridge`.
- **testkit**: `fonts::renamed_font(family)` renames the bundled Inter at test time, so no font files are committed.
- **docs**: CLI help, book CLI and MCP pages, `docs/mcp.md`, `docs/control-protocol.md`, `docs/development.md` (including `PHOTOCRAFT_NO_SYSTEM_FONTS=1` with `--font-dir` for machine-independent output).

A command whose params document `"layer":id` acts on that layer, but its availability check (`enabled`) looked at the **active** layer. So with any other layer selected, a call that names a valid layer is refused:

photocraft-cli run Template.psd --cmd layer.smartObjects.replaceContents \
  --params '{"layer":94,"path":"newbg.png"}'
error: command `layer.smartObjects.replaceContents` is not available right now:

title: Profile prompts on open: one file at a time, before it opens, and the answer goes to that file
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
## Problem

With Edit › Color Settings › Profile Mismatches: Ask When Opening on (PhotoCraft's default), opening several files at once whose embedded profile doesn't match the working space (three macOS screenshots, tagged "Display") went wrong:

- every file opened at once, and every Embedded Profile Mismatch prompt went up at once, stacked in the same place;
- each answer went to the **active** document (`color.profileMismatch` acts on `s.active()`), not to the file its prompt was for: "Discard" three times discarded only the last file's profile;
- no prompt said which file it was about.

## Photoshop

Checked in Photoshop 27.11 with Ask When Opening on, opening the same three files together:

- one prompt at a time, before that file opens: 'The document "Screenshot 2026-10-10 at 10…" has an embedded color profile that does not match the current RGB working space.', then Embedded and Working;
- the file's tab appears only after OK, then the next file's prompt comes up;
- Cancel cancels all the opens: that file and the ones still to come.

## Fix

A file that asks is held back until its prompt is answered, and the answer is applied to that file before it opens.

- **Engine.**
  - `ColorState::open_question(&doc)` says, without changing anything, whether opening asks: Ask When Opening is on and the profile is mismatched or missing. It returns what the prompt shows.
  - `ColorState::resolve_open(&mut doc, action)` applies the answer: preserve, convert, discard or assignWorking.
  - The background open job (`Session::start_open`) parks such a document instead of adding it. The job then returns `{held, name, warnings, color}`, and the shell takes the document with `Session::take_held_open`.
- **Shell: new `open_prompt` module.**
  - Files decoded inline or in the background join a queue. Only the first one's prompt is shown, and it names its file.
  - OK applies the answer, opens the file, then moves on to the next.
  - Cancel drops the file and everything still queued…

title: Brush: remember the last selected brush across restarts (split from #2516)
author: siraxe
body:
# Brush: remember the last selected brush across restarts (split from #2516)

**Split from #2516**, like the brush-outline PR: the persistence half is independent of the
outline, so it lands and is maintained on its own. Based directly on `main`.

## What

- The brush the tool was last using — settings, tip/pattern references and the name of the preset
  it was picked from — is saved to `Preferences::lastBrush` and restored at launch: options bar,
  painting cursor and Brushes panel highlight start where the session left off.
- Saved once the pointer is up (`last_brush::persist` in the frame loop, like the Brush Preset
  picker's view), restored by `last_brush::restore` from `prefs_ui::load`. Stored tips load with
  the preset store; a malformed remembered brush keeps the default.
- Bitmaps never enter the preferences document: remembered tips/patterns are references (a loaded
  stored tile drops its full bitmap) and a sampled bitmap too big to embed is skipped, so the
  previous value stands rather than the prefs file growing by megabytes.

## Review fix from #2516 — change-driven, no per-frame work

`remember_brush` no longer clones the brush and serialises it to JSON every frame to compare with
the stored value. `ToolState::brush_rev` is bumped by every setter of the brush or the picked
preset (`tools.setBrush`, preset save/delete/rename/setCurrent/deleteGroup,
`brush.defineFromSelection`, `brush.presets.importAbr`, the store's tip re-linking, and the shell's
tool-switch/reset paths); `remember_brush` serialises only when the revision moved since
`brush_saved_rev`. An unchanged brush costs one counter compare per frame. A restore counts as
saved, so the launch value is never rewritten.

5 new engine tests (revision gating — an unchanged brush never serialises, rejected changes don't
move the revision, picked-preset tracking, restore round trip, no embedded bitmaps).

title: Linux: StartupWMClass is the window's app id
author: atoslins
body:
`packaging/linux/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop` says `StartupWMClass=photocraft`, but the window carries the app id `ai.storyteller.photocraft` (`APP_ID`, through `with_app_id`), natively on Wayland and under XWayland alike. The key is meant to name the class the window maps with ([Desktop Entry spec](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/recognized-keys.html)), so anything that matches a window to its launcher by it never matches PhotoCraft. The entry predates `with_app_id` by a day, which is likely how they drifted apart.

VectorCraft, GridCraft and WordCraft already use the app id. This PR does the same, and adds a test that reads the entry and compares its `StartupWMClass` with `APP_ID`.

`StartupNotify=false` (#2089/#2097) stays as it is: GNOME on Wayland ends startup notification through an xdg-activation token, not the class. With the right class, X11 window managers could end it again (mutter matches the class in `find_startup_sequence_by_wmclass`), but turning it back on is a separate decision.

**Checked**
- Window class with PhotoCraft 0.7.0 on Hyprland 0.56.2: `ai.storyteller.photocraft` both on Wayland and with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY= photocraft` (XWayland).
- The new test fails on `main` and passes with the change.
- `cargo test -p photocraft --bin photocraft`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: perf: Edit > Clear works tile by tile on large selections (#3463)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #3463

Clear went through `try_clear_surface` (or `try_fill_surface` with the background colour on a Background layer). Both read the whole selection bounds into one f32 buffer (768 MB for 8000x6000 RGBA), looked up the selection's tile map once per pixel, and wrote every tile in the bounds back. All of it ran on one thread. Tiles the selection didn't touch were still copied, so they stopped being shared with the undo state.

Both functions now go through a small `edit_tiles` helper that works on the encoded tiles in parallel:

- a tile that is fully selected and fully cleared is dropped, since it would only hold empty pixels and the old code pruned it afterwards anyway
- a fully selected tile under an opaque fill that may set alpha becomes one shared solid tile
- everything else is edited pixel by pixel with the same decode, math and encode as before, and a tile is copied only when one of its pixels actually changes

The per-pixel math hasn't changed, so the results match the old pass exactly, including soft and feathered selections, locked transparency and transparent pixels that still carry a colour. `float_cmds` and `warp_cmds` call the same two functions, so they get the speedup too.

|---|---|---|

| layer, feathered ellipse (200 px) | 1.81 s | 37-51 ms |

title: Format: check pattern sizes on load (#3478)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3478

## Root cause
The `.pcraft` loader (`crates/format/src/convert.rs`) copied each pattern's `width`/`height` from the manifest without checking them. Pixels come from tiles, so a pattern with no tiles can claim 65535 × 65535 px in a file of about 1 KB. Painting it went through `compose::pattern::pattern_rgba`, which allocates `width × height × 16` bytes. That's an allocation failure, which aborts the process. `PreparedPatterns::get` also built an unbudgeted tile whenever the budget refused one. In `engine/src/pattern_cmds.rs`, `brush_texture` and `average_color` computed `(width * height) as usize` in `u32`, which overflows.

## Fix
- **format**: on load, reject a pattern that's 0 px on a side (`Corrupt`) or larger than 30 000 px on a side (`LimitExceeded`). 30 000 is the PSD reader's `MAX_EDGE`; Define Pattern stops at 4000.
- **doc**: add `Pattern::pixel_count()` (u64), `Pattern::is_paintable()` and `pattern::MAX_PAINT_PIXELS` (2^26 px, which keeps the f32 RGBA working copy at 1 GiB or less).
- **compose / gpu**: a pattern too large to paint now paints nothing, the same way a missing pattern does. This covers `Tile::new_in`, `pattern_rgba`, `PreparedPatterns::get` and the three pattern lookups in the GPU plan. Nothing gets allocated for it.
- **engine**: `brush.texturePattern` refuses such a pattern with an error. `average_color` uses overflow-free math over a bounded corner. The Fill, Paint Bucket and Pattern Stamp errors now say "empty or too large to paint".

## Tests
Each test fails without the fix:
- `format/tests/corruption.rs::pattern_sizes_from_the_file_are_checked`: 65535² gives `LimitExceeded` and 0 × 24 gives `Corrupt`; the sample still loads. Without the fix, the file loads.
- `compose pattern::tests::patterns_too_large_to_paint_are_skipped_without_allocating`: a 9000 × 8000 pattern with no tiles is skipped. Without the fix, it allocates 1.1 GB and returns a tile.
- `engine pattern_cmds::tests::a_pattern_too_large_to_paint_is_refused_not_all…

title: Save: show save progress as Saving NN% in the status bar and tab title (#3389)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3389.

## Why
Background saves (Ctrl+S, #2072) reported progress 0 the whole time: `photocraft_io::export` encoded the file in one call and the bytes were written in one call, so the status bar showed only an indeterminate bar and never a percentage. Photoshop shows "Saving NN%" in the status bar and appends " - Saving NN%" to the document tab while it saves.

## Change
- `photocraft_io::export_with(doc, name, opts, &Interrupt)` reports encoding progress and can be cancelled (`export` is unchanged and writes identical bytes): PSD/PSB per layer record and per composite band; layered TIFF likewise plus its encoder stages; .pcraft after its previews; flat formats once the composite is rendered.
- `photocraft_format::atomic_write_progress` writes in 8 MiB chunks and reports the fraction written (flush and rename unchanged).
- The desktop save maps encoding to 0–85 % and writing to 85–99 %; 100 % once the file is in place. Cancel during encoding now stops the encoder instead of waiting for it.
- Status bar: a save reads "Saving 45%" next to the bar (file name on hover); other jobs are unchanged. Percentages round down, so 100 % only shows when done.
- Tab title: " - Saving 45%" on the saving document's tab in both tab strips (e.g. `Untitled @ 100% (Layer 1, RGB/8)* - Saving 45%`), gone when the save ends.
- New string `Saving {percent}` in every complete catalog.

Measured on a 24 MP, 5-layer RGB/8 PSD (572 MB, release): progress now advances roughly linearly (13 % at 0.5 s … 90 % at 5.0 s, 100 % at 5.6 s on a loaded machine) instead of sitting at 0.

## Tests
- `crates/io/tests/export_progress.rs`: progress is monotonic and ends at 1.0 for PSD/PSB/layered TIFF/.pcraft/PNG/JPEG at 8 and 16 bit; same bytes as `export`; cancelling returns `Cancelled`.

title: Fix Windows desktop cursor stutter with non-vsynced presentation
author: sarseev
body:
Fixes storytold/photocraft#382

## Problem
With PhotoCraft focused, moving the pointer outside the window caused
the desktop cursor to stutter.

## Change
Request AutoNoVsync for Windows window presentation instead of the
default AutoVsync. Preserve backend selection, frame latency, and
on-demand repainting. Other platforms remain unchanged.

Add a configuration regression test and document the validation procedure.

## Validation
An A/B comparison on the affected machine confirmed that the original
presentation mode reproduces the stutter and the patched mode removes it.

## Tradeoffs
Non-vsynced presentation can introduce tearing and higher rendering
rates during activity. No continuous idle rendering is introduced.

title: Format: index ZIP entries by name and use crc32fast (#3474)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3474

## Root cause
- `ZipReader::find` (`crates/format/src/zip.rs`) scanned `entries` linearly by name. Loading a `.pcraft` ZIP bundle calls it once per tile/blob reference (`ZipSource::get` → `read_by_name`), so a load did O(refs × entries) string compares: with ~50k tile objects that is on the order of 10^9 compares. The OpenRaster reader in `photocraft-io` (`ora.rs`) uses the same lookup per layer.
- `crc32` was a hand-rolled byte-at-a-time table CRC-32, run over every entry on save and again on load.

## Fix
- `ZipReader::new` builds a `HashMap<String, usize>` name → index once (O(entries)); `find` is now an O(1) average lookup, so a load is O(refs + entries). For duplicate names the first entry wins, exactly as the old front-to-back scan did. `entries` stays public (tests and callers read it) and is documented as read-only.
- `crc32` delegates to `crc32fast::hash` (same IEEE polynomial; slicing-by-16 with SIMD where available, pure-Rust fallback on wasm). `crc32fast` 1.5.2 was already in `Cargo.lock` through `flate2`, so this adds no new crate to the build.

The improvement is argued from complexity only; **no timings were measured** (shared, heavily loaded build machine).

## Tests
- `crc_known_value` (kept) and new `crc_matches_bitwise_reference`: `crc32` matches a bit-at-a-time IEEE CRC-32 oracle over lengths 0..1000 that cross the SIMD/slicing block sizes.
- `find_locates_every_entry_in_a_large_archive`: 3000 entries, every name is found and reads back its own payload; missing names return `None`.
- `duplicate_names_resolve_to_the_first_entry`: preserves the old first-match behaviour. Verified it fails when the index uses plain `insert` (last wins) instead of `entry().or_insert`.

These are behaviour-preservation tests; the change itself is a complexity fix, so there is no failing-before case beyond the duplicate-name check above.

cargo clippy -j 4 -p photocraft-format -p photocraft-io --all-targ…

title: File › Save writes an edit copy handed over by another app back in place (LightCraft's Edit in PhotoCraft)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
PhotoCraft's half of storytold/lightcraft#918 ("Edit in Photocraft"). The LightCraft half is a separate PR there; each works without the other.

## The problem

A photo manager's "Edit in…" renders a copy of a photo, opens it in an editor and reads the file again after the save. LightCraft's copy is a 16-bit TIFF. File › Save sends a TIFF through Save As like any flat file (#416), so for a file that exists only to be changed the user gets a dialog on every save, and choosing another name or format there leaves LightCraft watching a file that never changes.

## What changes

A launch with the environment variable `PHOTOCRAFT_EDIT_IN_PLACE` set (anything but empty or `0`) marks the files on **that launch's command line** as edit copies (`DocState::edit_in_place`). For such a document File › Save writes back to the TIFF it was opened from: no Save As, no TIFF Options prompt, layers kept in the file.

The #416 rule is otherwise unchanged. The mark is narrow on purpose:

- **Only that launch's command-line files.** File › Open, drops, recent files and Apple events open ordinary files.
- **Only a TIFF, and only while it keeps the document's colour mode and channels** (`tiff_layers::holds`: RGB, Grayscale or CMYK, no alpha channels). Lab, Multichannel, Indexed, Bitmap and Duotone documents, and documents with alpha channels, go through Save As as before.
- **Until the document is saved to another file.** A Save As that writes a copy (a PNG of a layered document) leaves it on the TIFF.
- **The control channel's `app.save` is unchanged**: without a `path` it still writes back to layered files only.

Details and the contract for the calling app: `docs/edit-in-place.md`.

## Decisions a maintainer may want to change

- **An environment variable, not a flag.** An older PhotoCraft ignores an unknown variable; an unknown flag is opened as a file name (`Some(s) => files.push(..)` in `main.rs`). A flag can be added beside it.
- **The mark is kept per path until the document arrives…

title: Format: overflow-safe blob decode and bounds-checked ZIP reads (#3486)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3486

## Root cause
- `LoadFetch::blob` (`crates/format/src/store.rs`) capped the zstd decode with `take(self.opts.max_blob_bytes as u64 + 1)`. With `max_blob_bytes: usize::MAX` ("unlimited"), that addition overflows. Debug builds panic. Release builds wrap to `take(0)`, so every blob decodes empty and fails its hash, and no bundle with blobs loads. `ZipReader::read` already saturates the same bound.
- `ZipReader::read` (`crates/format/src/zip.rs`) sliced `&self.bytes[e.data_offset..e.data_offset + e.compressed]` unchecked, but `Entry` is `pub` and `Clone`, so an entry from another archive panics.

## Fix
- New `decompress_bounded(data, max, exact)`, used by both the blob read and the tile decode (`decompress`). Its bound saturates.
- `ZipReader::read` uses checked `get` and returns a `Corrupt` error for an out-of-range entry.
- Cleanup with no behaviour change: `Collect::tile` reuses `tile_le()` instead of its own big-endian branch, and `Object::content()` produces the stored bytes once. `existing_object_is_valid` no longer builds them twice, and `Object::compressed` uses `content()` too.

`#3339` touches `store.rs` only in `load()`, a few lines below these hunks, so the two shouldn't conflict.

## Tests
Each test fails without the fix:
- `format/tests/corruption.rs::an_unlimited_blob_budget_still_loads_blobs`. Without the fix: `attempt to add with overflow` at `store.rs:233`.
- `zip::tests::an_entry_from_another_archive_is_an_error_not_a_panic`. Without the fix: `range end index 4127 out of range for slice of length 101`.

## Commands
```
cargo test -p photocraft-format
cargo clippy -p photocraft-format --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt -p photocraft-format -- --check
cargo xtask layers
cargo xtask wasm
