title: Autosave: best-effort cleanup after commit; sweep orphaned recovery bundles (#3489)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3489

## Root cause
1. `PcraftWriter::save_dir` (`crates/format/src/store.rs`) commits by writing the manifest, then deletes objects the new manifest no longer references with `std::fs::remove_file(..)?`. Any failure there (a file that vanished, a locked file on Windows, a non-file at that path) returned `Err` from a save that had already completed, so autosave reported a failure for a good save.
2. Autosave writes the bundle before the `<key>.json` sidecar (`autosave.rs`). `list_recovery` skips bundles without a sidecar and nothing deletes them, so a crash during a document's first autosave left a partial `<key>.pcraft` folder in the recovery directory forever. Temp files from an interrupted atomic write (`.<name>.<pid>-<n>.pcsave.tmp`, `atomic::temp_name`) were never swept either (`list_objects` only looks at `.zst`).

## Fix
- `save_dir`: post-commit removal of unreferenced objects is best-effort. `objects_removed` counts only real removals; a leftover is retried on the next save (it is listed again).
- `RecoveryStore::new` (called once when the app opens its recovery directory) runs a conservative, best-effort `sweep_orphans`:
  - removes `<key>.pcraft` folders (real directories, sanitized key) that have **no** `<key>.json` (anything at that path, even a broken sidecar, keeps the bundle);
  - removes `*.pcsave.tmp` files in the recovery dir, in bundles and their `tiles/`/`blobs/`, whose embedded pid is **not** this process;
  - both only when untouched for 24 hours (bundle, `tiles/` and `blobs/` mtimes), so another running instance's in-progress first autosave is never touched. Symlinks, unparsable names and other files are left alone, nothing outside the recovery dir is visited, and errors are ignored.

## Tests
- `tests/autosave.rs::failed_cleanup_after_commit_does_not_fail_the_save`: a folder squatting on an unreferenced tile name makes the cleanup fail; the save must still return `Ok` (with `objects_removed == 0`) and load back identical. **Fails with…

title: fix(type): use the correct line at soft-wrap caret boundaries
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

At the beginning of a wrapped line, `type.caret` can report the
preceding line even though the caret geometry belongs to the next
visual line.

The same boundary error affects `type.navigate` with `lineStart`
and `lineEnd`.

Fixes #3068.

## Root cause

Adjacent visual lines can share a character offset.

The previous line-index lookup selected the first matching range,
while caret geometry could correctly resolve the following line.

## Changes

- Prefer the following visual line when resolving a shared caret
  boundary.
- Make line-edge navigation use the same line selection.
- Preserve pointer-based hit-testing by determining the visual line
  from the pointer's position.
- Add text-layout regression coverage for wrapped lines, forced
  breaks, and ordinary paragraph breaks.
- Add engine-level regression coverage for caret and line navigation.

title: Android tablet build with pen pressure (photocraft-android)
author: cristiancolosimo
body:
## What

A native Android build for tablets: new `apps/photocraft-android` crate running the same `PhotocraftApp` in an eframe NativeActivity on wgpu/Vulkan (no wasm, webview or JS). Built with `packaging/android/build.sh` (cargo-apk, arm64, minSdk 29). Details in `apps/photocraft-android/README.md`.

- **Pen pressure:** winit's Android touch force feeds the existing `stylus` module.
- **Pen vs. finger:** winit 0.30 drops the Android tool type, so `patches/winit` (0.30.13 plus one change, `patches/README.md`) encodes it in the high bits of `Touch::id`. `Stylus::finger_down()` makes the canvas use the Hand tool while a finger is down and no pen is, so fingers pan/pinch and only the stylus paints. Other platforms never set the flags, so nothing changes there.
- **File dialogs:** an in-app browser over shared storage (needs "All files access"); SAF needs a Java callback a NativeActivity can't receive.
- **System bars:** `target_sdk 34`, `NoActionBar.Fullscreen` theme, layout inside the activity content rect.
- `ui-egui`: eframe's `accesskit` is enabled only off Android (it requires `android-game-activity`).

## Things to look at

- `unsafe`: `android_main` needs `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]`, so this crate denies `unsafe` and allows it in one file (like `photocraft-tablet`) instead of inheriting the workspace `forbid`. One `// SAFETY:` comment.
- The vendored winit patch (3 MB) is a deliberate stopgap until winit 0.31's pointer kinds.

## Tested

`cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-android --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib stylus` (new finger/pen test), `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. On a real tablet: the app starts and pen pressure works. The system-bar fixes, file browser and finger pan were built but are not yet confirmed on a device. Not run: the full test suite, `panic_hunt` (no commands changed), `cargo xtask scorecard`.

title: feat(export): optionally trim transparent margins from layer files
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Layers to Files always exports each layer at the full document dimensions, even when its visible content occupies only a small area.

For workflows involving sprites, isolated assets, and reusable design elements, this leaves unnecessary transparent margins around every exported image.

Addresses #3447.

## Changes

- Add an optional `trim` parameter to `file.export.layersToFiles`.
- Expose a Trim checkbox in the Layers to Files dialog.
- Calculate the visible alpha bounds of each isolated layer before export.
- Crop the temporary export document to those bounds using the existing document-cropping implementation.
- Account for the rendered result, including masks and layer effects.
- Preserve full document dimensions when trimming is disabled.
- Keep entirely transparent layers exportable without creating zero-sized images.
- Leave the original document unchanged.

## Compatibility

Trimming is disabled by default, preserving existing export behavior and automation scripts.

The option applies independently to each exported layer.

## Tests

Added regression tests covering:
- Default full-canvas exports.
- Trimmed exports and pixel preservation.
- 8-, 16-, and 32-bit source documents.
- Non-destructive export behavior.
- Entirely transparent layers.

The tests have not been executed locally. CI validation is pending.

## Issue

Addresses #3447.

title: fix(io): a fresh Metrics type layer writes no empty Txt2 stub (#3514)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3514.

The report isolates the cause precisely: PSD export always writes a document-level `Txt2` block, and for a fresh document its document-resources dictionary (`/0`) is the empty `<< >>` that Photoshop never writes; Photopea's reader fails on it. Removing that block (or not writing it, as 0.3.0 did) makes Photopea open the file with live, editable text.

This writes the block only when it carries something:
- the file already had one - round-trip its resources, pen positions and extras;
- or a layer uses the **Optical** auto-kern mode, the one mode EngineData's `AutoKerning` cannot distinguish (#1348).

A plain Metrics document therefore writes no `Txt2`, matching 0.3.0 and fixing the report.

The `TySh` 4-byte-alignment warning Photopea logs is separate and not addressed here (Photopea tolerates it; psd-tools reads it).

Tests: `photocraft-text` `needs_txt2_only_for_optical`; `photocraft-io` `fresh_metrics_text_writes_no_txt2_block`. Full `photocraft-text` (123) and `photocraft-io` suites pass; fmt and clippy clean.

title: feat(raw): open monochrome LinearRaw DNGs, 1 sample per pixel (#3497)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3497.

A monochrome LinearRaw DNG (one sample per pixel - a Leica M Monochrom file, or a VueScan black-and-white film scan) was refused on open with `unsupported camera raw: LinearRaw data with 1 samples per pixel`, because `dng::decode` only accepted the 3-sample LinearRaw case. The develop path already handles a single-plane RGB image, so this expands a 1-sample LinearRaw plane to three identical channels at decode: the file opens as RGB with the grey in all three channels - the shape the report asked for.

The CFA (1 sample) and 3-sample LinearRaw paths are unchanged.

Tests: `crates/raw/tests/dng.rs` `gray_linear_raw_opens_as_rgb` (the synthetic DNG generator gains a monochrome-LinearRaw mode; the test checks the three channels are equal and that `develop` stays neutral grey). Full `photocraft-raw` suite passes; fmt and clippy clean.

title: History: jump to a state in one step (history.selectState) (#2966)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #2966.

**Why:** clicking a History state ran Edit › Undo / Redo once per state. Each step added 1 to the document revision, so the canvas could no longer tell what the jump changed: it recomposited the whole document and, on the GPU path, re-uploaded every changed layer. This is part of the "very laggy history usage" report.

**Merge order: please merge #3545 and #3567 (Snapshots, @itsF4LCON) first.** This PR touches the same History code; I'll rebase this onto them right after (both change `fn history` in `panels.rs`).

## Change
- New command `history.selectState {"state": index}` (same numbering as `history.deleteState`, redo states included). It returns the document to that state in one step: one revision, one damage rect, the state's targeted layers restored as Undo does. Later states stay redoable until the next edit. UI, CLI, control channel and MCP share it.
- The History panel runs it once per click (errors go to the status bar); an open Free Transform still blocks it, and the transform also refuses it for every caller.
- A floating selection goes back as with Undo instead of being dropped as a new step that would discard the redo states.
- History rows get accessibility labels.

## Measurements
Release build, 30 states back, click → drawn (offscreen harness, GPU sync):

| Document | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 24 MP, GPU canvas | 5.2 ms | 3.7 ms |
| 24 MP, CPU canvas | 363 ms | 230 ms |
| 175-layer layout, GPU canvas | 1249 ms | 836 ms (composite 500 → 110 ms) |

## Tests
- engine (`history_select_cmds`): every jump back and forward equals N undos/redos (same document, targeted layers, entries, redo list, one revision bump); bounded damage; redo states survive a jump; floating piece; bad params (missing, null, negative, out of range, huge, float, string, array, object, bool) and no document → Err, nothing changed; `enabled`. `panic_hunt` green.

title: Actions: a recorded File › Save of a flat file saves the file it is played on (#3531)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3531

Follow-up to #2032 (comment from MikeySnowspikes: a recorded Save says it saved but doesn't overwrite the original).

## Root cause
A layered document (PSD/PSB/.pcraft) already recorded a real `file.save` step. A flat file (PNG, JPEG, ...) has no in-place Save yet: Save opens the save dialog, and confirming it recorded a Save As with the fixed path of the file it was recorded on. Playing the action on another file wrote that first file again and reported "Saved a.png"; the document the action ran on was never written.

## Fix
- File › Save that had to ask for a file name and was confirmed with the document's own file is recorded as `file.save` (not a Save As to a fixed path). Save As keeps its recorded path.
- Replaying `file.save` writes back to the active document's own file for layered files and for flat formats the codecs can write; otherwise it returns an error that says what is needed.
- Interactive Save is unchanged (the dialog behaviour of #2515 is not touched).

## Tests
- `recorded_save_overwrites_the_flat_file_the_action_is_played_on` (real PNG files on disk): fails before the fix (b.png untouched, step recorded as `file.saveAs`), passes after.
- `recorded_save_overwrites_the_layered_file_the_action_is_played_on` (PSD, already worked) guards the layered path.

## Commands
`cargo test -j 4 -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- save actions:: file_dialog file_open`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p photocraft-ui-egui -- --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. No command added or changed, so no panic_hunt.

title: fix(gpu): require consent to persist CPU recovery
author: Ni-zav
body:
Fixes #3483.

## Problem

An interrupted GPU startup can trigger PhotoCraft's recovery
sequence:

Vulkan → OpenGL → CPU

On Linux/NVIDIA systems where the OpenGL adapter cannot present
to the window, this can end in CPU rendering.

Once the CPU renderer starts successfully, PhotoCraft
automatically saves CPU mode to the user's preferences.

Consequently, closing the recovery dialog without choosing
an option can leave every subsequent launch using software
rendering, even when Vulkan is available.

## Root Cause

The desktop startup callback persists CPU mode when a
fallback succeeds, independently of the user's decision.

The backend persistence logic can also save CPU as the
preferred backend.

## Changes

- Stop automatically persisting CPU rendering after startup
  recovery.
- Keep CPU fallback temporary for the current session.
- Preserve the recovery dialog's explicit preference controls.
- Continue remembering successful hardware backend fallbacks.
- Prevent CPU fallback from silently replacing the saved
  GPU backend.
- Update graphics recovery documentation.

## Regression Tests

Added tests covering:

- CPU fallback following an OpenGL startup failure.
- Temporary CPU mode requested through --safe-gpu.
- Preservation of the original automatic GPU policy.
- Persistence of successful hardware backend recovery.
- Explicit CPU selection remaining supported.

Existing recovery-dialog tests cover saving the user's
"Keep Using CPU" and "Retry GPU" choices.

## Scope

This addresses unintended preference persistence.

It does not change the Linux GPU adapter-selection algorithm
or the Vulkan → OpenGL → CPU fallback sequence.

## Validation

Changes committed and pushed to the fork.
Branch rebased onto current upstream main.

Local tests and CI have not been run.

title: psd: harden the standalone binary parsers (fuzz + property tests, gradient/swatch correctness)
author: agent-346022
body:
## Summary

Photoshop colour palettes (`.aco`/`.ase`), gradients (`.grd`) and patterns are files people download in bulk, so plenty are malformed. A broken or hostile one must raise a clean error — never crash (losing the user's work) and never silently produce a wrong colour. That is the project's first rule (`AGENTS.md`, "Never crash"). This hardens every standalone parser in `photocraft-psd` and puts each under a libFuzzer target plus deterministic property tests.

- `grd.rs` — one float guard (`finite`): only `NaN` falls back to a default; `±inf` and over-`f32::MAX` values saturate (monotonic, no snap-to-default that would invert a value). **Hue wraps** (`370° → 10°`) instead of clamping to a different colour at the boundary. RGB/CMYK/Gray clamped to `0..=1`, L\* to `0..=100`, a\*/b\* to the CIELAB gamut `-128..=127`.
- `aco.rs` / `ase.rs` / `io.rs` — a shared `utf16_units` caps swatch names **without splitting a surrogate pair** (the old `encode_utf16().take()` could write broken UTF-16 for emoji/CJK above U+FFFF).
- `patterns` / `filter_effects` / `metadata` / `resources` / `tagged` — already well defended; review found no latent panic, so these get fuzz targets + property tests only (no production change).

Touches only `crates/psd/` plus the fuzz CI matrix.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-psd` — 371 pass
- [x] `cargo clippy -p photocraft-psd --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check -p photocraft-psd --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- [x] `cargo +nightly fuzz build` — 13 targets; smoke runs clean (metadata 11.5M, patterns 2M, filter_effects 5.9M, resources 3.5M, tagged 5.4M execs)
- [x] `cargo xtask test-corpus -p psd -p io` — io oracle / round-trip / mutation corpora pass (no regression on real presets)
- [x] Mutation checks: a\*/b\* clamp-weakening and hue-guard-removal mutants both killed

title: PSD: Backgrounds survive a round trip through PhotoCraft
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Every PSD with a Background layer came back from PhotoCraft with an **ordinary bottom layer**. Opened in Photoshop it's no longer the Background: it's unlocked, can move and can hold transparency.

Measured with scripted Photoshop 27.11: I opened PhotoCraft's re-exports of all 427 PSD/PSB files in the corpus. **317 lost their Background** this way. Their composites were otherwise identical.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Photoshop opens a PSD's bottom layer as the Background **when that layer's record has no transparency (`-1`) channel**, whatever its name and lock flags say. It then locks it and shows it as "Background": psd-tools' "Фон" and ag-psd's "bg" or "Layer 1" all open as Backgrounds. PhotoCraft always wrote the `-1` channel.

| | channels | flags |
|---|---|---|
| Photoshop's Background (`photoshop/adjustments/rgb8/invert.psd`) | 0, 1, 2 | `00001001` |
| PhotoCraft's export of it (`main`) | **−1**, 0, 1, 2 | `00000001` |
| this PR | 0, 1, 2 | `00001001` |

## Change
- **Export** (`psd_export::psd_background`): the bottom top-level layer is written without the `-1` channel when it's a locked (transparency and position), unclipped, unmasked raster that's opaque over the whole canvas at full opacity and Normal, as a Background always is. Flags are written as Photoshop writes them: bit 4 marked meaningful, and "pixel data irrelevant" on adjustment layers.
- **Import** (`psd_import::mark_background`): like Photoshop, a bottom raster layer whose record has no `-1` channel becomes the Background (locked, named "Background").

## Results
- Of the 227 corpus files whose bottom layer is a Background, PhotoCraft's export now writes **227** the way the original does (`main`: 0), and no other bottom layer turns into one.
- Corpus oracles and round trips are unchanged: io 148/170, psd-tools 237/309, Photoshop 137/258 on the same commit, and every round trip renders the same.

- `psd_export::tests::a_background_is_written_without_a_transpar…

title: fix(engine): a PSD type layer names the installed font, not an invented one (#3556)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3556.

A type layer created with a font by family name stored no PostScript name, so PSD export invented one - the family with its spaces removed plus `-Regular` (e.g. `Franklin Gothic Demi Cond` → `FranklinGothicDemiCond-Regular`). Photoshop looks type up by PostScript name, so it flagged the font as missing and substituted Myriad Pro as soon as the text was edited, even though the font is installed.

`apply_char_props` now resolves the family's installed face (matching weight and italic) from the font database whenever the family, style, weight or italic is set, and stores that face's real PostScript name. An explicit `postscriptName` still wins, and a family PhotoCraft does not have keeps no name, so the export falls back as before.

Test: `a_family_font_gets_the_installed_postscript_name`; the existing named-face test now expects the resolved name.

Gates: `cargo test -p photocraft-engine` (including `panic_hunt`), `cargo xtask parity --check` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass.

title: Save As: a saved .pcraft manifest reports the file it was saved under
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #3312.

## Root cause

Every `.pcraft` writer serialises the document *before* `DocState::saved_to` adopts the new name, so the bytes always carry the previous identity:

```rust
let (bytes, warnings) = export(&st.doc, &path, settings)?;   // manifest gets the old name
write(&path, &bytes)?;
st.saved_to(path);                                           // name adopted here
```

Two funnels do that writing, and the report reproduces both (`doc.save` and `run --out`):

| writer | used by |
|---|---|
| `automation::files::{save, save_bytes}` | headless server, MCP `doc_save`, CLI `run --out` / `convert` |
| `photocraft_io::export` | desktop `File › Save As` and export, the engine's `encode` / `save_doc` |

The GUI has the same defect — the issue left that open ("worth checking before assuming the scope"): `services.export` hands `photocraft_io::export` the same stale document, and `saved_to` again runs after the write.

## Fix

`photocraft_io::named_for_file(doc, name) -> Cow<Document>`: when `name` is a file (a path, or `name.ext`) the document is serialised under that file's name, so what lands in `manifest.json` is the identity the save is about to adopt — the same rule every other format already follows on import, where `document.name` comes from the file it was read from. A bare extension (`"pcraft"`) names no file and changes nothing. Applied in the `.pcraft` branch of both funnels. `photocraft-format` itself and autosave are left alone: the recovery bundle is named after its key, not after a user file, and flat exports carry no manifest.

The session, the file and whatever reopens it now agree on all three paths.

## Tests

- `crates/io/tests/pcraft_manifest_name.rs` — a bundle written to `_nametest.pcraft` carries that name (read back both from the raw `manifest.json` through `ZipReader` and from `load_from_bytes`); a bare `"pcraft"` leaves `FirstTest.psd` untouched.
- `crates/automation/tests/pcraft_manifest_name.rs` — the issue's scenario end to end (ope…

title: fix(engine): image.canvasSize rejects unlisted anchors instead of landing between two (#2946)
author: agent-346022
body:
## Summary

`image.canvasSize` with a misspelled `anchor` silently anchored the canvas somewhere that is **neither** what the caller asked for **nor** the documented `center` default — a resize offset nobody chose, with no error.

`anchor_factors` resolved the x and y axes independently and with different rules (x looked for a capitalised `"Left"`/`"Right"`, y for a lowercase `"top"`/`"bottom"` prefix), so a typo matched one and missed the other:

| anchor | lands at |
|---|---|
| `"topLeft"` | top-left (correct) |
| `"topleft"` | top-**centre** — not one of the nine |
| `"TopLeft"` | **left**-centre — a different anchor, silently |

- `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs` — match `anchor` exactly against the nine documented values via one `ANCHORS` table; anything else is a `BadParams` error naming `anchor` and listing them (the convention #507 set for other command params). The nine valid values keep the exact factors they had, and an omitted `anchor` still means `center`. The Canvas Size dialog picks from a nine-cell grid, so the UI cannot hit this; only command/MCP callers could.

Fixes #2946.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib image_cmds::` — 23 pass (new `canvas_size_anchor_offsets_and_rejects_unlisted` covers the nine offsets, the omitted default, and the misspellings from the issue)
- [x] `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` — passes (no command panics on adversarial params)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers` — clean

Made with love by Claude

title: PSD: alpha channel resources count the merged transparency; 13-byte DisplayInfo
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Photoshop 27.11 **refuses to open** some PSDs that PhotoCraft writes. I opened PhotoCraft's re-exports of the 427 corpus files in scripted Photoshop, and two of them failed (`ag-psd/layer-mask/src.psd`, `psd-tools/effects/stroke-without-vector-mask.psd`) with:

title: Glows: Photoshop's precise ramp; centre-source glows inverted after the contour
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Two glow bugs, measured against Photoshop 27.11:
- **Precise** Outer and Inner Glows stayed solid for about half their size, then dropped off steeply. Up to **122 levels off**.
- **Centre-source** Inner Glows (Softer and Precise) were up to **115 levels off**, even though the edge-source Softer glow already matched.

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: a 128 px square with one glow (Normal, black, 100%, Range 50%), sampled pixel by pixel across its edges. Outer and inner, both techniques, sizes 10 and 20, spread 0/40%, choke 0/30%, edge and centre source: 16 cases.
- A **Precise** glow is `1 − D / (size + 1)` beyond the solid spread/choke part, where D is the centre-to-centre distance to the edge. Photoshop's black glow over white reads 47, 93, 140, 186, 232 at 2–10 px out. `main`'s ramp ended at `size`, and the default 50% Range then doubled it.
- A **centre-source** Inner Glow is **exactly `1 −` the edge glow** (0 levels apart, for both techniques), taken *after* the contour and Range. `main` inverted before them.

## Change
- `compose::effects::glow_map`: a Precise glow's raw coverage is 0.5 at the edge, falling to 0 at `size + 1`, and solid within the spread/choke. The shared Range step (`v / range`) then gives Photoshop's ramp at the default 50%. The centre-source inverse is now taken after the contour and Range.
- **GPU:** the same ramp in `fs_mglow`, and an "invert after the contour" mode (`p0.y = 2`) in `fs_mfinish`, used only by glows (Satin keeps its own invert).

Only Range 50% has been measured. For other Range values, this keeps PhotoCraft's existing `v / range` model for both techniques.

## Results

| | `main` (worst) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Precise outer (4 cases) | 110–122 | 1 |
| Precise inner, edge and centre (4) | 58–64 | 1 |
| Softer inner, centre (2) | 110–115 | 1 |
| Softer outer and inner-edge (6) | 1–4 | unchanged |

title: fix(smudge): smear smoothly on fast strokes instead of stamping echoes
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #3573

## Root cause
The Smudge tool carries a picked-up copy of the pixels from one dab to the next. Its dabs were placed at the brush **Spacing**, which is 10–25 % of the diameter. On a big brush that means a dab every 10 px or more, and each dab stamped the carried copy again, so every edge the stroke crossed left a row of bands or echoes instead of a smooth smear. This matches the "actual" screenshot. The path walker already interpolates between pointer events and carries the leftover distance across segments, so sparse pointer events weren't the problem. The problem was the distance between dabs.

## Fix
- `engine/retouch_cmds.rs`: a new `smudge_spacing` respaces Smudge strokes to about 1 px between dabs, with a floor of 1 % of the diameter, which is the walker's minimum. It applies to both the commit and the live preview (`DabTool::parse`). A Spacing of 100 % or more, where dabs don't touch, is a deliberate choice and is left as it is (#2140, `smudge_uses_the_brush_settings_spacing` still passes).
- With more dabs, each one keeps `strength^r` of the carried colour and lays down `1-(1-strength)^r`, where r = new spacing / old spacing. That keeps the same fade per pixel, so the smear still reaches about as far as before.
- `paint/retouch.rs`: `Smudge::with_laydown(k)` lets the amount laid down per dab differ from the amount kept. Nothing changes for other callers.

The regular Brush already gets its dabs from spacing plus interpolation and draws continuously in the issue's screenshot, so this PR only changes Smudge.

## Validation
- New `fast_smudge_smears_smoothly_without_echoes`: two pointer events 70 px apart across a dark line, with a 40 px brush at 25 % spacing, at 8, 16 and 32 bit. It checks that the smear profile never bounces back lighter by more than 0.01. On main it fails with bands of about +0.04.
- New `smudge_dabs_leave_no_gaps_on_a_fast_stroke`: across one 400 px segment, the largest gap between dab centres is 1 px or less (10 px on main), an…

title: test(engine): 32-bit Levels keep the float curve's range (#3546)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3546.

`destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit` asserted that a 32-bit document maps Levels black to 0 and white to 255 - the old 0..1 lookup-table behaviour. #2592 (`Preserve HDR range in float adjustments`) made a 32-bit RGB Levels adjustment evaluate the float curve directly, so it deliberately runs past the output range: black goes below 0 and white above 1. The test was left stale and now fails in the full engine lib run (and on its own).

title: Fuzz: ignore the same build leftovers in every fuzz crate
author: s17sh70x2jfl031ag
body:
Running the fuzz targets locally left untracked files in the checkout, because the five fuzz crates' `.gitignore` files don't match:

- `crates/raw/fuzz` has no `.gitignore` at all
- `crates/psd/fuzz` doesn't ignore `Cargo.lock`
- `crates/format/fuzz` doesn't ignore `coverage/`

This gives all five the same list that `codecs` and `affinity` already use: `target/`, `corpus/`, `artifacts/`, `coverage/` and `Cargo.lock`.

**How I checked:** I created the files a fuzzing run leaves behind (`Cargo.lock`, and files in `corpus/`, `artifacts/`, `coverage/` and `target/`) in all five fuzz crates. Before this change, `git status` listed six untracked paths: `format/fuzz/coverage/`, `psd/fuzz/Cargo.lock`, and `raw/fuzz`'s `Cargo.lock`, `artifacts/`, `corpus/` and `coverage/`. After it, it lists none. I found this while running the PSD, codecs, format, raw and Affinity fuzz targets overnight.

title: Edit › Transform › Skew: corners and sides move along one axis, like Photoshop (#3437)
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
Fixes #3437. @davidmann4 closed their draft (#3506) and asked for this PR.

## Problem

In Edit › Transform › Skew, a corner drag scaled the box like Free Transform, and the side handles moved freely in both directions. A drag outside the box rotated it.

## Photoshop

Checked in Photoshop 27.11 by @kayrockscreenprinting.

- **Image layer:** a corner moves alone, horizontally or vertically, whichever way the drag mostly goes.
- **Side handles:** the top and bottom handles slide only horizontally, the left and right ones only vertically.
- **⌥:** moves the opposite corner or edge the other way.
- **Type layer:** a corner slides its whole edge instead: the top or bottom edge for a sideways drag, the left or right one for an up/down drag. The text stays a parallelogram and remains live type.
- **Outside the box:** a drag doesn't rotate the box.
- **⇧:** changes nothing.

## Fix

All in `transform_tool.rs`. Free Transform, Distort and Perspective are unchanged.

- `apply_mode_drag` applies a handle drag for the current mode. The canvas calls it instead of turning the mode into modifier keys (`mode_mods`), which can't express "a corner moves on one axis".
- **Corners.** A corner moves along one of its two edges, whichever the drag mostly follows, in the box's own frame, so a rotated box skews along its sides.
  - On editable type (`moves_type`), the corner's edge partner moves with it. A trapezoid would make the commit fail ("Distort and Perspective need rasterized type").
  - ⌥ moves the opposite corner, or on type the opposite edge, by the same amount the other way.
- **Side handles.** These slide only along their edge, as ⌘⇧ does in Free Transform.
- **Outside the box.** `mode_allows` (was `distort_allows`) now also blocks outside drags in Skew mode, so neither the rotation nor the rotate cursor happens. A click outside still commits.

## Tests

Written first, each failing before its change:

- `skew_mode_moves_a_corner_or_an_edge_along_one_axis`:
  - corners on each …

title: Chisel bevels: Photoshop's facet slope and ramp ends
author: MrCloudy2
body:
## What's wrong

Bevel & Emboss with **Chisel Hard** or **Chisel Soft** drew facets about **twice as steep** as Photoshop's. On a 128 px square with an Inner Chisel Hard bevel (size 10, depth 100%, light from the top), the lit facet reads **217** where Photoshop shows **188**. The ends of each facet also differed. Up to 154 levels off (Outer Chisel Hard).

## What Photoshop does (measured)

Scripted on Photoshop 27.11: one Bevel & Emboss on a 128 px square, Global Light off, light at 90°/30°, sampled pixel by pixel across the edges. Chisel Hard and Soft, inner and outer, size 10 and 20, depth 100 and 300.
- **Slope:** a chisel facet rises to the same `depth × size / 2` as a Smooth bevel, but over `size + 1` px, so its slope is `depth × size / (2 (size + 1))`. Size 10 → 0.455 (measured 0.452–0.457). Size 20 → 0.476 (measured 0.471–0.480).
- **Ramp ends:**
  - **Inner Hard** runs from half a pixel beyond the edge to `size + ½`, so the facet is flat right up to the edge pixel.
  - **Inner Soft** starts a pixel further out (a steeper edge pixel) and is **not blurred**.
  - **Outer Hard** ends a pixel further out.
  - **Outer Soft** is a pixel shorter, with a steeper edge pixel.
  - Outer chisel bevels also shade, at half strength, the pixel where their ramp reaches zero. Emboss styles already did this.

(Smooth bevels already match Photoshop within 1–3 levels and are unchanged.)

## Change
- `compose::effects`: `bevel_geom`'s chisel depth scale is `depth × size / 2`, and `bevel_chisel_h` has the measured ramps. The Chisel Soft blur stays only for Emboss and Pillow, which aren't modelled yet. Outer chisel bevels reach one pixel past their ramp.
- **GPU:** the same ramps in `fs_mbevelh` (Chisel Soft flag in `p0.z`), the Emboss-only blur, and the outer reach-past flag in `p3.x` of `fs_mbevelshade`.

## Results

| case | `main` (worst) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Inner Chisel Hard (size 10, size 20, depth 300) | 27–29 | 0–1 |
| Inner Chisel Soft | 29 | 1 |
| Outer Chisel Ha…

title: Free Transform several selected layers together (#3592)
author: FredApps
body:
Fixes #3592

Selecting several layers and pressing Ctrl+T (Free Transform) now transforms all of them together, like Photoshop: one bounding box around every selected layer's content, the same move/scale/rotate/skew/distort applied to each layer around the shared pivot, committed as **one** undoable step. Cancel (Esc) leaves every layer as it was.

## Design
It reuses the existing single-layer path rather than adding a parallel one.

**Engine (`edit.transform`)**
- New optional `"layers": [id, …]` param. `multi_targets` filters the list. With two or more layers left, `transform_many` builds one homography from the shared `rect` (the union of each layer's `transform_bounds` by default) and the `quad`/`matrix`. It then runs the existing `transform_layer` and `refresh_text` on each layer inside a single `s.edit("Free Transform")`, and warps the selection outline once. With only one layer left, it falls back to the normal single-layer path.
- The quad/matrix parsing and the affine detection moved into small helpers (`homography`, `affine_of`, `rect_param`). The single-layer path uses them too and behaves the same as before.

**UI (`transform_tool`)**
- `begin()` checks `DocState::selected_layers()`. When `multi_targets` returns two or more layers, `begin_many` opens the box around `multi_bounds`. The document under the box has those layers hidden, or has their selected pixels lifted out for pixel layers when there's a selection. The moving content previews as one composite of just those layers, and what covers the topmost moving layer still draws over it (`Above`).
- `TransformSession` gets a `layers: Vec<u64>` field (serde default, empty for single-layer sessions). `commit()` adds `"layers"` to the `edit.transform` call. Box undo/redo, nudges, the options bar fields, the pivot and Esc all work unchanged, because they only act on the quad.

## Edge cases

This one-line change preserves the same sample decoding, sparse-tile defaults, runtime mask depth, coverage clamp and blending arithmetic. The regression test covers negative coordinates, tile boundaries, absent tiles with nonzero defaults, and zero/partial/full coverage across all U8/U16/F32 source and mask depth combinations.

title: Brush: symmetric live strokes update only what changed (#3593)
author: xsvm
body:
Draft: work in progress, opened to avoid duplicate work on #3593.

## Problem

With painting symmetry on, every pointer event in `LiveStroke::push` (`crates/engine/src/brush_cmds.rs`) clones the primary and every mirrored `StrokeRenderer`, finishes the copies, merges all passes again in `composite_union_many`, composites the whole stroke (`all = true`) and restores every pass's full bounding box from the pre-stroke pixels. The cost of one event grows with the area painted so far, so a stroke is quadratic. Without symmetry the live stroke composites only the dirty coverage tiles.

Measured on `main` (24 MP RGB 8-bit, one stroke of 1,200 pointer events, Xeon Platinum 8573C, 4 cores):

| Brush | Symmetry | First 100 events (avg) | Last 100 events (avg) | Whole stroke |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 30 px | off | 0.068 ms | 0.078 ms | 0.1 s |
| 30 px | vertical | 1.0 ms | 96 ms | 42.9 s |
| 30 px | dual | 2.2 ms | 192 ms | 84.2 s |
| 120 px | off | 0.13 ms | 0.14 ms | 0.17 s |
| 120 px | vertical | 2.9 ms | 119 ms | 56.7 s |
| 120 px | dual | 6.0 ms | 245 ms | 115.9 s |

The existing `bench_symmetry` example (121 events): off 8 ms, vertical 125 ms, dual 288 ms.

## Plan

- Merge the passes incrementally: per push, union only the coverage tiles any pass dirtied and composite those, restoring only the previous tail region, as the non-symmetric path does.
- Keep the output byte-identical to the current merge (overlapping dabs on an axis under one opacity ceiling, shared axes, smoothing tail), since release commits the pixels the live stroke drew (c6a525cc). Tests compare against the current full merge for every symmetry mode.
- Report before/after with `bench_symmetry` and a long-stroke run.

Fixes #3593

title: fix(engine): a pasted smart object keeps its PSD-embedded linked source (#3584)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3584.

A smart object whose contents are Photoshop's embedded linked-layer data (a `Linked` source whose uuid names an entry in the document's `lnk2` block) could not be opened after Copy + Paste into another document. `whole_layer` builds the scratch copy and carried `patterns` but not those linked-layer blocks, so the pasted object had no source bytes to read and `layer.smartObjects.editContents` failed.

This carries the source document's `lnk2`/`lnk3`/`lnkD` global blocks with the copy and lands them in the destination document on paste (skipping any it already has). Objects placed as `Embedded` already carried their bytes in the layer, so only this PSD-embedded case was broken.

title: Move: an unlinked layer mask moves alone when targeted (#3604)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3604

## Root cause
Dragging the layer already left an unlinked mask in place (`translate_layer` only shifts `linked` masks), but the other half of Photoshop's behaviour was missing: with the mask thumbnail targeted and its chain off, the Move tool moves the mask alone. `layer.translate` ignored the target, so it always moved the layer.

## Fix
- `layer.translate` takes `target: "mask"`: a layer with an unlinked mask shifts that mask only (position locks still apply); a linked mask moves with its layer as before.
- `channel_cmds::follows_target` includes `layer.translate`, so the shell adds the target when the Layers panel targets the mask (drag commit, arrow-key nudge).
- New `layer_multi_cmds::moved_target` for the live drag preview.

## Tests (fail without the fix)
- engine `translate_with_the_mask_targeted_moves_an_unlinked_mask_alone` (8 and 16 bit, undo) and `translate_leaves_an_unlinked_mask_in_place` (guards the existing drag-the-layer half)
- ui-egui `dragging_with_an_unlinked_mask_targeted_moves_the_mask_alone` (preview + commit; linked mask and pixel target still move the layer)

## Commands
`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- layer_multi channel_cmds hidden_target`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- move_`, `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`, clippy `-D warnings` (engine --all-targets, ui-egui --lib --tests), fmt --check, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`.

title: ops: count selection masks in history pixel budget
author: Streetblock
body:
Normal selection masks were omitted from history's pixel-memory accounting. Repeated selection edits could retain large masks while `pixel_bytes()` reported no selection memory, so `trim()` would not evict those older states when the byte budget was exceeded.

Include `Document::selection` in the shared `tiles::surfaces` visitor. This makes direct pixel-byte totals, history-only unique bytes, and the incremental tile-reference tracker account for the same selection surfaces. Shared tile allocations still count once; reference tracking includes aliases so removing one snapshot does not discard a tile still held by another owner.

The existing minimum-undo policy is preserved: the newest undo state is retained even when the current document plus that state exceed `max_bytes`.

### Reproduction and measurements

A document with no raster layers isolates selection memory: five independently allocated 24-MP GRAY8 selection masks, `History::new(50)`, an 8-MiB byte budget, and `trim()` after each recorded selection edit. Baseline: upstream `16bdcbd54e5d87cf0212b5961ac35347f27e0e21`. Release build on Windows, Intel i9-13900H.

| Metric | Upstream | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Actual unique selection-tile bytes retained by current + history | 120 MiB | 48 MiB |
| Reported pixel bytes | 0 MiB | 48 MiB |
| History-only unique bytes reported | 0 MiB | 24 MiB |
| Undo states retained | 5 | 1 |

That is **60% less retained selection-tile memory in this fixture**. The remaining 48 MiB are the current selection and the latest undo selection. Each uses 24 MiB of padded tile storage; keeping both follows the existing policy, so this is deliberately not a strict 8-MiB cap.

Separately sampled process peak working set was **147.61 → 99.36 MiB** in the two single fixture runs. This descriptive process metric also includes fixture construction, masks before trimming, allocator behavior and runtime overhead. It does not establish a general application-RAM reduction or a runtime improv…

title: Image Adjustments: Desaturate, Equalize and Replace Color on a smart object (#3606)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3606

## Root cause
#2229 routed most Image › Adjustments on a smart object through `adjust_as_smart_filter`, but Desaturate, Equalize and Replace Color had their own `enabled` checks (pixel layer only) and never called it, so they were refused with "not a pixel layer".

## Change
- All three are enabled on a smart object and record `image.adjustments.<kind>` as a smart filter (selection becomes the filter mask, one history step), re-run via `adjust_as_filter`.
- Replace Color records the foreground colour it was run with, so the filter does not change when the foreground does.
- Equalize's body is now `equalize_pixels`, shared by the command and the filter; Desaturate's adjustment is shared too.
- Not covered: Match Color (needs a source document) and HDR Toning (flattens).

## Tests
- `desaturate_equalize_and_replace_color_record_smart_filters`: each filter's render equals the destructive result on the same pixels, and undo removes it. Fails on main ("runs on a smart object"). Updated the older test that asserted Replace Color stays disabled.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib -- adjust_cmds::tests`, `--test panic_hunt -- --ignored`, clippy `-D warnings` --all-targets, fmt, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` pass. `adjust_params::tests::destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit` fails on upstream/main without this change too.

title: fix(ui): one eliding label for fixed-width chrome, so translations can't overrun (#3580)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3580. This is the app-wide mechanism, not a one-off guard.

**Root cause.** A translated label drawn beside a fixed-width control can run over its neighbours. The Layers Lock/Fill row guarded only the redundant "Lock:" caption, so "Fill:" ("Заливка:" in Russian; longer still as pt-br `Preenchimento:` / fr `Remplissage :`, the worst catalogs) overran the lock icons.

**The mechanism.** `widgets::elided_label(ui, text, max_w)` is the one primitive for fixed chrome: it lays the text out no wider than its room, cuts it with `…`, and shows the full string on hover. It builds on the existing `tab_strip::elided` (already used for document tabs, layer names and brush names), so overlap becomes structurally impossible in *every* locale with no per-language code. The Opacity/Fill scrub labels now elide to the room beside their field.

**The rule** is documented in `docs/ui-design.md`: wrap by default; beside a fixed control, elide; a *redundant* caption may drop on a narrow dock (the lock icons carry the meaning). This mirrors Photoshop — a fixed layout with elision + tooltips, not per-locale reflow.

**Other places to adopt this preventatively** (each is a label sharing a row with a fixed-width control, so it can overrun in a longer locale):
- the **Opacity** label — #2309 drops it on a narrow dock; it could elide instead,
- **options-bar** and **toolbar** labels (the densest rows),
- **filter / adjustment dialog** field labels,
- **brush / tool panel** rows,
- any new label added beside a fixed-width field.
Use `elided_label` when in doubt; the guard is structural, so it needs no per-language test.

Test: `widgets::tests::elided_label_never_exceeds_its_room`. Full `photocraft-ui-egui` suite (2077) passes; fmt and clippy clean.

title: test(ui): marquee shift+alt before the drag intersects the selection (#208)
author: agent-346022
body:
## Summary

The marquee already picks the **selection mode** from the modifier held at the press — `⇧` adds, `⌥` subtracts, `⇧⌥` intersects — rather than constraining the shape. `marquee_tests.rs` covered add and subtract but not **intersect**, which is the one case BUG-208-4 still calls out as missing (see #3516's note: *"Missing: a test that Shift+Alt held before a marquee drag intersects"*). This adds exactly that test.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/marquee_tests.rs` — `shift_alt_before_the_drag_intersects_the_selection`: fixes an existing selection, holds `⇧⌥` at the press (then releases the keys so the drag stays a plain rectangle, isolating the mode from the square/centre shape constraints) and drags a second rectangle. It samples three points — one in the overlap, one only in the existing selection, one only in the dragged rectangle — so it passes for intersect and fails for replace, add or subtract.

Test only, no production change. Scoped to the test alone so it does not touch the scorecard rows #3516 is editing; once both land, BUG-208-4's last gap is closed.

Part of #208.

title: fix(windows): strip sizing border and clear WFCPRESENT on custom titlebar (#2850)
author: Korg1ch
body:
Closes #2850, closes #3225, closes #3430, closes #3550

## Summary

On Windows 10 with Intel Haswell OpenGL (`ig75icd64.dll` on Intel Iris Pro 5200 #2850 / HD Graphics 4600 #2246), keeping `WS_THICKFRAME` and `WS_EX_WINDOWEDGE` on an undecorated window leaves a 7 px non-client sizing border (`WINDOWINFO.cxWindowBorders = 7, cyWindowBorders = 7`) that offsets the WGL surface by `(7, 7)` px relative to pointer input and inflates maximized windows beyond `rcWork`. In addition, because winit 0.30 swallows `WM_NCCALCSIZE(wparam = 1)` when `MARKER_DECORATIONS` is false, `DefWindowProcW(WM_NCCALCSIZE)` (`xxxCalcClientRect` in `win32kfull.sys`) never runs after `WS_CAPTION` is stripped — leaving the kernel's internal `WFCPRESENT` flag set on `tagWND` so `WM_NCACTIVATE` and `SetWindowTextW` still paint the classic Windows Basic caption bar (`[icon] PhotoCraft [-] [□] [X]`) over the top bar.

```diff
 window_frame::service(cc, custom_titlebar)
+  send_viewport_cmd(ViewportCommand::Decorations(true))
+    # winit forwards WM_NCCALCSIZE(wparam=1) to DefWindowProcW and clears MARKER_UNDECORATED_SHADOW
   on each frame (raw_input_hook)
-    strip WS_CAPTION | WS_BORDER (kept WS_THICKFRAME | WS_EX_WINDOWEDGE -> 7px border & WFCPRESENT=1)
+    resizing = primary_mouse_button_down() && pointer_pressing_resize_zone(8pt)
+    strip WS_CAPTION | WS_BORDER | WS_THICKFRAME(!resizing) and WS_EX_WINDOWEDGE
+    if maximized && rcWindow != monitor.rcWork
+      SetWindowPos(rcWork, SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE)
+    else if style_dirty
+      SetWindowPos(SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE | SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE)
+        -> DefWindowProcW(WM_NCCALCSIZE) clears WFCPRESENT=0 and sets rcClient == rcWindow
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** On Windows 10 (Intel Iris Pro Graphics 5200, OpenGL, 1920×1080 with top taskbar `rcWork = (0, 30, 1920, 1080)`):
  ```text
  Normal:    style=0x160F0000 ex=0x00040110 borders=(7,7) win=(240,90,1680,990) cli=(240,91,1680,991…

title: Mixer Brush: render mixed paint during the stroke and commit the live result
author: durtyrobbin
body:
Mixer Brush currently defers its mixed result until release on this branch's original baseline. This contribution renders the mixed pixels during the stroke, samples the evolving visible composite onto a separate paint layer, and commits the prepared result as one Undo step without repainting it on release.

This is the first, focused contribution from the studio work: two commits covering the live mixer transaction, spatial Alt-click pickup, sampling behavior, allocation reductions, regression tests, and reproducible CPU benchmarks. Dynamic tips, splatter, knife, palette/rack, and AI are not included in this PR. The complete tested development series is available on [the contributor's studio branch](https://github.com/durtyrobbin/photocraft/tree/mixer-brush-live) for context; it is not proposed here as one large merge.

The code was qualified against baseline `29f1ff9e90f2581ea2964e3276d85c71ab7e79a0`, not today's main. Main was refreshed to `9441484d` before publication. Integration currently conflicts in `crates/engine/src/brush_cmds.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/alt_grab.rs`, and `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`; this draft is not merge-ready. Preserve the ordinary-brush prepared-commit work merged in #2131 and coordinate with #3605's live symmetry updates. Prior brush work #3098, #2885, and #2379 is identified in the validation ledger; no speedups from those contributions are claimed here. PDF/Binder contributions are untouched.

title: Responsive artboards: rules, variants, overview and export
author: Elvis33LE
body:
Responsive artboards bring reusable semantic layout behavior to multi-format documents. Designers can keep a master artboard, create size variants, assign per-layer rules and overrides, review layout findings across every format, then export affected boards safely or batch a campaign from the CLI.

## Review guide: three commits

1. **Engine and persistence** — versioned responsive document model, `.pcraft` v1→v2 migration, bounded anchor/resize/text-flow solver, variants and overrides, atomic cancellable propagation, conflict reporting, safe areas and diagnostics, PSD semantic-role round-trip, and the persistence/compatibility decision record.
2. **UI and workflow** — localized responsive properties, roles and safe-area controls, background reflow, all-formats overview, finding filters/navigation, canvas overlays, variant switching, and pre-export review for Files/PDF exports. Export skipping is opt-in; failed or truncated checks count as affected.
3. **Delivery** — `photocraft-cli responsive-batch` applies named presets/templates to multiple documents and refuses invalid presets before writing outputs.

User workflow and current format limits are in [docs/responsive-artboards.md](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/codex/responsive-artboards-delivery/docs/responsive-artboards.md); implementation choices are in [docs/decisions.md](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/codex/responsive-artboards-delivery/docs/decisions.md).

## Validation

title: fix(ui): a launch does not restore the Brush Settings window (#3548)
author: dottedt
body:
Fixes #3548.

My first pass said this wasn't reproducible — I was wrong, and the reporter's repro (open Brush Settings from the options-bar toggle, quit, relaunch) pinned it: Workspace > Remember Workspace Changes persists `prefs.panel_layout`, which is `dock::snapshot`, and its `panels` object held every flag including the floating `brush_settings`. On the next launch `dock::restore` applied it, so the window came back with nothing open.

This drops `brush_settings` from the snapshot and ignores it when restoring a layout (older saved layouts that carry it are handled too), so the workspace still remembers the real dock panels and layout but the transient Brush Settings window is never restored.

Test: `dock::tests::restoring_a_saved_layout_never_reopens_brush_settings`. Full `photocraft-ui-egui` suite (2077) passes; fmt and clippy clean.

title: HEIF: move the heic-rs pin from 0.1.1 to 0.1.4
author: s17sh70x2jfl031ag
body:
heic-rs 0.1.2 to 0.1.4 fix six panics on malformed files, which I found by fuzzing and reported privately upstream (credited in the [heic-rs changelog](https://github.com/tbraun96/heic-rs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)). Four panic in release builds: a `uuid` box too small for its extended type, a block starting right of the picture, a conformance window larger than the picture, and a reference row below the picture. Two only panic with overflow checks on: a PCM bit depth above the sample bit depth, and a slice QP out of range. heic-rs reports the API, MSRV and output as unchanged.

On native, `guarded()` already turns these panics into errors. The web build enables `heif`, though, and wasm32 aborts on panic (as the root `Cargo.toml` notes), so there a malformed HEIC file could take down the tab. With 0.1.4 the decoder returns an error instead.

**The change:** both exact pins move to `=0.1.4`: `crates/heif` and the codecs fuzz target, which calls heic-rs directly (leaving that one at 0.1.1 would stop the fuzz target building). `Cargo.lock` changes only heic-rs. `guarded()` and its comments stay: they describe 0.1.1 and remain a useful backstop.

**Checked**, as the pin comment asks:
- **HEIF corpus tests** (`cargo xtask corpus --heif`; codecs and io with `corpus,heif`, plus `photocraft-heif`): 20 passed on 0.1.1 and the same 20 on 0.1.4, including the comparisons with Apple's decodes.
- **Fuzz targets:** `decode_heif` and `decode_any` build on 0.1.4. All 397 crashing inputs my earlier fuzzing collected on 0.1.1 run clean through both, and a fresh 5-minute run of each (1.1 million inputs) found nothing.

title: Crop tool: a resized frame snaps its handle, not the pointer (#3638)
author: davidmann4
body:
Fixes #3638 (split out of #1919).

When you resize the crop frame with View › Snap on, the snap line can show on an edge while the frame stops a few pixels away from it. This happens with Auto Center Preview off and in Classic Mode, whenever the handle isn't grabbed exactly. A recrop over hidden pixels (Delete Cropped Pixels off) then commits a transparent strip. In Photoshop the frame edge lands on the edge it snaps to.

### Change
- `snap_ui::live_crop_handle` → `crop_handle` now covers every crop resize, not just Auto Center Preview ones. It snaps the handle of the frame `crop_ui` would build (`crop_mode::resized_frame` with Auto Center, `crop_ui::resized_turned` without), then moves the pointer by the difference: 1:1 without Auto Center, 2:1 with it (1:1 with Alt).
- The corner formula for a held ratio uses the matching growth factor (both sides with Auto Center or Alt, otherwise only the grabbed side).
- Before, resizes without Auto Center fell back to `snap_point(pointer)`, so the frame missed the target by the grab offset (up to the 8 px grab radius).

### Tests
- New `crop_mode::tests::a_recrop_handle_snaps_exactly_to_the_hidden_pixels_edge`: Delete Cropped Pixels off, crop, then recrop outward to the hidden edge. It covers Classic on/off × Auto Center on/off × right/top edge, top-left/bottom-right corner × grab offset −4/0/+4 px, plus the corners with the original ratio held. It checks the frame lands exactly on the edge, the committed size, and that the layer bounds match the new canvas (no transparent strip). On main, 24 of 32 combinations failed; all pass with this change.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests crop`: 102 passed
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib snap`: 28 passed
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

### Not verified
- Turned frames (angle ≠ 0) in Classic Mode now also go through handle snapping. The maths is the one the Auto Center path already…

title: fix(linux): avoid duplicate AppImage desktop launcher (#3623)
author: Korg1ch
body:
Closes #3623

## Summary

When a user runs the PhotoCraft AppImage on a system with an external AppImage integrator (`AppImageLauncher`, `appimaged`, `Gear Lever`), two launchers appear in the application menu: one created by the external integrator and one created by `packaging/linux/AppRun` (#617).

```diff
 packaging/linux/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop
+  X-AppImage-Integrate=false

 packaging/linux/AppRun :: integrate()
-  write $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop
+  if $DESKTOPINTEGRATION is set OR another $apps/*.desktop Exec= references $appimage
+    rm -f $apps/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop (clean up existing duplicate)
+  else
+    write $apps/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop
   install hicolor icons into $XDG_DATA_HOME/icons/hicolor
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** Running `AppRun` alongside an `AppImageLauncher` entry (`appimagekit-photocraft.desktop`) kept both `.desktop` files in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/applications`, and the packaged `.desktop` lacked `X-AppImage-Integrate=false`.
  **After:** `bash packaging/linux/apprun-test.sh` passes all 11 checks (including external `.desktop` deduplication, `DESKTOPINTEGRATION=AppImageLauncher`, and `X-AppImage-Integrate=false`):
  ```text
  $ sh -n packaging/linux/AppRun && bash -n packaging/linux/apprun-test.sh && bash packaging/linux/apprun-test.sh
  AppRun desktop integration ok
  ```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Self-contained in `packaging/linux/` (`AppRun`, `ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop`, `apprun-test.sh`).

**Blast Radius:** low

Affects only Linux AppImage desktop-entry integration; hicolor icons are still installed so Wayland compositors and external `.desktop` launchers resolve `Icon=ai.storyteller.photocraft`.

title: fix(engine): support copying and pasting multiple selected layers (#3588)
author: buivanvu94
body:
Closes #3588.

### Summary of Changes
- **Enable multi-layer copy**: In `can_copy`, enable `edit.copy` when multiple layers are selected without an active marquee selection (`d.doc.selection.is_none() && d.selected_layers().len() > 1`).
- **Support packaging multiple layers**: Replaced single-layer `whole_layer` with `whole_layers`, which collects all selected top-level layers (`top_level(&d.doc, &sel)`) into the clipboard `Document`.
- **Render fallback composite surface**: In `copy`, render the composite surface of the copied layers so that Paste Into, masks, channels, and external apps receive the composite pixels.
- **Select all pasted layers**: In `paste_layers`, record all newly inserted layer IDs and reselect them using `reselect(s, new_ids, last)`, matching Photoshop behavior.
- **Added tests**: Added unit tests in `crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs` verifying copying and pasting multiple layers within the same document (including undo in 1 step), across documents (with mode/depth adaptation), and ensuring marquee selection copies pixels rather than whole layers.
